---
id: comp-cache-manager
title: Cache Manager
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: []
realizes: [P-ZERO-EDIT]
uses_var: [VAR-CACHE-STORE-URL]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
---

# Cache Manager

## Purpose

A content-addressed cache: a get/put store keyed by
`(spec_bundle_hash, artifact/gate-inputs hash, gate_version, model_pin)`,
used by `generator`, `test-author`, `license-scanner`, and
`secret-scanner` to avoid redundant work on unchanged inputs.

## Rationale

Backs the merge pipeline's "cache every gate" mandate — pure
cost-avoidance since `D30`, when the actual rollback mechanism moved
to `provenance-checker`. Also the worked example behind `D2`: its one
declared
behavioral guarantee (`interface/guarantees/G-CACHE-001.md`, a retrofit
of the consistency property `R-CACHE-003` already stated) is what let
`generator` narrow its own blast-radius dependency to specifically that
guarantee, via `depends_on_guarantees`.

## Scope

**In scope:** the key/value contract, key formation, fail-closed behavior on
store errors, protection against a caller writing a result under the wrong
gate's key.

**Out of scope:** deciding *what* is cacheable or *when* to check the cache
(that's each calling gate's own concern — `cache-manager` is a dumb,
trustworthy store, not a policy engine); the actual backing store's storage
engine/scaling characteristics (treated as an implementation detail behind
`VAR-CACHE-STORE-URL`, including whether it resolves to a shared store or
the local fallback, `R-CACHE-009`); deciding whether a component's work was
ever *verified*, not just *produced* — `provenance-checker`'s job
(`D30`), using a different data source entirely.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

Every criterion below is `kind: compiled` — a third real component, after
`spec-linter` and `impact-analyzer`, whose entire behavior is deterministic
store logic with no model call anywhere in it.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

- ~~R-CACHE-003's "last-write-wins is safe only because gates are
  deterministic" assumption depends entirely on every other component in
  this system actually upholding its own determinism constraint. This
  component cannot verify that from the inside.~~ — resolved (`D24`):
  the precondition was stated too strongly, and has been corrected in
  `G-CACHE-001` rather than enforced from the outside. `license-scanner`/
  `secret-scanner` are byte-identical-deterministic by their own
  `constraints.md`, making last-write-wins trivially safe for them.
  `generator`/`test-author` are **not** — their own `constraints.md`
  already says so — but the guarantee never actually needed identical
  payloads, only that whichever write survives a race is itself an
  uncorrupted, legitimately-produced answer for that key, which their
  single-call-then-cache flow (`R-GEN-006`) already guarantees
  regardless of what a concurrent sibling call produces. See
  `AC-CACHE-009`.
- ~~Cache eviction/retention policy (how long entries live, whether
  there's a size bound on the backing store) is undecided~~ — resolved
  (`R-CACHE-008`): it has no correctness dimension to pin down. Eviction
  is always permitted, unconditionally — a caller already treats a miss
  as fully correct and expected regardless of cause (`R-CACHE-001`/
  `004`), so eviction only ever costs hit rate, never correctness. The
  exact policy stays an operational, backing-store-specific tuning
  choice, not a spec'd number.

## Change log

- Initial draft.
- `D24`: corrected `G-CACHE-001`'s determinism precondition and added
  `AC-CACHE-009` for the non-deterministic-writer case; resolves the
  open question above.
- `D30`: `VAR-CACHE-STORE-URL` is now optional, falling back to a local
  `.hotdocs/cache/` store (`R-CACHE-009`); `merge-orchestrator` no
  longer uses this component to decide whether to skip verification —
  that moved to the new `provenance-checker`, narrowing this
  component's role to pure cost-avoidance.
- `D40`: `R-CACHE-007` now enumerates the exact required payload keys
  for all six gate types — previously real, enforced validation logic
  (`_REQUIRED_PAYLOAD_KEYS` in `cache_manager.py`) that no spec file
  ever documented, found only once a real `generator` self-regeneration
  candidate wrote a `put` payload missing `component_id`/`model` and
  was correctly rejected by this component's own `put`. That same
  table lived only in `requirements/R-CACHE-007.md` — invisible to any
  dependent, since `R-ASSEMBLE-002` means a dependent's bundle only
  ever carries a dependency's `interface/` content. Moved the real
  table to `interface/data/CachedResult.md`; `R-CACHE-007` now just
  points to it, restoring `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §10's one-definition rule.
- `D212`: the CLI, `stats`, and a set `VAR_CACHE_STORE_URL` pinned to
  exact, tested behavior.
documents.constraints.md:
# Cache Manager — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Fail closed to "miss," never to a crash.** Per R-CACHE-004 — the
  same "the tool must keep working" principle applied elsewhere for
  model availability, applied here to a different subsystem.
- **Never return a stale or wrong-version result.** Per R-CACHE-005 — a
  false cache hit is strictly worse than a miss (a miss just costs
  recomputation; a false hit serves an incorrect result as if it were
  verified).
- **Performance.** `get`/`put` MUST add negligible latency relative to the
  gate work they're short-circuiting — a slow cache defeats the "cache
  every gate" mandate's purpose.
- **No model calls.** Pure store logic, same trust tier as `spec-linter` and
  `impact-analyzer`.
- **Eviction policy is unspecified by design, not by oversight.** Per
  `R-CACHE-008`, this component may evict anything, anytime, without
  correctness consequence — the exact policy is an operational tuning
  choice specific to whichever backing store `VAR-CACHE-STORE-URL`
  resolves to, not a number this spec pins.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI ``` python -m cache_manager inspect --spec-bundle-hash= --gate-inputs-hash= --gate-version= --model-pin=

[--repo-root=

] python -m cache_manager stats [--repo-root=] ``` `main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int` takes the tokens after `python -m cache_manager` (no `hotdocs` verb routes here) and returns the exit code. Each flag also takes the space form (`--model-pin

`). `--repo-root` defaults to the current directory. Output is one line of JSON on stdout: - `inspect` — `{"result": "miss"}`, or on a hit `{"result": "hit", "gate_type": , "stored_at": }`; never the payload. - `stats` — `{"entry_count": }`, the number of entries the local store currently holds (`0` when `VAR_CACHE_STORE_URL` is set). **Exit codes:** | Code | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `0` | Command completed; a miss is an answer, not a failure. | | `2` | Usage error: no subcommand, an unknown one, or a missing or unknown flag. |
documents.interface/data/CacheKey.md:
# `CacheKey`

```json
{
  "spec_bundle_hash": "sha256:...",
  "gate_inputs_hash": "sha256:...",
  "gate_version": "license_scanner@4.0.3+9f2c41ab07de",
  "model_pin": "claude-sonnet-5"
}
```

`gate_version` is `<gate_type>@<version>`, the gate type being one of
`CachedResult.md`'s and the part before `@`. A `CachedResult` put under a
key MUST have that same `gate_type`, or `put` raises
`SchemaValidationError` (`R-CACHE-007`).
documents.interface/data/CachedResult.md:
# `CachedResult`

```json
{
  "gate_type": "license_scanner",
  "payload": { "...": "gate-specific result shape" },
  "stored_at": "2026-10-02T00:00:00Z"
}
```

`gate_type` MUST match one of the known gate types (`generator`,
`compiler`, `generated_test`, `llm_judge`, `license_scanner`,
`secret_scanner`) and `payload`'s shape MUST match that type's expected
schema — enforced by `put` (R-CACHE-007), not left to the caller's
discipline. `generator` was a real, pre-existing gap: this component's
own `Purpose` names `generator` as a consumer, but the original
gate-type list omitted it — found only once a real `generator` was
actually wired to call `put`/`get` for its own `GenerationResult`
payloads.

**Each gate type's exact required top-level payload keys** (`D40` —
  this table, not just R-CACHE-007's prose assertion that validation
  happens, MUST live here: a dependent only ever sees a dependency's
  `interface/` content, never its `requirements/` — R-ASSEMBLE-002 —
  so a `requirements/`-only copy of this table is invisible to a cold-
  mode caller assembling a real `put` call against this contract):

| `gate_type` | Required top-level payload keys |
| --- | --- |
| `generator` | `component_id`, `model`, `prompt_version`, `files` |
| `compiler` | `outputs`, `gate_version`, `summary` |
| `generated_test` | `component_id`, `criterion_id`, `model`, `file` |
| `llm_judge` | `result`, `rationale` |
| `license_scanner` | `component_id`, `gate_version`, `similarity_score`, `blocked`, `matches` |
| `secret_scanner` | `scope`, `gate_version`, `flagged`, `matches` |

A deliberately shallow key-presence check, not a full JSON-schema
validator — extra keys are permitted; only a missing required key
rejects a `put`.
documents.interface/guarantees/G-CACHE-001.md:
# G-CACHE-001

**G-CACHE-001** — Writes to the same cache key from concurrent callers
  MUST be safe under last-write-wins semantics: no write MUST corrupt,
  partially overwrite, or merge with another. For a deterministic gate
  (`license-scanner`, `secret-scanner`, any `compiled`-kind gate,
  deterministic by default), every concurrent writer produces an identical payload for a
  given key by construction, so it never matters which write survives.
  For a gate whose own `constraints.md` scopes determinism more
  narrowly (`generator`, `test-author` — only a cache *hit* is required
  to be byte-identical, not every call capable of producing one), two
  concurrent misses on the same key MAY legitimately produce two
  different, independently-valid payloads; last-write-wins then means
  whichever survives is still a correct, uncorrupted answer for that
  key — an arbitrary but valid choice between two acceptable results,
  not a sign anything broke. A caller MAY rely on `get`/`put`'s
  atomicity without its own locking or coordination; no caller MAY rely
  on a `put` it issued being the one a later `get` for the same key
  returns.

  **What a dependent is actually promised here, concretely:** a `get`
  issued shortly after a concurrent `put` for the same key, from a
  *different* caller than the one that wrote it, MAY safely be treated as
  authoritative the moment it returns a hit — no staleness window, no
  eventual-consistency delay, as long as the precondition above holds.
  This is the worked example `D2` was built around: if `cache-manager`'s
  backing store ever changes from a single-node store to one with weaker
  consistency (e.g. a distributed cluster with eventual consistency across
  nodes), *that* is a change to this guarantee, not an internal detail —
  it lives here, under `interface/`, specifically so such a change is
  visible to and propagates toward whatever depends on it (`D2`), rather
  than silently invalidating an assumption nobody could see was being
  relied upon.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
get(cache_key: CacheKey, *, repo_root: Path = None) -> CachedResult | Miss
put(cache_key: CacheKey, result: CachedResult, *, repo_root: Path = None) -> None
now_iso() -> str
stats(*, repo_root: Path = None) -> dict
class Miss
class SchemaValidationError(ValueError)
```

`CacheKey` and `CachedResult` are dataclasses with the fields of their
data documents, in that order, built by keyword. `Miss` is a class;
`get` reports a miss by returning an instance of it, never `None`, so a
caller tests `isinstance(result, Miss)`; any two `Miss` instances compare
equal. `put` raises `SchemaValidationError` for `R-CACHE-007`. `stats`
returns `{"entry_count": n}`, what the CLI's `stats` prints. `now_iso()` returns the current
UTC time as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, the form `CachedResult.stored_at`
takes.

Backed by the store at `VAR-CACHE-STORE-URL`. `get` never raises on a
backing-store error — it returns `Miss` (R-CACHE-004). `put` raises a
schema-validation error (not a silent no-op) if `result`'s shape doesn't
match what `cache_key.gate_version`'s gate type expects (R-CACHE-007).

`repo_root` (added `D30`, the same pre-existing-gap pattern
`llm-endpoint`'s `backend` parameter and `provenance-writer`'s
`ProvenanceInputs` each already were) — resolves which repository's
`.hotdocs/cache/` the local fallback (`R-CACHE-009`) reads/writes.
Defaults to the current working directory, matching `interface/cli.md`'s
own `--repo-root` flag, which implied this parameter existed all along.
documents.requirements/R-CACHE-001.md:
# R-CACHE-001

**R-CACHE-001** — `get` MUST return either the stored result for an exact
  key match, or a definitive miss — never a partial, approximate, or
  "probably equivalent" result.
documents.requirements/R-CACHE-002.md:
# R-CACHE-002

**R-CACHE-002** — The cache key MUST be exactly the 4-tuple
  `(spec_bundle_hash, artifact/gate-inputs hash, gate_version, model_pin)`
  (`notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D13), computed identically regardless of
  which calling component invokes
  `get`/`put` — the key-formation logic is this component's responsibility,
  not each caller's, so every gate hashes consistently.
documents.requirements/R-CACHE-003.md:
# R-CACHE-003

**R-CACHE-003** — `put` MUST uphold the consistency guarantee declared in
  `interface/guarantees/G-CACHE-001.md` — concurrent calls (from parallel
  gate runs, per the merge pipeline's "parallelize independent gates"
  rule) MUST NOT corrupt
  either entry, and `put` MUST NOT silently merge or partially overwrite a
  stored result. (Retrofitted during `D2` to reference the guarantee file
  directly rather than restate its content — the same "generated code
  MUST match `interface/` exactly" pattern `verifier-orchestrator`'s
  R-VERIFY-004 already established for type contracts, applied here to a
  behavioral one.)
documents.requirements/R-CACHE-004.md:
# R-CACHE-004

**R-CACHE-004** — On any backing-store error (unreachable
  `VAR-CACHE-STORE-URL`, timeout, corrupt stored entry), `get` MUST return a
  miss, never raise an exception or crash the caller — the same "the tool
  must keep working" posture `notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D10
  established for model availability, applied
  here to the cache: a broken cache degrades to "nothing is cached yet," not
  to a pipeline outage.
documents.requirements/R-CACHE-005.md:
# R-CACHE-005

**R-CACHE-005** — `gate_version` MUST be part of the lookup key itself, not
  metadata checked after retrieval — a `get` for `gate_version: "2.0.0"` MUST
  NOT return an entry stored under `gate_version: "1.0.0"`, even if every
  other key component matches.
documents.requirements/R-CACHE-006.md:
# R-CACHE-006

**R-CACHE-006** — MUST expose a CLI inspection command reporting hit/miss
  and (on hit) the stored result's provenance-relevant fields for a given key
  or its components, without requiring direct access to the backing store's
  native tooling, exactly as `interface/cli.md` defines it, with a
  `stats` command reporting the local store's entry count.
documents.requirements/R-CACHE-007.md:
# R-CACHE-007

**R-CACHE-007** — `put` MUST reject (not silently accept) a result payload
  whose shape doesn't match the schema expected for the `gate_version`'s
  declared gate type — guards against cache poisoning from a caller bug
  writing, e.g., a `LintReport`-shaped payload under a `license_scanner`
  `gate_version`.

  Each gate type's exact required payload keys are documented once, in
  `interface/data/CachedResult.md` (`D40`) — not repeated here, since a
  dependent only ever sees a dependency's `interface/` content, never
  its `requirements/` (`R-ASSEMBLE-002`); a copy living only in this
  file would be real and correct but invisible to anything cold-
  assembling a bundle against this contract.
documents.requirements/R-CACHE-008.md:
# R-CACHE-008

**R-CACHE-008** — This component MAY evict any entry at any time, for any
  reason, without coordinating with or notifying any caller. No caller
  MUST ever assume a prior `put` guarantees a later `get` for the same key
  will hit.

  **Resolves the eviction/retention open question by establishing that it
  has no correctness dimension to resolve:** `R-CACHE-001` already
  requires `get` to return a definitive miss, never an approximation, and
  `R-CACHE-004` already requires a backing-store problem to degrade to
  "nothing is cached yet," never a crash. An evicted entry is, from a
  caller's perspective, indistinguishable from either of those — a plain
  miss, already a fully specified, correct outcome everywhere a cache
  lookup happens in this corpus. Eviction only ever affects **hit rate**
  (and therefore cost, per `notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D13), never
  correctness. The exact
  policy — a size bound, a TTL, both, neither — is deliberately left
  unpinned here: the backing store is pluggable (`VAR-CACHE-STORE-URL`),
  and the right policy genuinely depends on which store it ends up being
  (a size bound makes sense for a local file-based store; a TTL makes more
  sense for a managed, shared one) — a single number pinned in this spec
  would be guessing at operational conditions this component has no
  visibility into.
documents.requirements/R-CACHE-009.md:
# R-CACHE-009

**R-CACHE-009** — When `VAR-CACHE-STORE-URL` is absent, `get`/`put`
  MUST fall back to a local, file-based store under `.hotdocs/cache/`
  rather than treating every call as a miss. This is a different backing
  store, not a different contract: `R-CACHE-001`/`002`/`005`/`007`
  apply exactly the same way regardless of which backing is active, and
  `R-CACHE-004`'s fail-to-miss behavior on a backing-store error applies
  unconditionally to the local fallback too. `.hotdocs/cache/`'s data is
  governed entirely by this component's own schema (`CacheKey`/
  `CachedResult`) — it is colocated with `merge-tracker`'s `.hotdocs/`
  subdirectories for convenience only, not governed by that component's
  rules.

  This fallback is correctness-neutral regardless of project size: since
  `D30`, a `cache-manager` hit or miss only ever affects whether a model
  gets called again, never whether verification is skipped (that
  question moved to `provenance-checker`, which never consults this
  store) — so a local-only backing carries no risk beyond its own
  (single-machine) hit rate.

  The store URL is read from the environment variable
  `VAR_CACHE_STORE_URL`. No client for a shared store exists yet, so
  when it is set to any non-empty value, `get` MUST return `Miss` and
  `put` MUST validate the result (`R-CACHE-007`) and then store nothing:
  the unreachable-store case of `R-CACHE-004`, never a crash.

---
id: comp-capability-scenario-verifier
title: Capability Scenario Verifier
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-criterion-compiler, comp-test-author, comp-llm-endpoint]
realizes: [P-ZERO-EDIT, P-AMBIGUITY-GATE]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
---

# Capability Scenario Verifier

## Purpose

Runs the capability scenarios of every product capability whose
`realizes`-set intersects a merge's blast radius, against the real,
fully assembled `gen/` output produced by that merge — the permanent,
cross-component backstop for behavioral risk no `interface/`-level
diffing can fully rule out by documentation alone. Structurally, the
cross-component analog of what `verifier-orchestrator` already does
per-component: same dispatch mechanisms
(`criterion-compiler`/`test_author`/`judge`), one scope level up.

## Rationale

Covers `interface/guarantees/` too (`D2`), for the reason `R-IMPACT-008`
states. Extracted from `merge-orchestrator` (`D14`) when that
component's fan-out and word caps crowded together. Renamed from
"golden-scenario-verifier": a capability-level analog of a component's
acceptance criteria, one scope level up.

## Scope

**In scope:** the capability-intersection lookup; dispatching each
scenario by its declared `kind` with the mechanisms `verifier-orchestrator`
established; one result per scenario, keyed by `P-id`; checking and
writing its own provenance for one capability, keyed on its realizing
components' actual content (`R-SCENARIO-004`) — called internally by
`provenance-tracker`'s `hotdocs verify`, never by a developer directly.

**Out of scope:** deciding whether a merge proceeds
(`provenance-tracker`'s readiness check does, `D88`); authoring
capability scenarios, a product-spec author's job; re-deciding a
scenario's `kind`, fixed at authoring time.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

Every criterion is `kind: generated-test` (`D43`) — dispatch-and-
aggregate logic, tested with fake dependencies placed under a temporary
`repo_root` and asserting on call arguments and results, the pattern
`verifier-orchestrator` established for coordination logic. None is
written in the step-phrase grammar, so `kind: compiled` would not
describe how they are really verified.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None — extracted whole from `merge-orchestrator`'s already-resolved
`R-MERGE-014`/`R-MERGE-020`, not a fresh design.

## Change log

- Initial draft (extracted from `merge-orchestrator`, `D14`); renamed
  from `golden-scenario-verifier`; per-scenario report granularity (`D23`).
- `D59`–`D61`, `D68`: first real implementation; where scenarios live;
  `realizes` is per-component; `generated-test` always dispatched fresh.
- `D87`–`D93`: own provenance mechanism (`R-SCENARIO-004`), keyed on
  realizing components' actual content; no CLI; wires its own closures.
- `D174`: specified `check_capability_provenance`/`run_capability_gates`,
  never built until now. Scenarios are actually run (`R-SCENARIO-005`),
  the key covers the capability's own scenarios, the closures are
  specified (`R-SCENARIO-007`/`008`), and `interface/cli.md` is removed.
- `D175`: cold-generated and landed at 12/12, `mutation_score` 0.84. A
  `compiled` capability scenario cannot pass with `surface=None`.
- `D198`: the test author's bundle names the realizing modules.
documents.constraints.md:
# Capability Scenario Verifier — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Determinism of dispatch, not of everything dispatched to.** This
  component's own capability-intersection lookup and aggregation MUST be
  deterministic given the same blast radius and corpus state; an injected
  `llm-judge` or `test_author` callable's actual output is explicitly not
  covered by that guarantee — the same caveat `verifier-orchestrator`'s
  own constraints already state, for the same reason.
- **`kind:` is read-only input, never written.** Same invariant
  `verifier-orchestrator` honors: a capability scenario's declared `kind`
  is fixed at spec-authoring time and never reinterpreted here.
- **Never conflated with a single component's own verification result.**
  `CapabilityScenarioReport` is a distinct namespace (`P-id`-keyed) from
  any component's `VerificationReport` — a cross-component finding and a
  single-component finding point a developer to different places to fix
  the problem.
- **Never a pass without a run.** A `compiled` or `generated-test`
  scenario passes only when its test actually ran and exited `0`
  (`R-SCENARIO-005`); producing a test, or compiling one, is not a pass.
- **A failure is recorded, never hidden.** A failing capability is
  written to its record and returned like a passing one, and a recorded
  failure is a hit until the code it was computed against changes.
- **Fail closed on the key.** Any doubt about a record — absent,
  unreadable, from another `gate_version`, or hashed over different
  content — is a miss, never a hit.
documents.interface/data/CapabilityProvenanceCheck:
# `CapabilityProvenanceCheckResult`

```json
{
  "hit": true,
  "capability_scenario_report": { "P-ZERO-EDIT": { "overall": "pass", "scenarios": [] } }
}
```

`capability_scenario_report` is a `CapabilityScenarioReport` holding
just the one `P-id`. `check_capability_provenance` sets it, copied from
the committed record, exactly when `hit` is `true`, and `null`
otherwise. `run_capability_gates` returns a hit unchanged; after a
fresh run it returns `hit` `false` with the fresh report, since nothing
was reused (`R-SCENARIO-004`). The shape mirrors `provenance-checker`'s
`ProvenanceCheckResult` so `provenance-tracker` reads both the same way.

## The committed record

`verification/capabilities/<capability_id>/.provenance.json`
(`R-SCENARIO-006`):

```json
{
  "capability_id": "P-ZERO-EDIT",
  "gate_version": "capability_scenario_verifier@2.0.0",
  "content_hash": "sha256:...",
  "realizing_components": ["comp-cache-manager"],
  "capability_scenario_report": { "P-ZERO-EDIT": { "overall": "pass", "scenarios": [] } },
  "model": "claude-sonnet-5",
  "seed": 0
}
```
# `CapabilityScenarioReport`

```json
{
  "P-ZERO-EDIT": {
    "overall": "pass",
    "scenarios": [
      { "id": "CS-ZERO-EDIT-001", "kind": "generated-test", "result": "pass" }
    ]
  }
}
```

A capability with more than one scenario, including one `llm-judge`-kind
scenario that failed:

```json
{
  "P-FOO": {
    "overall": "fail",
    "scenarios": [
      { "id": "CS-FOO-001", "kind": "compiled", "result": "pass" },
      { "id": "CS-FOO-002", "kind": "llm-judge", "result": "fail", "rationale": "..." }
    ]
  }
}
```

Keyed by `P-id` — one top-level entry per product capability whose
`realizes`-set intersected the blast radius this run
(`R-SCENARIO-001`/`002`), never one entry per component. `scenarios` is
one entry **per capability scenario** (`D23` — moved off the single
aggregate verdict `GoldenScenarioReport` used to have, the same
per-criterion granularity `VerificationReport.criteria[]` already has),
each carrying its own `id`, `kind`, and `result` (`pass`/`fail`/
`skipped`, mirroring `VerificationReport`'s vocabulary exactly).
`rationale` is present only on entries whose `kind` is `llm-judge` and
that actually dispatched — `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §5's existing,
corpus-wide rule ("An `llm-judge` criterion MUST emit structured
rationale alongside its verdict"), the same field `VerificationReport.
criteria[]` and `Finding` already carry for the same reason. `overall`
aggregates the capability's own `scenarios` the same way
`VerificationReport.overall` aggregates `criteria` (`R-VERIFY-005`): a
`skipped` `llm-judge` scenario alone doesn't fail `overall`, a genuine
`fail` does.

Embedded unchanged inside `CapabilityProvenanceCheckResult`
(`R-SCENARIO-004`, `D89`) and, read from there, into
`provenance-tracker`'s own `VerifyReport.capabilities` (`D88`) — this
component returns the value as part of `run_capability_gates`'s own
result; writing the committed provenance record is this component's
own job (`R-SCENARIO-004`), not a separate caller's.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
run_capability_scenarios(blast_radius: list[str], repo_root: Path, judge=None, test_author=None) -> CapabilityScenarioReport
check_capability_provenance(capability_id: str, repo_root: Path) -> CapabilityProvenanceCheckResult
run_capability_gates(capability_id: str, repo_root: Path, model: str | None = None, seed: int = 0, llm_backend=None) -> CapabilityProvenanceCheckResult
GATE_VERSION: str  # "capability_scenario_verifier@2.0.0" (R-SCENARIO-006)
class UnknownCapabilityError(ValueError)
class ModelRequiredError(ValueError)
```

`run_capability_scenarios` takes injected `judge`/`test_author`
callables of the shape the glossary defines under
"Injected `judge`/`test_author` callable shape" (`D65`), read
duck-typed on the way out. `run_capability_gates`
takes `model`, `seed`, and `llm_backend` instead and builds those
callables itself (`R-SCENARIO-007`, `R-SCENARIO-008`); this is the one
function `provenance-tracker`'s `hotdocs verify` calls, as
`run_capability_gates(capability_id, repo_root, model, seed,
llm_backend)`, passing its own three values through unchanged, after
`check_capability_provenance(capability_id, repo_root)` (`R-TRACK-010`).
A developer never invokes this component directly: it has no CLI
(`D92`, `D174`).

## Dependencies

Each is loaded lazily, at its first use, from `repo_root`, or from the
tool root when the directory shown is absent there (`D199`); never by a
bare `import`; as a flat `<module>.py` or
a `<module>/__init__.py` package under the directory shown, and its
results are read with dual dict-or-attribute access. No name beyond
these is used.

- `criterion-compiler`, a sealed component, from
  `<repo_root>/pipeline/criterion-compiler/`: `criterion_compiler.
  ParsedCriterion(criterion_id=, covers=, kind=, gherkin=, file=)`, and
  `compile_criterion(parsed, surface=None)`, returning `{"status":
  "compiled", "source": <pytest source>}` or `{"status": "error",
  "message": <text>}`.
- `test-author`, from `<repo_root>/gen/test-author/`: `test_author.
  author_test(bundle, model, seed=, repo_root=, llm_backend=)`, whose
  result has `model_call_error` and `file` (`path`, `content`).
- `llm-endpoint`, from `<repo_root>/gen/llm-endpoint/`: `llm_endpoint.
  complete(prompt, model, backend=)`, whose response has `text` and
  `model_call_error` (with `message`).

## Test fixtures

A test builds a temporary `repo_root` and supplies `test-author` and
`llm-endpoint` as small fake modules at the paths above, and copies the
real compiler from the live repository's `pipeline/criterion-compiler/`
to the same relative path. A fake embeds no secret-shaped string. Every
fixture uses exactly these shapes, because the code under test reads
them and nothing else:

- a component: `specs/components/<slug>/component.md` with frontmatter
  `id: comp-<slug>`, `realizes: [P-X]`, `sealed: false`, plus its code
  under `gen/<slug>/` (a sealed one instead has `sealed: true`,
  `source_path: pipeline/<slug>/`, and its code there);
- a capability: `specs/product/<name>.md` — never `specs/capabilities/`
  — with frontmatter `id: P-X`, then one `### CS-X-001` section per
  scenario holding `Covers: P-X`, `Kind: <kind>`, and a fenced
  `gherkin` block of plain `Given`/`When`/`Then` lines, no `Scenario:`;
- a fake `author_test` result: `{"model_call_error": None, "file":
  {"path": "verification/capabilities/P-X/generated-test/test_cs_x_001.py",
  "content": "def test_x():\n    assert True\n"}}` — the `path` is always
  repo-relative under `verification/`;
- a fake `author_test` is called as `author_test(bundle, model, seed=,
  repo_root=, llm_backend=)` with `R-SCENARIO-007`'s dict, so it reads
  `bundle["criterion_id"]` (the scenario id) and `bundle["criterion_text"]`
  (its Gherkin), never `scenario_id` or `gherkin`; only a callable
  passed to `run_capability_scenarios` receives the `R-SCENARIO-003`
  bundle with `scenario_id`. A fake `complete(prompt, model, backend=)`
  returns `{"text": ..., "model_call_error": None}`;
- a report: `{"P-X": {"overall": ..., "scenarios": [{"id": ..., "kind":
  ..., "result": ...}]}}`.
documents.requirements/R-SCENARIO-001.md:
# R-SCENARIO-001

**R-SCENARIO-001** — Given a blast-radius component-id set, MUST
  determine every product capability whose `realizes`-set intersects it
  (`R-SCENARIO-002`) and run each one's capability scenarios against the
  real, fully assembled `gen/` output — not a prediction. Each scenario
  is dispatched by its declared `kind` — `compiled` via
  `criterion-compiler`, `generated-test` via `test_author`, `llm-judge`
  via `judge` — with no new dispatch machinery, and `kind` is never
  reinterpreted. For `compiled` and `generated-test`, dispatch means
  producing a test **and running it** (`R-SCENARIO-005`): a scenario
  passes only if that run passes.

  **Where scenarios live** (`D59`): there is no `specs/capabilities/`
  directory. A capability's scenarios are `### CS-<id>` sections inside
  its own `specs/product/<name>.md` (`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §3.1), each
  with `Covers:`, `Kind:`, and a Gherkin block — a component's
  `acceptance/` file shape, nested in one file.

  **`compiled` MUST use `criterion-compiler`'s `compile_criterion`**
  (`R-COMPILE-012`), never its directory-scanning `compile`, with
  `surface=None`: a capability scenario is black-box against the whole
  system, so a step still referencing a function or type is a located
  compile error, never silently skipped.

  The report carries one entry **per scenario**, each with `id`,
  `kind`, and `result`; an `llm-judge` entry that dispatched also
  carries `rationale` (`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §5). It is keyed by `P-id`,
  never by component, so `provenance-tracker` can report it separately
  (`R-TRACK-010`). A capability's `overall` is `"fail"` if any scenario
  failed, else `"skipped"` if it has scenarios and all were skipped,
  else `"pass"` — and `"fail"` if it has no scenarios at all, since a
  capability that verifies nothing never passes.
documents.requirements/R-SCENARIO-002.md:
# R-SCENARIO-002

**R-SCENARIO-002** — The capability-intersection lookup
  (`R-SCENARIO-001`) MUST be one query against the shared `edges` view
  (`specs/architecture/graph-query-engine.md`), not a bespoke
  intersection: `SELECT DISTINCT target_id FROM edges WHERE edge_type =
  'realizes' AND source_id IN (<blast-radius ids>)`.

  **`realizes` is declared per component, never per capability**
  (`D61`): it is the `realizes:` frontmatter field of a component's own
  `component.md`. No `specs/product/<name>.md` carries one. Without
  `graph-query-engine` as a dependency, the equivalent edge set is
  built by scanning every `specs/components/*/component.md`.

  A capability's **realizing set** is every component whose `realizes`
  names it. A component's **code directory** is `gen/<slug>/`, or, when
  it is `sealed: true`, its frontmatter `source_path`, both under
  `repo_root`. Both are used by `R-SCENARIO-005` and `R-SCENARIO-006`.
documents.requirements/R-SCENARIO-003.md:
# R-SCENARIO-003

**R-SCENARIO-003** — **The `bundle` passed to an injected `judge` or
  `test_author`** (`D65`) MUST be `{capability_id, scenario_id, covers,
  kind, gherkin, file}`, never a single component's `CriterionBundle`,
  since no one component owns a cross-component scenario (see the
  glossary's "Injected `judge`/`test_author` callable shape").

  **`generated-test` scenarios are ALWAYS dispatched fresh to
  `test_author`, never pre-checked against a cache file** (`D68`):
  unlike `verifier-orchestrator`'s `R-VERIFY-002`, there is no
  `verification/<component>/` to anchor a cache path to. This is not an
  inefficiency: `test_author` already checks `cache-manager` before any
  model call (`R-AUTHOR-004`), so an unchanged scenario is a fast cache
  hit one layer down. Omitting `test_author` makes a `generated-test`
  scenario `fail`; omitting `judge` makes an `llm-judge` scenario
  `skipped`.
documents.requirements/R-SCENARIO-004.md:
# R-SCENARIO-004

**R-SCENARIO-004** — MUST expose `check_capability_provenance(capability_id,
  repo_root)` and `run_capability_gates(capability_id, repo_root,
  model=None, seed=0, llm_backend=None)`, each returning a
  `CapabilityProvenanceCheckResult` (`D89`, `D92`, `D174`). An unknown
  `capability_id` — no `specs/product/*.md` whose frontmatter `id` is it
  — raises `UnknownCapabilityError` from both.

  `check_capability_provenance` is a pure read. It returns `hit` `true`
  iff the committed record (`R-SCENARIO-006`) is a readable JSON object
  whose `gate_version` and `content_hash` both equal the current ones,
  and then carries the record's `capability_scenario_report`. Any other
  case — no record, an unreadable one, a stale one — is `hit` `false`
  with the report `null`. A recorded **failing** report is still a hit:
  fixing the cause changes the content, and so the key.

  `run_capability_gates` checks first. On a hit it returns that result
  unchanged: no dependency loaded, no scenario run, nothing written,
  and no `model` needed. On a miss with `model` `None` it raises
  `ModelRequiredError` before loading, running, or writing anything.
  Otherwise it runs the capability's scenarios (`R-SCENARIO-001`) with
  the callables `R-SCENARIO-007` and `R-SCENARIO-008` build, writes the
  fresh record, and returns `hit` `false` with the fresh report for just
  this capability. A failing run is recorded exactly like a passing one.
documents.requirements/R-SCENARIO-005.md:
# R-SCENARIO-005

**R-SCENARIO-005** — A `compiled` or `generated-test` scenario MUST be
  decided by running its test, never by a test merely having been
  produced.

  A `compiled` scenario's test is the `source` that `compile_criterion`
  returns; a `status` of `"error"` is a `fail` with nothing written or
  run. A `generated-test` scenario's test is the `file` (`path`,
  `content`) its `test_author` returns; a `model_call_error`, or no
  file, is a `fail`.

  The runner writes the test itself, overwriting any earlier copy. A
  `generated-test` file goes to its returned `path`, which MUST be
  relative, under `verification/`, with no `..` segment, else the
  scenario is a `fail` and nothing is written. A `compiled` test goes to
  `verification/capabilities/<P-id>/compiled/test_<scenario id
  lowercased, `-` as `_`>.py`.

  It then runs `<current Python interpreter> -m pytest -q -p
  no:cacheprovider <path>` with `repo_root` as the working directory,
  `PYTHONPATH` set to the code directory (`R-SCENARIO-002`) of every
  component in the capability's realizing set joined by `os.pathsep`,
  and a 120-second timeout. Exit code `0` is a `pass`. Any other exit
  code, a timeout, or a failure to start is a `fail`.
documents.requirements/R-SCENARIO-006.md:
# R-SCENARIO-006

**R-SCENARIO-006** — The provenance key is `content_hash`:
  `"sha256:"` plus the SHA-256 over, in order, the bytes of the
  capability's own `specs/product/<name>.md`; then, for each component
  in the realizing set (`R-SCENARIO-002`) in component-id order, its id
  and every regular file under its code directory in sorted relative-path
  order — excluding any `__pycache__` directory and any file named
  `.provenance.json` — as relative path and bytes, every field
  `\0`-terminated. A component with no code directory contributes its id
  alone.

  It hashes actual code, deliberately not `spec_bundle_hash`: a
  spec-level hash would reopen the blind spot this component exists to
  close (`D2`). It also covers the capability's own file, so editing a
  scenario invalidates a prior pass.

  The record is `verification/capabilities/<capability_id>/.provenance.json`,
  a JSON object (sorted keys, two-space indent) with exactly
  `capability_id`, `gate_version`, `content_hash`, `realizing_components`
  (sorted ids), `capability_scenario_report` (this capability's report),
  `model` (string or `null`), and `seed`. Only `run_capability_gates`
  writes it, on a miss. `gate_version` is the module constant
  `GATE_VERSION`, `"capability_scenario_verifier@2.0.0"`; any change to
  `R-SCENARIO-005`'s execution or this hash MUST raise it here.
documents.requirements/R-SCENARIO-008.md:
# R-SCENARIO-008

**R-SCENARIO-008** — `run_capability_gates` MUST build its own `judge`
  callable. It is the contract `component-gate-runner`'s `R-GATE-010`
  states, stated here too because a bundle never carries another
  component's requirements. Given a scenario bundle, it makes exactly one
  `llm-endpoint` `complete(prompt, model, backend=llm_backend)` call.
  The prompt contains the scenario's Gherkin and `covers`, and the full
  text of every file under the code directory of each realizing
  component (skipping `__pycache__`), and asks for JSON
  `{"result": "pass" | "fail", "rationale": "..."}`.

  A reply wrapped in a Markdown code fence is unwrapped first. The
  callable returns the parsed `{result, rationale}`. A
  `model_call_error`, unparseable text, or a `result` other than
  `"pass"` or `"fail"` returns `{"result": "fail", "rationale": "judge
  unavailable: <reason>"}` — never a pass, and never raised.

# Citation Checker

## Purpose

Checks that every citation in a spec corpus resolves: decision numbers,
pointers to a section of another file, glossary citations, and the
`supersedes` and `builds_on` links between decision records. It reports
each one that does not as a finding for the linter's report.

## Rationale

Split out of `spec-linter` with its citation rules (`D242`).

## Scope

**In scope:** the rules in `requirements/`. "The linter" in a
requirement means this component's `check`.

**Out of scope:** the report, the CLI and every other rule, which stay
with `spec-linter`.

## Definitions

A **live document** is every `Doc` in the corpus except decision records.
A citation of `D1`–`D14`, frozen at the baseline reset and never written
as files, always resolves.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

None.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`. All `generated-test`, over small corpora written to a
temporary `repo_root`.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- `D242`: split out of `spec-linter`, with `R-LINT-026`–`030` renumbered
  `R-CITE-001`–`005`.
documents.constraints.md:
# Non-Functional Constraints

- **Read-only and deterministic.** `check` writes nothing, makes no
  network or model call, and returns the same findings in the same order
  for the same files.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
check(repo_root: Path) -> list[dict]
```

Loads the corpus with `corpus-loader`'s `load_corpus(repo_root)`, from
`<repo_root>/gen/corpus-loader/` or the same path under the tool root,
the parent of the nearest `gen` directory above this module's own file
(`D199`), and returns this component's findings. Each is a dict with
exactly `rule_id` (the requirement that produced it), `severity`
(`fail` or `warn`), `file` (relative to `repo_root`), `line` (an `int`,
`1` when no better line applies) and `message`, in the order of the
corpus's sorted file paths.

Implements: `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md`

documents.requirements/R-CITE-002.md:
# R-CITE-002

**R-CITE-002** — Every `` `<file>`'s "<Section>" section `` pointer in a
  live document MUST resolve: the file MUST exist, and MUST contain a
  heading matching `<Section>` exactly. Whitespace inside the backticks,
  a hard wrap included, is deleted first, not collapsed; a path starting with `<` is a
  placeholder, not a pointer (`D222`).
documents.requirements/R-CITE-003.md:
# R-CITE-003

**R-CITE-003** — Every `` the glossary's "<Term>" `` citation in a live
  document MUST resolve to a real bolded entry header in
  `specs/glossary.md` — same mechanism as `R-CITE-001` and `R-CITE-002`
  (`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §3.6) — matched case-exactly after collapsing
  whitespace, since prose hard-wraps. One trailing `,.;:` inside the
  closing quote is not part of the term, and a quoted text not starting
  alphanumerically, such as `"<Term>"` itself, is a placeholder, not a
  citation (`D176`).
documents.requirements/R-CITE-004.md:
# R-CITE-004

**R-CITE-004** — `supersedes`/`status: deprecated` consistency
  (`D71`): (1) every `supersedes: D<N>` MUST resolve
  to a real `specs/decisions/D<N>.md`, except `D1`–`D14`, never
  formalized as files and exempt from (1) and (2); (2) when it resolves, that file's `status` MUST be
  `deprecated` — `supersedes` means full replacement; (3) the inverse:
  every `status: deprecated` record MUST be named by at least one
  other real decision's `supersedes` field — never a standalone edit.

  Queries `nodes`/`edges`.
documents.requirements/R-CITE-005.md:
# R-CITE-005

**R-CITE-005** — Every `builds_on` entry MUST resolve to a real
  `specs/decisions/D<N>.md`, except `D1`–`D14`, never formalized as
  files. Queries `nodes`/`edges`.

status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]

# Component Gate Runner

## Purpose

Runs one component through its full per-component gauntlet — provenance
check, generation on a miss, verification dispatch, compliance scanning,
provenance write — producing one `ComponentPipelineResult`. A developer
invokes this directly (`hotdocs generate <component-id>`) to produce a
component's `gen/` content and provenance explicitly, before checking
`hotdocs verify` and committing.

## Rationale

Extracted from the since-removed `merge-orchestrator` (`D76`), then made
a developer-invoked command in its own right (`D86`, `D93`): generating
code is a deliberate, potentially expensive action a developer triggers
by name, distinct from `hotdocs verify`'s read-only check. `R-SIZE-002`
fires here (`fan_out` crowding `component_doc_words`) and is accepted:
wiring its own dependencies is genuinely this component's job.

## Scope

**In scope:** obtaining the canonical provenance key and short-
circuiting on a passing hit (`R-GATE-001`); on a miss, assembling,
generating once (cold mode), and verifying with its own `test_author`
and `judge` closures (`R-GATE-002`, `R-GATE-003`, `R-GATE-010`);
reporting a block and why (`R-GATE-004`); running both scans
(`R-GATE-005`); recording the attempt and, when a candidate was
produced, its provenance (`R-GATE-008`, `R-GATE-006`); routing a sealed
component straight to re-verification and recording its sealed
provenance (`R-GATE-007`); and the
`hotdocs generate` CLI (`R-GATE-009`).

**Out of scope:** deciding merge readiness — `provenance-tracker`'s
`hotdocs verify`, reading what this component wrote; sequencing
`generate` calls across a multi-component change in `depends_on` order —
the developer's own discipline (`R-ASSEMBLE-011`).

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`. All `kind: generated-test`: every dependency is
faked under `gen/<slug>/` and the tests assert on call order,
arguments, and the returned `ComponentPipelineResult`.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- Initial draft (`D76`), extracted from `merge-orchestrator`.
- `D86`–`D93`: became the developer-invoked `hotdocs generate`, wiring
  its own closures and writing the attempt record via
  `provenance-tracker`.
- `D166`: rewritten before its first build — the canonical provenance
  key (`D163`), only a passing hit short-circuits, `blocked`/
  `block_reason` in the result, the exact dependency call list, the
  judge contract (`R-GATE-010`), CLI coverage (`R-GATE-009`).
  Cold-generated and landed at 13/13, `mutation_score` 0.88.
- `D170`: a sealed component now ends with a sealed provenance
  manifest written through `provenance-writer` (`R-GATE-007`);
  sealedness comes from `provenance-checker`'s `current_sealed_key`.

documents.constraints.md:
# Component Gate Runner — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Determinism of sequencing, not of everything sequenced.** Given the
  same mocked dependency outputs, this component's own call order and
  blocking decision for one component MUST be reproducible — the same
  posture `verifier-orchestrator` already follows.
- **No gate skipped silently.** A provenance hit (`R-GATE-001`) skips
  real work, but MUST be visible in `ComponentPipelineResult`.
- **Own wiring, own closures.** `test_author`/`judge` are constructed
  by this component itself from its own `model`/`seed`/`llm_backend`
  parameters (`R-GATE-002`, `D86`) — not received already-wired from a
  caller, since nothing calls this component on a developer's behalf
  anymore.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs generate <component-id> --model=<model-id> [--seed=<n>] \
  [--retry-feedback=<R-id>,...] [--repo-root=<dir>] [--format=json|text]
```

The one command a developer uses to (re)generate a component, distinct
from `hotdocs verify`'s read-only check (`D91`/`D93`). Run it across a
multi-component change in `depends_on` order; this component does not
sequence multiple calls itself (`R-ASSEMBLE-011`).

`main(argv)` receives `argv` beginning `["generate", <component-id>,
...]`. Every flag takes its value either as `--flag=value` or as the
next argument.

- `<component-id>` — `comp-<slug>`; it must have a
  `specs/components/<slug>/component.md` under `--repo-root`.
- `--model` — required, no default (`R-GATE-002`).
- `--seed` — integer, default `0`.
- `--retry-feedback` — comma-separated `R-id`s, passed to
  `run_component_gates` as a list; omitted means `None`.
- `--repo-root` — default the current directory.
- `--format` — `json` prints the `ComponentPipelineResult` as JSON,
  converting each nested value recursively: an object with `to_dict()`
  through it, a dataclass via `dataclasses.asdict`, any other object
  via `vars()`;
  `text` (default) prints the component id, `provenance hit` or the
  `block_reason` (`passed` when not blocked), and each scan's
  `blocked`/`flagged`; then `model_call_error: <category>: <message>`
  when one is set, and `license_scan not evaluated: <reason>` when the
  license scan's `evaluated` is false (read with dual dict-or-attribute
  access).

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | The gauntlet concluded — a hit, a pass, or a verification failure alike. |
| `1` | `block_reason` is `"model_call_error"`. |
| `2` | Usage error: a missing `<component-id>` or `--model`, an unknown component, a non-integer `--seed`, an invalid `--format`, an unknown argument, a wrong first word, or a flag given last with no value. |
documents.interface/data/ComponentPipelineResult.m:
# `ComponentPipelineResult`

```json
{
  "component_id": "comp-foo",
  "provenance_hit": false,
  "blocked": true,
  "block_reason": "verification_failed",
  "model_call_error": null,
  "verification": { "...": "a VerificationReport" },
  "license_scan": { "...": "a LicenseScanResult" },
  "secret_scan": { "...": "a SecretScanResult" }
}
```

`provenance_hit` (`R-GATE-001`) is `true` only on a short-circuiting
hit; `verification`/`license_scan`/`secret_scan` are then copied from
the `ProvenanceCheckResult`, `blocked` is `false`, and the other fields
are `null`.

Otherwise `blocked` (`R-GATE-004`) is `true` exactly when no passing
candidate exists: `block_reason` is `"model_call_error"` when
`generator` returned one (`model_call_error` copies it, `verification`
is `null`), or `"verification_failed"` when a candidate was produced
and `verification.overall` is not `"pass"`. A passing candidate has
`blocked` `false` and `block_reason` `null`. `model_call_error` and
`verification` are never both populated.

`blocked` concerns generation and verification only.
`license_scan.blocked` and `secret_scan.flagged` are reported as-is;
whether they stop a merge is `provenance-tracker`'s readiness check,
not this component's verdict.

Returned as a dict with exactly these keys.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
run_component_gates(
    component_id: str, repo_root: Path, model: str, seed: int = 0,
    llm_backend=None, retry_feedback: list[str] | None = None,
) -> ComponentPipelineResult
```

`model`/`seed`/`llm_backend` are this component's own parameters
(`D86`): it builds its own `test_author` and `judge` closures from
them (`R-GATE-002`, `R-GATE-010`). `retry_feedback` (`R-GATE-003`,
`D3`) is passed through to `generator` unchanged, never derived here.

Each dependency is loaded from `<repo_root>/gen/<slug>/`, or from the tool root's when absent (`D199`). The first
call, for every component, is `provenance-checker`'s
`current_sealed_key(component_id, repo_root)`: a non-`None` result means
the component is sealed and only the sealed calls below are made
(`D170`); `None` means every call in the next list, whose own first call
is `current_provenance_key`. On a non-sealed component, the calls are,
in this order:

1. `provenance-checker`'s `current_provenance_key(component_id,
   repo_root)`, then `check_provenance(component_id,
   key.spec_bundle_hash, key.gate_versions, repo_root)` — on a
   short-circuiting hit (`R-GATE-001`), nothing below is called
2. `spec-bundle-assembler`'s `assemble(component_id,
   repo_root=repo_root, mode="cold")`
3. `generator`'s `generate(bundle, model, retry_feedback,
   repo_root=repo_root, llm_backend=llm_backend)`
4. only if that result's `files` is non-empty: `verifier-orchestrator`'s
   `verify(component_id, repo_root, judge=<judge closure>,
   test_author=<test_author closure>)`
5. `license-scanner`'s `scan(component_id, repo_root)`, then
   `secret-scanner`'s `scan(repo_root)`
6. `provenance-tracker`'s `write_attempt_record(component_id,
   generation_result, verification_report_or_None,
   key.spec_bundle_hash, repo_root)`
7. only if step 3 produced files: `provenance-writer`'s
   `write_provenance(component_id, inputs, repo_root)`, with
   `ProvenanceInputs` as a plain dict `{component_id, generation_result,
   verification_report, license_scan_result, secret_scan_result,
   provenance_hit: false, attempts, gate_versions: key.gate_versions}`,
   where `attempts` is the number of files in
   `.hotdocs/attempts/<slug>/` after step 6

The `test_author` closure calls `test-author`'s
`author_test(criterion_bundle, model, seed=seed, repo_root=repo_root,
llm_backend=llm_backend)`. The `judge` closure calls `llm-endpoint`'s
`complete(prompt, model, backend=llm_backend)` (`R-GATE-010`).

A sealed component (`R-GATE-007`) makes exactly these calls, in this
order, passing both closures to `verify`:

1. `verifier-orchestrator`'s `verify(component_id, repo_root,
   judge=<judge closure>, test_author=<test_author closure>)`
2. `license-scanner`'s `scan(component_id, repo_root)`, then
   `secret-scanner`'s `scan(repo_root)`
3. `provenance-writer`'s `write_sealed_provenance(component_id,
   inputs, repo_root)`, with `inputs` a plain dict `{component_id,
   owners, source_path, source_hash, verifier_version,
   verification_report}`: `owners`, `source_path`, `source_hash`, and
   `verifier_version` are the `SealedKey`'s, `component_id` is the
   argument, and `verification_report` is the report from call 1

Each dependency module is loaded only when its first call is about to
be made, never earlier — a path that never reaches a call never loads
that module (the same rule `provenance-tracker`'s `R-TRACK-009` states).
No dependency name beyond this list is used: in particular,
`ProvenanceInputs` is a dict, never a class from `provenance-writer`.
Any stand-in for these dependencies must provide each name this list
gives. Results from every dependency are read with dual
dict-or-attribute access.

CLI: see `interface/cli.md`.
documents.requirements/R-GATE-001.md:
# R-GATE-001

**R-GATE-001** — For a non-sealed component, MUST first obtain the
  current provenance key from `provenance-checker`'s
  `current_provenance_key` and pass it to `check_provenance`
  (`D29`/`D163`) — never computing a hash or gate-version map itself.
  A hit whose `verification_report.overall` is `"pass"` and whose
  `license_scan.blocked` is not `true` MUST short-circuit: the result
  copies the hit's three reports, and nothing else in
  `interface/library.md`'s list is called — no generation,
  verification, scan, or write. Any other result, including a hit
  recording a failed attempt, proceeds as a miss, so a developer can
  always re-run a failed `hotdocs generate`. A sealed component is never
  checked (`R-GATE-007`).
documents.requirements/R-GATE-002.md:
# R-GATE-002

**R-GATE-002** — On a miss, MUST call `spec-bundle-assembler` then
  `generator` (cold mode) to produce a candidate, then, if it has
  files, `verifier-orchestrator` to check it — passing a `test_author`
  closure backed by `test-author` and a `judge` closure backed by
  `llm-endpoint` (`R-GATE-010`), each of the glossary's
  single-`bundle`-argument shape (`D65`).

  This component does its own wiring (`D86`): nothing calls it with
  closures already built, so its own `model`/`seed`/`llm_backend` are
  the only place a model identifier enters. Each closure captures
  them, exactly as `interface/library.md` states.
documents.requirements/R-GATE-003.md:
# R-GATE-003

**R-GATE-003** — MUST call `generator` **exactly once** per non-sealed
  miss per invocation — no automatic retry loop (`D3`). If that one call
  does not produce a passing candidate, the component is blocked
  (`R-GATE-004`) for this attempt. That call carries `retry_feedback`
  only when the caller supplied it (`--retry-feedback`, `D86`); this
  component never derives it.
documents.requirements/R-GATE-004.md:
# R-GATE-004

**R-GATE-004** — If the one generation attempt does not produce a
  passing candidate, the result MUST be `blocked`, never silently
  accepted, with a `block_reason` distinguishing `"model_call_error"`
  (no candidate was ever produced, and `verifier-orchestrator` was
  never called) from `"verification_failed"` (a candidate was produced
  and failed) — different facts for a developer deciding whether to
  re-run or fix the spec first (`D19`). Overall merge readiness stays
  `provenance-tracker`'s decision.
documents.requirements/R-GATE-005.md:
# R-GATE-005

**R-GATE-005** — On every path except a short-circuiting hit — a miss,
  whatever its generation outcome, and a sealed component — MUST invoke
  `license-scanner` and `secret-scanner`, never toggle-gated.
documents.requirements/R-GATE-006.md:
# R-GATE-006

**R-GATE-006** — On a non-sealed miss whose generation produced files,
  MUST invoke `provenance-writer` once, after verification, both scans,
  and the attempt record (`R-GATE-008`) have concluded, passing
  `ProvenanceInputs` built exactly as `interface/library.md` states —
  `gate_versions` from the same provenance key `R-GATE-001` obtained,
  so what is written and what is later checked come from one
  definition (`D163`). On a `model_call_error`, nothing new reached
  `gen/`, so no provenance is written.
documents.requirements/R-GATE-007.md:
# R-GATE-007

**R-GATE-007** — A component is sealed exactly when `provenance-checker`'s
  `current_sealed_key` returns a key for it (`D170`); this component
  never reads `component.md` itself. For a sealed component it MUST skip
  `provenance-checker`'s `check_provenance`, `spec-bundle-assembler`, and
  `generator` entirely, and call `verifier-orchestrator` to re-run its
  characterization tests against the code at `source_path`, then both
  scans (`R-GATE-005`). There is nothing to generate for a sealed
  component; re-running its tests unconditionally is what catches a hand
  edit at `source_path` that a spec-only hash would miss.

  It MUST then call `provenance-writer`'s `write_sealed_provenance`
  exactly once, after verification and both scans, whatever the
  verification outcome: a passing result records a current, passing
  manifest that makes the component ready, and a failing one records a
  failing manifest, so the owner and the failure are both on file. The
  key is read once, before verification, and its values are what is
  written. No attempt record and no `.provenance.json` is written for a
  sealed component. The result's `blocked` follows `R-GATE-004`'s
  `"verification_failed"` rule. `generator`'s `R-GEN-009` is the
  independent second layer of sealed-component write protection.
documents.requirements/R-GATE-008.md:
# R-GATE-008

**R-GATE-008** — On every non-sealed miss, MUST call
  `provenance-tracker`'s `write_attempt_record` (`R-TRACK-004`, `D19`)
  once, after generation, any verification, and both scans conclude,
  passing the full `GenerationResult`, the full `VerificationReport` or
  `None` when verification was never reached, and the provenance key's
  `spec_bundle_hash`. Called for every outcome — a failed attempt's
  detail is what a developer needs to choose `--retry-feedback` next
  time. An exception from this call MUST NOT change this component's
  result.
documents.requirements/R-GATE-009.md:
# R-GATE-009

**R-GATE-009** — `main(argv)` MUST implement `interface/cli.md`
  exactly: both flag-value forms, the defaults, `--retry-feedback`
  split on commas, JSON and text output, exit `0` whenever the gauntlet
  concluded, `1` when `block_reason` is `"model_call_error"`, and `2`
  for every usage error that document lists — each detected before
  `run_component_gates` is called (`D162`).
documents.requirements/R-GATE-010.md:
# R-GATE-010

**R-GATE-010** — The `judge` closure, given a `CriterionBundle`, MUST
  make exactly one `llm-endpoint` `complete` call whose prompt contains
  the bundle's `criterion_text`, `requirement_text`, and `interface`,
  and the full text of every file under `gen/<slug>/` (skipping
  `__pycache__`), and asks for JSON
  `{"result": "pass" | "fail", "rationale": "..."}`. A response
  wrapped in a Markdown code fence is unwrapped first. It returns that
  `{result, rationale}`. A `model_call_error`, unparseable text, or a
  `result` other than `"pass"`/`"fail"` returns `{"result": "fail",
  "rationale": "judge unavailable: <reason>"}` — never a pass, and
  never raised (`D166`).

---
id: comp-corpus-graph-builder
title: Corpus Graph Builder
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-graph-query-engine, comp-spec-linter, comp-provenance-writer, comp-verifier-orchestrator]
realizes: [P-AMBIGUITY-GATE]
sealed: false
---

# Corpus Graph Builder

## Purpose

Builds `verification/corpus-graph.json` — the single generated manifest
the corpus's traceability matrix and graph/docs explorer are both views
over. Walks `P-id → component → R-id → acceptance → verification-status`
and computes corpus-health aggregates.

## Rationale

The traceability-matrix need and the graph/docs explorer this manifest
also feeds were both established early on — this component is the
single source both read from, never two independently-computed copies.

## Scope

**In scope:** building the node/edge graph (products, components, vars);
attaching per-node status (verification, provenance, size-vs-caps,
sealed/override); computing orphan-capability, orphan-component, and
orphan-var rates as aggregate fields; the `hotdocs corpus-graph build`
command.

**Out of scope:** deciding when to rebuild (CI runs the command on
every merge to `main`); rendering anything visual (`docs-site-renderer`'s job);
computing verification or provenance itself (consumes what
`verifier-orchestrator`/`provenance-writer` already produced).

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

All ten are generated tests over small synthetic corpora, run against
the real `graph-query-engine`.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- Initial draft.
- `D29`: "cache hit" renamed "provenance hit" (`R-GRAPH-008`,
  `constraints.md`), following the corpus-wide rename.
- `depends_on` gained `comp-graph-query-engine` (R-GRAPH-009
  already required building from its views; the dependency was never
  declared — same drift `D13` found and fixed for `spec-linter`). First
  real `gen/corpus-graph-builder/` implementation, produced by a real
  generation step rather than hand-written.
- `D200`: acceptance criteria made concrete; nodes and provenance read
  as the manifest's own JSON; `graph-query-engine` loaded by path
  (`R-GRAPH-010`, `D199`); `R-GRAPH-007` now the CLI, the CI cadence
  moved to scope.
documents.constraints.md:
# Corpus Graph Builder — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Determinism.** Same corpus/provenance/verification state MUST always
  produce a byte-identical `corpus-graph.json` — needed both for
  `notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D6's commit discipline and so this file
  regenerates identically on a provenance hit like any other committed
  artifact.
- **Single source of truth.** No other component MUST produce a competing
  view of the corpus graph — `docs-site-renderer` and that file's own D8's
  traceability matrix both read this one file; neither recomputes any
  part of it.
- **No network access, no model calls.** Pure graph assembly over already-
  computed data.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs corpus-graph build [--repo-root=<dir>]
```

`main` receives the tokens from `build` on: `main(["build",
"--repo-root=/x"])`. `--repo-root <dir>` is accepted too; the default is
the current directory. On success it writes the file and prints its
path.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | `verification/corpus-graph.json` written. |
| `1` | Building failed, e.g. a `.provenance.json` that is not valid JSON. |
| `2` | Usage error: no `build`, another word, or an unknown argument. |

```json
      "type": "component",
      "verification": { "...": "the manifest's verification_report" },
      "provenance": { "...": "the manifest's other top-level fields" },
      "size_status": "ok",
      "sealed": false,
      "pinned_overrides": [],
      "owners": ["pipeline-team"],
      "documents": { "component.md": "<its text>", "requirements/R-FOO-001.md": "<its text>" }
    },
    "VAR-FOO-URL": { "type": "var" }
  },
  "edges": [
    { "from": "comp-foo", "to": "comp-bar", "kind": "depends_on" },
    { "from": "comp-foo", "to": "P-ZERO-EDIT", "kind": "realizes" },
    { "from": "comp-foo", "to": "VAR-FOO-URL", "kind": "uses_var" }
  ],
  "aggregates": {
    "orphan_capability_rate": 0.0,
    "orphan_component_rate": 0.0,
    "orphan_var_rate": 0.0
  }
}
```

`nodes` is keyed by id and holds only components, capabilities and
vars (never requirements, criteria or decisions). `edges` holds only
the three kinds shown, sorted by `from`, then `to`, then `kind`.

A component node's `verification` and `provenance` come from
`verification/<slug>/.provenance.json` read with `json.load`, so every
value is the file's own JSON (`generated_at` stays the string written
there): `verification` is its `verification_report`, `provenance` every
other top-level key. With no manifest both are `null`. `size_status` is
`"ok"` when the component's `component_size` word count is at most
`4000`, `"over"` above it, `"unknown"` with no row. `sealed` is the
frontmatter's `sealed` (absent is `false`). `pinned_overrides` is the
JSON list in `gen/<slug>/.overrides.json`, else `[]` (no file, or not a
list). `owners` is the frontmatter's `owners` list (absent is `[]`).
`documents` maps each `.md` file under `specs/components/<slug>/`, by its
path relative to that directory with `/` separators, to its whole text,
keys sorted.

Each rate is a count divided by a total, `0.0` when the total is `0`:
capabilities with no incoming `realizes` edge over all capabilities;
vars with no incoming `uses_var` edge over all vars; components with
neither an incoming `depends_on` edge nor an outgoing `realizes` edge
over all components.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

A package, `corpus_graph_builder/` (`__init__.py` plus `cli.py`, never a
flat module): `hotdocs-cli` runs `corpus_graph_builder.cli`'s `main`.
`__init__.py` exports:

```
build_corpus_graph(repo_root: Path) -> CorpusGraph
write_corpus_graph(graph: CorpusGraph, repo_root: Path) -> Path
```

`cli.py` exports `main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int`
(`interface/cli.md`, `R-GRAPH-007`).

`CorpusGraph` is a dataclass with attributes `nodes`, `edges` and
`aggregates` (`interface/data/CorpusGraph.md`), a `to_dict()` returning
that shape, and `to_json_bytes()` returning `json.dumps(to_dict(),
sort_keys=True, indent=2, ensure_ascii=True)` plus `"\n"`, UTF-8.
`write_corpus_graph` writes those bytes to
`<repo_root>/verification/corpus-graph.json`, creating `verification/`
if needed, and returns that path. `build_corpus_graph` writes nothing.

## graph-query-engine

`graph-query-engine` is loaded by file path (`R-GRAPH-010`), then used
on a fresh in-memory DuckDB connection: `INSTALL yaml FROM community`
(an error from it ignored), `LOAD yaml`, then `load_views(con,
repo_root)`. Tests use the real `graph-query-engine` and write no
stand-in for it: with no `gen/graph-query-engine/` under a test's
`repo_root` it comes from the tool root.

A test corpus therefore uses the files those views read, each opening
with a `---` YAML frontmatter block holding at least `id`, `title` and
`status`:

- a component: `specs/components/<slug>/component.md` with `id:
  comp-<slug>` and flow lists `depends_on: [comp-a]`, `realizes:
  [P-X]`, `uses_var: [VAR-Y]` (each may be `[]`), and `sealed: true` or
  `false`;
- a capability: `specs/product/<name>.md` with `id: P-<NAME>`;
- a var: `specs/vars/<name>.md` with `id: VAR-<NAME>`.

`component_size`'s `component_id` is the bare `<slug>`, not
`comp-<slug>`.

  `verification/corpus-graph.json` — the one artifact

documents.requirements/R-GRAPH-007.md:
# R-GRAPH-007

**R-GRAPH-007** — `corpus_graph_builder.cli.main(argv)` MUST implement
  `interface/cli.md` exactly: `build` with an optional `--repo-root`
  (`--repo-root=<dir>` or `--repo-root <dir>`, default the current
  directory) builds and writes the graph, prints the written path, and
  returns `0`; any exception while building returns `1`; anything else
  returns `2`, never raising. Rebuilding on every merge to `main` is
  the CI's job, not this component's (`D200`).
documents.requirements/R-GRAPH-008.md:
# R-GRAPH-008

**R-GRAPH-008** — The graph MUST be a deterministic function of corpus +
  provenance + verification state: the same inputs always produce the
  same `to_json_bytes()`, byte for byte, because this file is committed
  and must regenerate identically on a provenance hit like any other
  committed artifact. Every value in it is plain JSON; none is a type
  `json.dumps` cannot write, such as a timestamp DuckDB parsed out of a
  manifest (`D200`).
documents.requirements/R-GRAPH-009.md:
# R-GRAPH-009

**R-GRAPH-009** — Nodes and edges (R-GRAPH-001/002), the orphan rates
  (R-GRAPH-004/005) and size status MUST be computed from
  `graph-query-engine`'s shared `nodes`, `edges` and `component_size`
  views, never a third, independently written graph-construction step
  or word count (`D13`). Only the per-node verification and provenance
  are read from each manifest file itself, since a view's typed columns
  are not the file's JSON (`D200`).
documents.requirements/R-GRAPH-010.md:
# R-GRAPH-010

**R-GRAPH-010** — `build_corpus_graph` MUST load `graph-query-engine`'s
  `graph_query_engine.py` by file path from
  `<repo_root>/gen/graph-query-engine/`, or from the tool root's when
  that directory is absent (`D199`), never by a bare `import
  graph_query_engine`, which works only when a caller has already put
  that directory on `sys.path`.

id: comp-corpus-loader
title: Corpus Loader
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]

# Corpus Loader

## Purpose

Reads a spec corpus into one in-memory model: every spec file
classified, its frontmatter parsed, the components assembled from their
files, and the shared graph views loaded, so every component that needs
the corpus reads the same structure.

## Rationale

Split out of `spec-linter`, which had reached its size cap, because the
linter, both checkers and the bundle assembler read the same model
(`D242`).

## Scope

**In scope:** `load_corpus` and the `Corpus` model.

**Out of scope:** judging the corpus; every rule lives in `spec-linter`,
`citation-checker` or `size-checker`.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`. All `generated-test`, over small corpora written to a
temporary `repo_root`.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- `D242`: split out of `spec-linter`.
documents.constraints.md:
# Corpus Loader — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Read-only.** `load_corpus` writes nothing and makes no network or
  model call.
- **Deterministic.** The same files give the same `Corpus`, in the same
  order.
documents.interface/data/Corpus.md:
# `Corpus`

`spec-linter`, `citation-checker`, `size-checker`,
`spec-bundle-assembler` and `impact-analyzer` read the corpus only
through `load_corpus` (the last two by way of `spec-linter`, which
re-exports it). Dataclasses, fields in this order:

- `Doc(path, rel_path, doc_id, frontmatter, body, doc_type, component=None, has_frontmatter=False)`
- `Component(name, root, requirements, interface_cli, interface_library, interface_data, interface_guarantees, acceptance, constraints)`
- `Corpus(repo_root, docs, components, id_index, glossary_defs, glossary_files, graph)`

Each `specs/**/*.md` file, by sorted path, is one `Doc` (`path`
an absolute `Path`, `rel_path` a `str` relative to `repo_root` with `/`
separators), except `specs/glossary.md`, `README.md` files
and unlisted paths. `doc_type` under `specs/components/<c>/`:
`component.md` `component-root`, `requirements/R-*.md`
`component-requirement`, `interface/cli.md` and `library.md`
`component-interface-cli`/`-library`, `interface/data/*.md`
`component-interface-data`, `interface/guarantees/G-*.md`
`component-interface-guarantee`, `acceptance/AC-*.md`
`component-acceptance`, `constraints.md` `component-constraints`; files
directly in `specs/product|architecture|vars|decisions/` are `product`,
`architecture`, `var`, `decision`.

Frontmatter is a `---` block opening line 1: `[a, b]` a list of stripped
strings, `true`/`false` booleans, else a string with any surrounding
`"` or `'` removed (`title: "Quoted"` gives `Quoted`). `body` is `"\n".join(lines[k:])`, where `lines` is the file's
text split by `str.splitlines()` and `k` the index after the closing
`---`, so it has no trailing newline; with no block it is the whole
text unchanged.
`doc_id` is the file stem for requirements, criteria and guarantees, else
frontmatter `id`.

A `Component`'s `root` is the `Doc` of its `component.md` (`None` until
one is read), `interface_cli`/`interface_library`/`constraints` likewise
`Doc`s or `None`. `components` is keyed by directory name; `requirements`, `acceptance`,
`interface_guarantees` by `doc_id`; `interface_data` by stem. `id_index`
maps the `doc_id` of root, product, architecture, var and decision docs.
`glossary_defs` maps each lowercased `**term**` to its entry's text
after the bold header, leading `—`, `-` and whitespace removed, through
the entry's last line, stripped;
`glossary_files` lists absolute `specs/glossary*.md` paths. `graph` is a DuckDB
connection with `yaml` loaded and `graph-query-engine`'s views.
documents.interface/library.md:

```
load_corpus(repo_root: Path) -> Corpus
```

Returns the `Corpus` its data document defines, for the corpus under
`repo_root/specs/`. `graph-query-engine` is loaded from
`<repo_root>/gen/graph-query-engine/`, or the same path under the tool
root, the parent of the nearest `gen` directory above this module's own
file (`D199`).
