id: comp-criterion-compiler
title: Criterion Compiler
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: []
realizes: [P-ZERO-EDIT, P-AMBIGUITY-GATE]
sealed: true
source_path: pipeline/criterion-compiler/
---

# Criterion Compiler

## Purpose

Deterministically compiles `kind: compiled` Given/When/Then acceptance
criteria into executable test scaffolding, with no model involved at any
step. Sealed (`sealed: true`): the pipeline never regenerates or swaps it.

## Rationale

The trust anchor for `compiled`-kind criteria: they are the strongest
tier of evidence because nothing model-driven runs between the criterion
and the check. Its code is generated from this spec like every other
component's, but it is sealed. `generator` refuses it, and a person
installs each version only after it passes its generated tests and the
hand-maintained characterization suite in
`verification/criterion-compiler/`, which is also the only thing
`verifier-orchestrator` runs to verify it (`D206`). The trust rests on
that human-written suite and on the person installing the version, not
on who wrote the code. See `specs/architecture/pipeline-decomposition.md`.

## Scope

**In scope:** parsing the fixed Given/When/Then step grammar
(`specs/architecture/step-phrase-grammar.md`); resolving step references
against a component's `interface/` contract; emitting deterministic test
code under `verification/<component>/compiled/`; failing loudly and
specifically on any step that doesn't parse or doesn't resolve.

**Out of scope:** `generated-test` and `llm-judge` criteria (handled
elsewhere); anything requiring natural-language understanding — the step
grammar is intentionally small and fixed, not open English, precisely so this
component never needs a model call (see Non-functional constraints).

**A circularity this component's own acceptance criteria must resolve:**
none of them can be `kind: compiled`, since using the compiler to verify
the compiler proves nothing about its own bugs. All are
`kind: generated-test`, written by an agent from this spec's prose with no
access to the implementation.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/` (`CompileReport` schema). The step-grammar reference
itself lives at `specs/architecture/step-phrase-grammar.md`, not here — see
Purpose above for why.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`. All `kind: generated-test`, not `compiled` (see Scope).
Sealed verification runs the hand-maintained characterization suite
(`verification/criterion-compiler/test_*.py`), which a person writes and
no generated version ever touches.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None. The three earlier ones were resolved by `R-COMPILE-011` (one
`pytest` target), the grammar's move to `specs/architecture/`, and
`R-COMPILE-007` (where literal substitution ends).

## Change log

Each decision holds its full rationale.

- Initial draft.
- `D43`: every prose `compiled` criterion reclassified. `D44`: first
  implementation, hand-written. `D59`: `compile_criterion`. `D62`: emitted
  code imports and qualifies the target module. `D83`: dependents load
  this component lazily from `repo_root`.
- `D206`: generated from this spec and installed at `source_path` with
  `--sealed-install`; still sealed, the characterization suite still
  hand-maintained. `D214`: exact grammar forms and located errors.
- `D217`: how the interface surface is read, and substitution's emitted
  form. `D219`: emitted literals. `D226`: `AC-COMPILE-016`.
documents.constraints.md:
# Criterion Compiler — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Determinism.** The same component's `acceptance/` + `interface/` content
  MUST always compile to byte-identical output. Required for
  `notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D13's cache-key correctness — same
  obligation `spec-linter` carries, for the same reason.
- **No network access, no model calls, ever.** Structurally enforced, not
  just by convention: this is the strongest possible trust tier — the one
  component in the system where "no model in the loop" is not merely
  preferred (as `compiled`-kind criteria generally are) but load-bearing for
  the whole `compiled` mechanism's trust argument.
- **Performance.** Compiling one component's `acceptance/` against its
  `interface/` MUST complete in under 500ms on reference hardware — faster
  than `spec-linter`'s 2s budget, since this operates on a single component's
  content with no corpus-wide graph walk.
- **Idempotent on unchanged input.** Recompiling unchanged input MUST NOT
  touch already-written output files (R-COMPILE-009) — avoids spurious diffs
  that would otherwise defeat `notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D11's
  provenance-hit comparison.
- **Characterization coverage.** The hand-authored reference fixture suite
  (`acceptance/`+`interface/` content pairs with known-correct expected
  output, living in `verification/criterion-compiler/`) MUST cover every
  entry in the step grammar (`specs/architecture/step-phrase-grammar.md`)
  and every error path (R-COMPILE-001, 002, 007) — this is the actual trust
  mechanism §8 requires of a sealed component, and for this component
  specifically, it is the *only* thing standing behind the entire `compiled`
  tier's credibility. It MUST NOT be allowed to lag the grammar in practice
  the way it's easy for hand-written tests to lag a hand-written
  implementation.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs compile-criteria <component-id> [--target=pytest] [--out=<dir>] [--repo-root=<dir>]
```

`main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int` gets the tokens after
`compile-criteria` (`hotdocs-cli` strips the verb) and returns the exit
code.

- `<component-id>` — the component whose `acceptance/` directory to
  compile.
- `--target` — emitted test-framework target. Default and only supported
  value for v1: `pytest` (Python). `--target` affects only the emit phase
  of compilation, never parsing or interface-resolution (R-COMPILE-011);
  any value other than `pytest` is a usage error (exit `2`), never a silent
  fallback.
- `--out` — output directory for compiled test files. Default:
  `verification/<component>/compiled/`.
- `--repo-root` — repository root. Defaults to the current git repository
  root, same as every other CLI in this corpus.

Step templates are not redefined here — see
`specs/architecture/step-phrase-grammar.md`, the corpus-wide convention
this component implements.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Every `kind: compiled` criterion compiled successfully. |
| `1` | ≥1 criterion failed to compile (unrecognized step, unresolved reference, literal-safety violation). |
| `2` | Usage error — unknown component id, missing required argument, or an unsupported `--target` value (R-COMPILE-011). |
documents.interface/data/CompileReport.md:
# `CompileReport`

```json
{
  "outputs": [
    {
      "criterion_id": "AC-LINT-003",
      "covers": "R-LINT-003",
      "status": "compiled",
      "file": "verification/spec-linter/compiled/test_ac_lint_003.py"
    },
    {
      "criterion_id": "AC-LINT-999",
      "covers": "R-LINT-999",
      "status": "error",
      "file": "specs/components/spec-linter/acceptance/AC-LINT-999.md",
      "message": "line 7: step 'When a wizard appears' does not match any recognized template"
    }
  ],
  "gate_version": "criterion-compiler@1.0.0",
  "summary": {
    "compiled": 14,
    "errors": 0,
    "skipped_non_compiled_kind": 0
  }
}
```

`compile` returns a `CompileReport` dataclass with attributes `outputs`
(dicts as above), `gate_version` and `summary` (a dict). An entry's `file` is the emitted test for `compiled`, the acceptance
file for `error`: relative to `repo_root`, or absolute when outside it. An error's
`message` begins `line <n>: `, `<n>` the offending step's 1-based line
in its acceptance file (for `compile_criterion`, in its `gherkin`), then
quotes the offending name, or the step as written with its
keyword (`step 'When a wizard appears' does not match any recognized
template`) for an unmatched step, `unresolved
reference '<name>'` for an identifier no earlier `Given` binds, `does not
resolve` for a name the interface lacks, and `is not a literal`
for an expression, plus `field/index access` when it is one.

`gate_version` corresponds to the `gate_versions.compiler` entry in the
provenance manifest described in `notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D7
(R-COMPILE-010).
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
compile(component_id: str, repo_root: Path, target: str = "pytest", out_dir: Path | None = None) -> CompileReport

compile_criterion(criterion: ParsedCriterion, surface: InterfaceSurface | None = None) -> dict

GATE_VERSION: str  # exactly "criterion-compiler@1.0.0"
```

`GATE_VERSION` is a module-level constant, also the `gate_version` in
every `CompileReport`, read from the module when the report is built, so
replacing the module attribute changes the next report. `provenance-checker` reads it into every
component's provenance key, so it changes only when compiled output
would change.

`compile` is a pure function over corpus state at `repo_root` — no network
access, no model calls, no side effects beyond writing the files it's
asked to write. `out_dir` (the CLI's `--out`) is where compiled test files are
written, default `verification/<slug>/compiled/`.

`compile_criterion` (`R-COMPILE-012`, `D59`) is the lower-level
primitive `compile` itself uses for each criterion it finds — exposed
publicly for a caller compiling criterion content that doesn't live
under any one component's `acceptance/` directory (e.g.
`capability-scenario-verifier`'s product-capability scenarios). No
directory scanning, no file I/O: given an already-parsed
`ParsedCriterion` (a dataclass in this module, fields `criterion_id`,
`covers`, `kind`, `gherkin`, `file`, built by keyword; `gherkin` holds
the steps themselves, the ```` ```gherkin ```` fence lines already
removed, its first line being line 1) and
an optional `InterfaceSurface` (omit it for content black-box against
more than one component, which has no single surface to resolve
against), returns `{"status": "compiled", "source": <text>}` or
`{"status": "error", "message": <text>}` — never raises, and never
writes anything to disk itself. With no surface, only steps naming no
function, endpoint or type compile (`a <fixture-name> is <literal>`,
`<result-path> equals <literal>`); any other is an error naming it.

Emitted code writes a literal as Python source: a string or number as
`json.dumps` gives it (strings double-quoted), `true`/`false`/`null` as
`True`/`False`/`None`, an object as `{"k": v, ...}` and an array as
`[a, b]`, each joined by `, ` and keys by `: `.

`InterfaceSurface` is a dataclass, every field defaulted:
`functions` (name to parameter names, `{}`), `types` (name to field
names, `{}`), `module_name` (`""`). `compile` reads one from `interface/`:
each line of a plain fenced block in `library.md` that starts
`name(params)` (no `def`) declares function `name`, with the parameter
names before any `:` or `=`; each `interface/data/*.md` whose heading is
``# `Type` `` declares `Type`, its fields the keys of the file's first
`json` example when that parses as a JSON object, else none.

`InterfaceSurface.module_name` (`R-COMPILE-013`, `D62`) is the target
component's real importable module name (its underscored slug). Any
emitted reference to a function or type resolved against the surface
is qualified with it (`<module_name>.<name>`), and the emitted file
gets exactly one top-level `import <module_name>` line if — and only
if — at least one step actually needed it. A caller that *executes*
emitted output (anything dispatching a `compiled`-kind criterion, see
`R-COMPILE-013`) must scope its import search path to
`gen/<component>/` itself, not a broader ancestor.

Implements: `specs/architecture/step-phrase-grammar.md`
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-001.md:
# R-COMPILE-001

**R-COMPILE-001** — The compiler MUST recognize only the fixed, published
  step-phrase grammar (`specs/architecture/step-phrase-grammar.md`) for
  Given/When/Then steps, and MUST reject — with a specific, located compile
  error, never a best-effort guess — any step that does not match a
  recognized template.
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-002.md:
# R-COMPILE-002

**R-COMPILE-002** — The compiler MUST resolve every function, endpoint, or
  type name referenced in a step against the target component's `interface/`
  contract, and MUST fail to compile (not silently skip) any reference that
  does not resolve.
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-003.md:
# R-COMPILE-003

**R-COMPILE-003** — Compiling the same `acceptance/` + `interface/` content
  for a component MUST always produce byte-identical generated test code.
  Required for `notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D13's cache-key correctness.
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-004.md:
# R-COMPILE-004

**R-COMPILE-004** — Compiled test output for a criterion MUST carry that
  criterion's `Covers:` id as metadata in the emitted code, as the
  comment line `# Covers: <id>`, so a failing test
  traces back to its `R-id`/`P-id` without re-parsing `acceptance/`.
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-005.md:
# R-COMPILE-005

**R-COMPILE-005** — The compiler MUST compile only criteria whose `Kind` is
  `compiled`; it MUST pass through, not error on, criteria of any other
  `kind` — those are handled by other mechanisms entirely.
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-006.md:
# R-COMPILE-006

**R-COMPILE-006** — Compiled test code MUST be written under
  `verification/<component>/compiled/`, never under `specs/`
  (`notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D4).
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-007.md:
# R-COMPILE-007

**R-COMPILE-007** — A step's literal value arguments MUST be parsed as
  literal data (strings, numbers, JSON), never evaluated as code — the
  compiler MUST NOT become an arbitrary-code-execution vector via crafted
  Gherkin.

  **Exact boundary for cross-step fixture references (resolves the open
  question this requirement previously left open):** a bare identifier
  occupying an entire leaf/scalar position within the literal syntax —
  whether as a whole argument value or nested inside a larger object/array
  literal (e.g. `{"owner": user_id}`) — MUST be treated as literal
  substitution, not evaluation, when it exactly matches a fixture name
  bound by an earlier `Given` step in the same criterion. The compiler
  resolves it at **compile time** to that fixture's own already-known
  literal value, by simple lookup, so the emitted code holds the literal
  itself (`["u1", {"owner": "u1"}]`), never the fixture's name — never by runtime computation, which is
  the actual property that keeps this safe under R-COMPILE-007's intent.
  A bare identifier that does not match any fixture bound earlier in the
  same criterion MUST be a compile error (the same unresolved-reference
  discipline `R-COMPILE-001`/`002` already apply to unmatched steps and
  undeclared interface members, extended here to cover this position
  too) — never a silent fallback to treating it as a literal string.

  Anything beyond a bare identifier in a leaf position — an operator
  (`foo + 1`), field or index access (`foo.id`), concatenation, or a
  call — is expression evaluation and MUST be a specific, located compile
  error, never a best-effort evaluation. An author needing a bound value's
  field binds that value in its own `Given` step; allowing field access
  would mean extending the step-phrase grammar.
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-008.md:
# R-COMPILE-008

**R-COMPILE-008** — The compiler MUST NOT invoke any model or agent at any
  stage of compilation; its entire behavior is grammar parsing, interface
  binding, and deterministic code emission.
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-009.md:
# R-COMPILE-009

**R-COMPILE-009** — Recompiling unchanged `acceptance/` + `interface/`
  content for a component MUST NOT change already-written output files
  (avoids spurious diffs, supports `notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D11's
  provenance-hit comparison).
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-010.md:
# R-COMPILE-010

**R-COMPILE-010** — The compiler MUST report its own `gate_version`
  (`notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D7),
  and that version MUST change whenever the step grammar or interface-binding
  rules change.
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-011.md:
# R-COMPILE-011

**R-COMPILE-011** — The compiler's work MUST be structured as two distinct
  phases: **parse+bind** (matching steps against the step-phrase grammar
  and resolving references against the target component's `interface/`
  contract — entirely target-independent, the same for every `--target`
  value) and **emit** (turning the bound, target-independent result into
  literal source text for one specific test framework/language). No rule
  in this spec, `R-COMPILE-001` through `010` included, MUST depend on
  which `--target` is selected — those rules govern parse+bind only.

  For v1, exactly one emitter MUST be implemented: `pytest` (Python), the
  only accepted `--target` value. The compiler MUST reject any other
  `--target` value with a specific usage error (exit code `2`, naming the
  unsupported value) — never a silent fallback to `pytest` and never a
  best-effort guess at an unimplemented target, the same no-silent-guessing
  discipline `R-COMPILE-001` already applies to unrecognized steps.
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-012.md:
# R-COMPILE-012

**R-COMPILE-012** — The compiler MUST expose a public primitive that
  compiles one already-parsed `compiled`-kind criterion directly — no
  directory scanning, no file I/O, no assumption that the criterion
  lives under any one component's `acceptance/` — for callers compiling
  content that doesn't fit `compile`'s own "one component's
  `acceptance/` directory" scope. `compile` (`R-COMPILE-001`–`011`)
  MUST itself be implemented in terms of this primitive for each
  criterion it finds, never a second, duplicated compilation path.

  This primitive's interface surface (`surface`) MUST be optional: a
  criterion black-box against more than one component — a
  product-capability scenario, never scoped to one component's own
  `interface/` contract (`capability-scenario-verifier`'s
  `R-SCENARIO-001`, the real first caller this closes a gap for) — has
  no single surface to resolve against at all. A literal-only step
  (e.g. `Given a foo is "x"`) never needed a surface regardless; a step
  that *does* reference a function/type with no surface supplied MUST
  still be a located compile error (`R-COMPILE-002`'s own discipline,
  unchanged), never silently skipped for lack of one.

  Found missing only once a real second consumer
  (`capability-scenario-verifier`) actually needed to compile criterion
  content outside any component's `acceptance/` directory and
  `compile`'s own public surface had no way to serve that need without
  inventing a second, duplicate compilation path — exactly the
  "no new dispatch machinery" rule `R-SCENARIO-001` itself states
  (`D59`).
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-013.md:
# R-COMPILE-013

**R-COMPILE-013** — Emitted test code that references the target
  component's own functions or types (any `When ... is invoked` or
  `Given a <Type> with ...` step bound against a resolved
  `InterfaceSurface`) MUST import the target module by its
  `InterfaceSurface.module_name` and qualify every such reference with
  it (`<module_name>.<name>`) — never a bare, unqualified name relying
  on a caller to have pre-populated globals (`D62`).

  A caller that *executes* the emitted file (any `compiled`-kind
  dispatch, e.g. `verifier-orchestrator`'s `R-VERIFY-001`) MUST run it
  with its import search path (`PYTHONPATH` for `pytest`) scoped to the
  specific directory containing `gen/<component>/<module_name>.py` —
  `gen/<component>/` itself, not a broader ancestor such as `gen/`.
  Scoping any broader resolves `import <module_name>` as an empty
  implicit namespace package rather than the real module, since
  `gen/<component>/` has no `__init__.py` (R-COMPILE-006 writes
  compiled *test* output under `verification/`, but the target code
  under test lives under `gen/<component>/` per the generator's own
  output layout, R-GEN-015).
documents.requirements/R-COMPILE-014.md:
# R-COMPILE-014

**R-COMPILE-014** — Any component depending on this one directly (not
  via an injected callable — `verifier-orchestrator`'s `R-VERIFY-001`,
  `capability-scenario-verifier`'s `R-SCENARIO-001`) MUST import
  `criterion_compiler` lazily, at call time, resolved relative to its
  own `repo_root` parameter — never a static top-level
  `import criterion_compiler` statement, which only works by accident
  of load order and breaks across callers given different `repo_root`
  values (`D83`).

  The caller MUST try a plain `import criterion_compiler` first (the
  seam for a test to pre-register a fake in `sys.modules`), then on
  failure add `repo_root / "pipeline" / "criterion-compiler"` and
  `repo_root / "gen" / "criterion-compiler"`, in that order, to
  `sys.path` before retrying — `pipeline/` first since this component
  is `sealed: true` and lives there; `gen/` as a forward-compatible
  fallback.

# Decision Drift Detector

## Purpose

For every live spec file's `D<N>` citation, flags one whose cited
decision has since been superseded by a decision ratified after the
citing file's own last-modified commit — a candidate for staleness
review, never a verdict. Also answers the forward-looking question:
before altering or superseding a decision, what would be affected.

## Scope

**In scope:** resolving every `D<N>` citation in every live (non-
decision) spec file, the same citation shape `R-CITE-001` already
validates for existence; for each, querying `graph-query-engine`'s
`edges` for whether it has been superseded; for a superseded
citation, comparing the citing file's own last commit touching it
against the superseding decision's `last_ratified_commit`
(`decision_lineage`) via `git merge-base --is-ancestor`; reporting
every case where the file's commit predates the superseding
decision's ratification. Also: given any decision id, not
necessarily yet ratified, walking `edges` backward to find every
decision and live file that would be affected by altering it
(`R-DRIFT-003`).

**Out of scope:** judging whether a flagged file is actually wrong —
this surfaces candidates, never a correctness verdict, the same
posture `spec-completeness-assistant` takes for its own judgment
calls. Never read by `provenance-tracker`'s own checks or any gate's
block decision — purely diagnostic, run on demand or periodically, not
part of the verification-gate workflow (`specs/architecture/
pipeline-decomposition.md`'s "Advisory tooling" table).

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

All three criteria are `kind: generated-test` (`D133`) — each needs a
synthetic git repo built inside the test itself (real commits, real
ancestry), not a mock, since the actual behavior being checked is git
ancestry; `criterion-compiler`'s fixed step grammar has no step form
for constructing arbitrary commits, only literal-value fixtures and a
single function call, so this setup is unreachable through `kind:
compiled` despite the deterministic, judgment-free logic it exercises.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- Initial draft (`D75`).
- `D74`/`D75`: `R-DRIFT-001` rewired onto `edges` (decisions became
  graph-native, `decision_lineage` narrowed); `R-DRIFT-003` added
  pre-ratification impact analysis.
- `D133`: real cold-generation, first attempt. All three criteria
  were mis-declared `kind: compiled`; `criterion-compiler`'s fixed
  step grammar cannot express building a synthetic git repo with real
  commits, which these criteria's own tests genuinely need. Changed
  to `kind: generated-test`.
- `D134`: second attempt. Citation extraction MUST use the literal
  `\bD\d+\b` pattern, not a backtick-requiring one (`R-DRIFT-001`
  amended); `graph-query-engine` MUST resolve relative to `repo_root`,
  never this component's own `__file__` location — the `R-TRACK-011`/
  `R-VERIFY-013` bug class recurring a third time (`R-DRIFT-004`).
- `D135`: third attempt. A real DuckDB extension-registry conflict
  (bare `INSTALL yaml` vs. the required `FROM community`) traced to a
  `graph-query-engine` documentation gap, fixed there, not here.
- `D136`: fourth attempt, all four behaviorally passed. `main()`'s
  CLI entry point (`interface/cli.md`) had no requirement or
  acceptance criterion at all, same shape as `provenance-writer`'s
  own `D130` — caught by mutation score (`R-DRIFT-005`,
  `AC-DRIFT-005`).
- `D137`: mutation score oscillated `0.58`–`1.0` across seeds; nine
  consistently surviving mutants traced to three under-specified
  scenarios (multi-superseder tie-break, no-`--repo-root` CLI
  default, invalid `--format`) added directly to `AC-DRIFT-001`/
  `AC-DRIFT-005`, no new requirement needed. Landed 5/5,
  `mutation_score=0.84`. Full account in `BOOTSTRAP.md`.
documents.constraints.md:
# Decision Drift Detector — Non-Functional Constraints

- **No network access, no model calls.** Pure git/filesystem reads
  against the local repository.
- **Never gates anything.** Purely diagnostic — see
  `specs/architecture/pipeline-decomposition.md`'s "Advisory tooling"
  table. No mechanism anywhere calls this component as a merge
  precondition.
- **Ancestry, never timestamps.** `R-DRIFT-002`'s ordering check is
  always `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, never a commit-date
  comparison — a non-linear history has no trustworthy linear order
  by date alone.
- **A missing or unreadable git history is a usage error, not a
  silent empty report.** If `repo_root` is not a git repository, or a
  cited file has no commit history at all (uncommitted), this MUST
  fail loudly (exit `2`), never report zero drift as if the check
  actually ran.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs decision-drift [--format=json|text] [--repo-root=<dir>]
hotdocs decision-impact <decision-id> [--format=json|text] [--repo-root=<dir>]
```

- `--format` — `text` (human-readable, default) or `json` (the
  `DriftReport`/`DecisionImpactReport` schema, matching whichever
  subcommand ran).
- `--repo-root` — repository root. Defaults to the current git
  repository root.
- `<decision-id>` (`decision-impact` only) — the `D<N>` being
  considered for alteration or supersession. Need not resolve to a
  real file yet.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Ran successfully, report produced (an empty report is a clean result, not an error). |
| `2` | Usage error (not a git repository, unreadable path, missing `<decision-id>` for `decision-impact`). |

Always exits `0` on a successful run regardless of whether anything
was found — both are diagnostic tools, not gates; nothing about a
non-empty report is a failure to signal via exit code.
documents.interface/data/DecisionImpactReport.md:
# `DecisionImpactReport`

```json
{
  "decision_id": "D17",
  "dependent_decisions": ["D31"],
  "citing_files": [
    "specs/components/provenance-tracker/component.md",
    "specs/components/provenance-tracker/requirements/R-TRACK-009.md"
  ]
}
```

`dependent_decisions` is the transitive closure of every decision
whose `supersedes` or `builds_on` edge points at `decision_id`
(`R-DRIFT-003`) — empty if nothing depends on it yet.
`citing_files` is every live spec file citing `decision_id`, not
filtered by staleness — this report answers "what would need review,"
`DriftReport` answers "what already looks stale."
documents.interface/data/DriftReport.md:
# `DriftReport`

```json
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "file": "specs/components/foo/requirements/R-FOO-001.md",
      "cited_decision": "D17",
      "superseded_by": "D31",
      "file_commit": "2a68165",
      "superseder_ratified_commit": "86ab93f"
    }
  ]
}
```

One entry per `(file, cited_decision)` pair where `R-DRIFT-002`'s
ancestry check found the file's own last-touching commit predates the
superseding decision's ratification. An empty `entries` list is a
clean result — every live citation is either unsuperseded or already
reflects whatever superseded it.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
find_decision_drift(repo_root: Path) -> DriftReport
find_decision_impact(repo_root: Path, decision_id: str) -> DecisionImpactReport
```

Both pure functions over the filesystem state and git history at
`repo_root` — reads, never writes; no model calls. Each call opens one
DuckDB connection and calls `graph-query-engine`'s `load_views` on it
exactly once.
`find_decision_drift` walks the live corpus once, resolving each
`D<N>` citation's commit ancestry against `graph-query-engine`'s
`edges` (`supersedes` chain) and `decision_lineage`
(`last_ratified_commit`). `find_decision_impact` answers a different,
forward-looking question — usable on a decision before it is ever
ratified — by walking `edges` backward from `decision_id` and
collecting every live citation of it, unfiltered by staleness.
documents.requirements/R-DRIFT-001.md:
# R-DRIFT-001

**R-DRIFT-001** — For every live spec file (never one under
  `specs/decisions/` itself — mirroring `R-CITE-001`'s existing
  exemption), MUST extract every `D<N>` citation and, for each, walk
  `graph-query-engine`'s `edges` `supersedes` edges forward (`D74` —
  the relationship lives there, never `decision_lineage`, which
  carries only `last_ratified_commit`) to the latest decision (by
  ratification order, not citation order) that transitively
  supersedes it, if any. A citation with no superseder in its chain
  is never a candidate.

  **Edge direction, literally** (`interface/data/Edges.md`): for a
  `supersedes` edge, `source_id` is the newer decision (the one whose
  own frontmatter carries the scalar line `supersedes: D17`, a single
  id, never a list), `target_id` is the
  older, cited one — e.g. `('D31', 'D17', 'supersedes')` when `D31`
  supersedes `D17`, never the reverse.

  **Citation extraction MUST use the literal pattern `\bD\d+\b`**
  (`D134`) — the exact regex `spec-linter`'s own `R-CITE-001` check
  uses, matching a bare `D<N>` as a word regardless of surrounding
  backticks or punctuation. Found via a real cold-generation attempt:
  a candidate instead required citations wrapped in backticks
  (`` `(D\d+)` ``), missing every bare, backtick-free `D<N>` mention —
  "the same citation shape `R-CITE-001` already validates" was stated
  abstractly and implemented too narrowly on the first attempt.
documents.requirements/R-DRIFT-002.md:
# R-DRIFT-002

**R-DRIFT-002** — For a citation with a superseder found (`R-DRIFT-001`),
  MUST resolve the citing file's own last commit touching it
  (`git log -1 --format=%H -- <path>`) and compare it against the
  superseder's `last_ratified_commit` via
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor <file_commit> <superseder_commit>`.
  A zero exit code (the file's commit IS an ancestor of — predates —
  the superseding ratification) MUST be reported as a drift candidate;
  a non-zero exit code (the file was already touched at or after the
  superseding decision, or the two commits are unrelated) MUST NOT be.
  Never a timestamp comparison — commit ancestry is the only
  trustworthy "happened-before" relationship in a non-linear history.
documents.requirements/R-DRIFT-003.md:
# R-DRIFT-003

**R-DRIFT-003** — `find_decision_impact(repo_root, decision_id)` MUST
  report everything that would be affected by altering or superseding
  `decision_id`, usable before it is ever ratified: (1) every decision
  whose `edges` `supersedes` or `builds_on` edge points at
  `decision_id`, walked transitively (unlike `R-DRIFT-001`'s forward
  walk toward the latest superseder, this walks *backward*, toward
  everything that depends on the one being altered); (2) every live
  spec file citing `decision_id` — unlike `R-DRIFT-001`/`002`, every
  citation, not only ones whose commit predates something, since the
  question here is "what would need review," not "what is already
  stale." `decision_id` need not resolve to a real file yet — the
  query is defined over whatever `edges`/citations already point at
  it today, which is well-defined even for an id that does not exist
  as a ratified record.
documents.requirements/R-DRIFT-004.md:
# R-DRIFT-004

**R-DRIFT-004** — `graph-query-engine` (and any other dependency this
  component loads dynamically) MUST be resolved relative to the
  `repo_root` actually passed to `find_decision_drift`/
  `find_decision_impact`, never relative to this component's own
  `__file__` location while `repo_root` has it — the identical bug class `R-TRACK-011`/
  `R-VERIFY-013` already closed for `provenance-tracker` and
  `verifier-orchestrator`: a verification harness runs this candidate
  from one location while exercising it against a *different*,
  test-controlled `repo_root`, so a `__file__`-relative resolution
  silently finds the real sibling dependency instead of the test's own
  fake, defeating the fake entirely without ever raising.

  **Literal worked snippet, not prose alone** (`R-AUTHOR-010`): resolve
  `Path(repo_root) / "gen" / "graph-query-engine"` and load
  `graph_query_engine.py` (flat) or `graph_query_engine/__init__.py`
  (package) from it; only when that directory does not exist, use the
  same path under the tool root, the parent of the nearest directory
  named `gen` above this module's own `__file__` (`D199`). Cache the
  loaded module keyed by `(str(repo_root), module_name)`, never by bare
  module name alone.

  Found via a real cold-generation attempt (`D134`): a candidate
  resolved `graph_query_engine` from its own `__file__`'s location,
  which — inside this driver's own sandboxed verification — happens to
  coincidentally also contain a real copy of `graph-query-engine`,
  silently loading that instead of the test's fake and never calling
  it at all, masked as a behavioral assertion failure rather than an
  obvious crash.
documents.requirements/R-DRIFT-005.md:
# R-DRIFT-005

**R-DRIFT-005** — `main(argv)` MUST implement `interface/cli.md`
  exactly: `hotdocs decision-drift [--format=json|text]
  [--repo-root=<dir>]` and `hotdocs decision-impact <decision-id>
  [--format=json|text] [--repo-root=<dir>]`. Exit `0` once a report is
  produced, regardless of whether it is empty — neither subcommand is
  a gate. Exit `2` on any usage error: not a git repository, an
  unreadable `--repo-root`, or a missing `<decision-id>` for
  `decision-impact`. `--format=json` MUST print the report as JSON
  matching its own schema; the default/`--format=text` MUST print a
  human-readable rendering.

  Found via mutation testing, not a behavioral test failure (same
  shape as `R-PROV-015`/`D130` for `provenance-writer`): every
  acceptance criterion so far exercises `find_decision_drift`/
  `find_decision_impact` directly as a library call, none through
  `main()` — `interface/cli.md` documents the CLI but no requirement
  or acceptance criterion ever covered it.

# Docs Site Renderer

## Purpose

Renders `verification/corpus-graph.json` into the interactive graph/docs
explorer — a pure presentation layer over data the pipeline already
computed, nothing more.

## Rationale

The graph/docs explorer this renders was established as a product decision early on.

## Scope

**In scope:** rendering the DAG, the per-node detail view, and the
corpus-health dashboard, all directly from `corpus-graph.json`.

**Out of scope:** computing anything `corpus-graph.json` doesn't already
contain; hosting/deployment (a CI/infra concern, not this component's
behavior).

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`. Input only: `verification/corpus-graph.json` (`corpus-graph-builder`'s
output). This component produces no new data artifact of its own, only the
rendered site.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

All six criteria are `kind: generated-test` (`D43`) — rendering
already-computed data is pure, deterministic templating that needs no
model or judgment, but none are actually written in the step-phrase
grammar, so `kind: compiled` would not describe how they're really
verified.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

# Docs Site Renderer — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Purity.** A function of `corpus-graph.json` alone — no network access,
  no model calls, no other file reads.
- **Not committed.** Its output is a CI build artifact, deployed to a docs
  host — never checked into the repository (`notes/initial-ideas.md`'s
  own D9).
- **Cheap enough to run on every merge.** A render over already-computed
  data; MUST NOT become a merge-latency bottleneck the way a model-calling
  gate would.

# CLI

```
hotdocs docs-site build [--repo-root=<dir>] [--out=<dir>]
```

- `--out` — output directory for the rendered static site. Default:
  `dist/docs-site/` (a build artifact location, not `gen/` — this
  component's output is never committed, per `notes/initial-ideas.md`'s

**Exit codes:**

| --- | --- |

documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

A package, `docs_site_renderer/` (`__init__.py` plus `cli.py`, never a
flat module): `hotdocs-cli` runs `docs_site_renderer.cli`'s
`main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int`, which receives the tokens
after `build`, `hotdocs-cli`'s verb table stripping both verb words
(`interface/cli.md`).

```
render_docs_site(graph: CorpusGraph, out_dir: Path) -> None
```

A component's detail view (`R-DOCS-002`) is drawn from its node in
`corpus-graph-builder`'s `CorpusGraph` alone (`R-DOCS-004`): rendered
content from `documents`; each `R-id` and its live status from
`verification.requirement_results`; criteria by `kind` with their
results from `verification.criteria`; provenance from `provenance`;
size from `size_status`; exemptions from `sealed` and
`pinned_overrides`; owners from `owners`. A field that is `null` or
empty shows as absent, never as an error. Every value written into a
page is HTML-escaped.

The DAG view (`R-DOCS-001`) holds one element per node, linking to its
detail page, and one per edge, with no coordinates: a script embedded in
the page lays them out and filters them in the browser, so the Python
code computes no layout.

documents.component.md:
---
id: comp-generator
title: Generator
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-spec-bundle-assembler, comp-cache-manager, comp-llm-endpoint]
depends_on_guarantees: [G-CACHE-001]
realizes: [P-ZERO-EDIT]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
---

# Generator

## Purpose

Calls a pinned model to produce `gen/<component>/` from a `SpecBundle` —
cold, with no prior code (unless the bundle carries `hint_code`),
exactly one candidate per invocation.

## Rationale

`hint_code` is a feature-branch-only exception. Declares
`depends_on_guarantees: [G-CACHE-001]` (`D2`): R-GEN-005/006 trusts a
`get` hit as authoritative with no locking, safe only because
concurrent writers are last-write-wins-safe — not on `cache-manager`'s
other properties, so a change there won't pull in an unrelated blast
radius.

## Scope

**In scope:** constructing the model call from a `SpecBundle`, a model
identifier, and optional `retry_feedback` (`R-GEN-012`); checking the
cache first; in `cold` mode only, writing the result to
`gen/<component>/` and the cache (`R-GEN-016` — `hint` mode writes
neither); recording provenance.

**Out of scope (why `depends_on` excludes `verifier-orchestrator`):**
any retry of its own — exactly one candidate per call, single-shot.
`D3` retired the best-of-k loop; a human re-running
`hotdocs generate` is the only path back for a failed one.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

All `generated-test`, with an injected mock model.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

## Change log

- `D35`–`D209`: see the decisions; `D268` states the reply format.
documents.constraints.md:
# Generator — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Not deterministic, and that's expected — but bounded.** Unlike every
  other component specced so far, a fresh model call is not required to be
  reproducible. What MUST be deterministic: a **cache hit** (R-GEN-005)
  always returns byte-identical output for the same key — that's the
  property the cache-key correctness design actually depends on, not "the
  model always says the same thing."
- **`retry_feedback`'s content boundary is load-bearing, not cosmetic.**
  `R-GEN-012` (`D3`) restricts `retry_feedback` to a bare
  `R-id` list — this MUST hold at every layer that touches it here, not
  just at the CLI/library boundary: the prompt-construction logic MUST
  NOT enrich it with Gherkin text, `rationale`, or expected/actual values
  pulled from anywhere else this component can reach (e.g. by
  re-deriving them from `acceptance/` files that happen to be on disk).
- **Defense-in-depth on write paths.** R-GEN-009's sealed/pinned-override
  check MUST be enforced here even though `component-gate-runner`'s own
  routing requirement (`R-GATE-007`) means it should never call this
  component for a sealed component's regeneration in the first place — a
  second, independent layer, not a redundant one to remove now that the
  primary layer is a real requirement rather than an assumption.
- **No wasted model calls on a known-refused target.** R-GEN-009's
  precondition check MUST run, and MUST short-circuit, before any model
  call — paying for a call whose result can never be written is pure
  waste.
- **No silent partial output.** A model-call error MUST leave
  `gen/<component>/` untouched — never a half-written tree.
- **Credential handling.** Since `D18`, this component no longer holds
  `VAR-ANTHROPIC-API-KEY` at all — `llm-endpoint` does
  (`R-ENDPOINT-005`) — so it's structurally absent from
  `GenerationResult`, logs, and the provenance manifest, not merely
  filtered out of them. Only `model` (the identifier) is ever recorded.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

None (`D91`). This component had its own standalone CLI once
(`hotdocs generate <component-id> --model=...`, just the raw
candidate-producing step); that verb now belongs to
`component-gate-runner`'s full gauntlet (`hotdocs generate`, same
name, different and broader scope) — nobody has a reason to call just
this component's own narrower step directly, so this component no
longer exposes one. `generate()` (`interface/library.md`) is called
only internally now, by `component-gate-runner`.
documents.interface/data/GenerationResult.md:
# `GenerationResult`

```json
{
  "component_id": "comp-foo",
  "spec_bundle_hash": "sha256:...",
  "model": "claude-sonnet-5",
  "prompt_version": "v1",
  "cache_hit": false,
  "files": { "spec_linter.py": "<file content>" },
  "model_call_error": null,
  "refused": null,
  "retry_feedback": ["R-FOO-003"]
}
```

`generate` returns a `GenerationResult` dataclass with these fields, in
this order. `spec_bundle_hash` (`R-GEN-017`, `D67`) echoes `bundle.spec_bundle_hash`.

No `seed`/`sample_index` fields (`D3` retired best-of-k, no "which
sample won" left to record). `retry_feedback` (`D3`) is a plain echo
of whatever a caller supplied (`null` if nothing was) — an auditor
needs to know whether an attempt was informed or blind.

Exactly one of `files` (non-empty), `model_call_error`, or `refused` is
populated on any given result — never more than one, and `cache_hit` is
`false` whenever either `model_call_error` or `refused` is set (a failed or
refused call never produces partial or cached output). `model_call_error`
is a real API failure (R-GEN-008) — a model call was attempted. `refused`
(R-GEN-009) is the opposite: it means **no model call was attempted at
all** — the target was a sealed component's `source_path` or a pinned
`.overrides.json` file, caught by the precondition check before any cost
was incurred. The two MUST NOT be conflated: one implies "the model tried
and failed," the other implies "generation never tried, by design."
`refused`'s value is a short machine-readable reason string, e.g.
`"sealed-component"` or `"pinned-override"`.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
generate(
    bundle: SpecBundle, model: str, retry_feedback: list[str] | None = None,
    *, repo_root: Path = None, llm_backend=None,
) -> GenerationResult
```

Not a pure function — this is the one component in the corpus whose job
requires an external call. Side effects: in `cold` mode, writes
`gen/<component>/` and writes through `cache-manager`; in `hint` mode,
reads through `cache-manager` but writes to neither destination
(`R-GEN-016`).

`repo_root` locates `component.md`'s `sealed`/`source_path` and
`gen/<component>/.overrides.json` for `R-GEN-009`, and is where
`gen/<component>/` is written. `llm_backend` goes straight to
`llm-endpoint`'s `backend` parameter: the criteria's injected mock model.

The model's reply, a mock's included, wraps each file as a line
`-----BEGIN FILE <nonce>: <path>-----`, the file's content, then a line
`-----END FILE <nonce>-----`: `<path>` relative to `gen/<component>/`,
`<nonce>` the fresh `uuid.uuid4().hex` the prompt states for this call.
Text outside the blocks is ignored.

```
GATE_VERSION = "generator@2.0.0"
PROMPT_VERSION = "v10"
```

The cache key (`R-GEN-005`) is `cache-manager`'s `CacheKey` with
`spec_bundle_hash` the bundle's, `gate_version` `GATE_VERSION`,
`model_pin` the `model` argument, and `gate_inputs_hash` `"sha256:"`
plus the SHA-256 hex digest of
`json.dumps(sorted(retry_feedback or []), sort_keys=True)` encoded as
UTF-8. Every result's `prompt_version` is `PROMPT_VERSION`.
documents.requirements/R-GEN-001.md:
# R-GEN-001

**R-GEN-001** — Given a `SpecBundle` in `cold` mode, the model call MUST
  be constructed from exactly the bundle's `spec` / `interface` /
  `constraints` / `dependency_interfaces` / `vars` / `glossary` fields —
  never `hint_code` (which is `null` in cold mode anyway, per
  `spec-bundle-assembler` R-ASSEMBLE-008) and never the component's current
  `gen/<component>/` content from any other source.

  `retry_feedback` (`R-GEN-012`) is **not** an exception to this rule
  and does not weaken it — it carries no code, prior or otherwise, only
  a bare `R-id` list a caller supplies. A `cold` call that includes
  `retry_feedback` is still, by this requirement's own test, constructed
  from nothing but the current spec bundle (plus a caller-supplied,
  content-free fact) — never from external or stale state the way
  `hint_code` is.
documents.requirements/R-GEN-002.md:
# R-GEN-002

**R-GEN-002** — Given a `SpecBundle` in `hint` mode, the model call MUST
  additionally include `hint_code` as context, clearly distinguished from
  the cold bundle fields in the prompt — never silently merged in a way
  that makes a later audit unable to tell which parts of the prompt were
  "the spec" versus "the existing code."
documents.requirements/R-GEN-003.md:
# R-GEN-003

**R-GEN-003** — The prompt template MUST be frozen and versioned; the
  exact template text and its version MUST be recorded in the output
  (`prompt_version`, feeding `notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D7's
  provenance manifest).
documents.requirements/R-GEN-004.md:
# R-GEN-004

**R-GEN-004** — The model identifier MUST be an explicit parameter, never
  hardcoded to "the canonical pin," and MUST be passed through to
  `llm-endpoint` (`D18`) unchanged. Credential resolution for whichever
  vendor that identifier names is `llm-endpoint`'s own job
  (`R-ENDPOINT-002`) — this component no longer resolves a vendor or
  holds a credential itself.
documents.requirements/R-GEN-005.md:
# R-GEN-005

**R-GEN-005** — Before calling any model, generation MUST check
  `cache-manager` using the key `(spec_bundle_hash, gate_inputs_hash,
  gate_version, model_pin)`; on a cache hit, the cached result MUST be
  returned and no model call MUST occur.

  `gate_inputs_hash` MUST incorporate `retry_feedback` (`R-GEN-012`,
  `D3`) when present — a blind call and a call carrying
  `retry_feedback` are materially different inputs and MUST NOT be able
  to collide in the cache, even for the same `spec_bundle_hash`/
  `model_pin`. `retry_feedback` being absent and `retry_feedback` being
  present both still hash deterministically, so this only widens what
  counts as "the same inputs," it doesn't weaken determinism. (`D3`
  settled this key's final scope, including `retry_feedback`.)
documents.requirements/R-GEN-006.md:
# R-GEN-006

**R-GEN-006** — On a cache miss, after a successful model call, the result
  MUST be written to `cache-manager` under the same key before being
  returned.
documents.requirements/R-GEN-008.md:
# R-GEN-008

**R-GEN-008** — A model-call error, as `llm-endpoint` reports it
  (`R-ENDPOINT-004`, `D18` — network, auth, rate-limit, or timeout) MUST be
  distinct from generated code failing verification. Both block the merge
  (`R-GATE-004`), but a human choosing a re-run or a spec fix (`D3`) needs
  to know whether a candidate was produced.

  A response parsing to no files produced none:
  `model_call_error` is `{"category": "empty_response", "message": ...}`
  and nothing is written or cached.
documents.requirements/R-GEN-009.md:
# R-GEN-009

**R-GEN-009** — Writing output MUST be confined to `gen/<component>/` for
  the target component only. It MUST NOT write to any `sealed` component's
  `source_path`, and MUST NOT overwrite a file listed in that component's
  `gen/<component>/.overrides.json` (the two declared cold-regen exemptions,
  §8) — generation must never silently clobber a declared hands-off path.

  This MUST be a **precondition check, resolved before any model call is
  attempted** — refusing only at write-time, after already paying for a
  model call whose output can never be used, wastes real cost for no
  benefit. The refusal MUST be recorded as its own distinct outcome
  (`refused`, see `interface/data/GenerationResult.md`) — neither a
  `model_call_error` (R-GEN-008, a real API failure) nor "produced code
  that fails verification"; conflating a precondition refusal with either
  of those would misclassify why nothing was generated.

  This is one of two independent enforcement layers (§8):
  `component-gate-runner` is expected not to call this component for a
  sealed component's regeneration at all (its own routing requirement,
  `R-GATE-007`), and this check is the second, independent layer — in
  case it's ever invoked anyway, by a bug or a future caller that
  doesn't yet know the routing rule.
documents.requirements/R-GEN-011.md:
# R-GEN-011

**R-GEN-011** — This component MUST NOT implement its own retry-with-backoff
  logic around an `llm-endpoint` call — `llm-endpoint`'s own bounded-call
  guarantee (`R-ENDPOINT-004`, `D18`) is the right source of truth for "how
  long is reasonable," not a number this component invents, and not a
  loop this component adds on top. A single call either succeeds, or
  comes back as `model_call_error` (R-GEN-008) exactly once — there is no
  internal attempt loop to exhaust first.

  **Resolves the retry/timeout open question by making the retry mechanism
  someone else's job, deliberately:** a transient failure's recovery path
  is re-running the merge (R-MERGE-017), not a hidden retry loop inside a
  single `generate()` call. This is not a missing feature — `generator`
  never caches a failed call (R-GEN-006 only writes on success), so a
  re-run after any failure, transient or not, naturally only re-attempts
  the components that actually failed; everything that already succeeded
  is a cache hit, at no cost. Building retry-with-backoff into this
  component would duplicate a recovery path that already exists one layer
  up, for free, and would hide failures from the batch-level visibility
  R-MERGE-017 depends on.

  This was never the same thing as `merge-orchestrator`'s best-of-k
  retry loop, which used to retry *generation itself* on a verification
  failure — `D3` retired that loop entirely, but this requirement was
  always about a different layer (infrastructure-level call failures,
  before any code was ever produced to verify) and is unaffected by that
  retirement.
documents.requirements/R-GEN-012.md:
# R-GEN-012

**R-GEN-012** — The model call MAY optionally receive `retry_feedback` —
  a bare list of `R-id`s a **caller** supplies as having failed on some
  prior attempt. When present, it MUST be included as its own clearly
  distinguished context section, never merged with or indistinguishable
  from the `SpecBundle`'s own fields — the same clear-separation
  discipline `R-GEN-002` already established for `hint_code`.

  `retry_feedback` MUST contain **only** `R-id`s — never Gherkin text,
  `rationale`, expected/actual values, or any other acceptance-criterion
  content. This boundary is load-bearing, not a style preference: it is
  the entire reason this mechanism doesn't reopen
  `spec-bundle-assembler`'s R-ASSEMBLE-001 exclusion of `acceptance/`
  from what a generation model ever sees. A list of failed `R-id`s
  discloses nothing beyond "a prior attempt didn't satisfy text you
  already have" — the requirements themselves are already in the bundle
  via `requirements/`.

  **Restores the feedback mechanism that was removed along with
  automatic retry (`D3`).** `D3`'s actual point — no *automatic* loop deciding to
  retry on this component's behalf within one merge — never required
  removing the feedback mechanism itself; that was overreach. This
  component MUST NOT be the one deciding *whether* to use
  `retry_feedback` on a given call, and MUST NOT derive it from
  anything on disk itself — that decision, and the R-id list itself,
  come from whoever is invoking this generation call — a developer
  running `hotdocs generate` with `--retry-feedback` (`D86`/`D91`/`D93`) —
  never computed automatically in between.
documents.requirements/R-GEN-013.md:
# R-GEN-013

**R-GEN-013** — When the bundle's `dependency_usage` field
  (`R-ASSEMBLE-011`, `D37`) is non-empty for a dependency, the model
  call MUST include it as its own clearly distinguished section —
  never merged with `dependency_interfaces`, never treated as
  equivalent to `acceptance/` content (it names real, importable
  symbols, not test assertions). Empty for a dependency with no real
  code yet; this component MUST NOT treat that absence as an error or
  a reason to refuse.
documents.requirements/R-GEN-014.md:
# R-GEN-014

**R-GEN-014** — A static `sys.path`-relative-to-`__file__` import of
  this component's own dependencies (`cache-manager`, `llm-endpoint`)
  is a valid implementation choice (it's always correct in production,
  since this component's own installed location and the `repo_root`
  it's given always coincide there) **but silently reuses the first
  call's module if `generate` is ever invoked more than once in the
  same process against two *different* `repo_root` values** — exactly
  the shape of a pre-swap-in verification harness staging an untested
  candidate elsewhere while exercising it against real dependencies.
  An implementation that instead resolves dependencies dynamically,
  per call, from the `repo_root` actually passed in (avoiding that
  staleness) MUST register the loaded module in `sys.modules` under
  its load-time name *before* its code runs (`exec_module`) — never
  after, never omitted. Skipping this step is not harmless laziness:
  any dependency module that defines a `dataclass` (both
  `cache-manager` and this component's own `GenerationResult` do) can
  crash during its own class-body evaluation, because `dataclasses`'
  internals look up `sys.modules[cls.__module__]` to resolve the
  class's own annotations — found only once a real self-regeneration
  candidate chose exactly this per-call dynamic-loading technique,
  omitted the registration step, and crashed for real loading
  `cache-manager` (`D41`).
documents.requirements/R-GEN-015.md:
# R-GEN-015

**R-GEN-015** — The model call MUST instruct the candidate to lay out
  its own output as either a flat `<slug_with_underscores>.py` module
  or a `<slug_with_underscores>/` package (with `__init__.py`) directly
  under `gen/<component>/` — never a deeper layout (e.g. a `src/`
  subdirectory) and never a separately-installed distribution, since
  `spec-bundle-assembler`'s `dependency_usage` (`R-ASSEMBLE-011`) only
  looks in those two shapes (`D46`). This is fixed scaffolding the
  prompt always includes, like the nonce-delimiter format (`D38`), not
  bundle content. It names the real module, e.g. `widget_maker.py` or
  `widget_maker/` for `comp-widget-maker`.

  The reply format is in `interface/library.md`.

  Before writing, generator MUST also strip one redundant leading
  `gen/<component>/` or `<component>/` from any returned file path —
  the model restating the directory it is already writing into — so
  `<component>/<slug_with_underscores>.py` is written as
  `<slug_with_underscores>.py`. No other path is rewritten (`D165`).
documents.requirements/R-GEN-016.md:
# R-GEN-016

**R-GEN-016** — In `hint` mode (`bundle.hint_code` is not `null`),
  `generate()` MUST NOT write to `gen/<component>/` or to
  `cache-manager` — it returns the candidate (or cache hit) in the
  `GenerationResult` only. Reading the cache (`R-GEN-005`) is
  unaffected.

  Two independent reasons, not just a style preference: (1) a
  hint-mode preview runs speculatively, before a change is submitted
  (`R-ASSIST-003`), and must never overwrite the real, verified
  `gen/<component>/`; (2) `spec_bundle_hash` excludes `hint_code`
  (`spec-bundle-assembler` `R-ASSEMBLE-007`), so a `hint`- and
  `cold`-mode call for the same spec state share one cache key —
  writing a hint-informed candidate there could let a later `cold`
  build, which must see no prior code (`R-GEN-001`,
  `notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D1), silently reuse it.

  Reading a cache hit in `hint` mode stays safe: a hit only exists for
  a hash already matching some committed state, so reuse is correct
  and fast. Only a *write* can contaminate a future cold build.
documents.requirements/R-GEN-017.md:
# R-GEN-017

**R-GEN-017** — `GenerationResult.spec_bundle_hash` MUST always equal
  `bundle.spec_bundle_hash` (`D67`) — `provenance-writer`'s only source
  for it (`R-PROV-002`).
documents.requirements/R-GEN-018.md:
# R-GEN-018

**R-GEN-018** — Regardless of `depends_on`, the prompt MUST always
  instruct the candidate that any dynamic runtime load of a
  dependency module — bare `import <module_name>`, a `sys.modules`
  lookup on that bare name, or a path relative to the candidate's own
  `__file__` — MUST instead resolve from the `repo_root` parameter the
  candidate's own function actually received, joined to the module
  path `dependency_usage` gives: `gen/<dep-slug>/`, or a sealed
  dependency's own `source_path` (`D159`), or the same path under the

title: Graph Query Engine
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: []

sealed: false

# Graph Query Engine

## Purpose

Defines and generates the seven shared DuckDB views
(`specs/architecture/graph-query-engine.md`'s "Query surface") every
adopting component queries instead of writing its own frontmatter
parsing, file globbing, or text extraction.

## Rationale

Extracted from `specs/architecture/graph-query-engine.md`'s own prose
(`D13`) once that document's embedded SQL stopped being documentation
and started being the actual, unverified implementation — a spec
describing `CREATE VIEW` statements that had never been run is
exactly the "spec says X, code does Y" gap `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §10
now warns against. This component
makes the SQL a real, generated asset instead: `specs/architecture/
graph-query-engine.md` keeps the *why* (extension choice, adoption
history); this component owns the *what* (each view's exact
definition) and generates the SQL that runs it.

## Scope

**In scope:** the seven views' exact `CREATE VIEW` SQL; the loader
contract a consumer calls to create them against a given repo root.

**Out of scope:** deciding which queries a consumer runs against these
views once loaded (that's each consumer's own requirement, e.g.
`spec-linter`'s `R-LINT-020`/`021`); the `yaml`/`duckpgq` extension
choice itself (`specs/architecture/graph-query-engine.md`'s own
decision, unchanged here).

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

All nine criteria are `kind: compiled` — each view's SQL and the
loader's own behavior are fully deterministic, no model or judgment
involved.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- Initial draft (`D13`), extracted from
  `specs/architecture/graph-query-engine.md`.
- `D135`: `interface/library.md` states the literal yaml extension
  install incantation (`INSTALL yaml FROM community`, never a bare
  `INSTALL yaml`) — found once a fresh caller (`decision-drift-
  detector`) hit a real registry conflict that prose alone ("the
  `yaml` community extension") didn't prevent.
- `D176`: `views.sql` brought up to `R-GQE-001`/`002`/`008` — the `decision`
  node kind, the `supersedes`/`builds_on` edges, and `decision_lineage`
  had never been implemented. Decision fields are read from the
  frontmatter block only (a decision's prose quoted `supersedes:`).
documents.constraints.md:
# Graph Query Engine — Non-Functional Constraints

- **No model calls, no network access.** Pure local file I/O via
  DuckDB table functions, same trust tier as `spec-linter`.
- **Determinism.** Given the same corpus content and the same
  `repo_root`, every view MUST return byte-identical results on repeat
  queries — required for any consumer's own cache-key correctness
  (`notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D13) that reads through these views.
- **Never embeds `repo_root` into the generated SQL file itself.** The
  `{repo_root}` placeholder (`R-GQE-001`–`006`) MUST be substituted at
  `load_views()` call time, not baked in at generation time — the
  generated SQL is reusable across any checkout, not tied to the one
  it was generated against.
- **Hand-bootstrapped, not yet cold-regenerated** — the same honest
  exception `spec-linter` already documents (`generator`/
  `criterion-compiler` don't exist yet). See
  `verification/graph-query-engine/BOOTSTRAP.md`.

documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
load_views(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, repo_root: Path) -> None
```

Creates (or replaces) all seven views — `nodes`, `edges`,
`component_docs`, `component_context`, `component_provenance`,
`component_size`, `decision_lineage` — on `con`, scoped to the spec corpus under
`repo_root`. Requires the `yaml` community extension be installed and
loaded on `con` before calling (this component does not install it
itself) — **literally `INSTALL yaml FROM community` then
`LOAD yaml`, never a bare `INSTALL yaml`** (`D135`): a bare install
defaults to a different extension registry than the community one,
and conflicts outright on any machine where the community-origin
extension is already cached from a prior install, raising rather than
silently reusing it. `duckpgq` is not required by these views themselves —
none of them use its `MATCH` syntax — but a consumer MAY load it
separately to run its own traversal queries against the resulting
`nodes`/`edges` tables (see `specs/architecture/
graph-query-engine.md` for why these two extensions specifically).

Implements: `specs/architecture/graph-query-engine.md`
documents.requirements/R-GQE-001.md:
# R-GQE-001

**R-GQE-001** — The `nodes` view MUST return one row per spec id across
  eight kinds (`component`, `capability`, `var`, `decision`,
  `guarantee`, `requirement`, `acceptance`, `capability_scenario`),
  reading under the data contracts `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §2
  (frontmatter: `component`/`capability`/`var`/`decision` kinds) and
  §3.4/D1 (unit-file-per-id: `guarantee`/`requirement`/`acceptance`
  kinds carry no frontmatter, identity is the filename) and §5
  (capability scenarios are `### CS-...` headings inside a product
  capability file, not a file of their own). `decision` rows are safe
  via `read_yaml_frontmatter` despite `D13`'s sparse-column gotcha —
  `id`/`title`/`status` are unconditionally required on every decision
  record, never absent corpus-wide the way `supersedes`/`builds_on`
  are (`R-GQE-002` extracts those via `read_text` + regex instead, for
  exactly that reason):

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW nodes AS
SELECT id, title, status, 'component' AS kind, NULL AS owner_component_id
FROM read_yaml_frontmatter('{repo_root}/specs/components/*/component.md', filename:=true)
UNION ALL
SELECT id, title, status, 'capability', NULL
FROM read_yaml_frontmatter('{repo_root}/specs/product/*.md', filename:=true)
UNION ALL
SELECT id, title, status, 'var', NULL
FROM read_yaml_frontmatter('{repo_root}/specs/vars/*.md', filename:=true)
UNION ALL
SELECT id, title, status, 'decision', NULL
FROM read_yaml_frontmatter('{repo_root}/specs/decisions/*.md', filename:=true)
UNION ALL
SELECT
  regexp_extract(filename, '(G-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)\.md$', 1), NULL, NULL, 'guarantee',
  'comp-' || regexp_extract(filename, 'specs/components/([^/]+)/interface/guarantees/', 1)
FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/components/*/interface/guarantees/*.md')
UNION ALL
SELECT
  regexp_extract(filename, '(R-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)\.md$', 1), NULL, NULL, 'requirement',
  'comp-' || regexp_extract(filename, 'specs/components/([^/]+)/requirements/', 1)
FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/components/*/requirements/*.md')
UNION ALL
SELECT
  regexp_extract(filename, '(AC-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)\.md$', 1), NULL, NULL, 'acceptance',
  'comp-' || regexp_extract(filename, 'specs/components/([^/]+)/acceptance/', 1)
FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/components/*/acceptance/*.md')
UNION ALL
SELECT UNNEST(regexp_extract_all(content, '### (CS-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)', 1)), NULL, NULL, 'capability_scenario', NULL
FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/product/*.md');
```

  `{repo_root}` MUST be substituted with the caller's absolute repo
  root before execution (`R-GQE-007`) — this view's SQL is not valid on
  its own. `read_text` MUST NOT be called with `filename:=true` — it
  has no such parameter and errors if given one; it already
  returns `filename` unconditionally. `owner_component_id` MUST be
  `NULL` for `capability_scenario` rows — their parent is a capability,
  not a component; the `covers` edge (`R-GQE-002`) carries that
  relationship instead.
documents.requirements/R-GQE-002.md:
# R-GQE-002

**R-GQE-002** — The `edges` view MUST return one row per
  `(source_id, target_id, edge_type)`, reading under the data contracts
  `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §2 (`depends_on`/`realizes`/`uses_var`/
  `depends_on_guarantees`/`builds_on` as list-valued frontmatter
  fields, `supersedes` as scalar-valued) and §5 (`Covers:` as a
  body-text tag, never frontmatter — one per `component-acceptance`
  file per D1, one per capability scenario heading in a product
  file):

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW edges AS
SELECT
  regexp_extract(content, 'id:\s*(\S+)', 1) AS source_id,
  UNNEST(list_filter(list_transform(
    string_split(regexp_extract(content, 'depends_on:\s*\[([^\]]*)\]', 1), ','),
    lambda x: trim(x)
  ), lambda x: x != '')) AS target_id,
  'depends_on' AS edge_type
FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/components/*/component.md')
UNION ALL
SELECT
  regexp_extract(content, 'id:\s*(\S+)', 1),
  UNNEST(list_filter(list_transform(
    string_split(regexp_extract(content, 'realizes:\s*\[([^\]]*)\]', 1), ','),
    lambda x: trim(x)
  ), lambda x: x != '')),
  'realizes'
FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/components/*/component.md')
UNION ALL
SELECT
  regexp_extract(content, 'id:\s*(\S+)', 1),
  UNNEST(list_filter(list_transform(
    string_split(regexp_extract(content, 'uses_var:\s*\[([^\]]*)\]', 1), ','),
    lambda x: trim(x)
  ), lambda x: x != '')),
  'uses_var'
FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/components/*/component.md')
UNION ALL
SELECT
  regexp_extract(content, 'id:\s*(\S+)', 1),
  UNNEST(list_filter(list_transform(
    string_split(regexp_extract(content, 'depends_on_guarantees:\s*\[([^\]]*)\]', 1), ','),
    lambda x: trim(x)
  ), lambda x: x != '')),
  'depends_on_guarantees'
FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/components/*/component.md')
UNION ALL
SELECT
  regexp_extract(filename, '(AC-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)\.md$', 1),
  regexp_extract(content, 'Covers:\s*(\S+)', 1), 'covers'
FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/components/*/acceptance/*.md')
UNION ALL
SELECT m['cs_id'], m['target'], 'covers'
FROM (
  SELECT UNNEST(regexp_extract_all(
    content, '### (CS-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)\s*\nCovers:\s*(\S+)', ['cs_id', 'target']
  )) AS m
  FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/product/*.md')
)
UNION ALL
SELECT
  regexp_extract(fm, '(?m)^id:\s*(\S+)', 1),
  regexp_extract(fm, '(?m)^supersedes:\s*(\S+)', 1),
  'supersedes'
FROM (SELECT regexp_extract(content, '^---\n(.*?)\n---\n', 1, 's') AS fm
  FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/decisions/*.md')) AS d
WHERE regexp_extract(fm, '(?m)^supersedes:\s*(\S+)', 1) != ''
UNION ALL
SELECT
  regexp_extract(fm, '(?m)^id:\s*(\S+)', 1),
  UNNEST(list_filter(list_transform(
    string_split(regexp_extract(fm, '(?m)^builds_on:\s*\[([^\]]*)\]', 1), ','),
    lambda x: trim(x)
  ), lambda x: x != '')),
  'builds_on'
FROM (SELECT regexp_extract(content, '^---\n(.*?)\n---\n', 1, 's') AS fm
  FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/decisions/*.md')) AS d;
```

  `{repo_root}` substitution and the `read_text` `filename:=true`
  prohibition are the same as `R-GQE-001`. The four `depends_on`/
  `realizes`/`uses_var`/`depends_on_guarantees` arms MUST read
  `component.md` via `read_text` and extract each field with a regex
  over the flow-style `key: [a, b]` syntax `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §2
  requires (confirmed via corpus-wide grep: never YAML block-list
  style) — NOT via `read_yaml_frontmatter`'s struct-column
  auto-detection, which silently DROPS a declared column from its
  result schema (a bind-time "column not found" error at the call
  site, not a null value) when that key is absent from every file in
  the glob at once (`D13`) — true of `uses_var`/`depends_on_guarantees`
  in sparse corpora such as `graph-query-engine`'s own test fixtures,
  where no component happens to use either field. The same reasoning
  governs `supersedes`/`builds_on`'s two new arms (`D74`): neither is
  present on more than a handful of decision records today, so
  `read_yaml_frontmatter` would silently drop either column outright.

  The decision arms MUST read only a record's frontmatter block, never
  its whole text: a decision's prose can quote a field, and matching
  anywhere turned `D137`'s quoted `supersedes: [D17]` into a
  `supersedes` edge that no decision declares (`D176`). Each arm
  extracts the block (`regexp_extract(content, '^---\n(.*?)\n---\n', 1,
  's')`) first, then matches each field at a line start within it.
documents.requirements/R-GQE-003.md:
# R-GQE-003

**R-GQE-003** — The `component_docs` view MUST return one row per
  component, its frontmatter fields joined with its full raw text,
  reading under the data contract `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §3.4
  (`component.md` is the one file in a component's directory carrying
  frontmatter):

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW component_docs AS
SELECT fm.*, t.content AS body
FROM read_yaml_frontmatter('{repo_root}/specs/components/*/component.md', filename:=true) fm
JOIN read_text('{repo_root}/specs/components/*/component.md') t USING (filename);
```

  `{repo_root}` substitution and the `read_text` `filename:=true`
  prohibition are the same as `R-GQE-001`.
documents.requirements/R-GQE-004.md:
# R-GQE-004

**R-GQE-004** — The `component_context` view MUST return one row per
  component, just its `Purpose` section's text, reading under the data
  contract `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §3.4 (`Purpose` is `component.md`'s
  first section, dependent-safe by construction, `D21`):

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW component_context AS
SELECT
  id AS component_id,
  regexp_extract(body, '##\s*Purpose\s*\n(.*?)\n##', 1, 's') AS purpose
FROM component_docs;
```

  The `'s'` (DOTALL) flag MUST be present — without it, `.` does not
  match newlines, so a multi-line `Purpose` section silently extracts
  to an empty string instead of erroring. Depends on
  `R-GQE-003`'s `component_docs` view, not raw files directly.
documents.requirements/R-GQE-005.md:
# R-GQE-005

**R-GQE-005** — The `component_provenance` view MUST return one row per
  component, read directly from `provenance-writer`'s already-written
  manifests, reading under the data contract `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §7
  (the `.provenance.json` schema, including `provenance_hit` — `D29`):

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW component_provenance AS
SELECT
  'comp-' || regexp_extract(filename, 'verification/([^/]+)/\.provenance\.json$', 1)
    AS component_id,
  *
FROM read_json('{repo_root}/verification/*/.provenance.json', filename:=true);
```

  `{repo_root}` substitution is the same as `R-GQE-001`. `read_json`
  (unlike `read_text`) genuinely supports `filename:=true` — confirmed
  by running this view, not assumed.

  **MUST degrade to an empty, correctly-shaped view — never an error —
  when no `.provenance.json` files exist yet** (`D13`): `read_json`
  raises on a glob matching zero files, unlike `read_text`, and a new
  project has no manifests yet. `load_views` (`R-GQE-007`) MUST check for at least one
  matching file first and fall back to an explicitly-typed empty
  `SELECT ... WHERE false` (`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §7's field list) when
  none exists, so a query naming any of this view's columns still
  succeeds, just returns zero rows.

  **A real consumer dependency, not an optional extra:** once a
  real `.provenance.json` exists, `read_json`'s auto-detection types
  `generated_at` as `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE` (it looks like an
  ISO-8601 timestamp), and materializing that type requires the `pytz`
  package. Any caller that actually queries this view against real
  provenance data MUST have `pytz` installed — confirmed by hand that
  pinning `generated_at`'s type via `read_json`'s `columns` parameter
  isn't a clean alternative, since `columns` forces a closed schema
  (the same intersection-only behavior `R-GQE-002`'s rewrite already
  found), which would drop every other passthrough field this view's
  `SELECT *` otherwise preserves.
documents.requirements/R-GQE-006.md:
# R-GQE-006

**R-GQE-006** — The `component_size` view MUST return one row per
  component, the word count `spec-linter`'s `R-SIZE-001`
  (`component_doc_words`) measures, reading under the data contract
  `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §4 (the size-cap table's own definition: every
  doc under a component's directory):

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW component_size AS
SELECT
  regexp_extract(filename, 'specs/components/([^/]+)/', 1) AS component_id,
  sum(len(list_filter(
    regexp_split_to_array(
      trim(regexp_replace(content, '^---\n.*?\n---\n', '', 's')),
      '\s+'
    ),
    lambda x: x != ''
  ))) AS word_count
FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/components/*/**/*.md')
GROUP BY 1;
```

  `{repo_root}` substitution is the same as `R-GQE-001`. `trim()`
  without an explicit character set strips spaces only, not newlines —
  the `list_filter` MUST remain, to drop the spurious trailing empty
  token every file's own trailing newline otherwise produces (`D13`).
  The frontmatter-stripping `regexp_replace` MUST keep its `'s'` flag,
  for the same DOTALL reason as `R-GQE-004`.
documents.requirements/R-GQE-007.md:
# R-GQE-007

**R-GQE-007** — MUST expose a `load_views(con, repo_root)` call that
  creates all seven views (`R-GQE-001`–`006`, `R-GQE-008`) against a given DuckDB
  connection, substituting `repo_root` (an absolute path) for every
  `{repo_root}` placeholder in the generated SQL before executing each
  `CREATE VIEW` statement in dependency order (`component_context`
  after `component_docs`, since it selects from it). Idempotent: MUST
  NOT fail if called twice on the same connection (`CREATE OR REPLACE
  VIEW`, not bare `CREATE VIEW`). MUST raise, not swallow, any error a
  view's own `CREATE VIEW` statement raises — a caller needs to know
  immediately if a view it depends on failed to create, not discover
  it later as a missing-table error on first query.

  `read_yaml_frontmatter` MUST NOT be allowed to raise merely because a
  glob it reads matches zero files (unlike `read_text`, which already
  tolerates this natively — confirmed by hand, not assumed): a corpus
  legitimately has no `specs/vars/*.md`, `specs/product/*.md`,
  `specs/decisions/*.md` or `specs/components/*/component.md` files yet in
  some states (a project `hotdocs init` set up without `--example` has no
  component at all) (`graph-query-engine`'s own sparse test fixtures,
  `spec-linter`'s, `D13`), and that is expected state, not an error, the
  same posture `R-GQE-005` already requires for zero `.provenance.json`
  files. `load_views` MUST pre-check each such glob and substitute a
  typed, always-empty relation for that one call site when it has zero
  matches, rather than letting the bind-time error propagate.
  Every view then still exists and returns zero rows.
documents.requirements/R-GQE-008.md:
# R-GQE-008

**R-GQE-008** — The `decision_lineage` view MUST return one row per
  decision record: `id` and `last_ratified_commit` only (`D74`) —
  `status`/`supersedes`/`builds_on` live in `nodes`/`edges` directly,
  the single canonical home for anything graph-shaped;
  `last_ratified_commit` has no equivalent column there and stays
  here, the one fact only decision records carry:

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW decision_lineage AS
SELECT
  regexp_extract(fm, '(?m)^id:\s*(\S+)', 1) AS id,
  NULLIF(regexp_extract(fm, '(?m)^last_ratified_commit:\s*(\S+)', 1), '') AS last_ratified_commit
FROM (SELECT regexp_extract(content, '^---\n(.*?)\n---\n', 1, 's') AS fm
  FROM read_text('{repo_root}/specs/decisions/*.md')) AS d
WHERE fm != '';
```

  `R-CITE-004`/`030` MUST query `nodes`/`edges` for `status`/
  `supersedes`/`builds_on`, and this view only for
  `last_ratified_commit` when a temporal comparison is actually
  needed (`decision-drift-detector`'s own job, not spec-linter's).
