# Hotdocs CLI

## Purpose

The single `hotdocs` command: routes `hotdocs <verb> ...` to the component
that implements the verb.

## Rationale

Every component had its own `main` and nothing routed to them, so there was
no `hotdocs` command (`D184`). The table of verbs, with each component's
argument contract, is data so a verb is one row and a generation never
guesses a contract.

## Scope

**In scope:** the dispatcher, its verb table, and `help`/`--version`;
routing `init` to `hotdocs-init`.

**Out of scope:** what each verb does, including `init`; the `pyproject.toml`
and the entry module in `tools/`, hand-authored.

**Loose coupling, on purpose.** The only dependency is `llm-endpoint`, for
the configured model. Verb targets are reached by loading their `main` by
path from the table, not through their Python APIs, so no verb can break
this component's interface.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`. All `kind: generated-test`: a temporary project and fake components that log their `argv`.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- `D184`: initial design. `D185`: setup (`init`) split out to `hotdocs-init`.
documents.constraints.md:
# Hotdocs CLI — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Fresh loads.** Two projects in one process never share a loaded
  component module.
- **No hidden cost.** A model is injected only for verbs that cannot run
  without one; a read-only verb never gains one.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs <verb words> [args...]
hotdocs [--help | -h | help | --version]
```

`main(argv)` receives everything after the `hotdocs` word. Verbs route per
`interface/data/VerbTable.md` (`R-CLI-001`–`005`), `init` included; help and
version are `R-CLI-004`.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Help or version; or a routed verb whose component returned `0`. |
| `2` | Unknown verb; a verb whose component file or `main` is missing. |
| other | A routed verb returns its component's own code. |
documents.interface/data/VerbTable.md:
# `VerbTable`

The dispatcher's only knowledge of a verb (`R-CLI-001`). `strip` is how
many leading `argv` tokens are removed before the component's `main` is
called, because the components disagree about whether `main` wants its
verb words. `model` is `required` when the component cannot run without
`--model` (`R-CLI-003`). Entries in `module` containing a `.` are
packages' submodules.

| verb words | dir | module | strip | model | summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lint` | `gen/spec-linter` | `spec_linter` | 1 | no | validate the spec corpus |
| `impact` | `gen/impact-analyzer` | `impact_analyzer` | 1 | no | blast radius of a change |
| `assemble` | `gen/spec-bundle-assembler` | `spec_bundle_assembler` | 1 | no | build a component's spec bundle |
| `compile-criteria` | `pipeline/criterion-compiler` | `criterion_compiler` | 1 | no | compile the compiled criteria |
| `author-test` | `gen/test-author` | `test_author` | 0 | required | write one criterion's test |
| `verify-component` | `gen/verifier-orchestrator` | `verifier_orchestrator` | 1 | no | verify one component |
| `generate` | `gen/component-gate-runner` | `component_gate_runner` | 0 | required | generate and verify a component |
| `verify` | `gen/provenance-tracker` | `provenance_tracker` | 0 | no | is everything ready |
| `track feedback` | `gen/provenance-tracker` | `provenance_tracker` | 0 | no | last failing requirements |
| `track ui build` | `gen/provenance-tracker-ui` | `provenance_tracker_ui` | 0 | no | build the readiness page |
| `provenance check` | `gen/provenance-checker` | `provenance_checker` | 1 | no | is provenance a hit |
| `provenance write` | `gen/provenance-writer` | `provenance_writer` | 0 | no | write a provenance manifest |
| `license-scan` | `gen/license-scanner` | `license_scanner` | 1 | no | license scan one component |
| `secret-scan` | `gen/secret-scanner` | `secret_scanner` | 1 | no | scan for secrets |
| `review-packet build` | `gen/review-packet-builder` | `review_packet_builder` | 0 | no | build a review packet |
| `decision-drift` | `gen/decision-drift-detector` | `decision_drift_detector` | 0 | no | decisions out of step with specs |
| `decision-impact` | `gen/decision-drift-detector` | `decision_drift_detector` | 0 | no | what a decision touches |
| `docs-site build` | `gen/docs-site-renderer` | `docs_site_renderer.cli` | 2 | no | render the docs site |
| `corpus-graph build` | `gen/corpus-graph-builder` | `corpus_graph_builder.cli` | 1 | no | build the corpus graph |
| `assist` | `gen/spec-completeness-assistant` | `spec_completeness_assistant` | 1 | no | review a spec change |
| `init` | `gen/hotdocs-init` | `hotdocs_init` | 1 | no | set up a new project |

`init` is special (`R-CLI-005`). `cache` is documented by
`cache-manager` but that component defines no `main`, so it has no row.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
TOOL_VERSION = "0.1.0"
main(argv=None, *, tool_root=None, input_fn=None, output_fn=None,
     env=None, cwd=None) -> int
```

`argv` defaults to `sys.argv[1:]`, `input_fn` to `input`, `output_fn` to
`print`, `env` to `os.environ`, `cwd` to the current directory. Normal
messages go to `output_fn`, errors to `sys.stderr`. `tool_root` is the tool's
own repository, supplied by the entry module in `tools/`; when `None`, it is
the parent of the nearest `gen` directory above this module's file. A
project holds only its own components, so every verb falls back to it
(`R-CLI-001`).

## llm-endpoint

Found as any module is (`R-CLI-001`). The one name
used is `load_config(config_path=None)` — `{provider, model, base_url,
api_key_env, timeout_seconds}`, `None` when there is no `[llm]` table,
`ValueError` when invalid. Any stand-in must provide it.

## Test fixtures

A **fake component** at `<project>/<dir>/<module>.py` defines `main(argv)`,
which appends `json.dumps(argv)` as a line to `<project>/calls.log` (the path
written into its source) and returns `7`. For the `init` row the fake lives
at `<tool_root>/gen/hotdocs-init/hotdocs_init.py` and also logs the keyword
arguments it received. A **fake tool root** is a separate temporary
directory passed as `tool_root`, holding fakes at the same relative paths.
documents.requirements/R-CLI-001.md:
# R-CLI-001

**R-CLI-001** — A verb MUST be dispatched to the row of `interface/data/VerbTable.md` whose verb words are the longest prefix of `argv`: the component's `main` is called with exactly `argv[strip:]` (never `argv[len(words):]`: a `strip` of `0` keeps the verb words, so `generate x --flag` calls `main(["generate", "x", "--flag", ...])`; the `init` row, whose `strip` is `1`, receives the tokens after `init`, with every following token kept), and its return value is the exit code (`None` is `0`). A `SystemExit` raised by the component MUST be caught and its code returned (`None` is `0`, a non-integer is `1`). A module is `<dir>/<module>.py`, or when that file is absent the package `<dir>/<module>/__init__.py`, under the repo root when `<repo root>/<dir>` exists, and otherwise under the tool root (`D199`): the `tool_root` argument, or when it is `None` the parent of the nearest directory named `gen` above this module's own file. It is loaded by file path under a name unique to that repo root and registered in `sys.modules` before it runs; a module with a `.`, such as `docs_site_renderer.cli`, is imported with `<dir>` first on `sys.path`, every `sys.modules` entry for its package removed before and after. A module MUST be loaded fresh on every call and not left behind: a later call in the same process for another repo root never sees it.
documents.requirements/R-CLI-002.md:
# R-CLI-002

**R-CLI-002** — For every row but `init`, the repo root MUST be taken from `--repo-root` (as `--repo-root=<v>` or `--repo-root <v>`) among the arguments after the verb words, else the current directory, and used absolute to locate the component. When the argument is absent, `--repo-root=<root>` MUST be appended to the forwarded tokens; when present, the tokens are forwarded unchanged. While the component runs, `VAR_HOTDOCS_CONFIG` MUST be set to `<repo root>/hotdocs.toml` if that file exists and the variable is unset, and restored afterwards, since `llm-endpoint` otherwise looks for its configuration in the current directory, which is not necessarily the project.
documents.requirements/R-CLI-003.md:
# R-CLI-003

**R-CLI-003** — For a row whose `model` is `required`, when the arguments hold no `--model` token (`--model` or `--model=...`) and `load_config(<repo root>/hotdocs.toml)` (`load_config` of `gen/llm-endpoint/llm_endpoint.py`, found as `R-CLI-001` finds a module) returns a provider and model, `--model=<provider>:<model>` (a model string, per the glossary) MUST be appended last, after the `--repo-root` token `R-CLI-002` may have appended. If `load_config` raises `ValueError`, its message MUST be printed to stderr and nothing injected. Nothing is injected otherwise: an explicit `--model` passes unchanged, and rows whose `model` is `no` never gain one, since a model silently turns a read-only check into paid work.
documents.requirements/R-CLI-004.md:
# R-CLI-004

**R-CLI-004** — With no arguments, `help`, `--help` or `-h`, `main` MUST print `hotdocs <TOOL_VERSION>`, a usage line, and every verb of the table with its summary, and return `0`; `--version` prints `hotdocs <TOOL_VERSION>` and returns `0`. An unknown first word MUST print `unknown verb: <word>` and the same verb list to stderr and return `2`. A matched verb whose `<dir>/<module>.py` exists under neither root MUST print a message naming the tool-root path, and return `2`; one whose module has no `main` MUST print that it is not available and return `2`.
documents.requirements/R-CLI-005.md:
# R-CLI-005

**R-CLI-005** — The `init` row is special. Its module MUST be loaded from `<tool_root>/<dir>`, not from the project, since the project does not have it yet; no `--repo-root` is appended and `VAR_HOTDOCS_CONFIG` is not set; and its `main` is called with the remaining tokens plus the keyword arguments `tool_root`, `input_fn`, `output_fn`, `env`, and `cwd` that this component itself received, defaults filled in. Its return value is the exit code, as for any verb.
documents.requirements/R-CLI-006.md:
# R-CLI-006

**R-CLI-006** — `main` MUST implement `interface/cli.md` exactly: the exit codes `0` for help, `--version`, and a routed verb that returns `0`; `2` for an unknown verb or a missing component file or `main`; and a routed verb's own code otherwise (`D162`).

# Hotdocs Init

## Purpose

Sets up a new project for the tool: the directory skeleton, a check of what the machine still needs, and the choice and test of a
language-model provider.

## Rationale

A project needs a known layout and a working provider before anything else
runs. `init` once copied the tool into each project (`D184`); components
now fall back to the tool's own `gen/` (`D199`), so it copies nothing. It was first specified inside
`hotdocs-cli`, but one generated module covering both routing and setup was
too large for a single model response (`D185`).

## Scope

**In scope:** the project skeleton, the prerequisite report, the
provider step, and the `--example` project.

**Out of scope:** routing (`hotdocs-cli` calls this component's `main`);
installing anything (this component prints the command and never runs it).

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

None.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`. All `kind: generated-test`: a temporary project directory
and a fake tool root.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- `D184`: initial design, inside `hotdocs-cli`. `D185`: split out.
- `D197`: seeds a sealed allowlist. `D199`: copies nothing from the tool;
  the allowlist starts empty.
- `D203`: the Python floor is 3.11. `D205`: `.hotdocs-tool.json` marks
  an initialised project.
documents.constraints.md:
# Hotdocs Init — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Never installs, never reads a secret.** Missing prerequisites are
  reported with the command to run. An API key is never asked for, stored,
  or printed; only the NAME of its environment variable is.
- **Never overwrites.** Anything that exists is skipped, and reported.
- **Fail before writing.** A name collision or an unusable target stops
  `init` before anything is written.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs init [<dir>] [--example] [--reconfigure] [--provider <name>]
    [--model <name>] [--base-url <url>] [--api-key-env <NAME>]
    [--no-test] [--yes]
```

`main(argv)` receives everything after the `init` word. Every flag takes its
value as `--flag=value` or as the next argument; `--example`,
`--reconfigure`, `--no-test`, and `--yes` take none. `<dir>` defaults to the
current directory. Behavior is in `R-INIT-001`–`006`; usage errors in
`R-INIT-007`.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Finished, with every prerequisite present. |
| `1` | Refused before writing anything (a name collision, or `<dir>` is the tool's own repository), or `--reconfigure` on a directory that is not an initialised project, or on a failed save. |
| `2` | Usage error. |
| `3` | Finished, but a prerequisite is missing. |
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
main(argv, *, tool_root, input_fn=None, output_fn=None, env=None, cwd=None) -> int
```

`argv` is everything after the word `init`. `input_fn` defaults to `input`,
`output_fn` to `print`, `env` to `os.environ`, `cwd` to the current
directory. Normal messages go to `output_fn`, errors to `sys.stderr`.
Each question is passed to `input_fn` as its text plus one trailing space,
e.g. `"Save anyway? [y/N] "`.
`tool_root` is the tool's own repository. `init` copies nothing from it but
`examples/slugify/`, only with `--example`, to the project root, never under
`examples/`; it reads `requirements.txt` (`R-INIT-003`) and loads
`llm-endpoint` from it.

## llm-endpoint

Loaded from `<tool_root>/gen/llm-endpoint/llm_endpoint.py`, or when that
file is absent the package `llm_endpoint/__init__.py` there. Exactly these
names are used, read with dual dict-or-attribute access:

- `PROVIDERS` — `{provider: {default_base_url, default_api_key_env,
  needs_base_url, suggested_model}}`; `suggested_model` is `""` for
  `openai-compatible`;
- `detect_providers(env=None, probe_ollama=True)` — one entry per provider,
  `{provider, available, reason, suggested_model, api_key_env}`; called with
  `env=<the env given to main>`, and with no `env` when none was given;
- `check_connection(provider, model, base_url=None, api_key_env=None,
  timeout_seconds=30)` — `{ok, error}`, `error` `None` or `{category,
  message}`; raises `ValueError` for an unknown provider or a missing
  required `base_url`;
- `save_config(config_path, provider, model, base_url=None,
  api_key_env=None, timeout_seconds=None)` — keeps other file content,
  replaces `[llm]`, raises `ValueError` for anything invalid;
- `load_config(config_path=None)` — `{provider, model, base_url,
  api_key_env, timeout_seconds}`, `None` when there is no `[llm]` table,
  `ValueError` when invalid.

`hotdocs.toml` is written and read only through `save_config` and
`load_config`. Any stand-in must provide all five names.

## Test fixtures

A **fake tool root** holds `gen/<slug>/<module>.py` fakes for a few slugs,
among them `llm-endpoint` (fakes of the five names above that also log each
call to a file outside both the project and the tool root, so a log never counts as a change to either),
`examples/slugify/specs/product/slugs.md`, and a `requirements.txt` whose only line is
`pytest==` plus `importlib.metadata.version("pytest")` (so nothing is missing). A test embeds no secret-shaped string.
documents.requirements/R-INIT-001.md:
# R-INIT-001

**R-INIT-001** — `init [<dir>]` MUST, in `<dir>` (created when absent), create what is missing of: the directories `specs/product`, `specs/components`, `specs/decisions`, `gen`, `verification`, with an empty `.gitkeep` in each of `specs/product`, `specs/components`, `specs/decisions`, and `verification`; a `specs/glossary.md` holding `# Glossary`, a blank line, and one sentence on its purpose; `.secret-allowlist.json` (`R-INIT-008`); and the lines `/.hotdocs/`, `__pycache__/`, `*.pyc`, `.venv/` appended to `.gitignore` (created when absent), each only if not already a line. It MUST NOT overwrite or truncate anything that exists, and MUST print through `output_fn`, for every directory and file named above (each `.gitkeep` included), one line exactly `<path>: created` or `<path>: skipped (exists)`, with `<path>` relative to `<dir>`, so a second run changes nothing.
documents.requirements/R-INIT-002.md:
# R-INIT-002

**R-INIT-002** — `init` MUST NOT copy the tool into the project: the tool's components stay under `tool_root` and are found there (`D199`). It MUST write `<dir>/.hotdocs-tool.json`, only when absent and otherwise left byte for byte, holding `{"tool_version": TOOL_VERSION}`, the module constant `TOOL_VERSION = "0.1.0"` matching `pyproject.toml`. Before writing or loading anything, even `R-INIT-001`'s skeleton or `llm-endpoint` (an import writes `__pycache__`), it MUST refuse, exit `1`, if `<dir>` is `tool_root` itself, or if `<dir>/gen` holds a directory whose name is also a directory directly under `<tool_root>/gen/` (a project component would shadow the tool's), listing each such `gen/<name>`.
documents.requirements/R-INIT-004.md:
# R-INIT-004

**R-INIT-004** — Unless `<dir>/hotdocs.toml` exists (it is then kept and reported), or `--reconfigure` is given, `init` MUST configure the provider. If neither `--provider` nor `--yes` is given it asks, through `input_fn`, in this order: the provider (a name or its 1-based number in the printed list from `detect_providers`, default the first available, else the first listed; an unrecognised answer is asked again); the model (default its `suggested_model`; an empty answer with no default is asked again); the base URL, only if `needs_base_url` (default `default_base_url`, asked again if empty with no default); and the API-key environment variable NAME, for every provider except `claude-cli` (default `default_api_key_env`; empty means none). An empty answer is the default. With `--provider`, the values come from the flags and defaults and nothing is asked; with `--yes` alone, from the first available provider and its defaults, and with none available nothing is saved and `init` says so and carries on. `timeout_seconds` is never asked or passed. If `<tool_root>/gen/llm-endpoint/llm_endpoint.py` does not exist, nothing can be configured: `init` prints `provider not configured: gen/llm-endpoint is missing` and carries on.
documents.requirements/R-INIT-005.md:
# R-INIT-005

**R-INIT-005** — Then, unless `--no-test`, `init` MUST call `check_connection` and print `connection ok` or `connection failed: <category>: <message>`; a `ValueError` from it MUST be printed as `connection failed: invalid: <message>`. After a failure it asks `Save anyway? [y/N]` (interactive) or saves and warns (`--yes` or `--provider`); on `n` nothing is saved. Saving MUST be `save_config(<dir>/hotdocs.toml, provider, model, base_url=..., api_key_env=...)`, passing a keyword only when it has a value; a `ValueError` from it is printed as `could not save: <message>` to stderr, nothing is saved, and `init` carries on. `init` never asks for, reads, prints, or writes an API key.
documents.requirements/R-INIT-006.md:
# R-INIT-006

**R-INIT-006** — `--example` MUST additionally copy every file under `<tool_root>/examples/slugify/`, never overwriting, to its path relative to `examples/slugify/` in `<dir>`: `<tool_root>/examples/slugify/specs/product/slugs.md` becomes `<dir>/specs/product/slugs.md`, and nothing is created under `<dir>/examples/`. `--reconfigure` MUST exit `1` with a message when `<dir>/.hotdocs-tool.json` does not exist (that file, written by `R-INIT-002`, is what makes a directory an initialised project), and otherwise do only the provider step, replacing the `[llm]` table of `hotdocs.toml` through `save_config`, and exit `1` with a message if `<tool_root>/gen/llm-endpoint/llm_endpoint.py` does not exist or if saving fails. `init` MUST end by printing next steps: `hotdocs lint`, `hotdocs generate comp-slugify` only with `--example`, `hotdocs verify`, and `QUICKSTART.md`.
documents.requirements/R-INIT-007.md:
# R-INIT-007

**R-INIT-007** — `main` MUST implement `interface/cli.md` exactly. Its usage errors, all exit `2` before anything is written, are: an unknown flag, a flag given last with no value, a second positional argument, a `--provider` that is not a key of `PROVIDERS` (the message lists the keys), an `--api-key-env` that is not a valid environment-variable name (letters, digits, `_`, not starting with a digit; the message does not repeat the value, so a key pasted by mistake is never echoed or stored), `--base-url` or `--api-key-env` with `claude-cli`, a `--provider` whose `suggested_model` is empty given without `--model`, and one with `needs_base_url` given without `--base-url` (`D162`).
documents.requirements/R-INIT-008.md:
# R-INIT-008

**R-INIT-008** — When `init` creates `.secret-allowlist.json`, it MUST write it as the UTF-8 bytes of `json.dumps({"version": 1, "entries": []}, indent=2)` plus `"\n"`. An empty allowlist needs no sealing decision, so `init` MUST NOT create any file under `specs/decisions/` other than `R-INIT-001`'s `.gitkeep` (`D199`, withdrawing `D197`'s seeded entry). When the allowlist exists it is skipped as `R-INIT-001` says.

---
id: comp-impact-analyzer
title: Impact Analyzer
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-spec-linter]
realizes: [P-ZERO-EDIT]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5

# Impact Analyzer

## Purpose

From a set of changed spec ids, computes the minimal **blast radius**
(the term as defined in `specs/glossary.md`) — the set of components
that actually need regeneration or re-verification for this change.
Runs after `spec-linter` passes, assuming a validated, acyclic,
reference-resolved corpus graph; it does not re-validate that graph
itself.

## Rationale

Built on the engine named in `specs/architecture/graph-query-engine.md`
(R-IMPACT-009): the corpus graph is loaded directly from spec
frontmatter via DuckDB's `yaml` extension, and transitive propagation
is computed via `duckpgq` graph-pattern queries — this is the first
component rebuilt on that shared engine, not a bespoke traversal
implementation.

## Scope

**In scope:** determining, for a given set of changed spec ids, which
components are directly changed and which are transitively impacted because
something they depend on changed in a way that affects their contract.
Distinguishing a dependency's *contract* changing from its *internals*
changing, so an unrelated component's change doesn't force regeneration of
everything downstream of it. Per `D2`: distinguishing, within the
contract itself, type-level content (`cli.md`/`library.md`/`data/*.md` —
always coarse, always propagates) from behavioral guarantees
(`guarantees/*.md` — narrowable, opt-in, per `depends_on_guarantees`).

**Out of scope:** generation itself; deciding *how* to regenerate a component,
only *whether* it's in scope this merge; re-running `spec-linter`'s own
checks.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

Every criterion below is `kind: compiled` — blast-radius computation is a
pure graph traversal over corpus state, the same demonstration `spec-linter`
already made for the "prefer `compiled` whenever possible" guidance, applied
to a second real component.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None. The two originally recorded here are both resolved:

- ~~R-IMPACT-002/003 define contract-change detection as "is `interface.md`
  byte-identical" — blunt~~ — resolved by `D1` (one-file-per-unit hashing,
  no semantic diffing needed) and sharpened further by `D2`: true semantic
  diffing *within* one `interface/` file (e.g. a typo fix in `library.md`'s
  prose still forcing propagation) remains unsolved for `cli.md`/
  `library.md`/`data/*.md` — accepted as safe-but-wasteful, same as
  before — but for behavioral guarantees specifically, `D2`'s
  `interface/guarantees/` + `depends_on_guarantees` narrowing solves the
  *coarser* version of this same problem: a dependent that only cares
  about one guarantee no longer pays for changes to unrelated ones.
- ~~Should `R-IMPACT-004`/`005`'s transitive inclusion cascade further?~~ —
  resolved: stays one-hop, by design, **not** because the residual risk
  was dismissed, but because it's covered by a different, better-suited
  mechanism. One-hop risks a second-order change (e.g., component A's
  *behavior* shifting as a side effect of a var/capability-driven
  regeneration) going uncaught this merge if A's dependents aren't pulled
  in too. `D2` closes this two ways: (1) `interface/guarantees/` makes any
  *foreseen* behavioral dependency explicit and propagating, the same
  one-hop mechanism everything else uses — no cascading needed once the
  guarantee itself is visible; (2) `capability-scenario-verifier`, run
  as part of `hotdocs verify` once its realizing components pass
  (`D89`/`D92`/`D93`), is the permanent backstop for whatever wasn't foreseen,
  tested against the real regenerated system rather than guessed at here.
  Eager multi-hop cascading from every `transitive-var`/
  `transitive-capability` edge was rejected as the alternative — it would
  trade this bounded, already-covered risk for routinely ballooning the
  blast radius on pure speculation, undermining the methodology's own
  cost-containment premise (`P-ZERO-EDIT`).

## Change log

- Initial draft.

documents.constraints.md:
# Impact Analyzer — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Determinism.** Same `(changed_ids, corpus state)` input MUST always
  produce byte-identical output. Required for `notes/initial-ideas.md`'s
  own D13's cache-key correctness, same as `spec-linter`. DuckDB queries are themselves pure functions of
  their input tables (R-IMPACT-009) — this property is a consequence of
  the engine choice, not something layered on top of it afterward.
- **Performance.** Computing blast radius for a single-digit number of
  changed ids MUST complete in well under 1 second against a corpus with
  hundreds of components — it is a graph traversal, not a search, and must
  not become a merge-latency bottleneck (`notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own
  D13). An embedded analytical
  engine built for exactly this shape of query is expected to clear this
  bar comfortably; this constraint does not relax just because the engine
  changed.
- **No network access, no model calls.** Pure graph logic over the already-
  validated corpus graph `spec-linter` produces, now via DuckDB's `yaml`
  and `duckpgq` extensions (both embedded, local, no network dependency —
  `specs/architecture/graph-query-engine.md`) rather than bespoke
  traversal code.
- **Fail closed, not best-effort.** Per R-IMPACT-007, an invalid corpus graph
  MUST produce an explicit precondition error, never a partial or
  silently-wrong blast radius — an under-computed blast radius here directly
  threatens `P-ZERO-EDIT` (a component that needed regeneration silently
  not getting it).
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs impact --changed <spec-id>... [--repo-root=<dir>] [--format=json|text]
```

- `--changed <spec-id>...` — one or more spec ids known to have changed in
  this diff (as determined by the caller, e.g. from `git diff`'s changed
  paths resolved to spec ids). Required, ≥1.
- `--repo-root` — defaults to the current git repository root.
- `--format` — `text` (human-readable, default) or `json` (the
  `BlastRadiusReport` schema below).

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Blast radius computed successfully (may be empty if nothing depends on the changed ids and none are themselves components). |
| `1` | Precondition failure — the corpus did not pass `spec-linter` cleanly (R-IMPACT-007). |
| `2` | Usage error (no `--changed` ids given, an id that doesn't exist in the corpus at all). |
documents.interface/data/BlastRadiusReport.md:
# `BlastRadiusReport`

```json
{
  "impacted": [
    {
      "component_id": "comp-foo",
      "reason": "direct",
      "via": null
    },
    {
      "component_id": "comp-bar",
      "reason": "transitive-interface",
      "via": "comp-foo"
    },
    {
      "component_id": "comp-baz",
      "reason": "transitive-var",
      "via": "VAR-CACHE-STORE-URL"
    },
    {
      "component_id": "comp-qux",
      "reason": "transitive-capability",
      "via": "P-ZERO-EDIT"
    },
    {
      "component_id": "comp-quux",
      "reason": "transitive-guarantee",
      "via": "comp-foo",
      "guarantee_ids": ["G-FOO-001"]
    }
  ],
  "precondition_error": null
}
```

`component_id` is always the full `comp-<slug>` form (`glossary.md`'s
"Component id / component slug" entry), matching exactly what a
caller's own `--changed` argument would use — never the bare slug,
even though some of this component's own internal data (e.g.
`spec-linter`'s `corpus.components` dict) is keyed by the bare form.

Each component appears at most once. One named in the changed ids is
always `direct`, whatever else would also include it. `reason` is always one of `direct` | `transitive-interface` |
`transitive-var` | `transitive-capability` | `transitive-guarantee`
(R-IMPACT-001/003/004/005/008). `via` names the specific upstream id that
triggered inclusion, `null` only for `direct`. `guarantee_ids` is present
only for `reason: transitive-guarantee` — the specific `G-id`(s) that
changed and triggered this inclusion (R-IMPACT-008); when the dependent
declared no `depends_on_guarantees` for this upstream component (the
coarse default), this lists every guarantee file that changed, not just
ones the dependent explicitly claimed to rely on. A non-null
`precondition_error` means `impacted` is empty and MUST be ignored by
callers (R-IMPACT-007) — it is not "nothing was impacted," it is "the
question could not be answered."
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
compute_blast_radius(changed_ids: list[str], repo_root: Path) -> BlastRadiusReport
```

A pure function over the filesystem state at `repo_root` — no network
access, no model calls, no side effects. Raises/returns an explicit
precondition-failure result (not a best-effort partial one) if the corpus
graph isn't lint-clean.

So any corpus it is run on, a test's included, must lint clean under
`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` and `spec-linter`: for example, each requirement
or guarantee file opens with the heading `# <its id>`, equal to its
filename's stem, and states itself with an RFC 2119 keyword.

Implements: `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md`
documents.requirements/R-IMPACT-001.md:
# R-IMPACT-001

**R-IMPACT-001** — The analyzer MUST include every directly-changed spec id
  in the blast radius, tagged with reason `direct`, regardless of which file
  within that component's bundle changed.
documents.requirements/R-IMPACT-002.md:
# R-IMPACT-002

**R-IMPACT-002** — For a changed component, if `component.md`
(Purpose/Scope/Definitions), `requirements/`, `constraints.md`, or
`acceptance/` is what changed, and neither `interface/cli.md`,
`interface/library.md`, nor any file under `interface/data/` changed (per
R-IMPACT-003), the analyzer MUST NOT include that component's dependents in
the blast radius on that basis — such a change is internal and MUST NOT
propagate. (`interface/guarantees/` changes are handled separately by
R-IMPACT-008, not by this requirement.)

**This distinction was not previously specified anywhere in
`notes/initial-ideas.md` or `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` before this spec was
originally written** — the original brainstorm's size-cap discussion
states it only as a *sizing heuristic* ("a typical spec change stays
inside the component's own bundle and does not force an edit to a
depended-upon interface"), not as an executable rule
for this component. This requirement is the first place it becomes a
real, testable behavior rather than an aspiration.

**`D1` update:** originally this rule compared `interface.md` as one
whole file, hashed byte-for-byte — correct but blunt (a purely cosmetic
edit anywhere in the file still forced full propagation), and a later
working session explored section-scoped hashing as a refinement before
settling on the one-file-per-unit redesign (`D1`) instead, which achieves
the same precision — a prose-only edit to, say, `interface/library.md`'s
explanatory text still counts as that file changing, same as before, but
a change entirely confined to `requirements/`/`acceptance/`/
`constraints.md`/`component.md`'s narrative sections no longer touches
`interface/` at all and so no longer forces propagation. No new parsing
logic was needed to get this — directory structure already *is* the
section boundary.

**`D2` update:** split `interface/guarantees/` out from this requirement's
scope into its own, separately-narrowable requirement (R-IMPACT-008) —
behavioral guarantees are the one part of `interface/` where "a dependent
only cares about some of this" is a coherent claim; `cli.md`/`library.md`/
`data/*.md` stay coarse, always-propagating, under R-IMPACT-003.
documents.requirements/R-IMPACT-003.md:
# R-IMPACT-003

**R-IMPACT-003** — For a changed component whose `interface/cli.md`,
  `interface/library.md`, or any file under `interface/data/` changed
  relative to the prior commit (each compared independently; a file added
  or removed counts as changed) — **excluding `interface/guarantees/`,
  which R-IMPACT-008 handles separately and may narrow** — the analyzer
  MUST include every component with a `depends_on` edge to it, tagged with
  reason `transitive-interface`, naming the upstream component whose
  interface changed. These three file kinds always propagate in full,
  unconditionally — unlike `interface/guarantees/`, there is no coherent
  notion of "a dependent that only cares about some of a component's types
  or CLI surface" the way there is for behavioral guarantees (`D2`).
documents.requirements/R-IMPACT-004.md:
# R-IMPACT-004

**R-IMPACT-004** — For a changed `specs/vars/` declaration, the analyzer
  MUST treat it the same way as a changed `interface/` file: every
  component with a `uses_var` reference to that declaration is included,
  tagged `transitive-var`, naming the changed variable. (A variable's
  declared type/required/sensitivity is itself the contract a component
  depends on — there is no reason to treat it more loosely than an
  interface change.)
documents.requirements/R-IMPACT-005.md:
# R-IMPACT-005

**R-IMPACT-005** — For a changed product capability (a `P-<id>`'s own file,
  including its capability scenarios), the analyzer MUST include every component
  whose `realizes` lists that `P-<id>`, tagged `transitive-capability` — the
  capability's acceptance bar changed, so components claiming to satisfy it
  need re-verification against the new bar even if their own spec files
  didn't change.
documents.requirements/R-IMPACT-006.md:
# R-IMPACT-006

**R-IMPACT-006** — The analyzer's output MUST be a pure function of
  (changed spec ids, corpus state at the commit being analyzed) — no model
  calls, no network access, no dependence on wall-clock time or execution
  order.
documents.requirements/R-IMPACT-007.md:
# R-IMPACT-007

**R-IMPACT-007** — If the corpus has not passed `spec-linter` cleanly (any
  `fail`-severity finding present, including an unresolved cycle or a
  dangling reference anywhere in the graph, not only in the changed specs),
  the analyzer MUST fail closed — report a precondition error and compute no
  blast radius — rather than attempt a best-effort traversal over a graph it
  cannot trust.
documents.requirements/R-IMPACT-008.md:
# R-IMPACT-008

**R-IMPACT-008** — For a changed component whose `interface/guarantees/`
  content changed relative to the prior commit (compared per-file,
  independently), the analyzer MUST include every component with a
  `depends_on` edge to it — **narrowed** as follows: if the dependent
  declares one or more `depends_on_guarantees` entries whose owning
  component is this upstream component, the dependent MUST be included
  only if at least one of those *specifically declared* `G-id` files is
  among the changed guarantee files, tagged `transitive-guarantee` and
  naming the specific `G-id`(s) that changed. If the dependent declares no
  `depends_on_guarantees` entries for this upstream component at all, it
  MUST be included unconditionally whenever *any* file under that
  component's `interface/guarantees/` changed, tagged
  `transitive-guarantee` naming the upstream component — the same safe,
  coarse default every other `interface/` file kind already has (`D2`).

  **`depends_on_guarantees`'s real frontmatter shape** (`D49`, found
  missing from this bundle's own visible text, though already
  documented for humans in `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §2, which no
  `SpecBundle` ever includes): a flat list of bare `G-<comp>-NNN` id
  strings — e.g. `depends_on_guarantees: [G-CACHE-001]` — never a
  nested structure naming the owning component per entry. A `G-id`'s
  owning component is **never** parsed out of the id string itself
  (ambiguous once a component's own slug contains hyphens); it MUST be
  determined by which component's real `interface/guarantees/`
  directory actually contains a file with that id.

  This narrowing is **strictly opt-in**: a dependent's own silence (no
  `depends_on_guarantees` declared) MUST NEVER be read as "this dependent
  relies on nothing here" — only an explicit, non-empty declaration
  narrows anything. Getting a declared list wrong (under-claiming) is a
  real residual risk this requirement does not eliminate — it is
  structurally impossible for a graph-reachability computation to verify
  a claim about what code *actually* relies on — which is exactly why
  `D2`'s capability-scenario gate (`capability-scenario-verifier`, its
  own provenance checked by `provenance-tracker`'s `hotdocs verify`,
  `D89`) exists as a permanent backstop, not a transitional one,
  independent of how precise these declarations get.
documents.requirements/R-IMPACT-009.md:
# R-IMPACT-009

**R-IMPACT-009** — The corpus graph this component walks MUST be the
  `nodes`/`edges` views named in `specs/architecture/
  graph-query-engine.md`'s "Query surface" section — not a
  separately-written frontmatter load, and not a second definition of
  what counts as a node or edge. Those views already resolve every kind
  this component needs, guarantee nodes included (via `read_text()` over
  `interface/guarantees/*.md`, since those files carry no frontmatter to
  extract — `read_yaml_frontmatter()` alone cannot see them). Transitive
  propagation (R-IMPACT-003/004/005/008) MUST be expressed as
  graph-pattern queries (DuckDB's `duckpgq` extension, per `MATCH` syntax)
  over `edges`.

  This is an implementation requirement, not a behavioral one — it
  constrains *how* the graph is built and traversed, not *what*
  R-IMPACT-001 through R-IMPACT-008 require the answer to be. Rebuilt on
  this engine or not, this component still owes the exact same
  `BlastRadiusReport` for the same inputs; R-IMPACT-006's purity
  requirement is unaffected (DuckDB is embedded and local — no network
  access, no model calls, fully deterministic given the same input
  files) and is, if anything, strengthened: the graph construction and
  traversal steps are now backed by a maintained query engine instead of
  bespoke traversal code written once for this component alone.
documents.requirements/R-IMPACT-010.md:
# R-IMPACT-010

**R-IMPACT-010** — "The prior commit" (`R-IMPACT-002`/`003`/`008`'s own
  phrase) MUST resolve to the merge-base between `HEAD` and the repo's
  default branch — the commit this branch actually diverged from, not
  `HEAD~1` (which is meaningless after more than one commit on the
  branch) and not the default branch's own current tip (which would
  miss changes the default branch picked up after this branch forked).
  Per-file change detection for `R-IMPACT-002`/`003`/`008` MUST be a
  real comparison of each relevant file's content at that commit against
  its current working-tree content — never inferred from the shape or
  format of a `--changed` id alone. This was a real, previously-
  unspecified gap: nothing anywhere in this corpus defined which git
  ref "the prior commit" means, and a real generated candidate, lacking
  anywhere to look it up, implemented no git comparison at all —
  instead attempting to infer interface-vs-internal from `--changed`'s
  own id shape, which can never work since every real caller (every
  `AC-IMPACT-*` criterion, a developer's own `--changed` list) only
  ever supplies component-level ids, never a finer-grained one
  (`D48`).

---
id: comp-license-scanner
title: License Scanner
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-cache-manager]
realizes: [P-COMPLIANCE-GATE]
uses_var: [VAR-COMPLIANCE-WEBHOOK-URL, VAR-LICENSE-CORPUS-PATH]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
---

# License Scanner

## Purpose

Automated, unconditional scan of `gen/<component>/` against a reference
corpus of known-licensed-code fingerprints. No human sign-off is
required to clear a flag — a match blocks the merge the same way a
failed test does — but no result is ever silent: every scan result is
written to the provenance manifest regardless of outcome, and a scan
that had no corpus to compare against says it evaluated nothing rather
than reporting a clean pass.

## Rationale

The original brainstorm established this scan's unconditional, no-sign-off posture.

## Scope

**In scope:** fingerprinting generated code; comparing against the
reference corpus; the merge-blocking decision (confidence-based); the
severity-based notification path (risk-based, orthogonal to confidence —
see the addendum in `notes/initial-ideas.md`); cache-awareness.

**Out of scope:** legal interpretation of a match (explicitly out of scope
for an engineering component); maintaining the reference corpus's
content itself, including its per-entry `risk_tier` classifications
(treated as an external input, versioned via `gate_version` like the
signature database it is — assigning a license family's risk tier is
itself a judgment call made when the reference corpus is curated, not by
this component at scan time).

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

Every criterion is `kind: generated-test`: fingerprint hashing and
threshold comparison are deterministic and need no model, but none is
written in the step-phrase grammar.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

- ~~Exact k-gram window size and the reference-corpus format are
  implementation details not pinned down here~~ — resolved (`R-LICENSE-001`):
  9-token windows; the corpus is precomputed hashes plus metadata, sourced
  from a maintained external reference set, never raw license text and
  never a one-time list frozen into this spec.

## Change log

- Initial draft.
- `D26`: added `notification_delivery_error` to distinguish a webhook
  call that was never due from one that was due and failed to deliver.
- `D51`: new `VAR-LICENSE-CORPUS-PATH` — a real `generate()` candidate
  defaulted the reference corpus's location to `.hotdocs/`, which
  `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` forbids any gate decision from depending on.
  `R-LICENSE-001` now names the real location explicitly.
- `D52`: a second retry, with that fix in place, passed all 8 directly
  testable `AC-LICENSE-*` criteria for real — first successful
  implementation. `gen/license-scanner/license_scanner.py` is now that
  candidate. See `verification/license-scanner/BOOTSTRAP.md`.
- `D163`/`D164`/`D165`: `gate_version`, CLI coverage, test-environment facts.
- `D193`: honest gate — `evaluated`/`reason` on every result; no corpus
  is a visible, non-blocking `not evaluated`; a configured but unusable
  corpus fails closed. `gate_version` is now `license_scanner@4.0.x`.
documents.constraints.md:
# License Scanner — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Determinism.** Same `gen/<component>/` content and the same reference
  corpus version MUST always produce the same `similarity_score` — required
  for cache-key correctness (`notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D13), same as
  every other gate.
- **No model calls.** Pure hashing/comparison logic, same trust tier as
  `spec-linter`, `impact-analyzer`, and `cache-manager`.
- **Never silent.** A clean result is recorded with the same rigor as a
  flagged one, and a flagged-then-retried-clean history is never collapsed
  to the final state (`R-LICENSE-002`/`007`). A scan that checked nothing
  says so (`evaluated: false`), never passes as clean (`R-LICENSE-010`).
- **Fail closed.** A corpus the operator configured but that cannot be
  used blocks (`R-LICENSE-011`); only the absence of any corpus is allowed
  to pass, and it passes visibly.
- **Reference-corpus confidentiality.** The corpus of known-licensed-code
  fingerprints MAY itself be sensitive (e.g. proprietary code samples used
  only as hashes) — this component MUST only ever compare against
  precomputed hashes, never embed or expose the reference corpus's raw
  source in `LicenseScanResult` or logs.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs license-scan <component-id> [--repo-root=<dir>] [--format=json|text]
```

`main(argv)` receives `argv` beginning with `<component-id>` (the
`license-scan` verb is already consumed). Every flag takes its value
either as `--flag=value` or as the next argument; a flag given last
with no value, a missing `<component-id>`, an invalid `--format`, or
an unknown argument is a usage error. `--repo-root` defaults to the
current directory, `--format` to `text`. `--format=json` prints the
`LicenseScanResult` as JSON; `text` prints a human-readable summary
including `similarity_score` and `blocked`, and, when `evaluated` is
`false`, a plain line `NOT EVALUATED: <reason>` with a hint to set
`VAR_LICENSE_CORPUS_PATH` for `no-reference-corpus`.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Not blocked: below the block threshold, or not evaluated for want of any corpus (`NOT EVALUATED: no-reference-corpus`). |
| `1` | Blocked: at or above the block threshold, or a configured corpus that is unreadable or invalid (`R-LICENSE-011`). |
| `2` | Usage error. |
documents.interface/data/LicenseScanResult.md:
# `LicenseScanResult`

```json
{
  "component_id": "comp-foo",
  "gate_version": "license_scanner@4.0.3+9f2c41ab07de",
  "evaluated": true,
  "reason": null,
  "similarity_score": 0.55,
  "block_threshold": 0.70,
  "blocked": false,
  "matches": [
    { "reference_id": "ref-123", "license_family": "gpl-3.0", "risk_tier": "high", "score": 0.55 }
  ],
  "notified": true,
  "notification_delivery_error": null,
  "cache_hit": false
}
```

**`evaluated` and `reason`** (`R-LICENSE-010`): `evaluated` is `true` only
when a usable corpus was compared against. When `false`, `similarity_score`
and `block_threshold` are `null` and `matches` is `[]`, and `reason` is
`"no-reference-corpus"`, `"corpus-unreadable"`, or `"corpus-invalid"`. A
not-evaluated result is a different thing from a clean one, never an
absent-flag clean: any consumer MUST treat `evaluated: false` as "nothing was
checked".

`matches` is non-empty only when `similarity_score` is above a reporting
floor (always populated on a flagged result; may be empty on a clean one).
Each match entry carries its reference's own `license_family` and
`risk_tier`, curated with the reference corpus, not computed here.
`blocked` is `similarity_score >= block_threshold` (confidence only) when
`evaluated` is `true`; when `evaluated` is `false` it is `true` exactly for
`corpus-unreadable` and `corpus-invalid` (`R-LICENSE-011`), `false` for
`no-reference-corpus`.
`notified` is `(blocked) OR (any match's risk_tier == "high")`, **and**
`VAR-COMPLIANCE-WEBHOOK-URL` is configured: deliberately not a function of
`similarity_score` against a second threshold. It reflects whether a
notification was **due**, never whether it was delivered.
`notification_delivery_error` is `{category, message}` or `null`
(`category` one of `network`/`auth`/`timeout`), populated only when
`notified` is `true` and the webhook call failed (`R-LICENSE-003`); it never
affects `blocked`.
documents.interface/data/ReferenceCorpus.md:
# `ReferenceCorpus`

The JSON file `VAR-LICENSE-CORPUS-PATH` names (relative paths resolve
against `repo_root`):

```json
{
  "corpus_version": 3,
  "block_threshold": 0.70,
  "entries": [
    {"reference_id": "ref-001", "license_family": "GPL", "risk_tier": "high",
     "hashes": ["<sha256 hex of one 9-token window>", "..."]}
  ]
}
```

`corpus_version` defaults to `0` and `block_threshold` to `0.70` when
absent.

**Usable, unreadable, invalid** (`R-LICENSE-010`/`011`). *Unset*: the
variable is unset or empty. *Unreadable*: it is set and the file is
missing or cannot be read. *Invalid*: it is read but is not a JSON
object with an `entries` list; or `corpus_version` is present and not a
non-negative integer; or `block_threshold` is present and not a number
greater than 0 and at most 1 (a JSON `true` or `false` is never a valid
number or integer here); or any entry is not an object with a
`hashes` list of strings and a `risk_tier` of `"high"`, `"medium"`, or
`"low"`. *Usable*: none of those, with at least one entry; a configured corpus
with zero entries is invalid, since a gate that was switched on must
never pass by having nothing to compare.

**Window hashing.** Source text is stripped of `/* */`, `"""`, and
`'''` blocks and of `//` and `#` line comments, then tokenized into
identifiers (`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`) and digit runs (`\d+`), each
lowercased. Each run of 9 consecutive tokens, joined by the unit
separator `\x1f`, is hashed as the lowercase SHA-256 hex digest of its
UTF-8 bytes. An entry's score is the share of the component's distinct
window hashes found in that entry's `hashes`; `similarity_score` is
the highest entry score.

**`gate_version`** is `license_scanner@4.0.<corpus_version>+<H>` for a
usable corpus, `<H>` being the first 12 lowercase hex digits of the
SHA-256 of the corpus file's exact bytes, so any change to the corpus
changes the cache key even without a version bump. When the scan is not evaluated it is `license_scanner@4.0.0-<reason>`
(`R-LICENSE-005`): `license_scanner@4.0.0-no-reference-corpus`,
`license_scanner@4.0.0-corpus-unreadable`, or
`license_scanner@4.0.0-corpus-invalid`.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
scan(component_id: str, repo_root: Path) -> LicenseScanResult
gate_version(repo_root: Path) -> str
```

`gate_version` returns exactly the `gate_version` string `scan` would
put on its result for the same `repo_root` and environment, without
scanning anything or touching `cache-manager` (`R-LICENSE-008`).

`scan` loads `cache-manager` from `<repo_root>/gen/cache-manager/`, or from the tool root's when absent (`D199`), and
uses exactly four of its names: `CacheKey(spec_bundle_hash=...,
gate_inputs_hash=..., gate_version=..., model_pin=...)` to build the
key; `get(cache_key, repo_root=...)`; `CachedResult(gate_type="license_scanner",
payload=..., stored_at=...)`, whose `payload` is the `LicenseScanResult`'s
fields as a dict and whose `stored_at` this component computes
itself, as a UTC ISO-8601 string from its own clock; and, after a fresh scan, `put(cache_key,
cached_result, repo_root=...)`. Any stand-in for `cache-manager` must
provide all four, and no other `cache-manager` name is used — not
even a helper such as a timestamp function. A `get` result counts as a hit only if it has a
non-null `payload` (read with dual dict-or-attribute access); anything
else is a miss — never tested against `cache-manager`'s `Miss` type. `cache-manager` being unloadable means no cache
lookup, never a failed scan.
documents.requirements/R-LICENSE-001.md:
# R-LICENSE-001

**R-LICENSE-001** — The scanner MUST compute a similarity score between
  `gen/<component>/`'s content and the reference corpus using k-gram
  (shingle) hashing: normalize source (strip whitespace/comments),
  tokenize, hash overlapping **9-token** windows, and compute the ratio
  of matching window-hashes against the corpus's precomputed hash sets.
  A score at or above the configured **block threshold** MUST block the
  merge the same way a failed test does; no human sign-off can override
  it. Blocking is a pure confidence determination, independent of which
  entry matched or how risky it is (`R-LICENSE-003`).

  **Window size:** 9 tokens — large enough that one shared keyword or
  identifier cannot trigger a match, small enough that a copied passage
  of a few lines still yields many matching windows.

  **Corpus format:** a set of **precomputed k-gram hashes plus
  metadata** (`license_family`, `risk_tier`, a reference id), never raw
  licensed source, sourced from a maintained external reference set and
  never a one-time list frozen into this spec or code.

  **Where the corpus lives** (`D51`): `VAR-LICENSE-CORPUS-PATH`, never
  `.hotdocs/` (gitignored and local-only, `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §1, which
  forbids a gate's pass/fail depending on it). A scan with no usable
  corpus is never reported as a clean pass: `R-LICENSE-010`/`011`.
documents.requirements/R-LICENSE-002.md:
# R-LICENSE-002

**R-LICENSE-002** — Every scan result — clean or flagged, regardless of
  whether it ultimately blocks the merge — MUST be written into the
  provenance manifest's `license_scan` field. A clean result MUST be
  recorded just as faithfully as a flagged one; absence of a flag MUST NOT
  mean absence of a record.
documents.requirements/R-LICENSE-003.md:
# R-LICENSE-003

**R-LICENSE-003** — Each reference-corpus entry MUST carry a declared
  **`risk_tier`** (`high` / `medium` / `low` — reflecting the matched
  entry's license family: e.g. `high` for strong-copyleft or
  unlicensed/proprietary sources, `medium` for weak-copyleft, `low` for
  permissive). A notification to `VAR-COMPLIANCE-WEBHOOK-URL` MUST fire
  when **either** the match blocked the merge (R-LICENSE-001) **or** the
  matched entry's `risk_tier` is `high` — regardless of confidence in the
  latter case. Severity is deliberately **not** a function of the
  similarity score: block answers "are we confident," `risk_tier` answers
  "how bad if real," and conflating the two would both over-notify on
  confident-but-low-risk matches and under-notify on uncertain-but-
  high-risk ones. Notification is independent of the merge outcome,
  including when a later retry (R-LICENSE-007) produces clean code, so an
  auto-resolved flag still gets seen. When `VAR-COMPLIANCE-WEBHOOK-URL` is
  absent, no notification is sent, but the record from R-LICENSE-002 still
  exists regardless.

  The webhook call itself MUST be attempted at most once, with no
  retry-with-backoff — the same bounded-call posture `R-ENDPOINT-004`
  already established for model calls. A failure (network, auth, or
  timeout) MUST be caught and recorded as `notification_delivery_error`
  on the result, never retried, never raised, and never allowed to
  affect `blocked`. `notified` itself is unaffected by delivery outcome
  — it already reflects whether a notification was *due*, computed
  purely from the preconditions above, before any call is attempted;
  whether it was actually delivered is `notification_delivery_error`'s
  job to report.
documents.requirements/R-LICENSE-004.md:
# R-LICENSE-004

**R-LICENSE-004** — Before scanning, the scanner MUST check
  `cache-manager` using key `(spec_bundle_hash, gate_inputs_hash,
  gate_version, model_pin)` — `cache-manager`'s own canonical field
  name (`interface/data/CacheKey.md`), not an informal alias; on a
  cache hit, the cached result MUST be reused and no rescan MUST occur.
documents.requirements/R-LICENSE-005.md:
# R-LICENSE-005

**R-LICENSE-005** — `gate_version` MUST be
  `license_scanner@4.0.<V>+<H>` when the scan was evaluated, `<V>` being
  the reference corpus's `corpus_version` and `<H>` the first 12 hex
  digits of the SHA-256 of its exact bytes, and
  `license_scanner@4.0.0-<reason>` (e.g. `0-no-reference-corpus`) when
  it was not (`R-LICENSE-010`). So a not-evaluated result and an
  evaluated one never share a cache key (`D30`) or a provenance match,
  and any change to the corpus, with or without a version bump,
  invalidates every cached result.
documents.requirements/R-LICENSE-006.md:
# R-LICENSE-006

**R-LICENSE-006** — The scanner MUST produce exactly one structured
  `LicenseScanResult` per component per scan, consumed by
  `provenance-writer` and `review-packet-builder`.
documents.requirements/R-LICENSE-007.md:
# R-LICENSE-007

**R-LICENSE-007** — When a component's flagged attempt blocks a merge
  and a later merge attempt (a human re-running `hotdocs merge` after
  `D3`'s retirement of automatic retry) scans clean, the **original**
  flagged result MUST remain recorded — never overwritten or erased.
  Before `D3`, this held within one merge's own provenance manifest (a
  later best-of-k sample's clean result recorded alongside the original
  flag). A blocked merge now commits nothing at all (`R-MERGE-012`), so
  there is no manifest for the flagged attempt to live in — `D19`'s
  per-attempt record (`.hotdocs/attempts/`) is what preserves it instead.
  "Auto-resolved by retry" still means the merge is no longer blocked; it
  still does not mean the flag never happened.
documents.requirements/R-LICENSE-008.md:
# R-LICENSE-008

**R-LICENSE-008** — `gate_version(repo_root)` MUST return exactly the
  `gate_version` that `scan(component_id, repo_root)` would report, for
  any component, under the same `repo_root` and the same
  `VAR-LICENSE-CORPUS-PATH` value — including when there is no usable
  corpus (`R-LICENSE-005`). It MUST NOT scan any file under `gen/`, call
  `cache-manager`, or write anything. This is how a caller learns the
  scanner's current version without running a scan (`D163`).
documents.requirements/R-LICENSE-009.md:
# R-LICENSE-009

**R-LICENSE-009** — `main(argv)` MUST implement `interface/cli.md`
  exactly: both flag forms, the default `--repo-root` and `--format`,
  JSON and text output, a plain `NOT EVALUATED: <reason>` line in text
  output whenever the result is not evaluated, exit `1` when the result
  is `blocked`, `0` otherwise (so a scan with no corpus exits `0`), and
  `2` for every usage error that document lists (`D162`).
documents.requirements/R-LICENSE-010.md:
# R-LICENSE-010

**R-LICENSE-010** — Every `LicenseScanResult` MUST carry `evaluated`
  (boolean) and `reason`. `evaluated` is `true`, with `reason` `null`,
  only if a usable reference corpus (`interface/data/ReferenceCorpus.md`)
  with at least one entry was loaded and compared against. Otherwise
  `evaluated` is `false`, `similarity_score` and `block_threshold` are
  `null` (never `0.0`: no score was measured), `matches` is `[]`, and
  `reason` is exactly one of `"no-reference-corpus"` (the variable is
  unset or empty),
  `"corpus-unreadable"`, or `"corpus-invalid"` (`R-LICENSE-011`).
  `no-reference-corpus` MUST NOT block: a project with no corpus is
  not stopped, but its result says plainly that nothing was checked
  (`D193`). The webhook payload carries `evaluated` and `reason` too.
documents.requirements/R-LICENSE-011.md:
# R-LICENSE-011

**R-LICENSE-011** — A corpus the operator configured but the scanner
  cannot use MUST fail closed, never degrade silently to
  not-evaluated. If `VAR-LICENSE-CORPUS-PATH` is set and the file is
  missing or cannot be read, `reason` is `"corpus-unreadable"`; if it
  is read but breaks a rule in `interface/data/ReferenceCorpus.md`,
  `reason` is `"corpus-invalid"`. In both cases `evaluated` is `false`
  and `blocked` is `true`: a gate that was switched on and cannot run
  stops the merge. `notified` follows `R-LICENSE-003` unchanged.

id: comp-llm-endpoint
title: LLM Endpoint
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: []
realizes: [P-ZERO-EDIT, P-AMBIGUITY-GATE]
uses_var: [VAR-ANTHROPIC-API-KEY, VAR-OPENAI-API-KEY, VAR-GEMINI-API-KEY, VAR-HOTDOCS-CONFIG]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
