# LLM Endpoint

## Purpose

A single, vendor-agnostic transport for every model call this pipeline
makes — `generator`, `test-author`, `spec-completeness-assistant`, and
the real `judge` callable `merge-orchestrator` wires into
`verifier-orchestrator`/`capability-scenario-verifier` all dispatch through
here instead of each independently knowing how to authenticate to, and
call, a specific vendor's API.

## Rationale

Callers each knew how to reach a vendor until this component took the
mechanics over, so the model identifier stays a plain string everywhere
else (`D18`).

## Scope

**In scope:** every rule in `requirements/`, for the six providers and
the setup helpers `hotdocs init` uses.

**Out of scope:** building or parsing any task's prompt, which each
caller owns, and retrying (`R-ENDPOINT-004`).

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

Mixed `kind`, mirroring `generator`'s own split: the external call itself
is `generated-test` (exercised via an injected mock backend); backend
resolution and credential-safety are pure, deterministic checks,
`compiled`.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

- `ollama` silently truncates a prompt longer than its server's context
  window unless `num_ctx` is passed; no default is set, since a safe
  value depends on the model and the machine (`D182`).

## Change log

Each decision holds its full rationale.

- `D18`, `D33`: first, hand-written implementation through the `claude`
  command. `D34`/`D35`/`D52`: timeout floor, `--tools ""`. `D82`:
  `--safe-mode` without an API key.
- `D180`–`D183`: the six providers, `hotdocs.toml`, setup helpers.
- `D209`, `D220`, `D221`, `D223`, `D224`: the interface stated exactly for
  generation from this spec. `D225`: the `claude` command's whole reply.
documents.constraints.md:
# LLM Endpoint — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Deterministic resolution, not responses.** Resolution
  (`R-ENDPOINT-002`) is a function of the identifier and configuration;
  two identical `complete()` calls MAY return different text, and caching
  that is each caller's concern through `cache-manager`.
- **The one component that reaches the network** for a model call, with
  the standard library only, no retry and a bounded wait
  (`R-ENDPOINT-004`).
- **Credentials stay here** (`R-ENDPOINT-005`): `hotdocs.toml` names a
  variable, never holds a key.
- **The call log is not a gate input.** `.hotdocs/calls/` is read by
  people and tools afterwards, never by a pass/fail decision
  (`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §1).
documents.interface/data/ModelResponse.md:
# `ModelResponse`

```json
{
  "text": "...",
  "model": "anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5",
  "backend": "anthropic",
  "model_call_error": null
}
```

A failed call looks like:

```json
{
  "text": null,
  "model": "claude-sonnet-5",
  "backend": "anthropic",
  "model_call_error": { "category": "rate_limit", "message": "429 from backend" }
}
```

Exactly one of `text` or `model_call_error` is populated, never both and
never neither — mirroring `GenerationResult`'s existing
mutually-exclusive-fields convention rather than inventing a second one
for the same shape of outcome. `model_call_error.category` MUST be one
of `R-ENDPOINT-004`'s four values (`network`/`auth`/`rate_limit`/
`timeout`) — not a bare boolean, so `R-ENDPOINT-006`'s call log can
actually answer "how many failures this month were rate-limits vs. auth
errors," the question a flattened `true`/`false` could never answer
(`D20`). `message` is a short, backend-agnostic description — never the
raw vendor exception text or anything from `R-ENDPOINT-005`'s credential
boundary. `model` is the identifier exactly as the caller passed it, prefix
included (`R-ENDPOINT-002`). `backend` (added by `D20`) is the provider
name (`claude-cli`, `anthropic`, `openai`, `openai-compatible`,
`gemini`, `ollama`; a mock's own name when injected). It is never a
caller *input* — resolution stays internal to a `complete()` call — but
is recorded on the *output*, for the same observability
reason `model_call_error` needs real structure: "which backend is
flaky" is a question only answerable if the fact is captured somewhere.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
complete(prompt: str, model: str, *, backend=None, **params) -> ModelResponse
parse_model(model: str) -> tuple[str | None, str]
resolve_provider(model: str, config: dict | None = None) -> dict
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 600
```

`complete` returns a plain dict with exactly `ModelResponse`'s keys.
`parse_model` splits an identifier into `(provider, model)`, the provider
`None` for a bare name (`R-ENDPOINT-002`). `resolve_provider` returns
`{provider, model, base_url, api_key_env, timeout_seconds}` for an
identifier under `config` (`load_config`'s shape, or `None`), filling a
provider's defaults from `PROVIDERS` and `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`; both
raise `ModelResolutionError` exactly where `R-ENDPOINT-002` says.

Not a pure function: it reaches a network (or the `claude` command).
`model` is `<provider>:<model>` or a bare name (`R-ENDPOINT-002`).
`**params` goes to the resolved backend: the HTTP providers understand
`max_tokens` and `temperature` (`ollama` also `num_ctx`) and ignore the
rest; `claude-cli` turns each into a command-line flag. A rejected
param is the provider's concern, surfaced as `model_call_error`
(`R-ENDPOINT-004`), not validated here.

`backend` (`D33`) — omitted, `complete()` resolves a real backend; a
caller supplying a callable `backend(prompt, model, **params) ->
ModelResponse` bypasses resolution, for testing dispatch,
classification, and logging against a mock, never a real call.

`PROVIDERS` holds exactly (`default_base_url`, `default_api_key_env`,
`suggested_model`): `claude-cli` (none, none, `claude-sonnet-5`),
`anthropic` (`https://api.anthropic.com`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`,
`claude-sonnet-5`), `openai` (`https://api.openai.com/v1`,
`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `gpt-6-astra`), `openai-compatible` (none, none, `""`),
`gemini` (`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`,
`gemini-4-argon`), `ollama` (`http://localhost:11434`, none, `llama3.2`);
`needs_base_url` is true only for `openai-compatible`. None is `None`.

## Setup helpers (`R-ENDPOINT-007`, `R-ENDPOINT-009`)

```
PROVIDERS: dict[str, {default_base_url, default_api_key_env, needs_base_url, suggested_model}]
load_config(config_path: Path | None = None) -> dict | None
save_config(config_path: Path, provider: str, model: str, base_url: str | None = None,
            api_key_env: str | None = None, timeout_seconds: int | None = None) -> None
detect_providers(env: dict | None = None, probe_ollama: bool = True) -> list[dict]
check_connection(provider: str, model: str, base_url: str | None = None,
                 api_key_env: str | None = None, timeout_seconds: int = 30) -> dict
```

`load_config` returns `{provider, model, base_url, api_key_env,
timeout_seconds}` (unset entries `None`), or `None`; it raises
`ValueError` for an invalid file. `save_config` creates the file's
directory when missing and replaces only its `[llm]` table.
`detect_providers` returns, per
provider, `{provider, available, reason, suggested_model,
api_key_env}`; given `env`, only that dict supplies keys and `PATH`.
`check_connection` sends one prompt, with `max_tokens=1024` except to
`claude-cli`, and returns `{ok, error}`, `error` being `None` or
`{category, message}`; an unknown provider, or `openai-compatible`
without a `base_url`, raises `ValueError`. `ModelResolutionError` is
raised by `complete()` for `R-ENDPOINT-002`'s failures.
`resolve_backend_name(model)` is kept only for compatibility: it returns
`"anthropic"` for a bare `claude-*` name, the label the `claude`
command's backend had before there were several providers.

## HTTP, the call log, and config messages

Discovery reads `VAR_HOTDOCS_CONFIG` and the current directory; a
resolution test unsets the one and uses a fresh other.

Every HTTP request, the Ollama probe included, is
`urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=<seconds>)`, looked up on the
`urllib.request` module when the call is made (never imported by name,
so replacing `urllib.request.urlopen` reaches every call). The reply is
used only as a context manager and through `.read()`. Headers go into
`urllib.request.Request`, which stores names capitalized (`X-api-key`, `User-agent`),
so a recorded request's headers are read case-insensitively. An error status
arrives as `urllib.error.HTTPError` (its `code` and `read()`), a timeout
as `socket.timeout`, `TimeoutError` or a `URLError` wrapping one, and any
other failure as `URLError` or `OSError`. The Ollama probe requests
`<base_url>/api/tags` with a 1-second timeout and counts as available
whenever `urlopen` returns.

Each `complete()` call writes one JSON file under `.hotdocs/calls/` in
the current directory: `{"timestamp", "model", "backend", "text_present"}`
on success, `text_present` a boolean, or `{"timestamp", "model",
"backend", "model_call_error"}` on failure; `timestamp` is ISO 8601 UTC.

`complete()` raises `ModelResolutionError`, never `ValueError`, for an
invalid `hotdocs.toml`, and nothing else: an exception an injected
`backend` raises is returned as `model_call_error`, classified as HTTP
failures are (`HTTPError` 401 or 403 `auth`, 429 `rate_limit`, 408 or
504 or any timeout `timeout`, anything else `network`), with `text`
`null` and no retry. `load_config`'s message for an entry whose name
suggests a secret contains `must never hold a secret`; every refusal of an
`api_key_env` value contains `never the key itself`.
documents.requirements/R-ENDPOINT-001.md:
# R-ENDPOINT-001

**R-ENDPOINT-001** — MUST expose exactly one entry point,
  `complete(prompt, model, **params) -> ModelResponse`, given an explicit
  model identifier as a required parameter — never hardcoded to a
  canonical pin, never defaulted to a specific vendor. A caller supplies
  the prompt text and which model to use; this component owns everything
  between that call and a response coming back.
documents.requirements/R-ENDPOINT-002.md:
# R-ENDPOINT-002

**R-ENDPOINT-002** — MUST resolve a model identifier to a provider
  internally. A caller names a model and nothing else, apart from the
  optional `hotdocs.toml` (`R-ENDPOINT-007`). An identifier is
  `<provider>:<model>` — the prefix counts only when it is one of
  `R-ENDPOINT-003`'s provider names, so `llama3.1:8b` is a bare name and
  `ollama:llama3.1:8b` is not — or a bare name. A bare name uses the
  provider `hotdocs.toml` configures; with no configuration, a bare name
  beginning `claude-` uses `claude-cli` and any other fails. A prefix
  naming a provider other than the configured one uses that provider's
  defaults.

  An identifier that resolves to no usable provider — an unconfigured
  non-`claude-` name, a prefix with no model after it, `openai-compatible`
  with no `base_url`, or an invalid configuration — MUST fail
  immediately with a specific usage error (`ModelResolutionError`):
  never a silent fallback to whichever provider happens to be
  configured, and never conflated with `model_call_error`
  (`R-ENDPOINT-004`), and raised before any call.

  The provider receives only the part after the prefix, but the
  returned `ModelResponse.model` MUST be the identifier exactly as the
  caller passed it, as callers record it in provenance.
documents.requirements/R-ENDPOINT-003.md:
# R-ENDPOINT-003

**R-ENDPOINT-003** — MUST implement exactly these providers, each as an
  adapter behind `R-ENDPOINT-002`'s resolve/dispatch split: `claude-cli`
  (the `claude` command), `anthropic` (Messages API), `openai` (Chat
  Completions), `openai-compatible` (the same wire format at a required
  `base_url`, covering OpenLLM, vLLM, LM Studio, LiteLLM, OpenRouter and
  similar servers), `gemini` (`generateContent`), and `ollama`. The HTTP
  providers use the Python standard library only, adding no dependency.
  A further provider is one more adapter and `PROVIDERS` entry, never a
  plugin or registry, and never a change to `complete()`
  (`R-ENDPOINT-001`) or any caller.

  **When `claude-cli` dispatches via the `claude` command's
  non-interactive mode (`D33`), it MUST pass `--tools ""` on every call**
  (`D35`), or the command keeps its tools. **It MUST also pass `--bare`
  when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, or `--safe-mode` when it is not**
  (`D82`), since `--bare` refuses a subscription login. It MUST NOT check for a credential and refuse
  early; it dispatches and classifies what the command reports
  (`R-ENDPOINT-004`).

  **It MUST pass `--output-format stream-json --verbose`, and the reply
  is every text block of every `assistant` message, in order, joined with
  nothing between them** (`D225`): a long reply spans several messages,
  and plain output keeps only the last. A `result` line with `is_error`
  true is a failure; output that is not that stream is the reply
  unchanged, never stripped.
documents.requirements/R-ENDPOINT-004.md:
# R-ENDPOINT-004

**R-ENDPOINT-004** — MUST NOT retry a provider call, and MUST NOT leave
  one with an unbounded wait (`D7`/`R-GEN-011`, owned here at the layer
  that touches the network). A call either succeeds, or fails within
  its provider's bounded timeout as a `model_call_error` with a
  `category` of exactly one of `network`/`auth`/`rate_limit`/`timeout`
  (`D20`; see `ModelResponse`), exactly once.

  **The bound MUST be at least 300 seconds** (`D34`) for a completion:
  a 120-second bound timed out `generator`'s larger bundle. Default 600;
  `timeout_seconds` in `hotdocs.toml` MAY raise it, never lower it below
  300. `check_connection` (`R-ENDPOINT-009`) is a probe, not a
  completion, and takes its own short bound.

  **HTTP providers** map a reply to a category: 401 or 403 `auth`; 429
  `rate_limit`; 408 or 504, and a socket timeout, `timeout`; any other
  non-2xx status, a connection failure, an unreadable body, or a reply
  with no text, `network`. `gemini` also maps a 400 whose body says the
  API key is not valid to `auth`. The `message` is a short static
  description: never the vendor's text, a header, or a credential
  (`R-ENDPOINT-005`). A provider that needs a key and finds none in the
  environment reports `auth` without making a call.
documents.requirements/R-ENDPOINT-005.md:
# R-ENDPOINT-005

**R-ENDPOINT-005** — A provider credential MUST never appear in a
  `ModelResponse`, a log line, an error message, a URL, or
  `hotdocs.toml`; only the model identifier is ever recorded. A key is
  read only from the process environment variable `hotdocs.toml`'s
  `api_key_env` names, else the provider's standard one
  (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`: each vendor's
  own name, not `VAR_<NAME>`). `claude-cli` reads none itself. The
  credential never reaches any caller (`generator`, `test-author`,
  `spec-completeness-assistant`, `component-gate-runner`'s and
  `capability-scenario-verifier`'s `judge` wiring), so it is structurally
  unable to leak from any of them: a stronger guarantee than "must not
  appear in output".

  For `anthropic`, `openai` and `gemini` a missing key MUST be an `auth`
  `model_call_error` returned without any network call, its message
  naming the missing variable;
  `openai-compatible` and `ollama` send a key only when one is present.
documents.requirements/R-ENDPOINT-006.md:
# R-ENDPOINT-006

**R-ENDPOINT-006** — Every `complete()` call MUST write one record to
  `.hotdocs/calls/` (gitignored, local-only, non-gating —
  `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §1, same posture `provenance-tracker`'s
  `.hotdocs/attempts/` already has) — success or failure, before
  returning to the caller. The record MUST carry: a timestamp, `model`,
  `backend`, and either `text`'s presence (not its content — this is a
  transport-level log, not a copy of every prompt/response) or the full
  `model_call_error` object.

  This is deliberately a different, lower-level record than anything a
  caller (`generator`, `test-author`, `component-gate-runner`'s `judge`
  wiring) separately persists about its own attempt — `D19`. This one
  is caller-agnostic: it answers "how many calls, to which backend, with
  what error rate" across the whole pipeline, independent of which
  component's semantics any individual call served. Writing it here,
  once, is what `D18` already made this component the right place for —
  every model call already passes through here regardless of caller.
documents.requirements/R-ENDPOINT-007.md:
# R-ENDPOINT-007

**R-ENDPOINT-007** — Provider choice MAY be configured in a committed
  `hotdocs.toml`, which MUST never hold a secret. Its one table is:

  ```toml
  [llm]
  provider = "openai"            # required: a name from R-ENDPOINT-003
  model = "gpt-6-astra"          # required: the model setup chose
  base_url = ""                  # optional http(s) URL; required for openai-compatible
  api_key_env = "OPENAI_API_KEY" # optional: the NAME of the variable
  timeout_seconds = 600          # optional; at least 300
  ```

  Discovery: the file `VAR-HOTDOCS-CONFIG` names (a missing file is an
  error), else `hotdocs.toml` in the current directory, else none.
  `load_config` returns the validated table, `None` when there is no file or
  it has no `[llm]` table,
  and raises `ValueError` naming the problem otherwise. An unknown entry
  is invalid; an entry whose name suggests a secret (`api_key`, `token`,
  `password`...) is rejected with a message saying so. `api_key_env`
  MUST be a variable name: a value that fits the name pattern but equals
  some environment variable's value is a pasted key and is rejected.
  `claude-cli` takes no `base_url` or `api_key_env`.
documents.requirements/R-ENDPOINT-008.md:
# R-ENDPOINT-008

**R-ENDPOINT-008** — Each HTTP adapter MUST speak its provider's
  documented wire format, confirmed against that provider's current
  public documentation (`D180`), with a descriptive `User-Agent`. The
  caller's `max_tokens` and `temperature` params are understood;
  `ollama` also takes `num_ctx`; other params are ignored.

  | provider | request | auth | answer |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `anthropic` | `POST {base}/v1/messages`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, `max_tokens` always sent (default 32000) | `x-api-key` | the `text` blocks of `content`, joined (thinking blocks may precede them) |
  | `openai` | `POST {base}/chat/completions`, `max_completion_tokens` | `Authorization: Bearer` | `choices[0].message.content` |
  | `openai-compatible` | as `openai`, `max_tokens` | Bearer, only if a key is configured | as `openai` |
  | `gemini` | `POST {base}/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`, `generationConfig.maxOutputTokens` | `x-goog-api-key` header, never the URL | the non-`thought` text parts of `candidates[0].content` |
  | `ollama` | `POST {base}/api/chat`, `stream` false, `options.num_predict` | none (Bearer if a key is configured) | `message.content` |

  Default bases: `https://api.anthropic.com`,
  `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com`,
  `http://localhost:11434`. A `gemini` model written `models/<name>` is
  sent as `<name>`. An `openai-compatible` `base_url` includes
  its version prefix (e.g. `http://localhost:8000/v1`).
documents.requirements/R-ENDPOINT-009.md:
# R-ENDPOINT-009

**R-ENDPOINT-009** — MUST expose the setup helpers `hotdocs init` builds
  on, all in `interface/library.md`: `PROVIDERS` (per provider
  `default_base_url`, `default_api_key_env`, `needs_base_url`,
  `suggested_model`; the suggestion is a hint, never applied by
  `complete()`); `save_config`, which validates exactly as
  `load_config` does, refuses an unknown provider or anything that looks
  like a secret, writes nothing then, keeps any other content of an
  existing file, and writes no secret; `detect_providers`, one entry per
  provider saying whether it looks usable now (`claude` on `PATH`, a
  non-blank key variable, an Ollama server answering within about a
  second), reading only the `env` it is given; and `check_connection`,
  one tiny real completion reporting `{ok, error}` with the same
  `error` shape as `model_call_error`, never logged as a pipeline call,
  never echoing a key.

documents.component.md:
---
id: comp-provenance-checker
title: Provenance Checker
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-spec-bundle-assembler, comp-criterion-compiler, comp-test-author, comp-verifier-orchestrator, comp-license-scanner, comp-secret-scanner, comp-provenance-writer]
realizes: [P-ZERO-EDIT]
uses_var: [VAR-TRUST-JUDGE-PROVENANCE]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
---

# Provenance Checker

## Purpose

Decides whether a component's already-committed `.provenance.json`
proves it was already verified against the exact spec state a merge is
currently checking — so `component-gate-runner` can safely skip
regeneration and re-verification for that component.

## Rationale

This is the mechanism behind the original claim that a merge whose spec
state exactly matches an already-verified prior state can skip
regeneration and re-verification entirely. That claim was previously
implemented (`D29`) by asking `cache-manager` a question its own data
could never answer: `cache-manager` records that a candidate was
*produced*, not that it was ever *verified* — `verifier-orchestrator`
never writes to it. A candidate that failed verification gets cached
under the same key as one that passed, with nothing distinguishing them
on a later `get`. `.provenance.json` doesn't have this problem: it is
written only by `provenance-writer`, only from `verifier-orchestrator`'s
real output (`R-PROV-005`), and only ever reaches a component's
committed directory because `R-MERGE-011` already blocked the commit
otherwise — the same discipline that makes `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §7 call
it an SBOM/SLSA-style attestation. The fact a matching one exists on
disk, for the exact current `spec_bundle_hash`, *is* the proof — no
separate store, no new cryptography, nothing `cache-manager` needs to
change.

## Scope

**In scope:** reading a component's committed `gen/<component>/
.provenance.json`, comparing its `spec_bundle_hash` and `gate_versions`
against the caller-supplied current ones (defined once, by
`current_provenance_key`), and — when they match —
deciding whether to honor that match given
`VAR-TRUST-JUDGE-PROVENANCE` and whether the embedded
`verification_report` includes any `llm-judge`-kind criterion.

Also, for a sealed component (`D170`): computing its current key — owners,
a hash of its source, the verifier version — and deciding whether its
sealed provenance manifest (`provenance-writer`'s schema) is valid and
current.

**Out of scope:** computing the current `spec_bundle_hash`
(`spec-bundle-assembler`'s job); writing or modifying `.provenance.json`
(`provenance-writer`'s job); deciding whether a *candidate* should be
regenerated to avoid a redundant model call — that's `cache-manager`'s
narrower, still-unchanged job, answering a different question
("has this exact work already been done") from the one this component
answers ("has this exact work already been proven correct").

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

Every criterion is `kind: generated-test` (`D43`) — reading a committed
file, comparing a hash, and reading one boolean var is pure,
deterministic logic that needs no model or judgment, but none of this
component's criteria are actually written in `specs/architecture/
step-phrase-grammar.md`'s fixed step vocabulary, so `kind: compiled`
would not describe how they're really verified.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- Initial draft (`D29`).
- `D47`: first real implementation, via three real `generate()`
  retries (the first two found real, corpus-wide gaps — `D45`'s
  `component_id`-to-slug mapping, `D46`'s output-layout requirement —
  fixed in `generator`/`glossary.md`, not here). `gen/provenance-
  checker/` is now a real top-level package. See `verification/
  provenance-checker/BOOTSTRAP.md` for the full account.
- `D163`: gains `current_provenance_key`, the one definition of the
  `spec_bundle_hash`/`gate_versions` a hit compares, so the writer of
  `.provenance.json` and every checker of it agree. `R-PROVCHECK-006`
  covers the CLI (`D162`), whose hash validation rejected every real
  `sha256:`-prefixed hash.
- `D170`: `current_sealed_key`/`check_sealed_provenance` — the sealed
  counterpart (`R-PROVCHECK-007`/`008`); depends on `provenance-writer`
  for the manifest schema.
  Regenerated and landed at 13/13, `mutation_score` 0.91.
documents.constraints.md:
# Provenance Checker — Non-Functional Constraints

- **No network access, no model calls.** Pure local file I/O plus one
  var read — same trust tier as `provenance-writer`.
- **Read-only.** Never writes, modifies, or deletes `.provenance.json`
  or any other file (`R-PROVCHECK-004`).
- **Determinism.** Given the same working-tree content, the same
  supplied `spec_bundle_hash`, and the same `VAR-TRUST-JUDGE-PROVENANCE`
  value, the result MUST be byte-identical.
- **Never a cache-manager client.** This component answers a different
  question ("was this proven correct") from `cache-manager`'s ("has
  this work already been done") and MUST NOT call `cache-manager` to
  answer it — conflating the two is the exact gap this component exists
  to close.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs provenance check <component-id> --spec-bundle-hash=<h> --gate-versions=<json> [--repo-root=<dir>] [--format=json|text]
```

Reports hit/miss for the given component and hash, same shape and
intent as `cache-manager`'s own `hotdocs cache inspect` — a developer
debugging why a component did or didn't skip regeneration can check
this directly.

`main(argv)` receives `argv` beginning `["check", ...]` (the
`provenance` verb is already consumed). Every flag takes its value
either as `--flag=value` or as the next argument. `--gate-versions` is
a JSON object of strings. `--repo-root` defaults to the current
directory, `--format` to `text`. `--format=json` prints the
`ProvenanceCheckResult` as JSON; `text` prints `hit` or `miss` and the
component id. A missing `<component-id>`, `--spec-bundle-hash`, or
`--gate-versions`; a `<component-id>` not of the form `comp-<slug>`
or `<slug>` (lowercase letters, digits, single hyphens); a
`--spec-bundle-hash` not of the form `sha256:` followed by one or more
lowercase hex digits; `--gate-versions` that is not a JSON object of
strings to strings; an
invalid `--format`; an unknown argument or subcommand; or a flag given
last with no value is a usage error.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Command completed (a reported "miss" is still exit `0` — it's an answer, not a failure). |
| `2` | Usage error. |
documents.interface/data/ProvenanceCheckResult.md:
# `ProvenanceCheckResult`

```json
{
  "hit": true,
  "verification_report": { "...": "a VerificationReport" },
  "license_scan": { "...": "a LicenseScanResult" },
  "secret_scan": { "...": "a SecretScanResult" }
}
```

`verification_report`/`license_scan`/`secret_scan` are populated only
when `hit` is `true` — `null` on a miss, never a partial or
best-guess value (`R-PROVCHECK-003`). On a hit, all three are the
matching `.provenance.json`'s own fields, copied verbatim — this
component never recomputes or summarizes them.
documents.interface/data/ProvenanceKey.md:
# `ProvenanceKey`

```json
{
  "spec_bundle_hash": "sha256:...",
  "gate_versions": {
    "compiler": "criterion-compiler@1.0.0",
    "generated_test": "generated_test@1.0.0",
    "verifier": "verifier-orchestrator@2.0.0",
    "license_scanner": "license_scanner@4.0.3+9f2c41ab07de",
    "secret_scanner": "secret_scanner@0.0.0"
  }
}
```

`gate_versions` has exactly these five keys, each value copied
unchanged from the gate it names (`R-PROVCHECK-005`). Returned as an
object exposing both fields as attributes.
documents.interface/data/SealedCheckResult.md:
# `SealedCheckResult`

```json
{
  "hit": true,
  "sealed": true,
  "reason": null,
  "verification_report": { "overall": "pass" },
  "license_scan": null,
  "secret_scan": null,
  "owners": ["pipeline-team"],
  "source_hash": "sha256:...",
  "written_at": "2026-11-02T00:00:00Z"
}
```

Returned as a dict (`R-PROVCHECK-008`). `sealed` is `false` only when
`reason` is `not_sealed`, `true` otherwise. `hit` is `true` exactly when
`reason` is `null`; otherwise `reason` is one of `not_sealed`,
`manifest_missing`, `manifest_invalid`, `component_mismatch`,
`source_changed`, `owners_changed`, `verifier_changed`, or
`characterization_failed`. `verification_report`, `owners`,
`source_hash`, and `written_at` are copied from the manifest only when
`hit` is `true` (`verification_report` holds only `overall`, taken from
`characterization.overall`) and are `null` on every miss: nothing is
taken from a manifest that is not a current, passing hit, so a stale one
never feeds a readiness result. `license_scan` and
`secret_scan` are always `null`: a sealed component's readiness rests on
its characterization run alone. The shape mirrors `ProvenanceCheckResult`
so a reader of `hit` and `verification_report.overall` needs no
special case.
documents.interface/data/SealedKey.md:
# `SealedKey`

```json
{
  "owners": ["pipeline-team"],
  "source_path": "pipeline/criterion-compiler/",
  "source_hash": "sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "verifier_version": "verifier-orchestrator@2.0.0"
}
```

Returned as an object exposing the four fields as attributes
(`R-PROVCHECK-007`). `owners` and `source_path` are copied from the
component's `component.md` frontmatter; `source_hash` and
`verifier_version` are computed or read as that requirement states.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
check_provenance(component_id: str, spec_bundle_hash: str, gate_versions: dict[str, str], repo_root: Path) -> ProvenanceCheckResult
current_provenance_key(component_id: str, repo_root: Path) -> ProvenanceKey
current_sealed_key(component_id: str, repo_root: Path) -> SealedKey | None
check_sealed_provenance(component_id: str, repo_root: Path) -> SealedCheckResult
```

`check_provenance` is a pure function of the working tree's current
state plus `VAR-TRUST-JUDGE-PROVENANCE` — no network access, no model
call.

`current_provenance_key` is the one definition of the values a caller
passes to `check_provenance`, and that `component-gate-runner` passes
to `provenance-writer` (`R-PROVCHECK-005`, `D163`). It loads each
dependency from `<repo_root>/gen/<slug>/`, or for the sealed
`criterion-compiler` from its `source_path`, `pipeline/criterion-compiler/`, each, or from the tool root's when absent (`D199`),
and reads, in this order:

1. `spec-bundle-assembler`'s `assemble(component_id, repo_root=...,
   mode="cold")`, taking only its `spec_bundle_hash`
2. `criterion-compiler`'s `GATE_VERSION`
3. `test-author`'s `GATE_VERSION`
4. `verifier-orchestrator`'s `GATE_VERSION`
5. `license-scanner`'s `gate_version(repo_root)`
6. `secret-scanner`'s `gate_version(repo_root)`

Any stand-in for these dependencies must provide each name this list
gives. No network access, no model call, no write.

## Sealed components (`D170`)

`current_sealed_key` is also the one test of whether a component is
sealed: it returns `None` for a component that is not (`R-PROVCHECK-007`).
Callers (`component-gate-runner`, `provenance-tracker`) route on it
rather than reading `component.md` themselves. It reads
`<repo_root>/specs/components/<slug>/component.md` and, for
`verifier_version`, `verifier-orchestrator`'s `GATE_VERSION` from
`<repo_root>/gen/verifier-orchestrator/`. `check_sealed_provenance`
reads the sealed manifest (`provenance-writer`'s
`interface/data/SealedProvenance.md`) and compares it to the current
key (`R-PROVCHECK-008`). Both are read-only and make no network or
model call. Any stand-in for `verifier-orchestrator` provides
`GATE_VERSION`.
documents.requirements/R-PROVCHECK-001.md:
# R-PROVCHECK-001

**R-PROVCHECK-001** — Given a component id, its current
  `spec_bundle_hash`, the current `gate_versions` map, and a repo root,
  MUST read `gen/<component>/.provenance.json` as it currently sits in
  the working tree (not from any store), and compare both its own
  `spec_bundle_hash` field and every entry of its own `gate_versions`
  map against the supplied ones — a hit requires every value to match
  exactly, not just `spec_bundle_hash`. `check_provenance` never computes
  either value itself — both are always caller-supplied, obtained from
  `current_provenance_key` (`R-PROVCHECK-005`), the same
  "gate version is part of the key, not metadata checked after" rule
  `R-CACHE-005` already established for a different store, applied
  here for the same reason: a stale manifest must not paper over a
  gate's own detection logic having since improved.
documents.requirements/R-PROVCHECK-002.md:
# R-PROVCHECK-002

**R-PROVCHECK-002** — On a `spec_bundle_hash` match, MUST report a hit
  — returning the matching manifest's `verification_report`,
  `license_scan`, and `secret_scan` verbatim, never recomputed or
  summarized — **unless** the embedded `verification_report.criteria[]`
  contains an `llm-judge`-kind entry **and** `VAR-TRUST-JUDGE-PROVENANCE`
  resolves to `false`, in which case this is R-PROVCHECK-003's job
  instead. A hash match for a component whose acceptance set has no
  `llm-judge`-kind criterion at all is always honored as a hit,
  unconditionally — the variable only ever governs the one criterion
  kind that cannot be cheaply re-derived.
documents.requirements/R-PROVCHECK-003.md:
# R-PROVCHECK-003

**R-PROVCHECK-003** — MUST report a definitive miss — never a partial
  or approximate result — when `gen/<component>/.provenance.json` is
  absent, when its `spec_bundle_hash` or any `gate_versions` entry does
  not match the supplied ones, or when they match but R-PROVCHECK-002's
  `llm-judge`/
  `VAR-TRUST-JUDGE-PROVENANCE` exception applies. A miss here always
  means the caller MUST run the full generation/verification/scan
  sequence for that component — there is no partial-credit result that
  trusts some of a manifest's fields while re-deriving others; the one
  piece of nuance that kind of split would require (which specific
  criteria to trust) is exactly the complexity this component is
  deliberately not taking on, per D4/D6's precedent against building
  machinery nothing has asked for yet.
documents.requirements/R-PROVCHECK-004.md:
# R-PROVCHECK-004

**R-PROVCHECK-004** — MUST be read-only: MUST NOT write, modify, or
  delete `.provenance.json` or any other file. Mirrors `cache-manager`'s
  own `get`-side discipline (`R-CACHE-001`), applied here to committed
  repository content instead of a cache store.
documents.requirements/R-PROVCHECK-005.md:
# R-PROVCHECK-005

**R-PROVCHECK-005** — `current_provenance_key(component_id, repo_root)`
  MUST return a `ProvenanceKey` whose `spec_bundle_hash` is exactly
  `spec-bundle-assembler`'s cold-mode bundle hash for that component,
  and whose `gate_versions` maps exactly `compiler`, `generated_test`,
  `verifier`, `license_scanner`, and `secret_scanner` to the values
  `interface/library.md` names, unchanged. It MUST NOT run any scan,
  generation, or verification, and MUST NOT write anything. A
  dependency that cannot be loaded, or an exception from
  `assemble`, propagates to the caller unchanged — never a guessed or
  empty key, which would make every check a miss without saying why
  (`D163`).

documents.requirements/R-PROVCHECK-007.md:
# R-PROVCHECK-007

**R-PROVCHECK-007** — `current_sealed_key(component_id, repo_root)` MUST
  return `None` unless `<repo_root>/specs/components/<slug>/component.md`
  exists and its frontmatter has the line `sealed: true`. Otherwise it
  MUST return a `SealedKey` (`interface/data/SealedKey.md`):

  - `owners` and `source_path` read from the frontmatter lines
    `owners: [a, b]` and `source_path: <path>`, each a single line;
    either missing, or failing `provenance-writer`'s
    `interface/data/SealedProvenance.md` rules for that field, raises
    `ValueError`;
  - `source_hash` is `"sha256:"` plus the SHA-256 over every file under
    `<repo_root>/<source_path>`, recursively, except any directory named
    `__pycache__` and any file named `.sealed-provenance.json`, taken in
    sorted order of posix path relative to `source_path`, feeding each
    file's relative path as UTF-8, a NUL byte, the file's bytes, and a
    NUL byte. A missing directory hashes as no files;
  - `verifier_version` is `verifier-orchestrator`'s `GATE_VERSION`.

  It MUST NOT write anything. This is the one definition of a sealed
  component's key, as `current_provenance_key` is of a generated
  component's (`D163`, `D170`).

documents.component.md:
---
id: comp-provenance-tracker
title: Provenance Tracker
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-provenance-checker, comp-impact-analyzer, comp-capability-scenario-verifier]
realizes: [P-MERGE-VISIBILITY]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
---

# Provenance Tracker

## Purpose

Answers "would a merge pass right now" (`hotdocs verify`) by checking
every component's current provenance and checking-then-running every
intersecting capability's scenarios, across a scope — a blast radius or
the whole corpus — and reports one ready/not-ready verdict with
per-item detail. Also keeps a durable, local-only history of `hotdocs
generate` attempts (`AttemptRecord`) so a developer can see why a
component's provenance check is currently failing.

## Rationale

(`D88`, renamed from `merge-tracker`.) `merge-orchestrator`'s removal
(`D87`) left nothing that still needed a per-merge-attempt log —
`TrackingRecord` existed specifically to record outcomes of an
automated action that no longer exists. What a developer actually
needs is different: a live answer to "is everything ready," not a
history of past attempts at something no component does automatically
anymore. The per-component attempt history (`AttemptRecord`) is kept —
a developer running `hotdocs generate` still benefits from seeing why a
prior attempt failed, same as always.

`D92` briefly combined `hotdocs generate`/`check-capability`/`verify`
into one `hotdocs build` command, reasoning that this component
already had to compute whether provenance was current for every item
in scope — the only thing missing was acting on a miss. `D93` reversed
the component half of that: a developer genuinely wants `generate` and
`verify` as independently runnable commands, since generating new code
is a deliberate, potentially expensive action that `verify` should
never spring as a side effect. The capability half of `D92`'s
reasoning stands, unreversed: `verify` still checks-then-runs
`capability-scenario-verifier`'s own gauntlet for every intersecting
capability, since capability-scenario verification never produces new
source code, only exercises what already exists — triggering it from
`verify` costs a developer nothing they wouldn't expect. `D93` also
removes the dependency cycle `D92` introduced: this component no
longer calls `component-gate-runner` for anything, so
`component-gate-runner` can safely depend on this component again (to
call `write_attempt_record`) without creating a two-node cycle.

## Scope

**In scope:** for a given scope (`changed_ids`, via `impact-analyzer`,
or the whole corpus), checking `provenance-checker` for every component
— a pure, read-only check, never triggering generation (`R-TRACK-009`,
`D93`) — and checking-then-running `capability-scenario-verifier`'s
`run_capability_gates` for every intersecting capability (`R-TRACK-010`,
unreversed by `D93`), then reporting one `ready` verdict plus per-item
detail; writing one `AttemptRecord` per `hotdocs generate` attempt,
taken as direct parameters from `component-gate-runner`
(`R-TRACK-004`/`007`); exposing `last_requirement_failures` as a pure,
read-only convenience over that history (`R-TRACK-008`).

**Out of scope:** deciding whether a merge *should* proceed — nothing
gates on this component's output (`D87`; a human reads `hotdocs
verify`'s verdict and decides); triggering component generation on a
miss — that is `hotdocs generate`'s own job, by name, never a side
effect of checking readiness (`D93`); re-deriving `provenance-checker`'s
or `capability-scenario-verifier`'s own hit/miss logic — this component
calls their real functions, never re-implements them against raw
`.provenance.json`/capability-provenance files itself.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

All criteria are `kind: compiled` — sequencing already-defined calls and
assembling their results into one report is pure, deterministic logic;
nothing here needs a model or judgment itself (the components it calls
may make model calls internally, but that is their own concern, not
this one's).

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

See the decisions, `D25` onward; `D292` makes usage errors print their reason.
documents.constraints.md:
# Provenance Tracker — Non-Functional Constraints

- **No network access, no model calls for the component half of
  `check_readiness`.** The component check reuses `provenance-checker`'s
  own deterministic logic and never calls `component-gate-runner`
  (`D93`). The capability half may make real model calls, through
  `capability-scenario-verifier`'s `run_capability_gates`, on a
  capability miss — that cost is `capability-scenario-verifier`'s own,
  incurred inside its own real function call, not this component's.
- **Never an automated gate input.** `hotdocs verify` answers a
  question; no component's own pass/fail decision reads this
  component's output, and nothing programmatically enforces that a
  developer ran it before committing (`D87`). It is nonetheless a
  stated workflow MUST, not merely optional, that a developer run it
  — over the full blast radius of whatever was just regenerated, not
  just the one component in isolation — before committing (`D99`);
  this component enforces none of that itself, the same absence of
  automation `D87` already describes.
- **`AttemptRecord` is append-only, never mutated.** Once written, it
  MUST NOT be edited or deleted by this component — history is the
  entire value of this data.
- **Determinism of assembly, not of the capability half's side
  effects.** Given the same mocked `ProvenanceCheckResult`/
  `CapabilityProvenanceCheckResult` values for a scope,
  `check_readiness`'s own `VerifyReport` assembly MUST be
  byte-identical — a claim about this component's own aggregation
  logic, not a claim that two real `hotdocs verify` runs against a
  changing corpus, or against a capability that gets re-run, produce
  identical reports.
- **No retention/eviction policy specified here.** `.hotdocs/attempts/`
  growing without bound over a long-lived local checkout is a real,
  known cost — deliberately left unaddressed in this version, the same
  posture `cache-manager`'s own eviction-policy open question already
  has. Local, gitignored, disposable data a developer can delete at any
  time with no correctness consequence.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs verify [--changed=<spec-id>...] [--model=<model-id>] [--seed=<n>] \
  [--repo-root=<dir>] [--format=json|text]
hotdocs track feedback <component-id> [--repo-root=<dir>]
```

`main(argv)` receives `argv` beginning `["verify", ...]` or `["track",
"feedback", ...]`; every flag takes its value as `--flag=value` or as the
next argument, and `--changed` may repeat. `main` calls `check_readiness`
and `last_requirement_failures` through this module's own global names,
so a test may replace them.

`hotdocs verify` (`R-TRACK-009`/`010`, `D88`/`D93`) answers "will a merge
pass": without `--changed` it checks the whole corpus, with it that blast
radius. Components are only checked against `provenance-checker`,
read-only, never triggering `component-gate-runner` (`D93`); intersecting
capabilities are checked-then-run against `capability-scenario-verifier`
(`D89`/`D92`). `--model` is needed only when a capability needs a fresh
run. `--format=text` (default) prints `ready` or `not ready` and then each
`not_ready_reasons` entry on its own line; `--format=json` prints the
result as JSON, converted as `R-TRACK-007` converts its inputs. Nothing requires running it before a commit (`D87`).

`track feedback` (`R-TRACK-008`, `D3`) prints the named component's most
recent failing `R-id`s, comma-separated, ready for `hotdocs generate
<component-id> --retry-feedback=...` (`D86`/`D93`), or nothing if no
failed attempt exists.

There is no `hotdocs track write`: `component-gate-runner` calls
`write_attempt_record` directly.

**Exit codes (`hotdocs verify`):**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Ready — every item in scope has current, passing provenance. |
| `1` | Not ready — see `not_ready_reasons`. |
| `2` | Usage error: an unknown argument, a non-integer `--seed`, an invalid `--format`, a flag given last with no value, or a capability in scope that needs a fresh run without `--model`. |

**Exit codes (`hotdocs track feedback`):**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Ran (output may be empty if no failed attempt exists). |
| `2` | Usage error: no `<component-id>`, an unknown argument, or a first word other than `verify` or `track feedback`. |

Every usage error, for either command, prints one line naming its cause
to stderr before exiting `2`, never a traceback.
documents.interface/data/AttemptRecord.md:
# `AttemptRecord`

```json
{
  "attempt_id": "2026-10-25T14:32:01Z-a1b2c3",
  "component_id": "comp-foo",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-25T14:32:01Z",
  "spec_bundle_hash": "sha256:...",
  "generation": { "...": "a GenerationResult" },
  "verification": { "...": "a VerificationReport, null if generation itself failed" }
}
```

One file per attempt, under `.hotdocs/attempts/<component_id>/`,
`attempt_id`-prefixed for chronological glob ordering. `verification`
is `null` exactly when `generation.model_call_error` is populated (no
candidate was ever produced to verify) — the same mutually-exclusive
relationship `ComponentPipelineResult` already has between
`model_call_error` and `verification`, preserved here at the
per-attempt level.

**`verification.requirement_results`'s own real shape** (`D95`) — the
one sub-field of `VerificationReport` this component actually reads
(`last_requirement_failures`, `R-TRACK-008`), stated here directly
since this component never depends on `verifier-orchestrator` for the
rest of that type: a flat JSON object mapping each `R-id` string
directly to the string `"pass"` or `"fail"` — never a list of
per-requirement objects, never a nested status field. For example:
`{"R-FOO-001": "pass", "R-FOO-002": "fail"}`.

Never mutated once written, append-only — a later, separate
`hotdocs generate` attempt on the same component writes its own new
file, never edits this one.

**The `AttemptRecord` `write_attempt_record` returns in memory carries
`generation`/`verification` in exactly this same JSON-equivalent plain
form** (`D100`) — a dict matching this document's own shape precisely,
never the original caller-supplied `GenerationResult`/`VerificationReport`
object echoed back by reference. A caller needing the original object
already has it, having passed it in; this field exists to describe
what was recorded, not to hand back what was received.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

One module file, `provenance_tracker.py`, never a package: `hotdocs-cli`
loads it by that path.

```
check_readiness(
    repo_root: Path, changed_ids: list[str] | None = None,
    model: str | None = None, seed: int = 0, llm_backend=None,
) -> VerifyReport
```

The live provenance query (`R-TRACK-009`/`010`, `D88`/`D93`) — "would a
merge pass right now." Omitting `changed_ids` checks the whole corpus.
Every component is checked against `provenance-checker` only: first its
`current_sealed_key`, whose `None` means a generated component, checked
with `current_provenance_key` and `check_provenance`, and whose key means
a sealed one, checked with `check_sealed_provenance` (`D170`). Any stand-in
for `provenance-checker` must provide all four names, `current_sealed_key`
returning `None` for a component that is not sealed. It is a pure read, never a call to `component-gate-runner` (`D93`). Every
intersecting capability is first checked with
`capability-scenario-verifier`'s `check_capability_provenance`; only a
miss is run with `run_capability_gates`, passing `model`/`seed`/
`llm_backend` straight through unchanged (`R-TRACK-010`). `model` is
optional here, unlike `component-gate-runner`'s `run_component_gates`:
it is only consulted for such a miss, and a miss with `model` still
`None` raises `ValueError`, never silently skipped.

```
write_attempt_record(
    component_id: str,
    generation_result: GenerationResult,
    verification_report: VerificationReport | None,
    spec_bundle_hash: str,
    repo_root: Path,
) -> AttemptRecord
```

Writes to `.hotdocs/attempts/<component_id>/` (R-TRACK-007) and returns
the record. Called once per `hotdocs generate` attempt, by
`component-gate-runner`, regardless of outcome.

```
last_requirement_failures(component_id: str, repo_root: Path) -> list[str]
```

Reads the most recent `AttemptRecord` for `component_id` with a
non-null `verification` and returns its `requirement_results`' failing
`R-id`s, or `[]` if none exists (R-TRACK-008). A pure convenience
lookup for a human deciding what to pass as `--retry-feedback` on
their next `hotdocs generate` call — never called by any component
itself.
documents.requirements/R-TRACK-004.md:
# R-TRACK-004

**R-TRACK-004** — This component MUST NOT read or depend on
  `component-gate-runner`'s own result type. `write_attempt_record`
  MUST receive `generation_result`/`verification_report` as plain-value
  parameters, handed over directly by the caller, never as a reference
  to a `component-gate-runner`-owned type.

  **This is what keeps the dependency graph acyclic:** `component-gate-runner`
  depends on this component (it calls `write_attempt_record`); if this
  component also depended on `component-gate-runner`'s own result type,
  that would be a two-node cycle, which `spec-linter`'s `R-LINT-004`
  would correctly reject. `review-packet-builder` already established
  the precedent this requirement follows — needing some of a caller's
  facts without depending on the caller's own type, by receiving them
  as plain parameters instead.
documents.requirements/R-TRACK-007.md:
# R-TRACK-007

**R-TRACK-007** — MUST expose `write_attempt_record`, writing one
  `AttemptRecord` per component per `hotdocs generate` attempt to
  `.hotdocs/attempts/<component_id>/` — the full `GenerationResult` and,
  if generation reached it, the full `VerificationReport`, taken as
  direct parameters from `component-gate-runner`.

  Written for both outcomes, success and failure — `D19` closes a real
  gap: a failed attempt commits no provenance at all, so without this,
  its full diagnostic detail (why, not just that) would exist only in
  `component-gate-runner`'s process memory for the duration of one
  `generate` run, then vanish. `AttemptRecord` is the full-detail
  companion a human (or `provenance-tracker-ui`, `D88`) reads when a
  component's provenance check fails and they need to know why.

  **The returned `AttemptRecord`'s own `generation`/`verification`
  fields MUST be the same JSON-equivalent plain form written to disk**
  (`D100`, `AttemptRecord.md`) — never the original
  `GenerationResult`/`VerificationReport` object echoed back by
  reference. Each input may be a dict, a dataclass, or any object
  with attributes (the real `GenerationResult` is a dataclass), and is
  converted recursively to plain JSON values before writing: a
  dataclass via `dataclasses.asdict`, another object via its `vars()`.
documents.requirements/R-TRACK-008.md:
# R-TRACK-008

**R-TRACK-008** — MUST expose `last_requirement_failures(component_id,
  repo_root) -> list[str]`: the failing `R-id`s from the most recent
  `AttemptRecord` (written via this component's own
  `write_attempt_record`, called by `component-gate-runner`,
  `R-GATE-008`/`R-TRACK-007`) for that component whose `verification` is
  non-null, or an empty list if no such record exists. Pure read,
  read-only against `.hotdocs/attempts/` — this component only reads
  what it already wrote there itself. Exists solely so a human — or the
  CLI convenience built on it (`interface/cli.md`), or
  `provenance-tracker-ui`'s own display (`D88`) — has a one-step way to
  see what to pass as `hotdocs generate`'s own `--retry-feedback`
  (`D86`/`D93`), without removing the decision to actually pass it
  from their hands.

  **`verification.requirement_results` MUST be read as a flat `R-id ->
  "pass"|"fail"` string mapping** (`D95`), exactly as
  `AttemptRecord.md` now states directly — never assumed to be a list
  of per-requirement objects, a shape a real candidate guessed instead
  once nothing in this component's own assembled spec bundle stated
  the real shape (this component correctly never depends on
  `verifier-orchestrator`, whose own type this sub-field otherwise
  comes from).
documents.requirements/R-TRACK-009.md:
# R-TRACK-009

**R-TRACK-009** — MUST expose `check_readiness(repo_root: Path,
  changed_ids: list[str] | None = None, model: str | None = None,
  seed: int = 0, llm_backend=None) -> VerifyReport` (`D88`/`D93`): given
  `changed_ids`, MUST call `impact-analyzer` to compute the blast
  radius and check each component; given none (or an empty list), MUST
  check every directory under `specs/components/` holding a
  `component.md`, identified by that file's frontmatter `id` (parsed
  with `yaml.safe_load`, never by hand), never by the directory name.

  **Each component is checked by exactly one of two paths, chosen by
  `provenance-checker`'s `current_sealed_key(component_id, repo_root)`**
  (`D170`). If it returns `None`, call `current_provenance_key(component_id,
  repo_root)` and pass its `spec_bundle_hash` and `gate_versions`,
  unchanged, to `check_provenance` — never computing either value or the
  hit/miss logic itself (`D163`). If it returns a key, the component is
  sealed: call `check_sealed_provenance(component_id, repo_root)` instead,
  and treat `hit` as the whole verdict — a sealed component's license and
  secret scans are not part of it. Its `components` entry is the
  `SealedCheckResult` verbatim, and a miss is reported as
  `<id>: sealed provenance <reason> — run hotdocs generate <id>`.

  **MUST NOT call `component-gate-runner` for any component, on a hit or
  a miss** (`D93`): generating code is a deliberate, potentially
  expensive action a developer triggers with `hotdocs generate`, never a
  side effect of checking readiness. This half is pure and read-only, so
  `depends_on` ordering does not matter here.

  A non-sealed component whose check is a miss, or whose hit carries a
  failing `verification_report` or blocking scan, is not ready, never a
  bare boolean: its `not_ready_reasons` entry names the component and
  which check failed — `verification`, `license_scan`, or `secret_scan` —
  and, for a failing report, every `R-id` its `requirement_results`
  marks `"fail"`.

  **`impact-analyzer` MUST be loaded lazily, only at the point it is
  called** (`D98`): given no `changed_ids`, its module is never loaded at
  all. `provenance-checker` is needed by every scope and MAY be loaded
  unconditionally.
documents.requirements/R-TRACK-010.md:
# R-TRACK-010

**R-TRACK-010** — `check_readiness` (`R-TRACK-009`) MUST additionally
  check every product capability whose `realizes`-set intersects the
  component scope just resolved, through `capability-scenario-verifier`
  (`D89`/`D92`, unreversed by `D93`), never re-deriving its hit/miss
  logic. Unlike the component half this is check-then-run, since
  capability verification never produces source code, only exercises
  what exists. For each such capability, in this order:

  1. call `check_capability_provenance(capability_id, repo_root)`;
  2. if its `hit` is true, that result is the capability's result and
     nothing further is called for it;
  3. if its `hit` is false and `model` is `None`, raise `ValueError` (a
     usage error) before any further call, never skipping the capability
     or running it without a model;
  4. otherwise call `run_capability_gates(capability_id, repo_root,
     model, seed, llm_backend)`, passing this function's own three values
     through unchanged (`D174`'s signature) — never
     `run_capability_scenarios`, a different function for a different
     purpose.

  **The `realizes` edge is declared per-component, never per-capability**
  (`D77`, `D122`): scan every `specs/components/*/component.md` for its
  own `realizes:` frontmatter; a product capability's file, under
  `specs/product/<name>.md`, has no `realizes` field to read back.

  `VerifyReport.ready` MUST be `true` if and only if every component in
  scope is ready (`R-TRACK-009`, a sealed one by its sealed manifest)
  **and** every intersecting capability comes back passing — a single
  failing component or capability makes `ready` false, with that item
  named in the report.

  **`capability-scenario-verifier` MUST be loaded lazily, only when at
  least one capability's `realizes`-set intersects the resolved scope**
  (`D98`): a scope with no intersecting capability never loads it.
documents.requirements/R-TRACK-011.md:
# R-TRACK-011

**R-TRACK-011** — `check_readiness` MUST resolve every dependency
  module (`provenance-checker`, `impact-analyzer`,
  `capability-scenario-verifier`) relative to the `repo_root` it was
  called with — from `<repo_root>/gen/<dependency-slug>/<module_name>.py`
  (flat) or `<repo_root>/gen/<dependency-slug>/<module_name>/__init__.py`
  (package), or the tool root's when absent (`D199`); never trusting a prior `sys.modules` entry keyed by module name alone across
  two different `repo_root` calls in one process. This is the dynamic
  loading convention of `test-author`'s `R-AUTHOR-010`; a candidate that
  resolved from its own location loaded the real dependency instead of a
  test's isolated fake (`D111`).
documents.requirements/R-TRACK-012.md:
# R-TRACK-012

**R-TRACK-012** — `check_readiness` MUST read every field of a value a
  dependency returns (`provenance-checker`'s `ProvenanceCheckResult`,
  `SealedKey`, and `SealedCheckResult`, `impact-analyzer`'s
  `BlastRadiusReport` and each `impacted` entry,
  `capability-scenario-verifier`'s result) using dual dict-or-attribute
  access, never bare `.attr` alone: under this corpus's duck-typing
  convention (`D94`) a dependency may return either shape (`D121`).

documents.component.md:
---
id: comp-provenance-tracker-ui
title: Provenance Tracker UI
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-provenance-tracker, comp-corpus-graph-builder]
realizes: [P-MERGE-VISIBILITY]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
---

# Provenance Tracker UI

## Purpose

A static, self-contained page showing corpus readiness: every
component and capability in scope, colored by current provenance
status, for either a blast-radius or a whole-corpus view, with
per-node drill-down into `AttemptRecord` history and retry-feedback
suggestions for anything currently failing. The visual answer to the
same question `hotdocs verify` answers as an exit code, snapshotted at
build time.

## Rationale

(`D88`, renamed from `merge-tracker-ui`.) `merge-orchestrator`'s removal
(`D87`) retired the per-merge-attempt log this component used to
render; what replaced it (`provenance-tracker`'s live `VerifyReport`) is
naturally graph-shaped — components and capabilities as nodes, their
current provenance status as the thing being rendered — so this
component's own shape follows. Reading `corpus-graph-builder`'s
committed graph for topology, alongside `provenance-tracker`'s
local-only provenance state, is the first time this component crosses
the boundary its own `component.md` previously ruled out (`R-UI-004`,
old) — the concrete cross-referencing need that boundary's own open
question said would justify revisiting it has now actually surfaced.

## Scope

**In scope:** calling `provenance-tracker`'s `check_readiness` once per
build for the chosen scope (`R-UI-007`); reading `corpus-graph.json`
for topology (`R-UI-004`); mapping each node to a status (`R-UI-002`);
attaching `AttemptRecord` history and `last_requirement_failures` as
retry-feedback suggestions to failing or missing nodes (`R-UI-008`);
writing one self-contained page (`R-UI-001`).

**Out of scope:** a "generate" action of its own (`R-UI-003`) — a
developer runs `hotdocs generate` themselves; any view-time query or
server (`R-UI-006`); any write except the page itself.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

All `kind: generated-test` — every criterion needs a faked
`provenance-tracker` and real files on disk, which no fixed step
grammar can set up.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- Initial draft, as `merge-tracker-ui`.
- `D16`: resolved how a developer opens this locally (`hotdocs track ui
  serve`, a trivial local static-file server, not `file://`).
- `D29`: "cache hit" renamed "provenance hit", following
  `TrackingRecord`'s own field rename — superseded below.
- `D87`/`D88`: renamed `provenance-tracker-ui`. No longer renders
  `TrackingRecord` history (removed, nothing produces it anymore) —
  renders `provenance-tracker`'s live `VerifyReport` as an interactive
  graph instead, now also reading `corpus-graph-builder`'s committed
  graph for topology (`R-UI-004`, reversing the prior "never reads
  committed corpus state" boundary now that a concrete need surfaced).
  `AttemptRecord`/retry-feedback drill-down kept, now graph-attached
  rather than a flat per-component list.
- `D93`: wording only — every reference to the since-reversed combined
  `hotdocs build` command now names `hotdocs generate` (the recovery
  action for a failing component) or `hotdocs verify` (the readiness
  query this UI visualizes), whichever it actually meant.
- `D154`: rebuilt as a build-time snapshot — `check_readiness` called
  once in Python, all data inlined into one `file://`-openable page.
  DuckDB-WASM, `duckpgq`, and `hotdocs track ui serve` dropped; the
  spec's static-page and render-`check_readiness` requirements could
  not both hold. Build takes `--model`, passed through. New
  `R-UI-009` (CLI).
- `D161`: `AC-UI-003`'s no-generate-action check excludes the
  `tracker-snapshot` data block; `R-UI-009` covers every CLI flag form.
  Cold-generated and landed (`mutation_score` 0.95).
documents.constraints.md:
# Provenance Tracker UI — Non-Functional Constraints

- **All computation at build time, none at view time.** `render_tracker_ui`
  does every read once, in Python; the written page only renders data
  already inlined into it (`R-UI-001`, `D154`).
- **No network access from the rendered page.** It fetches nothing,
  local or remote, and references no external resource; it opens
  directly from `file://` (`R-UI-006`).
- **Never the gate.** Nothing about this component's output, or whether
  a developer ever builds it, affects any provenance check's outcome —
  the same boundary `provenance-tracker` itself observes (`D87`).
- **Graceful on a node with no provenance at all.** A fresh checkout
  with nothing yet `hotdocs generate`-d MUST render a clear "not yet
  attempted" state per component (`R-UI-005`), not an error — the
  common case for anyone just cloning the repo, not an edge case.
- **Deterministic.** The same `VerifyReport`, `corpus-graph.json`, and
  `.hotdocs/attempts/` contents MUST produce a byte-identical
  `index.html`: no timestamp, random id, or unordered iteration in the
  output.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs track ui build [--changed=<id>...] [--repo-root=<dir>] [--out=<dir>] [--model=<model>] [--seed=<n>]
```

`main(argv)` receives `argv` beginning `["track", "ui", "build", ...]`.
Every flag takes its value either as `--flag=value` or as the next
argument (`--flag value`); a flag given last with no value, a
non-integer `--seed`, or `argv` not beginning with those three words is
a usage error.

- `--changed` — repeatable, or comma-separated; omitted means the
  whole-corpus view (`R-UI-007`).
- `--out` — output directory. Default: `.hotdocs/ui/` — local-only, the
  same as the tracking data it renders (`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §1), never
  `dist/`: unlike `docs-site-renderer`'s output, this page is never
  published.
- `--model`/`--seed` — passed straight through to `check_readiness`
  (`D154`), only consulted if a capability in scope is a provenance
  miss.

Prints the path of the written `index.html`, which opens directly from
`file://` (`R-UI-006`).

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Page written — including when `.hotdocs/attempts/` is empty or missing (`R-UI-005`). |
| `1` | A file that exists failed to parse as JSON (`corpus-graph.json`, or an `AttemptRecord`). |
| `2` | Usage error — bad arguments, a missing `corpus-graph.json`, or the `ValueError` `provenance-tracker`'s `check_readiness` raises for a capability miss with no `--model`. |
documents.interface/data/TrackerSnapshot.md:
# `TrackerSnapshot`

```json
{
  "scope": "blast-radius",
  "changed_ids": ["comp-foo"],
  "ready": false,
  "not_ready_reasons": ["comp-bar: no provenance for current spec state — run hotdocs generate comp-bar"],
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "comp-foo", "kind": "component", "status": "passing", "attempts": [], "retry_feedback": [] },
    { "id": "comp-bar", "kind": "component", "status": "missing",
      "attempts": [ { "attempt_id": "2026-10-25T14:32:01Z-a1b2c3", "...": "an AttemptRecord" } ],
      "retry_feedback": ["R-BAR-002"] },
    { "id": "comp-baz", "kind": "component", "status": "not-attempted", "attempts": [], "retry_feedback": [] },
    { "id": "P-ZERO-EDIT", "kind": "capability", "status": "failing", "attempts": [], "retry_feedback": [] }
  ],
  "edges": [ { "from": "comp-foo", "to": "P-ZERO-EDIT", "kind": "realizes" } ]
}
```

`scope`, `ready`, and `not_ready_reasons` are copied verbatim from the
`VerifyReport`; `changed_ids` is the argument passed (`null` for the
whole-corpus view). `nodes` holds exactly the keys of
`VerifyReport.components` and `VerifyReport.capabilities`, sorted by
`id`. `edges` holds every `corpus-graph.json` edge whose `from` and `to`
are both in `nodes`.

`status` is one of exactly four strings, each a direct mapping of
report fields (`R-UI-002`/`R-UI-005`), never a recomputation:

- component, `hit` true, `verification_report.overall` `"pass"`, not
  `license_scan.blocked`, not `secret_scan.flagged` → `"passing"`
- component, `hit` true, anything else → `"failing"`
- component, `hit` false, at least one `AttemptRecord` → `"missing"`
- component, `hit` false, no `AttemptRecord` → `"not-attempted"`
- capability, `capability_scenario_report[<id>].overall` `"pass"` →
  `"passing"`, otherwise `"failing"`

`attempts` is every `AttemptRecord` for that component, oldest first;
`retry_feedback` is `last_requirement_failures`' result. Both are `[]`
for a capability and for a `"passing"` component.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
render_tracker_ui(
    out_dir: Path, repo_root: Path, changed_ids: list[str] | None = None,
    model: str | None = None, seed: int = 0, llm_backend=None,
) -> TrackerSnapshot
```

Calls `provenance-tracker`'s `check_readiness(repo_root, changed_ids,
model, seed, llm_backend)` exactly once, passing every argument
straight through, then writes one self-contained `out_dir/index.html`
(`R-UI-001`) and returns the `TrackerSnapshot` it inlined
(`interface/data/TrackerSnapshot.md`). `changed_ids` omitted means the
whole-corpus view; present means the blast-radius view (`R-UI-007`).
The `ValueError` `provenance-tracker`'s `check_readiness` raises for a
capability provenance miss with no `model` propagates unchanged.

Topology comes from `<repo_root>/verification/corpus-graph.json`
(`corpus-graph-builder`'s committed output); attempt history from
`<repo_root>/.hotdocs/attempts/<component_id>/*.json` (`AttemptRecord`,
`provenance-tracker`'s own data type), and retry-feedback suggestions
from `provenance-tracker`'s `last_requirement_failures(component_id,
repo_root)`, called once for every component whose status is
`failing` or `missing`. Any stand-in for `provenance-tracker` must
therefore provide both `check_readiness` and
`last_requirement_failures`. A missing
`.hotdocs/attempts/` directory is normal, not an error (`R-UI-005`); a
file there that exists but fails to parse as JSON raises `ValueError`.
documents.requirements/R-UI-001.md:
# R-UI-001

**R-UI-001** — `render_tracker_ui` MUST write exactly one
  self-contained `out_dir/index.html`: the full `TrackerSnapshot`
  (`interface/data/TrackerSnapshot.md`) inlined once as JSON, plus
  plain JavaScript and CSS inline in the same file. No external
  script, stylesheet, image, or font reference; no `fetch`,
  `XMLHttpRequest`, `import`, or WebAssembly anywhere in it (`D154`).
  Every query happened at build time; the page only renders.

  The inlined block MUST be exactly this element, with any `</` inside
  the JSON written as `<\/` so it cannot close the tag early:

  ```html
  <script type="application/json" id="tracker-snapshot">{...}</script>
  ```

  Each node MUST render as one flat element directly carrying its own
  identity and status, never under a per-node heading (`D150`/`D153`),
  and MUST be present literally in the written `index.html` — rendered
  in Python at build time, never constructed by JavaScript at view
  time. JavaScript may only show, hide, or select elements already in
  the file:

  ```html
  <li class="node status-missing" data-node-id="comp-bar" data-kind="component" data-status="missing">
  ```
documents.requirements/R-UI-002.md:
# R-UI-002

**R-UI-002** — MUST render every node in the snapshot, each with the
  `status` `TrackerSnapshot.md` defines — a direct mapping of
  `provenance-tracker`'s `VerifyReport` fields (`D88`), never a
  recomputation of anything it already decided. The four statuses
  (`passing`, `failing`, `missing`, `not-attempted`) MUST each carry
  their own `status-<status>` CSS class with a visually distinct style,
  and the node element's `data-status` attribute MUST equal the
  snapshot's `status` for that node.
documents.requirements/R-UI-003.md:
# R-UI-003

**R-UI-003** — This component MUST NOT implement a "generate" action of
  its own. Running `hotdocs generate` is already the complete recovery
  path for a failing or missing component; this component's job ends
  at making it obvious which nodes still need it. The page MUST contain
  no `<form>`, no link whose `href` leaves the page, and no script that
  does anything beyond showing, hiding, or selecting content already in
  the page. The `tracker-snapshot` JSON block (`R-UI-002`) is data, not
  script: its text, including `not_ready_reasons` that may themselves
  say "run hotdocs generate", is copied verbatim and is not an action
  (`D161`). A future convenience button that shells out to the same CLI
  command a developer would type is a plausible later addition, not a
  gap in this version.
documents.requirements/R-UI-004.md:
# R-UI-004

**R-UI-004** — `render_tracker_ui` MUST read exactly four sources:
  `provenance-tracker`'s `check_readiness` (status), its
  `last_requirement_failures` (retry feedback),
  `<repo_root>/verification/corpus-graph.json` (topology, committed),
  and `<repo_root>/.hotdocs/attempts/<component_id>/*.json` (history,
  local-only). It MUST NOT read anything else under `specs/`, `gen/`, or
  `verification/` directly, and MUST write nothing except
  `out_dir/index.html` (Python's own `__pycache__` bytecode, written by
  the interpreter when a dependency module is imported, is not this
  component's write).

  Committed topology and local-only provenance are still read
  separately and never conflated (`D10`); the page itself stays
  local-only and per-developer even though one input is committed,
  CI-rendered data.
documents.requirements/R-UI-005.md:
# R-UI-005

**R-UI-005** — A component that is a provenance miss and has no
  `AttemptRecord` at all (never touched by `hotdocs generate`) MUST
  render with status `not-attempted` and the visible label "not yet
  attempted" — distinct from `passing`, `failing`, and `missing`, never
  an error and never a blank or unlabeled node. A missing or empty
  `.hotdocs/attempts/` directory is the normal fresh-checkout state,
  not a failure: `render_tracker_ui` still writes the page. Same "never
  silent" posture this corpus applies to every other absence-vs-failure
  distinction (`R-LINT-015`'s skip-vs-fail handling).
documents.requirements/R-UI-006.md:
# R-UI-006

**R-UI-006** — The written `index.html` MUST render correctly opened
  directly from `file://`, with no server of any kind. Every datum is
  already inlined (`R-UI-001`), so nothing is fetched at view time and
  the browser CORS restrictions that once motivated a local server
  (`D16`) never arise. `hotdocs track ui serve` is retired (`D154`);
  this component starts no process and leaves nothing running.
documents.requirements/R-UI-007.md:
# R-UI-007

**R-UI-007** — MUST support two scopes, chosen at build time:
  whole-corpus (`changed_ids` omitted) and blast-radius (`changed_ids`
  given — the same scope `check_readiness` accepts). Every call to
  `render_tracker_ui` MUST call `check_readiness` afresh with exactly
  the `changed_ids` it was given, never reusing or client-side
  filtering an earlier result, since provenance state can change
  between builds. The page MUST state its own scope visibly: the
  snapshot's `scope` string, plus the `changed_ids` for a blast-radius
  view.

  The page shows state as of its last build; switching scope or
  refreshing means rebuilding (`D154`). Further views (by capability,
  by owner) are a natural later extension, not assumed here.
documents.requirements/R-UI-008.md:
# R-UI-008

**R-UI-008** — For a component node with status `failing` or
  `missing`, the page MUST show its `AttemptRecord` history (one
  element per attempt carrying `data-attempt-id`, oldest first) and,
  when its `retry_feedback` is non-empty, a ready-to-copy suggestion
  in an element with class `retry-feedback` whose text is exactly
  `--retry-feedback=` followed by the `R-id`s joined with commas (e.g.
  `--retry-feedback=R-BAR-002`). This is the same information
  `last_requirement_failures` returns, attached to the node instead of
  requiring a separate lookup. It is never auto-filled into anything
  or acted on (`R-UI-003`): a developer reads it and chooses to pass it
  to `hotdocs generate`.
documents.requirements/R-UI-009.md:
# R-UI-009

**R-UI-009** — `main(argv)` MUST implement `interface/cli.md` exactly,
  with `argv` beginning `["track", "ui", "build", ...]`: `--changed`
  (repeatable or comma-separated), `--repo-root`, `--out` (default
  `<repo-root>/.hotdocs/ui/`), `--model`, `--seed` (both passed to
  `check_readiness` as `model` and `seed`). Each flag accepts
  `--flag=value` or `--flag value`. Exit `0` once the page is written
  and its path printed; `1` when an existing JSON input fails to parse;
  `2` on a usage error (per `interface/cli.md`), a missing
  `corpus-graph.json`, or the `ValueError` `provenance-tracker`'s
  `check_readiness` raises for a capability miss with no model.

  Covered from the start: three other components' CLIs went uncovered
  until mutation testing exposed them (`D130`, `D136`, `D145`).
