documents.component.md:
---
id: comp-provenance-writer
title: Provenance Writer
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-generator, comp-verifier-orchestrator, comp-license-scanner, comp-secret-scanner, comp-cache-manager]
realizes: [P-ZERO-EDIT, P-COMPLIANCE-GATE]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
---

# Provenance Writer

## Purpose

Assembles `.provenance.json` (`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §7) from every other
gate component's own output, and writes it. The single place that schema is
populated — every other component reports its own result; this component
collects, never invents.

## Scope

**In scope:** collecting each dependency's reported output into the one
canonical schema; writing it to both required locations; the
provenance-hit copy-forward behavior. Also the sealed
counterpart: writing a sealed component's ownership and verification
manifest (`R-PROV-018`/`019`), whose schema this component owns.

**Out of scope:** deciding *whether* a component's result is a
provenance hit (`provenance-checker`/`component-gate-runner` already
decided that and supplied the already-sourced fields by the time this
component runs, `D29`/`D76`); running any gate itself.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`. (the provenance manifest schema is `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md`
§7 itself — this component does not redefine it).

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

All ten criteria are `kind: compiled` — collecting and writing already-
produced results is pure, deterministic logic. A sixth component in this
corpus with a fully `compiled` acceptance set.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- Initial draft.
- `D29`: `cache_hit` renamed `provenance_hit` throughout (`R-PROV-004`);
  `R-PROV-009`'s lookup is now the caller's job, not this component's —
  `cache-manager` never held a `VerificationReport` to look up.
- `D67`: found via a pre-generation audit, before this component was
  ever built: `pipeline_version` and `verification_run_id` had no
  stated source anywhere. `R-PROV-012`/`013` fix this — the former is
  this component's own version constant, the latter a deterministic
  `"<slug>-attempt-<attempts>"`. Also found `R-PROV-002`'s claim that
  `spec_bundle_hash` comes from `generator`'s `GenerationResult` was
  false against that component's real schema at the time — fixed
  there instead (`GenerationResult` gained the field, `R-GEN-017`),
  since `provenance-writer` has no other dependency that could supply it.
- `D128`: real cold-generation, first attempt. `inputs` itself (not
  only fields nested inside it) MUST be read via dual
  dict-or-attribute access, never bare `.attr` (`R-PROV-014`,
  `AC-PROV-014`) — the identical bug class `R-TRACK-012` closed for
  `provenance-tracker`, one level removed: there, a called
  dependency's return value; here, a parameter the caller hands in
  directly.
- `D130`: `main()`'s CLI entry point (`interface/cli.md`) had no
  requirement or acceptance criterion at all, leaving its
  argument-parsing and exit-code branches permanently unexercised —
  caught by mutation score, not a failing assertion (`R-PROV-015`,
  `AC-PROV-015`).
- `D131`: converting a nested upstream value for writing MUST handle
  any attribute-bearing object (e.g. `SimpleNamespace`), not only a
  dict or a `dataclasses` instance (`R-PROV-016`) — the same `D94`
  shape range `R-PROV-014` already required on the read side.
- `D132`: `ProvenanceInputs` MUST remain a real, importable
  `dataclass` in this module, never dropped in favor of duck-typed
  `Any` alone (`R-PROV-017`) — matching every sibling component's own
  `interface/data/` type (`cache-manager`'s `CachedResult`,
  `license-scanner`'s `LicenseScanResult`). Full account in
  `BOOTSTRAP.md`.
- `D170`: `write_sealed_provenance` and the `SealedProvenance` schema
  (`R-PROV-018`/`019`): a sealed component's own provenance file.
  Regenerated and landed at 20/20, `mutation_score` 0.87.
documents.constraints.md:
# Provenance Writer — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Never invents data.** If a required input is missing, this component
  MUST fail loudly (exit `1`) rather than write a manifest with a guessed
  or default value in that field — a provenance manifest with a fabricated
  field is worse than no manifest at all, since it would be trusted as
  evidence during incident debugging.
- **Determinism.** Given the same `ProvenanceInputs`, the written manifest
  MUST be byte-identical across runs (field ordering included), so it
  participates correctly in any future tooling that diffs or hashes
  provenance manifests themselves.
- **No network access, no model calls.** Pure aggregation and file writing.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs provenance write <component-id> [--repo-root=<dir>]
```

`main(argv)` receives `argv` beginning exactly `["provenance", "write",
<component-id>, ...]`, the verb words kept (`D184`'s dispatcher strips
none). `argv` not beginning `["provenance", "write"]` is a usage error.
`--repo-root` defaults to the current directory and takes its value as
`--repo-root=<dir>` or as the next argument; `--repo-root` given last with
no value, any other `--` flag, or a second positional argument is a usage
error.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Manifest written to both required locations. |
| `1` | A required upstream result (e.g. `verifier-orchestrator`'s report) was missing — this component cannot invent what it didn't receive. |
| `2` | Usage error. |
documents.interface/data/ProvenanceInputs.md:
# `ProvenanceInputs`

```json
{
  "component_id": "comp-foo",
  "generation_result": { "...": "a GenerationResult" },
  "verification_report": null,
  "license_scan_result": { "...": "a LicenseScanResult" },
  "secret_scan_result": { "...": "a SecretScanResult" },
  "provenance_hit": false,
  "attempts": 2,
  "gate_versions": { "compiler": "1.0.0", "license_scanner": "k-gram@1.0.0" }
}
```

**Previously referenced in `library.md`/`constraints.md`/`AC-PROV-001` but
never actually defined here — a real, pre-existing gap, fixed now rather
than propagated further.** `generation_result` is always populated —
`GenerationResult`'s own `files`/`model_call_error`/`refused` fields (never
more than one populated, per that type's own contract) already carry
whether a candidate exists at all. `verification_report` is `null`
whenever `generation_result.files` is empty (nothing was ever produced to
verify) and populated otherwise; a `null` report alongside non-empty `files` is
a missing upstream result, so `write_provenance` raises `MissingInputError`
(`R-PROV-014`'s `inputs` shapes apply), never writing a manifest for it — this mirrors `ComponentPipelineResult`'s
own `model_call_error`/`verification` split (`component-gate-runner`'s
`R-GATE-004`), so
`provenance-writer` can write a coherent manifest for a component that
never reached verification, not only for one that did.

`license_scan_result`/`secret_scan_result` are always populated
regardless of generation outcome — both scans run unconditionally
(`component-gate-runner`'s `R-GATE-005`) and don't depend on `generation_result` having
succeeded. This bundle previously listed a `cross_model_check` field
(`CrossCheckResult` or `None`) from when `cross-model-divergence-checker`
existed; removed along with that component (the second-model scope cut) —
not re-added speculatively.
documents.interface/data/SealedProvenance.md:
# `SealedProvenance` and `SealedProvenanceInputs`

The sealed provenance manifest, `<repo_root>/<source_path>/.sealed-provenance.json`
(`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §7). This document is its one definition: the
writer produces it, `provenance-checker` reads it, and both follow the
rules below exactly.

```json
{
  "kind": "sealed-provenance",
  "version": 1,
  "component_id": "comp-criterion-compiler",
  "owners": ["pipeline-team"],
  "source_path": "pipeline/criterion-compiler/",
  "source_hash": "sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "verifier_version": "verifier-orchestrator@2.0.0",
  "characterization": { "overall": "pass", "criteria_passed": 15, "criteria_total": 15 },
  "written_at": "2026-11-02T00:00:00Z"
}
```

**Validity.** A document is a valid manifest only if all hold, and an
invalid one is never honored in any part:

- it is a JSON object with exactly the keys above, in no other shape;
  `characterization` has exactly its three keys;
- `kind` is `"sealed-provenance"`; `version` is the integer `1` (JSON
  `true` is not an integer, here or in any count below);
- `component_id` matches `^comp-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`;
- `owners` is a non-empty list of strings, each matching
  `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`;
- `source_path` matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*/?$`
  and its first segment is not `gen`;
- `source_hash` matches `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`;
- `verifier_version` matches `^verifier-orchestrator@[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`;
- `characterization.overall` is `"pass"` or `"fail"`; `criteria_passed`
  and `criteria_total` are integers (never booleans) with
  `0 <= criteria_passed <= criteria_total`; `"pass"` additionally needs
  `criteria_total >= 1` and `criteria_passed == criteria_total`;
- `written_at` matches `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$`.

No field holds free text, so nothing can be smuggled into a manifest.

`SealedProvenanceInputs` is what the writer is handed (`R-PROV-018`):
`component_id`, `owners`, `source_path`, `source_hash`,
`verifier_version`, and `verification_report` (a `VerificationReport`).
`characterization` is derived from the report: `overall` is the
report's `overall`, `criteria_total` the number of entries in its
`criteria`, `criteria_passed` those whose `result` is `"pass"`.
Every entry in the report's `criteria` MUST have a `result` of `"pass"`,
`"fail"`, or `"skipped"`, and the report's `overall` MUST be `"pass"` or
`"fail"`; anything else makes the inputs invalid (`R-PROV-019`).
documents.interface/data/provenancemanifest.md:
# provenance manifest

The schema is `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §7 itself, reproduced here only for
convenience, not as a second definition:

```json
{
  "spec_bundle_hash": "sha256:...",
  "model_pin": "claude-sonnet-5",
  "prompt_version": "v1",
  "retry_feedback": null,
  "pipeline_version": "v1",
  "gate_versions": { "compiler": "1.0.0", "license_scanner": "k-gram@1.0.0" },
  "provenance_hit": false,
  "generated_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "verification_run_id": "run-123",
  "verification_report": { "...": "a VerificationReport" },
  "license_scan": { "...": "a LicenseScanResult" },
  "secret_scan": { "...": "a SecretScanResult" }
}
```
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
write_provenance(component_id: str, inputs: ProvenanceInputs, repo_root: Path) -> None
write_sealed_provenance(component_id: str, inputs: SealedProvenanceInputs, repo_root: Path) -> None
```

`ProvenanceInputs` (see `interface/data/`) bundles the other components'
already-produced results (`GenerationResult`, `VerificationReport` or
`null`, `LicenseScanResult`, `SecretScanResult`, cache/attempt/gate-version
data) — this component does not call any of those components itself, it
only assembles what it's handed.

`write_sealed_provenance` is the sealed counterpart (`R-PROV-018`,
`R-PROV-019`): it writes a sealed component's ownership and verification
manifest (`interface/data/SealedProvenance.md`). It raises
`InvalidSealedInputError`, defined in this module, for any input that
would not yield a valid manifest. `SealedProvenanceInputs` is a real
dataclass in this module, and a plain dict of the same fields is
accepted too (`R-PROV-014`, `R-PROV-017`).

The manifests are the hidden files `<repo_root>/gen/<slug>/.provenance.json`
and `<repo_root>/verification/<slug>/.provenance.json` (and, for a sealed
component, `<repo_root>/<source_path>/.sealed-provenance.json`). Read one by
its exact path, never by a glob such as `*.provenance.json`, which a hidden
file never matches.
documents.requirements/R-PROV-001.md:
# R-PROV-001

**R-PROV-001** — The written manifest MUST contain exactly the fields
  `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §7 declares — no more, no less. That document is the
  single source of truth for the schema; this component's job is populating
  it, not redefining it.
documents.requirements/R-PROV-002.md:
# R-PROV-002

**R-PROV-002** — `spec_bundle_hash`, `model_pin`, `prompt_version`, and
  `retry_feedback` MUST be populated from `generator`'s
  `GenerationResult` — `retry_feedback` copied through exactly as
  recorded there (`R-GEN-012`, restored by `D3`), including `null`
  when the call was blind. No `sample_index` field — `D3` retired the
  best-of-k retry loop that gave it a meaning, and nothing since has
  reintroduced multiple samples per merge.
documents.requirements/R-PROV-003.md:
# R-PROV-003

**R-PROV-003** — `gate_versions` MUST be populated by collecting each
  gate's own reported version (`cache-manager`, `criterion-compiler`,
  `license-scanner`, `secret-scanner`, the mutation-testing harness) —
  never invented or hardcoded here.
documents.requirements/R-PROV-004.md:
# R-PROV-004

**R-PROV-004** — `provenance_hit` MUST be populated from the caller's
  own `ProvenanceInputs` field of the same name — never recomputed or
  inferred from any gate's own result. Renamed from `cache_hit` by
  `D29`: this field has never meant "`cache-manager` had an entry" (a
  per-gate concern, e.g. `GenerationResult.cache_hit`) — it means
  `provenance-checker` reported a hit for the whole component, a fact
  only `component-gate-runner` knows, since it's the one that asked
  (`D76`).
documents.requirements/R-PROV-005.md:
# R-PROV-005

**R-PROV-005** — `verification_report` MUST be populated from
  `verifier-orchestrator`'s `VerificationReport`, in full — not summarized
  or truncated, since this is the hard evidence trail for incident
  debugging (`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §7).
documents.requirements/R-PROV-007.md:
# R-PROV-007

**R-PROV-007** — `license_scan` and `secret_scan` MUST always be
  populated — both scans are unconditional, so there is no
  "not-run" state for either.
documents.requirements/R-PROV-008.md:
# R-PROV-008

**R-PROV-008** — `generated_at` MUST be this component's own write-time
  timestamp, not copied from any upstream component's internal timestamp.
documents.requirements/R-PROV-009.md:
# R-PROV-009

**R-PROV-009** — When `provenance_hit` is `true`, this component MUST
  still just write whatever `verification_report`/`license_scan`/
  `secret_scan` its `ProvenanceInputs` carries, unchanged — the same
  "collects, never invents" discipline as every other field. It MUST
  NOT look anything up itself. Sourcing those fields from the matching
  prior manifest, via `provenance-checker` (`D29`), is
  `component-gate-runner`'s job before this component is ever called
  (`D76`) —
  this requirement previously described that lookup as this
  component's own, pointed at `cache-manager`, which never held a
  `VerificationReport` to look up in the first place.
documents.requirements/R-PROV-010.md:
# R-PROV-010

**R-PROV-010** — The manifest MUST be written identically to both
  `gen/<component>/.provenance.json` and
  `verification/<component>/.provenance.json` — two copies of one logical
  artifact, which MUST NEVER be permitted to diverge.
documents.requirements/R-PROV-011.md:
# R-PROV-011

**R-PROV-011** — The written file MUST be syntactically valid JSON whose
  top-level keys exactly match `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §7's field set — no
  extra keys, no missing ones.
documents.requirements/R-PROV-012.md:
# R-PROV-012

**R-PROV-012** — `pipeline_version` MUST be this component's own
  version constant (`PIPELINE_VERSION`, mirroring `generator`'s
  `PROMPT_VERSION`/`GATE_VERSION` pattern) — bumped whenever this
  component's own manifest-population logic changes meaningfully, never
  computed from `ProvenanceInputs` or any other input (`D67`, found
  previously unsourced — `ProvenanceInputs` has no field it could come
  from).
documents.requirements/R-PROV-013.md:
# R-PROV-013

**R-PROV-013** — `verification_run_id` MUST be deterministically
  constructed from `ProvenanceInputs.component_id` (slug) and
  `ProvenanceInputs.attempts` as `"<slug>-attempt-<attempts>"` — never
  a freshly generated random value (`D67`, found previously
  unsourced). `constraints.md`'s determinism requirement (byte-identical
  output given the same input) already forbids a random id; this makes
  the specific construction explicit rather than leaving it to be
  independently guessed.
documents.requirements/R-PROV-014.md:
# R-PROV-014

**R-PROV-014** — `build_manifest`/`write_provenance` MUST read every
  top-level field of `inputs` itself (`generation_result`,
  `verification_report`, `license_scan_result`, `secret_scan_result`,
  `provenance_hit`, `attempts`, `gate_versions`) using dual
  dict-or-attribute access, never a bare `.attr` access alone: this
  corpus's duck-typing convention (`D94`) means `ProvenanceInputs`
  itself, not only the values nested inside it, may arrive as either
  shape (`D128`). The same applies to `R-TRACK-012`'s dependency return
  values, one level removed.
documents.requirements/R-PROV-015.md:
# R-PROV-015

**R-PROV-015** — `main(argv)` MUST implement `interface/cli.md` exactly:
  `hotdocs provenance write <component-id> [--repo-root=<dir>]`, reading
  a JSON-encoded `ProvenanceInputs` from stdin. Exit `0` once
  `write_provenance` succeeds; exit `1` on `MissingInputError` (a
  required upstream result was absent); exit `2` on any usage error —
  wrong/missing positional arguments, an unrecognized `--` flag, a
  `--repo-root` with no value, or malformed JSON on stdin. Found by
  mutation testing, since no criterion had covered the CLI (`D130`).
documents.requirements/R-PROV-016.md:
# R-PROV-016

**R-PROV-016** — Converting a nested upstream value (`license_scan`,
  `secret_scan`, `verification_report`) into the manifest's
  JSON-serializable form MUST handle every shape the duck-typing
  convention (`D94`) permits — a plain `dict`, a `dataclasses`-decorated
  instance, **or any other object that exposes its fields as plain
  attributes** (e.g. `types.SimpleNamespace`), never only
  `dict`/dataclass. Such an object is converted from its public,
  non-callable attributes, never left as the original object for
  `json.dumps` to reject (`D131`).
documents.requirements/R-PROV-017.md:
# R-PROV-017

**R-PROV-017** — `ProvenanceInputs` (`interface/data/ProvenanceInputs.md`)
  MUST be a real, importable `dataclass` in this component's own module,
  never only a type-hint name or a bare `Any` parameter.
  `write_provenance`/`build_manifest` still accept an equivalent plain
  dict (`R-PROV-014`); the dataclass is an additional, always-present
  construction path, as with every sibling component's documented
  `interface/data/` type (`D132`).
documents.requirements/R-PROV-018.md:
# R-PROV-018

**R-PROV-018** — `write_sealed_provenance(component_id, inputs,
  repo_root)` MUST write exactly one file,
  `<repo_root>/<source_path>/.sealed-provenance.json`, whose content is
  a valid sealed provenance manifest
  (`interface/data/SealedProvenance.md`): the six input fields copied
  unchanged, `characterization` derived from `verification_report` as
  that document states, `kind` and `version` fixed, and `written_at`
  this component's own write time (`R-PROV-008`). Keys are written in
  the document's order, two-space indented, with a trailing newline. It
  creates `<source_path>` if absent and writes nothing else: no
  `gen/` or `verification/` copy, no change to any other file.
documents.requirements/R-PROV-019.md:
# R-PROV-019

**R-PROV-019** — `write_sealed_provenance` MUST validate before
  writing, never invent. If `component_id` differs from
  `inputs.component_id`, any input is missing, or the manifest the
  inputs would produce is not valid (`interface/data/SealedProvenance.md`
  — a bad `source_path`, `owners` entry, or hash, or a
  `verification_report` with no `criteria`, or an entry whose `result`
  is not `pass`, `fail`, or `skipped`, say), it MUST raise
  `InvalidSealedInputError` and write nothing, leaving any existing
  manifest untouched. Inputs are read with dual dict-or-attribute
  access (`R-PROV-014`), and the report's entries likewise
  (`R-PROV-016`).

documents.component.md:
---
id: comp-review-packet-builder
title: Review Packet Builder
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-provenance-tracker]
realizes: [P-ZERO-EDIT, P-COMPLIANCE-GATE]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
---

# Review Packet Builder

## Purpose

Assembles the human-readable summary a reviewer actually reads before
merging (`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §6 steps 4/6): the spec diff, changed
requirements, regenerated components, verification results, flags, and
residual risk — never the generated code itself.

## Scope

**In scope:** formatting already-computed results — verification,
license/secret scan, provenance-hit status, and capability-scenario
results — into one reviewable document, read entirely from
`provenance-tracker`'s own `check_readiness` (`R-PACKET-011`, `D90`),
which already assembles all of it, component and capability alike; no
live dependency on `verifier-orchestrator`, `license-scanner`,
`secret-scanner`, `provenance-checker`, or `capability-scenario-verifier`
is needed to do this.

**Out of scope:** computing any of those results itself; deciding whether
the merge is allowed (gates already decided that; this component reports,
it doesn't gate).

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

All fourteen criteria are `kind: generated-test` — real git-history
scenarios (sealed/override transitions, CLI invocation, markdown
rendering) need arbitrary setup code no fixed step grammar can
express, not purely literal-value fixtures.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- Initial draft.
- `D29`: `cache_hit_status` renamed `provenance_hit_status`
  (`R-PACKET-006`); `R-PACKET-011`'s source list drops `cache-manager`,
  which this field never actually came from.
- `D90`: `depends_on` swaps `provenance-writer` for `provenance-tracker`
  directly — reads its `check_readiness` aggregate instead of the
  `component_provenance` view over `provenance-writer`'s manifests.
  `ReviewPacket` gains `capability_scenarios` (`R-PACKET-011`), closing
  a real gap: the old `merge-orchestrator`'s own spec always assumed
  this packet carried capability-scenario results, but nothing in this
  component's own requirements ever actually added them.
- `D140`/`141`: `spec_diff`'s base ref (merge-base with default
  branch), `changed_ids`'s own semantics (never git-derived),
  `residual_risk`/`compliance_flags` entry shapes, and
  `regenerated_components`'s source (`provenance-tracker`'s own
  `components` map, never `impact-analyzer` directly) all pinned down
  with worked examples — real test-authoring rounds kept guessing
  differently each time without them.
- `D145`/`150`/`153`: `R-PACKET-012`, the CLI entry point
  (`main`/`cli.md`) had zero coverage; its markdown rendering's own
  structure is now normative — flat lines or bold labels, never a
  nested per-entry sub-heading, after that ambiguity repeatedly broke
  a generated test's own section-boundary parse.
- `D147`/`148`/`149`/`151`/`152`: `sealed`-transition detection
  landed on comparing each file against its own first commit in
  `HEAD`'s history, independent of `R-PACKET-001`'s own PR diff-base
  — three earlier, each-plausible-looking approaches (diff-status
  letter, PR-diff-base existence, "doesn't exist implies unsealed")
  each broke a different real git-history shape before this one held.
- Landed (`D151`'s own retry, `mutation_score=0.82`): swapped in.
- `D201`: `R-PACKET-013` covers the tool-root fallback (`D199`); the
  CLI's `--flag value` form and the markdown's remaining fields are
  covered.
documents.constraints.md:
# Review Packet Builder — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Determinism.** Given the same upstream results, the packet MUST be
  byte-identical across runs.
- **No network access, no model calls.** Pure formatting of already-
  computed data.
- **Readable by a human in the time it takes to review a spec diff.** Not a
  dump of every field every upstream component produced — organized into
  the sections R-PACKET-001–008 name, in that order, so a reviewer always
  finds the same kind of information in the same place.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs review-packet build --changed=<spec-id>... [--repo-root=<dir>] [--format=markdown|json]
```

- `--changed` — spec ids changed in this PR (same input shape as
  `impact-analyzer`'s `--changed`).
- `--format` — `markdown` (default; what actually gets posted on a PR) or
  `json` (structured data for other tooling).

`argv` begins `["review-packet", "build"]`. Every flag takes its value as
`--flag=value` or as the next argument (`--flag value`); `--changed` may
repeat; a flag given last with no value is a usage error.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Packet built. |
| `1` | A required upstream result was missing. |
| `2` | Usage error. |
documents.interface/data/ReviewPacket.md:
# `ReviewPacket`

```json
{
  "spec_diff": "<unified diff text>",
  "changed_requirements": ["R-FOO-001"],
  "regenerated_components": ["comp-foo"],
  "verification_results": { "comp-foo": { "...": "a VerificationReport" } },
  "compliance_flags": {
    "license_scan": [
      { "component_id": "comp-foo", "result": { "blocked": true, "...": "a LicenseScanResult" } }
    ],
    "secret_scan": []
  },
  "provenance_hit_status": { "comp-foo": false },
  "capability_scenarios": { "P-ZERO-EDIT": { "P-ZERO-EDIT": { "overall": "pass", "scenarios": [] } } },
  "exemption_changes": { "sealed": ["comp-foo"], "pinned_overrides": [] },
  "residual_risk": [
    { "component_id": "comp-foo", "message": "mutation_score 0.92 < 1.0 despite overall=pass" }
  ]
}
```

Each `residual_risk` entry is an object with `component_id` (the
affected component) and `message` (a human-readable description of
the non-blocking finding, per `R-PACKET-008`) — never a bare string.

Each `compliance_flags.license_scan`/`secret_scan` entry is a
`{"component_id", "result"}` pair, included only for a component
whose own `license_scan.blocked` / `secret_scan.flagged` is `true`
(`R-PACKET-005`) — the array is `[]`, not omitted, when none are.

`exemption_changes.sealed`/`pinned_overrides` entries are bare
component ids (`"comp-foo"`, matching `regenerated_components`'s own
shape) — never the `specs/components/<slug>/component.md` or
`gen/<slug>/.overrides.json` file path the change was detected in.

`capability_scenarios` (`R-PACKET-011`, `D90`) is every product
capability whose `realizes`-set intersects `regenerated_components`,
keyed by `P-id`, each value that capability's `capability_scenario_report`
exactly as read (itself keyed by `P-id`, never unwrapped) — read from `provenance-tracker`'s `VerifyReport.capabilities`,
never a live `capability-scenario-verifier` call. A distinct section
from `verification_results`, never conflated with it — a cross-component
finding and a single-component one point a reviewer to different
places to look.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
build_review_packet(changed_ids: list[str], repo_root: Path) -> ReviewPacket
```

`changed_ids` is the caller's own authoritative list of every spec id
that changed in this PR (component ids, `R-id`s, `AC-id`s, capability
ids) — never independently rediscovered from git by this component.
`changed_requirements` (`R-PACKET-002`) is simply its `R-id`-shaped
subset.

`provenance-tracker` is one flat module file,
`gen/provenance-tracker/provenance_tracker.py`, loaded per `R-PACKET-013`.

## Test fixtures

Unless a criterion says otherwise, every criterion builds `repo_root`
as a git repository with at least one commit and a `provenance-tracker`
stand-in at `<repo_root>/gen/provenance-tracker/provenance_tracker.py`
in place of the real one (the real one calls `impact-analyzer`, which
rejects a spec id the corpus does not hold). The stand-in defines
`check_readiness(repo_root, changed_ids=None, model=None, seed=0,
llm_backend=None)` returning a `VerifyReport`-shaped dict written as a
Python literal (`True`, `False`, `None`, never JSON spelling, never
`repr` of an already-`repr`'d value) and
`last_requirement_failures(component_id, repo_root)` returning `[]`.
Each criterion states what that dict reports; a spec id such as
`R-FOO-002` exists only in the fixture's files and that dict.
documents.requirements/R-PACKET-001.md:
# R-PACKET-001

**R-PACKET-001** — The packet MUST include the actual spec diff for this
  change — the primary thing a human reviews (`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §6).
  Computed as the diff, over `specs/`, between the merge-base of `HEAD`
  and the repo's default branch, and `HEAD` — reusing `R-IMPACT-010`'s
  already-ratified convention for "the prior commit," never a bare
  working-tree-vs-`HEAD` diff (empty once every change is committed,
  which a real PR always is by review time). **Fallback:** when that
  merge-base **is** `HEAD` itself (no divergence from the default
  branch — e.g. the PR's commits sit directly on the current branch,
  no separate feature branch exists), diff the empty tree (the
  canonical all-zero-content git object, hash
  `4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904`) against `HEAD` instead
  — never `HEAD~1`, which only shows the single most recent commit
  and silently drops everything earlier whenever more than one commit
  sits on the current branch with no feature-branch base to diff
  against. The whole accumulated history becomes "the PR" in that
  case, which is the only interpretation that doesn't depend on how
  many commits happen to be involved.
documents.requirements/R-PACKET-002.md:
# R-PACKET-002

**R-PACKET-002** — The packet MUST list which `R-id`s changed in this PR.
documents.requirements/R-PACKET-003.md:
# R-PACKET-003

**R-PACKET-003** — The packet MUST list which components were
  regenerated — exactly the keys of `provenance-tracker`'s own
  `VerifyReport.components` (`D90`), never a live `impact-analyzer`
  call of this component's own: `check_readiness` already resolved
  the blast radius internally before returning.
documents.requirements/R-PACKET-004.md:
# R-PACKET-004

**R-PACKET-004** — The packet MUST include verification results per
  regenerated component — the full pass/fail/skipped breakdown, not just an

documents.requirements/R-PACKET-005.md:
# R-PACKET-005

**R-PACKET-005** — License- and secret-scan results MUST appear as their
  own explicit section, even when both are clean — never folded into a
  generic results blob where a flag could be missed — every flag stays
  strictly tracked and communicated.

  `compliance_flags.license_scan` is a `{"component_id", "result"}`
  entry for exactly the components whose per-component `license_scan`
  value's own `blocked` field (verbatim from `license-scanner`'s
  `LicenseScanResult.blocked`, flowing through `provenance-tracker`
  unmodified) is `true` — `[]` when none are. `secret_scan` is the
  same, keyed on `.flagged` (`secret-scanner`'s own
  `SecretScanResult.flagged`). Never a heuristic guess across other
  possible key names — `blocked`/`flagged` are the one real signal.
documents.requirements/R-PACKET-006.md:
# R-PACKET-006

**R-PACKET-006** — Provenance-hit status MUST be shown per component,
  visibly — never left for the reader to infer from the absence of
  other detail. Renamed from "cache-hit status" by `D29`: this field
  has never been about `cache-manager`.
documents.requirements/R-PACKET-007.md:
# R-PACKET-007

**R-PACKET-007** — Any new or changed `sealed` or
  `gen/<component>/.overrides.json` declaration in this PR MUST appear as
  its own explicit section (principle 7/§8) — a declared exemption from the
  normal discipline is exactly the kind of thing a reviewer must see called
  out, not buried in a frontmatter diff.

  **"Changed `sealed`" means a genuine transition, detected against
  the file's own first commit in `HEAD`'s history, never against
  `R-PACKET-001`'s own PR diff-base** (`git log --follow --format=%H
  -- <path>`, oldest result = that file's own first commit reachable
  from `HEAD`; read `sealed` there and at `HEAD` via `git show
  <rev>:<path>`). This is deliberately a *different* comparison point
  than `spec_diff`'s own base: the PR diff-base is sometimes the
  empty tree (`R-PACKET-001`'s own fallback for "no feature branch"),
  against which *every* file in the repo reads as "doesn't exist" —
  using it here would either flag every already-sealed component as
  newly sealed (treating "doesn't exist at base" as "not sealed
  there") or exclude every genuine transition more than one commit
  back (requiring the file to exist at that same base). Comparing
  each file against *its own* first commit sidesteps both failure
  modes at once, regardless of how many commits separate that
  transition from `HEAD` or whether a feature branch exists:
  `sealed: false`/absent at that first commit and `sealed: true` at
  `HEAD` is the transition; `sealed: true` already at that first
  commit (the component was sealed from birth) is not. A brand-new
  `gen/<component>/.overrides.json` keeps the simpler, original rule
  — its mere existence at `HEAD` and absence at `R-PACKET-001`'s own
  PR diff-base **is** the complete signal, since an override file has
  no in-file "unsealed" state to transition from and a reviewer does
  need to see every override newly introduced *in this PR*, not
  merely ever.

  **Both are discovered entirely from the git diff's own file paths**
  (`specs/components/<slug>/component.md`, `gen/<slug>/.overrides.json`)
  — never filtered against, or restricted to, `changed_ids`. Unlike
  `changed_requirements` (`R-PACKET-002`, a simple filter *of*
  `changed_ids`), a sealed/override change can affect a component
  `changed_ids` never named at all (the caller's list is about blast
  radius, not about which `component.md`/`.overrides.json` files
  this diff happens to touch) — restricting the scan to
  `changed_ids` would silently miss a real exemption declared on any
  component not literally present in that list.
documents.requirements/R-PACKET-008.md:
# R-PACKET-008

**R-PACKET-008** — "Residual risk" — non-blocking findings still worth a
  human's attention (e.g. a component whose `mutation_score` is below
  `1.0` even though its `overall` result still reads `"pass"`) — MUST
  be its own section, distinct from pass/fail results. Sourced
  entirely from `provenance-tracker`'s own `verification_report`
  (`R-PACKET-011`) — never a metric, such as `spec-linter`'s own
  `component_doc_words`, that no field this component actually reads
  ever carries.
documents.requirements/R-PACKET-009.md:
# R-PACKET-009

**R-PACKET-009** — A packet MUST be produced for every merge, including a
  fully clean one with no flags or warnings — never skipped, so the review
  habit stays consistent merge to merge rather than only appearing when
  something is wrong.

  This MUST hold even when `repo_root` is not a git repository at
  all, not only when it is one with zero commits — every git call
  this component makes (for `spec_diff`/`R-PACKET-001` and
  `exemption_changes`/`R-PACKET-007` specifically) MUST tolerate
  failure by treating the result as empty, never letting a git
  failure raise out of `build_review_packet` and abort the whole
  packet. Every other field (`changed_requirements`,
  `regenerated_components`, `verification_results`,
  `compliance_flags`, `provenance_hit_status`,
  `capability_scenarios`) depends on `changed_ids` and
  `provenance-tracker` alone, never on git, and MUST still be
  produced correctly regardless of `repo_root`'s own git state.
documents.requirements/R-PACKET-010.md:
# R-PACKET-010

**R-PACKET-010** — The packet MUST NOT include the generated code diff as
  primary content. This is deliberate, not an oversight: including a wall
  of generated-code diff would invite exactly the line-by-line code review
  principle 6 moved away from.
documents.requirements/R-PACKET-011.md:
# R-PACKET-011

**R-PACKET-011** — Every field sourced from `verifier-orchestrator`,
  `license-scanner`, `secret-scanner`, or `capability-scenario-verifier`
  (R-PACKET-004, 005, and the capability-scenario section this
  requirement adds) MUST be read via `provenance-tracker`'s own
  `check_readiness` (`D90`) — its `VerifyReport.components`/
  `capabilities` maps already carry `verification_report`,
  `license_scan`, `secret_scan`, and the real field named literally
  `hit` (never `provenance_hit` — that's only this *packet's own*
  output field name, `provenance_hit_status`, R-PACKET-006), and each
  intersecting capability's own `CapabilityScenarioReport` — never a
  live call into any of those components directly, nor a live
  `provenance-checker` call either.

  **The review packet now includes a capability-scenario section** —
  found missing entirely from this component's own prior scope, even
  though the component this packet reports for always intended it
  (`merge-orchestrator`'s old `R-MERGE-010`, before `D87` removed that
  component, already assumed review packets carried this; nothing in
  this component's own spec ever added the requirement to actually do
  it). `provenance-tracker`'s uniform component/capability aggregation
  (`D88`/`D89`) is what makes this straightforward now — one read
  source instead of a second, bespoke one for capability results alone.

  This is an implementation requirement, not a behavioral one —
  R-PACKET-001 through 010 are unaffected beyond gaining the new
  capability-scenario section. It is also why this component's
  `depends_on` lists only `provenance-tracker` (`D90`): no other
  component's own output needs to be read directly, only
  `provenance-tracker`'s already-assembled aggregate.
documents.requirements/R-PACKET-012.md:
# R-PACKET-012

**R-PACKET-012** — `main(argv)` MUST implement `interface/cli.md`
  exactly: `hotdocs review-packet build --changed=<spec-id>...
  [--repo-root=<dir>] [--format=markdown|json]`. Exit `0` once a
  packet is built, exit `1` when a required upstream result was
  missing, any exception `provenance-tracker`'s `check_readiness`
  raises included (such as its `ValueError` for a capability needing a
  fresh run, `D288`), printing its message, exit `2` on any usage error (no subcommand, no `--changed`,
  an invalid `--format`). `--format=json` MUST print the packet as
  `json.dumps(packet, indent=2, sort_keys=True)`, and every JSON value
  in the markdown is dumped with `sort_keys=True`; the default/`--format=markdown` MUST print the human-readable
  rendering actually posted on a PR.

  Found via mutation testing, not a behavioral test failure (same
  shape as `R-PROV-015`/`D130`, `R-DRIFT-005`): every acceptance
  criterion so far exercises `build_review_packet` directly as a
  library call, none through `main()` or its markdown renderer —
  `interface/cli.md` documents the CLI but no requirement or
  acceptance criterion ever covered it.

  **The markdown rendering's own content is normative, not left to
  guesswork** — prose alone has already proven insufficient twice for
  this exact rendering (`D145`'s own retry): the "## Exemption
  Changes" section MUST always render both a `**Sealed:**` and a
  `**Pinned Overrides:**` bold-labeled line (never an actual `###`
  sub-heading — `D152`'s own correction, after a `###` sub-heading
  sitting immediately after `## Exemption Changes` with no
  intervening content repeatedly broke a generated test's own
  "find the next heading" section-boundary parse, the identical
  ambiguity the "## Verification Results"/"## Capability Scenarios"
  fix below already closed), even when one list is empty — never
  omitting the label just because its own list has no entries, the
  same "present, explicitly empty, never omitted" convention
  `R-PACKET-005` already states for `compliance_flags`.
  The "### License Scan"/"### Secret Scan" sub-sections MUST render
  each flagged entry's own `result` content (e.g.
  `json.dumps(entry["result"])` or an equivalent human-readable
  rendering of its real fields) — never a bare status word like
  `"blocked"`/`"flagged"` standing in for the actual flagged detail a
  reviewer needs to act on.

  **"## Verification Results" and "## Capability Scenarios" MUST
  render each entry as a plain, flat line directly under that one
  section heading — `- <component-id>: <json or summary>` — never a
  nested per-entry sub-heading** (e.g. never `### comp-foo`,
  `### P-ZERO-EDIT`). A per-entry sub-heading makes a per-entry id
  indistinguishable, by any generic heading-boundary parse, from the
  section's own content boundary — found after this exact ambiguity
  repeatedly broke a generated test's own section-extraction helper
  across several real rounds. Flat lines (or bold labels) under one
  fixed heading, the same shape "## Residual Risk" and the corrected
  "## Exemption Changes" above both use, removes the ambiguity
  entirely.
documents.requirements/R-PACKET-013.md:
# R-PACKET-013

**R-PACKET-013** — `build_review_packet` MUST load `provenance-tracker`
  from `<repo_root>/gen/provenance-tracker/` when that directory
  exists, and otherwise from the same path under the tool root: the
  parent of the nearest directory named `gen` above this module's own

# Secret Scanner

## Purpose

Unconditional scan of the entire repository for committed
secrets, using `detect-secrets`. Same trust shape as `license-scanner`:
no human sign-off to clear a flag, but no result is ever silent.

## Rationale

Detection is a maintained library's: a hand-built entropy check flagged
ordinary identifiers yet could never match a random hex secret (`D168`).

**Known gaps, accepted (`D168`):** the entropy detectors read quoted
strings only, so an unquoted random token goes unseen, and
`KeywordDetector`, the only plugin catching a low-entropy password, is
off because it flags any key containing a word like `secret`.

## Scope

**In scope:** whole-repository detection; the confidence-based
blocking decision; the risk-based notification path; the sealed
allowlist (`R-SECRET-012`) and `propose`; caching; a pre-commit form.

**Out of scope:** `spec-linter`'s `R-LINT-013` (checks `specs/vars/`), and
whether a flagged scan stops a merge (`provenance-tracker` decides).

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

Every criterion is `kind: generated-test` (`D43`).

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- Initial draft.
- `D26`/`D53`/`D54`/`D163`/`D164`: notifications, first generation, `gate_version`, CLI.
- `D168`: `detect-secrets`, whole repository, allowlist, `propose`.
- `D195`: sealed allowlist.
documents.constraints.md:
# Secret Scanner — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Determinism (full-scan form).** The same repository content,
  allowlist, and `detect-secrets` version MUST give the same result,
  which cache-key correctness requires (`D30`).
- **No model calls**; no network but the webhook.
- **Never silent.** A clean result is recorded as rigorously as a
  flagged one (`R-SECRET-003`/`009`), and every suppressed finding is
  listed.
- **Fail closed:** doubt about the allowlist reports more findings.
- **Precommit** scans only the given files.
- **Matches never carry the secret or its hash;** hashes appear only in
  the allowlist and `propose`'s output.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs secret-scan [--repo-root=<dir>] [--format=json|text]
hotdocs secret-scan precommit [--files=<path>]... [--repo-root=<dir>] [--format=json|text]
hotdocs secret-scan propose [--repo-root=<dir>]
```

- First form — full, cache-aware scan (`R-SECRET-001`–`007`).
- `precommit` — `R-SECRET-008`, scoped to `--files`, by default the
  union of `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR HEAD` and `git diff
  --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR`, run in `--repo-root` (no
  files if `git` fails); no `cache-manager`. A relative `--files` path
  resolves against `--repo-root`.
- `propose` — prints an `AllowlistProposal` as JSON (`R-SECRET-013`);
  accepts no `--format`.

`main(argv)` receives the arguments after the `secret-scan` verb (a
leading `secret-scan` token is ignored). Every flag takes its value as
`--flag=value` or as the next argument; `--files` repeats.
`--repo-root` defaults to the current directory, `--format` to `text`.
`json` prints the `SecretScanResult`; `text` prints `CLEAN` or
`FLAGGED` and one line per match. A flag last with no value, an invalid
`--format`, or an unknown argument or subcommand is a usage error.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Clean; or, for `propose`, every finding can be allowlisted. |
| `1` | Flagged (merge blocked, or commit/push stopped for `precommit`); for `propose`, at least one finding is `ineligible`. |
| `2` | Usage error; for `propose`, also an invalid allowlist. |
documents.interface/data/Allowlist.md:
# `Allowlist` and `AllowlistProposal`

`<repo_root>/.secret-allowlist.json` (`R-SECRET-012`):

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "entries": [
    {
      "file": "verification/secret-scanner/generated-test/test_ac_secret_001.py",
      "type": "AWS Access Key",
      "hashed_secret": "sha1:abac545fc3bf803134bc8f78fb6160a5c6a87b26",
      "reason": "planted-fixture"
    }
  ]
}
```

It holds only SHA-1s of secrets a person judged deliberate fixtures or
public constants; the `sha1:` prefix stops the hex detector flagging the
list. A decision with `allowlist_sha256: sha256:<hex>` in its
frontmatter seals it (`R-SECRET-012`, `D195`).

`propose(repo_root)` returns (`R-SECRET-013`):

```json
{
  "allowlist": { "version": 1, "entries": [ "..." ] },
  "ineligible": [ { "file": "gen/foo/config.py", "line": 12, "rule_id": "AWS Access Key" } ]
}
```
documents.interface/data/SecretScanResult.md:
# `SecretScanResult`

```json
{
  "scope": "full",
  "gate_version": "secret_scanner@3.1.0+detect-secrets.1.5.0",
  "flagged": false,
  "matches": [
    { "rule_id": "AWS Access Key", "risk_tier": "high", "file": "gen/foo/config.py", "line": 12 }
  ],
  "allowed": [
    { "rule_id": "AWS Access Key", "file": "verification/foo/test_x.py", "line": 3 }
  ],
  "unused_allowlist_entries": [
    { "file": "verification/foo/old.py", "type": "AWS Access Key" }
  ],
  "notified": false,
  "notification_delivery_error": null,
  "cache_hit": false
}
```

`scope` is `"full"` or `"precommit"`; a `precommit` result always has
`cache_hit: false` and MAY omit `gate_version` (`R-SECRET-008`).
`flagged` is `true` iff `matches` is non-empty. A match never carries
the secret or its hash (`R-SECRET-001`).

`allowed` lists every finding the allowlist suppressed and
`unused_allowlist_entries` every entry that matched nothing
(`R-SECRET-012`); neither affects `flagged`. An invalid allowlist adds
one match with `rule_id` `"allowlist-invalid"`.

Each match's `file` is relative to `repo_root` with `/` separators
(also in the precommit form); a path given to `scan_files` with no
`repo_root` is reported as given.

`notified` is `flagged` or any `high` match, **and**
`VAR-COMPLIANCE-WEBHOOK-URL` is configured (`R-LICENSE-003`): whether a
notification was **due**, never whether it was delivered. `notification_delivery_error` is
`{category, message}` or `null`, set only when `notified` is `true` and
the call failed (`R-SECRET-004`), and never affects `flagged`;
`category` is `auth` (HTTP 401/403), `timeout`, or `network` (anything
else).
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

One module file, `secret_scanner.py`, never a package.

```
scan(repo_root: Path) -> SecretScanResult
scan_files(paths: list[Path], repo_root: Path | None = None) -> SecretScanResult
gate_version(repo_root: Path) -> str
propose(repo_root: Path) -> AllowlistProposal
```

`scan` and `scan_files` return a `SecretScanResult` object, never a dict:
a dataclass whose fields are attributes, with a `to_dict()` returning
the JSON shape, `matches` and the other lists holding plain dicts.
`scan` is the cache-aware form (`R-SECRET-001`); `scan_files` the
precommit form, with no cache lookup (`R-SECRET-008`); `gate_version`
returns what `scan` would report, without scanning (`R-SECRET-010`);
`propose` (`R-SECRET-013`) raises `AllowlistInvalidError`, defined in
this module, when the allowlist is invalid. All three read the
allowlist through one shared loader, so the seal and every validity
rule apply identically.

## External library

Detection is `detect-secrets`, pinned `==1.5.0` in `requirements.txt`,
with no fallback detector: if it cannot be imported, the call raises
`ImportError`. Only these names are used:

- `detect_secrets.SecretsCollection()`, its `scan_file(path_str)`, and
  iteration over it, yielding `(filename, secret)` pairs;
- `detect_secrets.settings.transient_settings(config)`, a context
  manager, with `config` `{"plugins_used": [{"name": <class name>},
  ...], "filters_used": []}`;
- `detect_secrets.core.plugins.util.get_mapping_from_secret_type_to_class()`,
  whose values are the plugin classes (`<class name>` is `__name__`);
- a secret's `type`, `line_number`, and `secret_hash` (the SHA-1 hex
  digest of the secret); its `secret_value` is never read or kept;
- `importlib.metadata.version("detect-secrets")`.

## cache-manager

`scan` loads `cache-manager` from `<repo_root>/gen/cache-manager/`, or from the tool root's when absent (`D199`), and
uses exactly four of its names: `CacheKey(spec_bundle_hash=...,
gate_inputs_hash=..., gate_version=..., model_pin=...)`;
`get(cache_key, repo_root=...)`; `CachedResult(gate_type="secret_scanner",
payload=<the result's fields as a dict>, stored_at=<UTC ISO-8601>)`, `stored_at` computed by `scan` itself; and `put(cache_key,
cached_result, repo_root=...)` after a fresh scan. A `get` result is a hit only
if its `payload` (read with dual dict-or-attribute access) is non-null.
`cache-manager` being unloadable means no lookup, never a failed scan.

`scan` covers every file under `repo_root`, a test's stand-ins
included, so a stand-in embeds no long random-looking literal, above all
no temporary-directory path; it reads such values from an environment
variable. The compliance webhook is POSTed with `urllib.request.urlopen`
and nothing else, so a test replaces that function.
documents.requirements/R-SECRET-001.md:
# R-SECRET-001

**R-SECRET-001** — A full scan MUST check every text file under
  `repo_root`, with no per-directory or per-component exceptions, using
  the `detect-secrets` library (`interface/library.md`), never a
  detector of its own (`D168`). Only these are skipped: any directory
  named `.git`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `.venv`, `.hotdocs`, or
  `node_modules`, and any file that does not decode as UTF-8.

  The scan runs every plugin the installed library provides except
  `KeywordDetector` and `IPPublicDetector`, each with its own default
  settings, and with **no** `detect-secrets` filters: nothing may
  suppress a finding except `R-SECRET-012`'s allowlist.

  Each finding is one match. `rule_id` is the library's secret type
  string unchanged (e.g. `"AWS Access Key"`). `risk_tier` is `"low"`
  for `"Base64 High Entropy String"` and `"Hex High Entropy String"`
  and `"high"` for every other type. A match carries `file`, `line`,
  `rule_id`, and `risk_tier`, never the secret itself or its hash.
  `matches` is sorted by `file`, then `line`, then `rule_id`.
documents.requirements/R-SECRET-002.md:
# R-SECRET-002

**R-SECRET-002** — A match MUST block the merge, the same way a failed
  test does; no human sign-off can override it. Blocking is a pure
  confidence determination (did a detector match at all), independent
  of the rule's risk, which is `R-SECRET-004`'s concern.
documents.requirements/R-SECRET-003.md:
# R-SECRET-003

**R-SECRET-003** — Every scan result — clean or flagged — MUST be written
  into the provenance manifest, regardless of outcome. Absence of a flag
  MUST NOT mean absence of a record.
documents.requirements/R-SECRET-004.md:
# R-SECRET-004

**R-SECRET-004** — A notification to `VAR-COMPLIANCE-WEBHOOK-URL` MUST
  fire when **either** a match blocked the merge (`R-SECRET-002`) **or**
  a match's `risk_tier` is `high` (an allowed finding is no match), the same orthogonal block/severity
  split as `license-scanner`'s `R-LICENSE-003`. It writes no `.hotdocs/` attempt record (`D19`); a later
  clean scan never un-notifies. The webhook
  call is attempted at most once: a failure (network, auth, timeout)
  MUST be caught and recorded as `notification_delivery_error`, never
  raised, never affecting `flagged`. `notified` stays precondition-only.
documents.requirements/R-SECRET-005.md:
# R-SECRET-005

**R-SECRET-005** — Before scanning, the scanner MUST check
  `cache-manager` using key `(spec_bundle_hash, gate_inputs_hash,
  gate_version, model_pin)` (`interface/data/CacheKey.md`). `spec_bundle_hash` is
  `"sha256:"` plus the hash of the scanned files under `specs/`;
  `gate_inputs_hash` is `"sha256:"` plus the hash of all other scanned
  files, which includes the allowlist (`R-SECRET-012`); `model_pin` is
  `"none"`. A file set's hash covers each file's relative path and
  content, in sorted path order. A cache hit MUST be reused; a cache
  failure never fails or alters a scan.
documents.requirements/R-SECRET-006.md:
# R-SECRET-006

**R-SECRET-006** — `gate_version` MUST be
  `secret_scanner@3.1.0+detect-secrets.<V>`, where `<V>` is the
  installed `detect-secrets` package's version, so upgrading the
  library invalidates every cached result (`D30`). The `3.1.0` MUST be raised in this requirement whenever the
  skipped-directory list, the plugin set, or `R-SECRET-012`'s rules
  change.
documents.requirements/R-SECRET-007.md:
# R-SECRET-007

**R-SECRET-007** — The scanner MUST produce exactly one structured
  `SecretScanResult` per scan, consumed by `provenance-writer` and
  `review-packet-builder`.
documents.requirements/R-SECRET-008.md:
# R-SECRET-008

**R-SECRET-008** — The scanner MUST support a pre-commit/pre-push
  invocation, scoped only to the given files, with no
  `cache-manager` dependency. It uses the same engine, plugin set, skip
  rules, and result shape as a full scan, with `scope` `"precommit"`. When given a `repo_root`, it reports each
  path relative to it and applies the allowlist (`R-SECRET-012`)
  as a full scan does; given none, it reports paths as given
  and applies no allowlist.
documents.requirements/R-SECRET-009.md:
# R-SECRET-009

**R-SECRET-009** — When a scan flags, the files are then cleaned, and the
  scan runs again, the flagged `SecretScanResult` MUST remain recorded in
  `cache-manager` under its own key; the clean result is written under
  a different key and never overwrites it (as `R-LICENSE-007`).
documents.requirements/R-SECRET-010.md:
# R-SECRET-010

**R-SECRET-010** — `gate_version(repo_root)` MUST return exactly the
  `gate_version` that `scan(repo_root)` would report (`R-SECRET-006`).
  It MUST NOT scan any file, call `cache-manager`, or write anything.
  This is how a caller learns the scanner's current version without
  running a scan (`D163`).
documents.requirements/R-SECRET-011.md:
# R-SECRET-011

**R-SECRET-011** — `main(argv)` MUST implement `interface/cli.md`
  exactly: the full-scan, `precommit`, and `propose` forms, both
  flag-value forms, repeatable `--files`, the defaults, JSON and text
  output, exit `1` when the result is `flagged`, `0` otherwise, and `2`
  for every usage error that document lists (`D162`).
documents.requirements/R-SECRET-012.md:
# R-SECRET-012

**R-SECRET-012** — A finding MUST be suppressed only by an exact entry in
  `<repo_root>/.secret-allowlist.json`, and by nothing else. The file is
  scanned like every other file (`R-SECRET-001`), never exempted. It is
  a JSON object with exactly the keys `version` (the integer `1`) and
  `entries` (a list). Each entry has exactly `file`, `type`,
  `hashed_secret`, and `reason`:

  - `file` — a repo-relative path of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . / -` only, with no
    leading `/` or `..` segment: never a pattern;
  - `type` — a finding's `rule_id`;
  - `hashed_secret` — `"sha1:"` plus 40 lowercase hex digits, the SHA-1
    of the secret;
  - `reason` — `"planted-fixture"`, valid only for a `file` under
    `verification/` or `specs/`, or `"public-constant"`, valid only for
    `type` `"Hex High Entropy String"`.

  A finding is suppressed iff some entry matches its `file`, type, and
  `"sha1:"` plus its secret's SHA-1, all exactly, and is then listed in
  `allowed`; an entry matching nothing goes in `unused_allowlist_entries`
  and never blocks.

  **Sealed.** An otherwise valid file with no entries needs no seal; one with entries is honored only if
  `sha256:` plus the SHA-256 hex of its exact bytes equals the
  `allowlist_sha256` frontmatter value of the highest-numbered
  `specs/decisions/D<N>.md` that is `ratified` and has that key. With no
  such decision or another hash it is invalid (below): an edit is inert
  until a new decision records its hash (`D195`).

  **Fail closed.** An absent file allows nothing. A file that is not
  valid JSON, has any other key, has any entry breaking a rule above, or
  is unsealed invalidates the **whole** allowlist: no entry is honored,
  every finding is reported, and one extra match is added with `rule_id`
  `"allowlist-invalid"`, `risk_tier` `"high"`, `file`
  `".secret-allowlist.json"`, `line` `1` (`D168`).

```

```

Loads the corpus with `corpus-loader`'s `load_corpus(repo_root)`, from
`<repo_root>/gen/corpus-loader/` or the same path under the tool root,
the parent of the nearest `gen` directory above this module's own file
(`D199`), and returns this component's findings. Each is a dict with
exactly `rule_id` (the requirement that produced it), `severity`

documents.requirements/R-SIZE-001.md:
# R-SIZE-001

**R-SIZE-001** — The linter MUST compute the eight `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md`
  §4 size-cap dimensions per component (`generated_code_loc`,
  `component_doc_words`, `requirement_count`, `interface_surface`,
  `fan_out`, `fan_in`, and — since `D17` — `guarantee_count`,
  `acceptance_count`) and report each at `warn` or `fail` severity per
  the published thresholds. `component_doc_words` MUST be queried from
  the `component_size` view (`specs/architecture/graph-query-engine.md`'s
  "Query surface" section, `D13`), never recomputed independently —
  `R-GRAPH-009` queries the same view, one definition, not two to drift.
documents.requirements/R-SIZE-002.md:
# R-SIZE-002

**R-SIZE-002** — The linter MUST emit a distinct warning when two or more
  of R-SIZE-001's size-cap dimensions are over their *warn* threshold for
  the same component at once — naming which dimensions and their current
  values, and pointing at `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §4's decomposition-signal
  guidance. Keyed off *warn*, it surfaces the signal before a hard-fail
  forces the question; it MUST NOT itself ever hard-fail.
documents.requirements/R-SIZE-003.md:
# R-SIZE-003

**R-SIZE-003** — The linter MUST additionally check each individual file
  under `requirements/` and `acceptance/` against a per-file word count
  (warn above 250, fail above 500), distinct from R-SIZE-001's
  `component_doc_words` aggregate — naming the specific file, not just the
  bundle total. Each such file is meant to be one atomic unit (D1); one
  running long is a signal an aggregate cannot isolate.
documents.requirements/R-SIZE-004.md:
# R-SIZE-004

**R-SIZE-004** — A component's `Purpose` section MUST stay within a
  per-section word cap (warn above 80, fail above 150) — `SPEC_
  GUIDELINES.md` §3.4's "one paragraph" rule, checked mechanically.
  A long `Purpose` is several paragraphs disguised as one, the same
  signal `R-SIZE-003` gives for an oversized file.

id: comp-spec-bundle-assembler
title: Spec Bundle Assembler
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-graph-query-engine, comp-spec-linter]
realizes: [P-ZERO-EDIT]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
