# Spec Bundle Assembler

## Purpose

Assembles a component's full generation input — its own `component.md` +
`requirements/` + `interface/` + `constraints.md`, its dependencies'
`interface/` content and `Purpose` text, its referenced `specs/vars/`
declarations, and `specs/glossary.md` — into one payload (`SpecBundle`).
Reused by canonical generation and hint-mode previews — one assembly
implementation, not two.

## Scope

**In scope:** reading and concatenating the right files for a given
component id; computing `spec_bundle_hash`; the cold-vs-hint distinction
at the bundle level; including each dependency's `Purpose` text
alongside its `interface/` content (`R-ASSEMBLE-010`), so a generating
model sees not just a dependency's contract but what it's for.

## Rationale

The cold-vs-hint split traces to the original brainstorm.

**Out of scope:** calling any model (`generator`'s job); deciding *whether*
to regenerate (`impact-analyzer`'s job); verifying anything.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

Every criterion is `kind: generated-test`, over the synthetic corpus the
"Test fixtures" section of the library interface defines.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

- ~~Whether `spec_bundle_hash` should hash the files' raw bytes or a
  normalized form (e.g. with trailing whitespace stripped)~~ — resolved:
  raw bytes, permanently, not provisionally. Normalizing the hash itself
  was rejected once a concrete risk surfaced: these are Markdown files, and
  Markdown is not whitespace-insensitive (two-or-more trailing spaces are
  CommonMark's hard-line-break syntax; indentation is load-bearing inside
  nested lists and code fences) — there is no universally-safe
  normalization rule to hash against instead, so "ignore whitespace
  differences" risks silently treating two *meaningfully* different
  bundles as identical. The cache-hit-rate concern this question raised is
  real but belongs at a different layer: `spec-linter`'s new R-LINT-019
  rejects trailing whitespace outright, so the cosmetic diff never reaches
  a committed file in the first place — the hash stays simple and
  trustworthy, and the cache-hit benefit is real rather than approximate.

## Change log

Each decision holds its full rationale.

- Initial draft; first implementation hand-written, `depends_on` gains
  `comp-graph-query-engine`.
- `D37`: `dependency_usage` (`R-ASSEMBLE-011`). `D60`: a sealed
  dependency's card reads its `source_path`.
- `D69`: the target's own Rationale, Open questions and Change log are
  excluded (`R-ASSEMBLE-001`).
- `D100`: `CriterionBundle.dependency_interfaces`. `D101`: corpus
  structure comes only from `spec-linter` (`R-ASSEMBLE-012`).
- `D109`, `D118`: cold-generated; the hand-written suite retired.
  `D114`: one level of transitive types (`R-ASSEMBLE-013`).
- `D177`: `AC-ASSEMBLE-011`'s failure traced to its test's fixture.
- `D207`: the synthetic corpus every criterion uses is stated once, in
  the library interface.
documents.constraints.md:
# Spec Bundle Assembler — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Determinism.** Same corpus content, byte-for-byte, MUST always produce
  the same `SpecBundle`. Required for `spec_bundle_hash` to be a valid
  cache key (`D5`/`D30`).
- **Performance.** Assembling one component's bundle MUST complete in well
  under 1 second on reference hardware — this runs on every generation call
  (canonical and every hint-mode preview), so it must stay negligible
  relative to the model call it precedes.
- **No network access, no model calls.** Pure file I/O and hashing.
- **Isolation between modes.** A `cold`-mode bundle's non-`hint_code` fields
  MUST be identical to what a `hint`-mode call for the same component would
  produce — `hint_code` is strictly additive, never a substitute for any
  cold-mode field.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs assemble <component-id> [--mode=cold|hint] [--repo-root=<dir>] [--format=json|text]
```

- `<component-id>` — the component's `component.md` frontmatter `id`.
- `--mode` — `cold` (default; canonical bundle only) or `hint` (adds
  `hint_code`, R-ASSEMBLE-008).
- `--format` — `text` (summary) or `json` (the `SpecBundle` schema below).

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Bundle assembled. |
| `1` | Precondition failure — corpus not lint-clean (R-ASSEMBLE-005). |
| `2` | Usage error (unknown component id, bad `--mode`). |
documents.interface/data/CriterionBundle.md:
# `CriterionBundle`

```json
{
  "component_id": "comp-foo",
  "criterion_id": "AC-FOO-003",
  "covers": "R-FOO-003",
  "criterion_text": "<Given/When/Then prose>",
  "requirement_text": "<the covered R-id's own text from requirements/>",
  "interface": "<interface/ content>",
  "glossary": "<specs/glossary.md body>",
  "dependency_interfaces": { "comp-bar": "<bar/interface/ content>" }
}
```

A dataclass with these fields in this order, `dependency_interfaces`
defaulting to `{}`, that also reads as a mapping (`bundle["covers"]`,
`bundle.get("covers")`), as `SpecBundle` does.

Narrower than `SpecBundle` by design (R-ASSEMBLE-009) — `test-author`'s
consumer of this schema.
documents.interface/data/SpecBundle.md:
# `SpecBundle`

```json
{
  "component_id": "comp-foo",
  "spec_bundle_hash": "sha256:...",
  "spec": "<component.md body + requirements/ content>",
  "interface": "<interface/ content>",
  "constraints": "<constraints.md body>",
  "dependency_interfaces": { "comp-bar": "<bar/interface/ content>" },
  "dependency_context": { "comp-bar": "<bar's Purpose section text>" },
  "dependency_usage": { "comp-bar": "<bar's real, importable module path + public symbol signatures/docstrings, or \"\" if bar has no real code yet>" },
  "vars": { "VAR-FOO-URL": "<the var declaration's body>" },
  "glossary": "<specs/glossary.md body>",
  "hint_code": null
}
```

`hint_code` is `null` in `cold` mode; in `hint` mode it holds the component's
current `gen/<component>/` file contents, keyed by relative path.

A dataclass with these fields in this order (the four dicts default to
`{}`, `glossary` to `""`, `hint_code` to `None`) that also reads as a
read-only mapping: `bundle["spec"]` and `bundle.get("spec")` work.
Each text field joins its documents' bodies, each stripped, empty ones
dropped, with one blank line between. `interface` ends with any
documents `R-ASSEMBLE-014` appends.
`dependency_context` (`R-ASSEMBLE-010`) holds each dependency's `Purpose`
only. `dependency_usage` (`R-ASSEMBLE-011`) is introspected from a
dependency's real code, `""` when it has none, and nothing flows the
other way. `spec_bundle_hash` is defined in `R-ASSEMBLE-007`.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
assemble(component_id: str, repo_root: Path, mode: str = "cold") -> SpecBundle
assemble_criterion(component_id: str, criterion_id: str, repo_root: Path) -> CriterionBundle
```

Both are pure functions over the filesystem state at `repo_root` — no
network access, no model calls, no side effects.

## Test fixtures

Every criterion's synthetic corpus lives under a fresh temporary
`repo_root`, and `assemble`/`assemble_criterion` lint it first
(`R-ASSEMBLE-005`), so it MUST pass lint. `spec_linter` is never importable by name; a test
that lints its fixture first loads it from the tool root, as `assemble`
does (`R-ASSEMBLE-015`):

```python
import importlib.util, sys
from pathlib import Path
gen = next(p for p in Path(spec_bundle_assembler.__file__).resolve().parents if p.name == "gen")
base = gen / "spec-linter"
path = base / "spec_linter.py" if (base / "spec_linter.py").is_file() else base / "spec_linter" / "__init__.py"
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("spec_linter", path)
spec_linter = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
sys.modules["spec_linter"] = spec_linter
spec.loader.exec_module(spec_linter)
assert spec_linter.lint(None, repo_root).hard_failures == 0
```
Each file is written exactly as shown, `---` in column 0 of line 1,
never through `textwrap.dedent` over interpolated text.

`specs/glossary.md`:

```
# Glossary

- **Foo** — a test term.
```

`specs/components/foo/component.md` (a dependent adds
`depends_on: [comp-foo]` in place of `[]`, with its own id and
`source_path`):

```
---
id: comp-foo
title: Foo
status: draft
owners: [team-a]
sealed: true
source_path: legacy/foo/
depends_on: []
---

# Foo

## Purpose

Foo doubles a number.
```

`requirements/R-FOO-001.md`: `# R-FOO-001`, a blank line, then
`**R-FOO-001** — \`foo(x)\` MUST return \`2 * x\`.`

`acceptance/AC-FOO-001.md`:

````
# AC-FOO-001

Covers: R-FOO-001
Kind: generated-test

```gherkin
Given x = 2
When foo(x) is called
Then it returns 4
```
````

`interface/library.md`: `# Library` and a fenced `foo(x: int) -> int`.
`constraints.md`: `# Constraints` and `None.`

Deleting the `Kind:` line from an acceptance file is a hard lint
failure, the way to build a corpus `assemble` refuses. A sealed
component's real code goes under its `source_path`
(`legacy/foo/foo.py`), never `gen/`.
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-001.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-001

**R-ASSEMBLE-001** — The bundle MUST include the target component's own
  `component.md`, everything under `requirements/`, everything under
  `interface/`, and `constraints.md`. It MUST NOT include anything under
  `acceptance/`. This is deliberate, not an oversight: the generation model
  seeing its own acceptance criteria risks overfitting to specific test
  assertions rather than genuinely implementing the normative requirements
  — already implied by `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §6 step 2's bundle definition,
  made an explicit, enforced requirement here for the first time.

  **"The target's own `component.md`" excludes that file's own
  `## Rationale`, `## Open questions`, and `## Change log` sections**
  (`D69`, measured: 15-60% of a real component.md's body, depending on
  the component). `R-ASSEMBLE-002` already applies "a dependent needs
  the contract, not the internal rationale" to every *dependency* this
  bundle includes; this closes the one place that same principle was
  never applied to the target itself, even though these three sections
  explain *why* past decisions were made, not what the model must
  build. `Purpose`/`Scope`/`Definitions`/the `Behavior`/`Interfaces`/
  `Data`/`Acceptance criteria`/`Non-functional constraints` pointer
  text are unaffected — unlike a dependency's `component.md`, the
  target's own Scope and Definitions genuinely describe what to build,
  not just its public contract.
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-002.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-002

**R-ASSEMBLE-002** — For each id in the component's `depends_on`, the
  bundle MUST include that component's `interface/` content only — never
  its `requirements/` or `constraints.md`, and never any part of its
  `component.md` except the single, narrow exception `R-ASSEMBLE-010`
  names. A dependent needs the contract, not the internal rationale;
  this is the same interface-vs-internal distinction `impact-analyzer`
  already established for blast-radius propagation (R-IMPACT-002/003),
  applied here to what a dependent is allowed to *see*, not just what
  triggers its regeneration.
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-003.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-003

**R-ASSEMBLE-003** — For each id in the component's `uses_var`, the bundle
  MUST include that `specs/vars/` declaration's full content (name, type,
  required/optional, description, sensitivity — never a value, because
  there is none to include).
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-004.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-004

**R-ASSEMBLE-004** — The bundle MUST include the full current content of
  `specs/glossary.md`.
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-005.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-005

**R-ASSEMBLE-005** — Assembly MUST fail (refuse to produce a bundle,
  returning a precondition-failure result, not a partial one) if the corpus
  does not pass `spec-linter` cleanly at hard-fail severity. Mirrors
  `impact-analyzer`'s R-IMPACT-007.
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-006.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-006

**R-ASSEMBLE-006** — The assembled bundle MUST be a deterministic function
  of corpus content — the same spec/interface/constraints/vars/glossary
  bytes always produce the same bundle bytes. Required for `spec_bundle_hash`
  to mean anything as a cache key (`D5`/`D30`).
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-007.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-007

**R-ASSEMBLE-007** — `spec_bundle_hash` MUST be `"sha256:"` plus the
  SHA-256 hex digest of one byte stream built from the files the bundle
  reads, so every correct implementation computes the same value. The
  stream is the mode (`cold` or `hint`) and a NUL byte, then, for each
  path below in sorted order without duplicates, the repo-relative POSIX
  path in UTF-8, a NUL byte, the file's raw bytes, and a NUL byte:

  - the target's `component.md`, `constraints.md`, and every `.md` file
    under its `requirements/` and `interface/`;
  - each document `R-ASSEMBLE-014` appends;
  - for each `depends_on` component, its `component.md`, every `.md` file
    under its `interface/`, and every file under its code directory
    (`source_path` when sealed, else `gen/<slug>/`);
  - each type file `R-ASSEMBLE-013` appends, each `uses_var` declaration,
    and `specs/glossary.md`;
  - in `hint` mode, every file under `gen/<target>/`.

  A code directory never contributes a file whose name starts with `.`
  or anything under `__pycache__`, so writing a manifest there changes no
  hash. A missing file or directory contributes nothing.
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-008.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-008

**R-ASSEMBLE-008** — In `hint` mode (vs. the default `cold` mode), the
  bundle MUST additionally include the component's *current*
  `gen/<component>/` content as a clearly separate `hint_code` field — never
  merged into, or indistinguishable from, the cold bundle's own fields. This
  is the original design's hint-vs-cold distinction, concretely implemented
  at the bundle level for the first time; nothing before this assigned
  which component actually produces the two different payloads that
  distinction describes.
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-009.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-009

**R-ASSEMBLE-009** — MUST also expose a narrower assembly entry point
  producing a `CriterionBundle` — one acceptance criterion's own text, its
  covered requirement's text, the target component's `interface/` content,
  the glossary, and `dependency_interfaces` (`D100`, below) — for
  `test-author`'s use. A `CriterionBundle` MUST NOT include the target
  component's `gen/<component>/` content, any other file under
  `requirements/`, or `constraints.md` — narrower than the `SpecBundle`
  R-ASSEMBLE-001–008 describe, not a variant of it, because
  `test-author`'s independence requirement (its own R-AUTHOR-002) depends
  on it seeing *less* than `generator` sees, not the same bundle with
  something added.

  **`dependency_interfaces` is the one deliberate exception to "less,
  never more"** (`D100`): for each id in the target component's own
  `depends_on`, its full `interface/` content, exactly the same content
  and the same `R-ASSEMBLE-002` rule `SpecBundle.dependency_interfaces`
  already follows. This is a third party's already-public,
  already-documented contract, never the target's own implementation —
  it does not let a test author see anything about the component under
  test it couldn't already see, only lets a fake it writes for a
  *dependency* match that dependency's real, documented signature and
  return shape instead of guessing. Found only once three real
  `generated-test` authorings for a component with real dependencies
  guessed wrong about a dependency's call shape in three different ways
  (`D100`), despite every one of those shapes being fully documented
  and already available to `generator` via this exact mechanism.
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-010.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-010

**R-ASSEMBLE-010** — For each id in the component's `depends_on`, the
  bundle MUST also include that component's `Purpose` section text,
  leading and trailing whitespace stripped, as `dependency_context[id]`, read via `component_context`
  (`specs/architecture/graph-query-engine.md`, `D22`) — never read
  directly from the dependency's `component.md` by this component's own
  logic, and never any other part of `component.md`.

  This is the single, explicit exception `R-ASSEMBLE-002` names, scoped
  to exactly `Purpose` and nothing else: `D21` made `Purpose`
  dependent-safe by construction (no decision citations, no historical
  rationale, enforced by `R-LINT-024`), which is what makes handing it
  to a dependent safe in the first place. If a future need arises to
  share more of a dependency's `component.md`, that is a new decision
  with its own safety argument — this requirement does not imply one.
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-011.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-011

**R-ASSEMBLE-011** — For each id in the component's `depends_on`, the
  bundle MUST also include a mechanically-derived usage card as
  `dependency_usage[id]`: that dependency's module name and the
  directory it is loaded from, relative to `repo_root` with a trailing
  `/` (`gen/bar/`, or a sealed dependency's `source_path`), and — for each
  public top-level function or class its real module defines, by sorted
  name — its name, its `inspect.signature` text, and the first line of
  its docstring; one whose signature `inspect` cannot read (an exception
  class, say) is left out. No model call; derived by introspecting
  the dependency's own real, already-verified code (`inspect`-level
  facts: callable, signature, docstring — never source text, never
  anything from `acceptance/`).

  **Absent (an empty string) for a dependency with no real code yet** —
  the same graceful-degradation posture `component_provenance` already
  takes for a component with no `.provenance.json` (`R-GQE-005`): a
  spec-only dependency has nothing real to introspect, and that is
  expected state, not an error.

  **A `sealed` dependency's real code lives at its declared
  `source_path`, never under `gen/<dependency>/`** (`D60`): its card is
  built from `source_path` only, and is `""` when nothing is there.

  **Requires the dependency to already have been (re)generated before
  the dependent's bundle is assembled** — a developer running
  `hotdocs generate` across more than one component in the same change
  MUST do so in dependency order, dependencies before dependents
  (`D86`, `D91`, `D93`).

  **Deliberately one-directional — a dependency's bundle MUST NOT
  include anything about how its dependents use it.** Feeding call-site
  usage back would reintroduce a cycle `depends_on` keeps out and let
  calling patterns steer behavior instead of `interface/`. A missing
  contract is an `interface/` change, never a prompt input.
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-012.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-012

**R-ASSEMBLE-012** — `assemble`/`assemble_criterion` MUST read all
  corpus structure — every `component.md` frontmatter field,
  `depends_on`, the parsed contents of `requirements/`, `interface/`,
  `acceptance/`, everything `spec-linter`'s own `load_corpus` already
  parses — exclusively through that one call's returned `Corpus`/
  `Component` objects. Neither function MUST independently re-parse
  any spec file's YAML frontmatter or Markdown structure, and MUST NOT
  introduce a new third-party dependency (a standalone YAML library,
  a Markdown parser, or similar) for anything a declared dependency
  — `spec-linter`, reached via DuckDB's own `yaml` community extension
  through its own dependency on `graph-query-engine` — already
  provides.

  **Found only once a real candidate reinvented frontmatter parsing
  from scratch** (`D101`): `R-ASSEMBLE-005` already required *checking*
  that the corpus passes `spec-linter` cleanly, but nothing required
  *reusing* that same call's already-parsed result for everything else
  assembly needs, leaving room for a candidate to re-parse the same
  content independently — and reach for a package (`PyYAML`) this
  corpus has never installed, since every other component that reads
  YAML frontmatter does so through DuckDB's SQL-level extension
  instead, never a Python package.
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-013.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-013

**R-ASSEMBLE-013** — `dependency_interfaces`' entry for each
  dependency MUST also resolve, one level deep, any data type that
  dependency's own `interface/` content names but does not itself
  own. For each identifier (a maximal run matching `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`)
  in the dependency's `interface/` `.md` files that it does not own as
  `interface/data/<identifier>.md`, search the whole corpus (not only the
  target's own `depends_on`) for exactly one component whose
  `interface/data/<TypeName>.md` exists; if found, append that type's
  own content to the same dependency's entry, under a clearly labeled
  heading naming the type and its real owning component — never
  merged in as if the dependency owned it. Ambiguous (more than one
  owner) or unresolved (no owner) names are skipped silently — never
  a guess. Expansion is one level only: a referenced type's own
  further references are never followed (`D114`).
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-014.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-014

**R-ASSEMBLE-014** — A line of the target's `interface/library.md` that
  begins `Implements:` names, each in backticks, the documents whose rules
  the component implements: `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` or a file under
  `specs/architecture/`. `assemble` MUST append each named document's full
  text to `SpecBundle.interface`, and `assemble_criterion` to
  `CriterionBundle.interface`, in the listed order, each as a blank line, the line
  `## Implements: <path>`, a blank line, then the document's text. A named path that does not exist raises
  `PreconditionFailure`. A dependency's own `Implements:` line is never
  followed.
documents.requirements/R-ASSEMBLE-015.md:
# R-ASSEMBLE-015

**R-ASSEMBLE-015** — `assemble` and `assemble_criterion` MUST load
  `spec-linter` and `graph-query-engine` from `<repo_root>/gen/<slug>/`
  when that directory exists, and otherwise from the same path under the
  tool root, the parent of the nearest `gen` directory above this
  module's own file (`D199`). A project holds none of the tool's
  components, so without the fallback no project could assemble a
  bundle.

documents.component.md:
---
id: comp-spec-completeness-assistant
title: Spec Completeness Assistant
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-spec-linter, comp-impact-analyzer, comp-spec-bundle-assembler, comp-generator, comp-llm-endpoint]
realizes: [P-AMBIGUITY-GATE]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
---

# Spec Completeness Assistant

## Purpose

Helps a developer land a *complete* spec change on a feature branch —
dependencies updated, no logical discrepancies, no redundancies — using
hint-mode previews to evaluate completeness **before** a change is even
submitted to the real merge pipeline.

## Rationale

The assist agent the original brainstorm describes but never names. This is the component
`notes/metrics.md` already assumes exists (its "Completeness-agent
confidence" and "Assist-agent acceptance rate" metrics predate this
spec) but that, until now, had never actually been specced.

## Scope

**In scope:** running the cheap, deterministic checks first (lint, blast
radius); producing a hint-mode preview; producing a judgment-based
completeness assessment and a redundancy/overlap check.

**Out of scope, and load-bearing, not incidental:** gating anything. This
component's output is advisory only — it is never read by
`provenance-tracker`'s own checks or any other component's `depends_on`,
and it has no mechanism to block a merge. The actual gates
(`spec-linter` at hard-fail severity, `verifier-orchestrator`, the
compliance scans) are the only things that can do that; this component
exists entirely on the feature-branch side of the cold-vs-hint split,
never the merge side. Also out of scope: **re-deciding anything a ratified
spec already declares** — same boundary `verifier-orchestrator`/
`test-author` observe for a criterion's `kind:`. This component may
*suggest* a spec change before ratification; it has no standing to override
one after.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

Mixed `kind`, and deliberately the opposite mix from most of this corpus:
every criterion is a `generated-test` except R-ASSIST-004/005 — this
component's actual reason to exist — which are `llm-judge`. Unlike every coordination component specced so far
(`verifier-orchestrator`, `merge-orchestrator`), this one's core value
genuinely *is* judgment, not dispatch around it — a useful contrast case
against the corpus's usual "prefer compiled" guidance rather than
another confirmation of it.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

- Initial draft.
- `D28`: defined `redundancy_flags`' populated-entry shape
  (`{new_requirement, overlaps_with, rationale}`, `R-ASSIST-005`).
- `D155`–`D157`: hard-fail lint short-circuits; the dependency call
  order and signature are pinned; no model means no model call at all.
- `D160`: `R-ASSIST-009` covers the CLI; `R-ASSIST-010` pins the
  model-call response contract. Cold-generated and landed
  (`mutation_score` 0.81).
- `D201`: `R-ASSIST-011` covers the tool-root fallback (`D199`);
  dependencies are flat modules; more response-parsing cases.
documents.constraints.md:
# Spec Completeness Assistant — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Never a gate.** This is a structural property, not a convention to be
  followed: no code path in this component, and no entry in any other
  component's `depends_on` or `provenance-tracker`'s own checks, gives
  it any way to block a merge. If a future change ever needs this
  component's judgment to be load-bearing, that is a different, new
  capability — not a tightening of this one.
- **Fast enough for iteration.** This runs repeatedly during feature-branch
  development, not once at commit time — it SHOULD be noticeably cheaper
  and faster than running `hotdocs generate` against every impacted
  component, since hint mode (R-ASSIST-003) exists specifically to make
  that true.
- **Graceful degradation, not a hard model requirement.** Per R-ASSIST-007,
  this component keeps producing useful output (lint + blast radius + hint
  preview) even with no model configured at all — unlike most gates in this
  corpus, whose primary model is effectively required (`VAR-ANTHROPIC-API-
  KEY` is `required: yes`), this component's *judgment* half is allowed to
  be fully absent without the tool becoming useless.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs assist --changed=<spec-id>... [--repo-root=<dir>] [--format=json|text] [--model=<model>]
```

`main` receives the tokens after `assist`: `main(["--changed=R-FOO-001"])`.
Every flag takes its value either as `--flag=value` or as the next
argument (`--flag value`); a flag given last with no value is a usage
error.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Report produced. Always `0` on a non-error run — this tool never fails a build; a low completeness score is reported, not a failure exit. |
| `1` | A hard-fail `spec-linter` finding was present (R-ASSIST-001) — reported, not blocking anything outside this CLI invocation itself. |
| `2` | Usage error. |
documents.interface/data/CompletenessReport.md:
# `CompletenessReport`

```json
{
  "lint_findings": [
    { "rule_id": "R-LINT-003", "severity": "fail", "file": "specs/components/foo/component.md", "line": 12, "message": "depends_on references 'comp-bar', which does not exist" }
  ],
  "predicted_blast_radius": ["comp-foo"],
  "hint_previews": { "comp-foo": { "...": "a hint-mode SpecBundle-derived preview" } },
  "completeness_score": 0.9,
  "completeness_rationale": "...",
  "redundancy_flags": [
    { "new_requirement": "R-FOO-005", "overlaps_with": "R-BAR-002", "rationale": "Both require retry exhaustion to surface as a distinct failure mode, worded differently." }
  ],
  "degraded": false
}
```

`lint_findings` entries are exactly `spec-linter`'s own `Finding` shape
(`interface/data/LintReport.md`'s `findings[]`, bundle-visible via
`depends_on`) — passed through unchanged, never restated or
summarized here: a finding that is a dict stays that dict, with no key
added (no `rationale` when lint gave none) or removed.

`completeness_score`, `completeness_rationale`, and `redundancy_flags` are
`null`/empty with `degraded: true` when no model was configured
(R-ASSIST-007) — never silently omitted. Each `redundancy_flags` entry is
`{new_requirement, overlaps_with, rationale}` (`R-ASSIST-005`):
`new_requirement` and `overlaps_with` are both `R-id`s, and `rationale`
is always present on a populated entry — there is no "fired but
unexplained" state, since an entry exists here only because a real
judgment call actually flagged it.
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
assist(
    changed_ids: list[str], repo_root: Path, model: str | None = None,
    *, llm_backend=None,
) -> CompletenessReport
```

`model` omitted (the default) runs in degraded mode, per R-ASSIST-007.
When present, dispatched via `llm-endpoint` (D18) — this component holds
no credential of its own. `llm_backend` is passed straight through to
`generator` and `llm-endpoint` unchanged, the same injection point
every other model-calling component in this corpus exposes (`D156`).

Each dependency is one flat module file, `<repo_root>/gen/<slug>/<module>.py`,
or the tool root's when that directory is absent (`R-ASSIST-011`), called in
this order, stopping early per `R-ASSIST-001`:

1. `spec-linter`'s `lint(paths, repo_root)`
2. `impact-analyzer`'s `compute_blast_radius(changed_ids, repo_root)`
3. for each component in the blast radius: `spec-bundle-assembler`'s
   `assemble(component_id, repo_root=..., mode="hint")`, then, with a
   `model` only, `generator`'s `generate(bundle, model, None,
   repo_root=..., llm_backend=...)`
4. with a `model` only: `llm-endpoint`'s `complete(prompt, model,
   backend=llm_backend)`, called exactly twice — completeness first,
   then redundancy — each response parsed per `R-ASSIST-010`

Any stand-in for these dependencies must provide each function this
list names, with the full parameter list of its real signature (a
`lint` stand-in takes `(paths, repo_root, strict=False, judge=None)`).
documents.requirements/R-ASSIST-001.md:
# R-ASSIST-001

**R-ASSIST-001** — MUST run `spec-linter` against the draft spec change
  first. If any finding has `severity` `"fail"`, `assist` MUST return
  immediately with `lint_findings` populated and nothing else run:
  `predicted_blast_radius` `[]`, `hint_previews` `{}`,
  `completeness_score`/`completeness_rationale` `null`,
  `redundancy_flags` `[]`, and no model call of any kind, including
  `generator`'s hint preview. Same "cheap, deterministic gate first"
  ordering `hotdocs generate`'s own workflow uses, on the feature-branch
  side.

  Stopping, not merely ordering, is load-bearing (`D155`): `assist`
  returns one report, so "surfaced before" is only observable as a
  stop, and running a paid judgment or preview against a spec that
  already hard-fails lint spends money on a result the developer must
  discard anyway. `degraded` still reports only whether a model was
  configured (`R-ASSIST-007`); a caller tells a lint halt apart by the
  `"fail"`-severity entry in `lint_findings`.
documents.requirements/R-ASSIST-002.md:
# R-ASSIST-002

**R-ASSIST-002** — MUST compute the predicted blast radius via
  `impact-analyzer` for the draft change and surface it — this is the
  "Predicted blast radius" metric (`notes/metrics.md`, Ideation phase),
  which had no component computing it until now.
documents.requirements/R-ASSIST-003.md:
# R-ASSIST-003

**R-ASSIST-003** — MUST produce a hint-mode preview for each component
  in the predicted blast radius — the original design's exact described
  use of hint mode, concretely implemented here for the first time.
  `spec-bundle-assembler` assembles each bundle in `hint` mode; with a
  `model` configured, `generator` then generates from it and that
  result is the preview. With no `model` (`R-ASSIST-007`), `generator`
  is never called — it cannot run without a model — and the preview is
  the hint-mode bundle itself (`D157`).
documents.requirements/R-ASSIST-004.md:
# R-ASSIST-004

**R-ASSIST-004** — MUST produce a completeness confidence score (0.0–1.0)
  with structured rationale: whether touched requirements have present,
  non-trivial acceptance criteria; whether a dependent's `interface/`
  content looks like it needs a matching update that wasn't made; whether the
  change's `Definitions` entries conflict with the glossary (reusing
  `spec-linter`'s R-LINT-011/015 distinction — this component does not
  reimplement that detection, it surfaces `spec-linter`'s own findings
  plus whatever this component's own broader judgment adds on top).
documents.requirements/R-ASSIST-005.md:
# R-ASSIST-005

**R-ASSIST-005** — MUST run a redundancy/overlap check — does this change
  restate behavior already specified elsewhere in the corpus — matching the
  "Overlap / duplication score" metric (`notes/metrics.md`, Ideation
  phase). Judgment-based: detecting that two differently-worded passages
  describe the same behavior is semantic, not structural, the same category
  of problem `spec-linter`'s R-LINT-015 was split out for.

  Each populated entry in `redundancy_flags` MUST be `{new_requirement,
  overlaps_with, rationale}`: `new_requirement` is the draft change's own
  `R-id` (from `changed_ids`), `overlaps_with` is the pre-existing `R-id`
  it restates, and `rationale` is required — never optional — since an
  entry only ever exists here because a real judgment call actually
  fired and flagged it (unlike `VerificationReport.criteria[]`, which
  mixes ran and not-ran entries in one array, `redundancy_flags` holds
  only fired findings; `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §5's "an `llm-judge`
  criterion MUST emit structured rationale alongside its verdict" rule
  applies with no exception here).
documents.requirements/R-ASSIST-006.md:
# R-ASSIST-006

**R-ASSIST-006** — This component's output MUST NOT gate anything. It
  MUST NOT be read by `provenance-tracker`'s `check_readiness` or
  appear in any component's `depends_on` in a way that could influence
  a pass/fail decision, and its result MUST have no mechanism by which
  it can block a merge — advisory only, by construction, not by
  developer discipline.
documents.requirements/R-ASSIST-007.md:
# R-ASSIST-007

**R-ASSIST-007** — When no model is configured, MUST make no model
  call of any kind — neither `llm-endpoint` directly nor `generator`
  (which dispatches through it) — and MUST still run R-ASSIST-001–003:
  lint findings, predicted blast radius, and hint previews, each
  preview being the hint-mode bundle alone (`R-ASSIST-003`). It MUST
  report R-ASSIST-004/005 as skipped: `degraded` true,
  `completeness_score`/`completeness_rationale` null,
  `redundancy_flags` empty. The same graceful-degradation posture
  `spec-linter`'s R-LINT-015 established, now a further instance.
documents.requirements/R-ASSIST-008.md:
# R-ASSIST-008

**R-ASSIST-008** — A developer's response to this component's suggestions
  (accepted / overridden) SHOULD be recorded to feed the "Assist-agent
  acceptance rate" metric (`notes/metrics.md`) — but *capturing and storing*
  that response is explicitly out of scope for this component's own
  behavior (a UI/tooling-layer concern, not specced here); this requirement
  only establishes that the hook for doing so exists.
documents.requirements/R-ASSIST-009.md:
# R-ASSIST-009

**R-ASSIST-009** — `main(argv)` MUST implement `interface/cli.md`
  exactly, with `argv` the tokens after `assist` (`hotdocs-cli`
  strips the verb): `--changed`
  (repeatable or comma-separated, required), `--repo-root` (default the
  current directory), `--format=json|text` (default `text`), and
  `--model` (omitted means degraded mode; given, its value is passed to
  `assist` as `model`). Each flag accepts `--flag=value` or
  `--flag value`. Exit `0` once a report is produced, `1` when any
  `lint_findings` entry has `severity` `"fail"`, `2` on a usage error
  (no `--changed`, an invalid `--format`, an unknown argument, a flag
  given last with no value). `--format=json` prints the
  `CompletenessReport` as JSON; `text` prints a human-readable rendering
  naming every lint finding's `rule_id`, every predicted-blast-radius
  component, and, when present, the `completeness_score`.

  Covered from the start of its own repair rather than discovered again
  later: three other components' CLIs went uncovered until mutation
  testing exposed them (`D130`, `D136`, `D145`), and this one did too
  (`D160`).
documents.requirements/R-ASSIST-010.md:
# R-ASSIST-010

**R-ASSIST-010** — With a `model` configured, `assist` MUST make exactly
  two `llm-endpoint` `complete` calls, completeness first, then
  redundancy, and parse each response's `text` as JSON of exactly this
  shape:

  ```json
  {"completeness_score": 0.9, "completeness_rationale": "..."}
  {"redundancy_flags": [{"new_requirement": "R-FOO-005", "overlaps_with": "R-BAR-002", "rationale": "..."}]}
  ```

  A response wrapped in a Markdown code fence is unwrapped first. A
  `completeness_score` outside 0.0–1.0 is clamped to that range; a
  completeness response missing either field, with a score that is not
  a number (a boolean is not), or with an empty
  `completeness_rationale`, does not parse as that shape. A
  redundancy entry missing any of its three fields, or with an empty
  one, is dropped (`R-ASSIST-005`). If a call returns a
  `model_call_error`, or its text does not parse as that shape, that
  call's own fields stay `null`/`[]` — never guessed — and `assist`
  still returns normally; the other call's result is unaffected.

  These are the deterministic mechanics around the model call,
  testable with a faked `llm-endpoint`; whether the judgment itself is
  good is `AC-ASSIST-004`/`005`'s concern (`D160`).
documents.requirements/R-ASSIST-011.md:
# R-ASSIST-011

**R-ASSIST-011** — `assist` MUST load each dependency from
  `<repo_root>/gen/<slug>/` when that directory exists, and otherwise
  from the same path under the tool root: the parent of the nearest
  directory named `gen` above this module's own file (`D199`). A
  project made by `hotdocs init` has no copy of the tool's components.

id: comp-spec-linter
title: Spec Linter
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-graph-query-engine, comp-corpus-loader, comp-citation-checker, comp-size-checker]
realizes: [P-AMBIGUITY-GATE]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
---

# Spec Linter

## Purpose

Mechanically validates a spec corpus against `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md`'s
structural, traceability, citation and size-cap rules, before anything
downstream (impact analysis, generation, verification) runs. It is the pipeline's first
gate and the component everything else assumes has already run.

## Scope

**In scope:** every rule in `requirements/`, one report and CLI that also
carry the findings of `citation-checker` and `size-checker`, and
re-exporting `corpus-loader`'s `load_corpus`.

**Out of scope:** generation; verifying generated code's actual
behavior. **Mostly free of model calls and judgment** — only
R-LINT-015 is a deliberate exception, about meaning.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

documents.constraints.md:
# Spec Linter — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Determinism.** The same spec bundle, byte for byte, MUST produce the
  same result for every rule but the `llm-judge` R-LINT-015, which is
  excluded from the cache-key contribution.
- **Performance.** The `compiled` rules together MUST finish in under 2
  seconds on reference hardware; R-LINT-015 has its own budget.
- **No network, no model calls,** except R-LINT-015, which with no model
  configured is `skipped`, never a silent pass or a crash.
- **Tested on real content,** not only synthetic fixtures (see
  `verification/spec-linter/BOOTSTRAP.md`).
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs lint [<path>...] [--format=json|text] [--strict] [--repo-root=<dir>]
```

`main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int` gets the tokens after `lint`
(`hotdocs-cli` strips the verb) and returns the exit code; `python -m
spec_linter` passes `sys.argv[1:]`.

- `<path>...` — files or directories under `specs/` to lint; default the
  whole `specs/` tree.
- `--format` — `text` (default) or `json` (a `LintReport`).
- `--strict` — `warn` findings count as failures too.
- `--repo-root` — the repository root; default the current git
  repository's.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | No `fail`-severity findings (`skipped` never fails). |
| `1` | ≥1 `fail`-severity finding. |
| `2` | Usage error (bad arguments, unreadable path). |
documents.interface/data/LintReport.md:
# `LintReport`

```json
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "rule_id": "R-LINT-003",
      "severity": "fail",
      "file": "specs/components/foo/component.md",
      "line": 12,
      "message": "depends_on references 'comp-bar', which does not exist"
    }
  ],
  "summary": { "hard_failures": 1, "warnings": 0, "skipped": 0 }
}
```

`lint` returns a `LintReport` dataclass: `findings`, a list of
`Finding(rule_id, severity, file, line, message, rationale=None)`
dataclasses, and read-only `hard_failures`, `warnings` and `skipped`
counts. Their `to_json()` gives the JSON above, with `rationale` only
when set. `severity` is `fail`, `warn` or `skipped` (R-LINT-015 with no
model). `rationale` is set only when an `llm-judge` evaluation ran
(`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §5).
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
lint(paths: list[Path] | None, repo_root: Path, strict: bool = False, judge=None) -> LintReport
load_corpus(repo_root: Path) -> Corpus
```

A pure function over the filesystem state at `repo_root` — no network
access, no model calls, no side effects. `paths=None` lints the whole
corpus. `judge` is optional, for `R-LINT-015`'s model-backed check;
omitted, it reports `skipped` rather than running or crashing. It is
called as `judge(term, local_text, glossary_text)` and returns
`(conflicts, rationale)`, a conflict when `conflicts` is true, or `None`
when it could not judge, also reported `skipped`.

`load_corpus` is `corpus-loader`'s, re-exported unchanged; `lint` and both
checkers load their corpus through it. `corpus-loader`, `citation-checker`
and `size-checker` load from `<repo_root>/gen/<slug>/`, or the same path
under the tool root (`D199`).

Implements: `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md`, `specs/architecture/graph-query-engine.md`
documents.requirements/R-LINT-001.md:
# R-LINT-001

**R-LINT-001** — The linter MUST verify that every spec file's frontmatter
  contains all fields `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §2 marks required for that
  document's type, correctly typed (e.g. `depends_on` is a list, `sealed` is a
  boolean).
documents.requirements/R-LINT-002.md:
# R-LINT-002

**R-LINT-002** — The linter MUST fail any spec with `status: ratified` that
  has a non-empty "Open questions" section, or lacks a `last_ratified_commit`.
documents.requirements/R-LINT-003.md:
# R-LINT-003

**R-LINT-003** — The linter MUST resolve every `depends_on`, `realizes`, and
  `uses_var` entry against the corpus and fail on any entry that does not
  resolve to an existing, non-`deprecated` spec id.
documents.requirements/R-LINT-004.md:
# R-LINT-004

**R-LINT-004** — The linter MUST verify the corpus-wide `depends_on` graph
  contains no cycles. A cycle's finding names every component on it by
  its `comp-<slug>` id.
documents.requirements/R-LINT-005.md:
# R-LINT-005

**R-LINT-005** — The linter MUST fail a component with `sealed: true` and no
  `source_path`, and MUST fail a component with `source_path` set but
  `sealed` false or absent.
documents.requirements/R-LINT-006.md:
# R-LINT-006

**R-LINT-006** — The linter MUST fail a non-`sealed` component with zero
  `realizes` entries.
documents.requirements/R-LINT-007.md:
# R-LINT-007

**R-LINT-007** — The linter MUST verify every file under a component's
  `requirements/` directory has a unique `R-<comp>-NNN` id (matching its
  own filename, per D1) and uses at least one RFC 2119 keyword.
documents.requirements/R-LINT-008.md:
# R-LINT-008

**R-LINT-008** — The linter MUST fail any `R-id` with zero covering
  acceptance criteria (forward traceability).
documents.requirements/R-LINT-009.md:
# R-LINT-009

**R-LINT-009** — The linter MUST fail any `Covers:` tag that does not
  resolve to a real `R-id` or `P-id` in the corpus (backward traceability).
documents.requirements/R-LINT-010.md:
# R-LINT-010

**R-LINT-010** — The linter MUST fail any acceptance criterion missing a
  `kind` or a complete Given/When/Then block.
documents.requirements/R-LINT-011.md:
# R-LINT-011

**R-LINT-011** — The linter MUST fail a `Definitions`-section entry for a
  glossary term whose local text is **near-verbatim identical** (normalized
  token-overlap ratio ≥ 0.8 against the glossary's own definition text) to
  `specs/glossary.md`'s definition — restating the definition is not a delta.
  This is a textual-similarity check only: deterministic, no model call, no
  judgment of meaning. (Resolved from an earlier, broader wording that didn't
  distinguish "restating" from "conflicting" — see R-LINT-015.)
documents.requirements/R-LINT-013.md:
# R-LINT-013

**R-LINT-013** — The linter MUST fail a `specs/vars/` declaration with
  `sensitivity: secret` that carries an `example` or `default` field.
documents.requirements/R-LINT-014.md:
# R-LINT-014

**R-LINT-014** — The linter MUST fail if more than one glossary-like file
  exists under `specs/` without a corresponding `architecture/`-level
  bounded-context split decision (`notes/initial-ideas.md`'s own D14).
documents.requirements/R-LINT-015.md:
# R-LINT-015

**R-LINT-015** — For a `Definitions`-section entry that names a glossary
  term but is *not* caught by R-LINT-011 (i.e. not a near-verbatim copy), the
  linter MUST run an `llm-judge` evaluation of whether the local text is
  consistent with (a permitted delta on) the glossary's definition, versus
  substantively conflicting with it (a redefinition in different words).
  A conflict MUST be reported as a `fail`-severity finding with structured
  rationale (per `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §5). **When no model is configured at
  all, this one requirement MUST be skipped with a visible, non-silent
  notice** — not treated as passing, not a crash.
documents.requirements/R-LINT-016.md:
# R-LINT-016

**R-LINT-016** — The linter MUST fail any unit file (under a component's
  `requirements/`, `interface/` — including `interface/data/` — or
  `acceptance/`, or its `constraints.md`) that carries a YAML frontmatter
  block at all. Frontmatter lives only on a component's `component.md`
  (D1, `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §2); a unit file's identity is its filename.
documents.requirements/R-LINT-017.md:
# R-LINT-017

**R-LINT-017** — The linter MUST verify every file under a component's
  `interface/guarantees/` directory has a unique `G-<comp>-NNN` id, its
  `# G-...` heading equal to its filename's stem (D1, as R-LINT-007 does
  for requirements), and at least one RFC 2119 keyword.
documents.requirements/R-LINT-018.md:
# R-LINT-018

**R-LINT-018** — The linter MUST resolve every `depends_on_guarantees`
  entry against the corpus and fail on any entry that does not resolve to
  an existing `G-<comp>-NNN` id, **and** separately fail when the resolved
  id's owning component is not already listed in this component's own
  `depends_on` (D2) — a distinct check from R-LINT-003's plain existence
  check. That second finding names the owning component by its
  `comp-<slug>` id.
documents.requirements/R-LINT-019.md:
# R-LINT-019

**R-LINT-019** — No line in any spec file (including its frontmatter block)
  MUST end in trailing whitespace. A fail-severity finding, not a warning.
  `spec_bundle_hash` is a function of the bundle's raw bytes — Markdown
  is not whitespace-insensitive (trailing spaces are CommonMark's
  hard-line-break syntax), so this rule keeps that byte difference from
  ever reaching a committed file, keeping the hash simple and trustworthy.
documents.requirements/R-LINT-020.md:
# R-LINT-020

**R-LINT-020** — R-LINT-003 (reference resolution), R-LINT-004 (acyclic
  `depends_on`), and R-LINT-018 (`depends_on_guarantees` resolution) MUST
  be implemented as queries over the `nodes`/`edges` views named in
  `specs/architecture/graph-query-engine.md`'s "Query surface" section —
  not independently-written frontmatter parsing or traversal code.

  Implementation requirement, not behavioral: R-LINT-018's second check
  is a join against `nodes.owner_component_id`. R-LINT-008/009 are
  `R-LINT-021`'s.

  Exception (D13): `nodes`/`edges` are component-level only, so
  R-LINT-003/004 each keep one native residual check for `architecture`-
  doc `depends_on` (grep-confirmed, the one other doc_type with any).
documents.requirements/R-LINT-021.md:
# R-LINT-021

**R-LINT-021** — R-LINT-008 (forward traceability) and R-LINT-009
  (backward traceability) MUST be implemented as queries over
  `graph-query-engine`'s `nodes`/`edges` views — not
  independently-written traversal code.

  R-LINT-008 becomes: every `requirement` node MUST be the target of at
  least one `covers` edge. R-LINT-009 becomes: every `covers` edge's
  target MUST resolve to a real `requirement` or `capability` node, and
  (per its existing distinct-message behavior) report separately whether
  a non-resolving target looked like an `R-id`, a `P-id`, or neither.

  Implementation requirement, not behavioral. Exception: R-LINT-009's
  line-reporting stays a native scan (`nodes`/`edges` don't map a
  `CS-id` to its `product` doc).
documents.requirements/R-LINT-024.md:
# R-LINT-024

**R-LINT-024** — A component's `Purpose` section MUST NOT cite a
  decision id (`D<N>`, bare or backtick-wrapped) — a fail-severity
  finding, not a warning. `Purpose` MUST be dependent-safe (`D21`): what
  a unit does and why, never how the design was arrived at. Decision
  citations and history belong in a `Rationale` section
  (`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §3.4).
documents.requirements/R-LINT-031.md:
# R-LINT-031

**R-LINT-031** — For every component with a CLI document under
  `interface/`, the linter MUST warn unless one of that component's
  requirements cites that document by its relative path and a
  criterion covers that requirement. The finding names the component
  id (`comp-<slug>`) and points at `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §5. Warn only, until every built
  component is covered (`D162`).
documents.requirements/R-LINT-032.md:
# R-LINT-032

**R-LINT-032** — When the linted `repo_root` holds `.hotdocs-tool.json`
  (a project made by `hotdocs init`), each component whose slug is also
  a directory directly under the tool root's `gen/` (the tool root
  being the parent of the nearest `gen` directory above the linter's
  own file) MUST get a `fail` finding naming that slug: the project's
  copy would shadow the tool's (`D199`).
documents.requirements/R-LINT-033.md:
# R-LINT-033

**R-LINT-033** — `lint` MUST include, after its own findings and as
  `Finding`s, every finding `citation-checker`'s and then
  `size-checker`'s `check(repo_root)` returns, limited to `paths` the
  same way as its own (`D242`). `load_corpus` MUST be `corpus-loader`'s
  function itself.

```gherkin
When author_test builds its prompt
Then the prompt contains "import slugify" and "import url_tools", and
  never contains "import capabilities"

Given a bundle whose component_id is "comp-semver" and whose
  module_names is []
When author_test builds its prompt
Then the prompt contains "import semver"
```
documents.component.md:
---
id: comp-test-author
title: Test Author
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-spec-bundle-assembler, comp-cache-manager, comp-llm-endpoint]
realizes: [P-ZERO-EDIT, P-AMBIGUITY-GATE]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
---

# Test Author

## Purpose

Authors the test code for one `generated-test`-kind criterion, from
spec prose alone, with no access to the implementation under test.
Invoked by `verifier-orchestrator` via an injectable callable — it
decides *when* (a criterion's `kind`); this decides *how*.

## Rationale

The "independent generation path" a `generated-test` criterion needs
to be trustworthy. Mirrors `llm-judge`'s own `judge` parameter.

## Scope

**In scope:** test code from a criterion's Given/When/Then prose plus
the target's `interface/`; canonical-model selection (R-AUTHOR-003);
caching.

**Out of scope:** deciding if a criterion needs a test — the `kind:`
tag, lint-checked (R-LINT-010), never re-decided here.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

All `kind: generated-test` (`D43`) — the model call uses an injected
mock, `generator`'s pattern; none fit the step-phrase grammar.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

None.

## Change log

See the decisions, `D56` onward; `D269` adds the reply format to `interface/`.
documents.constraints.md:
# Test Author — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Not deterministic, and that's expected — but bounded**, same posture as
  `generator`'s own constraints.md: a cache hit MUST be byte-identical for
  the same key; the recorded `seed`/model MUST match what was actually
  requested.
- **Independence is a preference, not a hard requirement.** Model selection
  prefers a different model than `generator` used (R-AUTHOR-003), but MUST
  NOT fail or block when only one model is available — consistent with
  every other instance of this posture in the corpus.
- **No silent partial output.** A model-call error MUST leave
  `verification/<component>/generated-test/` untouched for that criterion.
- **Credential handling.** Mirrors `generator`'s constraint exactly, for
  both credentials this component may use.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs author-test <component-id> <criterion-id> --model=<model-id> [--seed=<n>] [--repo-root=<dir>] [--format=json|text]
```

- `<criterion-id>` — the acceptance criterion's own id (e.g. `AC-FOO-003`).
- `--model` — required, same discipline as `generator`'s `--model`: never
  an implicit default.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Test code produced (from cache or a fresh model call) and written. |
| `1` | Model-call error (R-AUTHOR-007). |
| `2` | Usage error. |
documents.interface/data/CriterionBundle.md:
# `CriterionBundle`

```json
{
  "component_id": "comp-foo",
  "criterion_id": "AC-FOO-003",
  "covers": "R-FOO-003",
  "criterion_text": "<Given/When/Then prose>",
  "requirement_text": "<the covered R-id's own text from requirements/>",
  "interface": "<interface/ content>",
  "glossary": "<specs/glossary.md body>",
  "dependency_interfaces": {
    "comp-bar": "<comp-bar's own interface/ content>"
  },
  "module_names": ["foo"]
}
```

Assembled by `spec-bundle-assembler`'s narrow entry point, never with
`gen/<component>/` content (`R-AUTHOR-002`). `dependency_interfaces`
(`D100`) is keyed by every id in the target's `depends_on`, each value
that dependency's full `interface/` content (`R-ASSEMBLE-002`): a
public contract, so a fake can match the real signature and return
shape instead of guessing. `module_names` is optional and read with a
default, since the assembler's bundles do not carry it
(`R-AUTHOR-026`).
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
author_test(
    bundle: CriterionBundle, model: str, seed: int = 0,
    *, repo_root: Path = None, llm_backend=None,
) -> TestAuthoringResult
```

Not a pure function: like `generator`'s `generate()`, it makes an
external call. `llm_backend` is passed straight to `llm-endpoint`'s
`backend` parameter, the seam every `AC-AUTHOR-*` mock uses (`D57`).
A mock replies `-----BEGIN FILE <n>-----`, the file, then
`-----END FILE <n>-----`, `<n>` the `secrets.token_hex(16)` nonce read
from the prompt.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-001.md:
# R-AUTHOR-001

**R-AUTHOR-001** — Given a criterion's Given/When/Then text, its `Covers:
  R-id`, the covered requirement's own text from `requirements/`, the
  target component's `interface/` content, and the glossary (a
  `CriterionBundle`, assembled by `spec-bundle-assembler`), this component
  MUST produce test code that exercises the component's public interface as
  described, asserting the criterion's `Then` clause.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-002.md:
# R-AUTHOR-002

**R-AUTHOR-002** — The `CriterionBundle` MUST NOT include the target
  component's actual `gen/<component>/` source code — only its
  `interface/` contract. This is the same "write against the contract,
  not by reading the implementation" discipline `spec-bundle-assembler`
  already enforces for `generator` (R-ASSEMBLE-001), applied here to
  preserve the independence a `generated-test` check requires.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-003.md:
# R-AUTHOR-003

**R-AUTHOR-003** — Model selection MUST use the canonical model alone —
  the single-model-must-keep-working posture applied throughout this
  corpus.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-004.md:
# R-AUTHOR-004

**R-AUTHOR-004** — Before calling any model, MUST check `cache-manager`
  using a key derived from `(criterion content hash, gate_inputs_hash,
  gate_version, model)` — mirrors `generator`'s R-GEN-005 exactly, at
  criterion granularity instead of component granularity.

  **`gate_version`'s `<gate_type>@<semver>` prefix MUST be exactly
  `generated_test`** — `cache-manager`'s own six-entry `gate_type`
  registry (`interface/data/CachedResult.md`) names the *kind of cached
  artifact*, not the producing component; it has no `test_author` entry
  at all. `generator`'s own `gate_version` happens to equal its gate
  type only by coincidence — not a pattern to copy. Found at `D56`:
  a real candidate used `test_author@<version>` and crashed on its
  own first cache write.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-005.md:
# R-AUTHOR-005

**R-AUTHOR-005** — On a cache miss, after a successful call, the result
  MUST be written to `cache-manager` under that key before being returned —
  mirrors R-GEN-006.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-006.md:
# R-AUTHOR-006

**R-AUTHOR-006** — Output MUST be written only under
  `verification/<component>/generated-test/` — never under `gen/` (it is a
  test, not application code), and never overwriting `criterion-compiler`'s
  own output directory. The filename itself MUST be the glossary's
  "Criterion test filename" formula (`D63`) — never a content hash or
  any other suffix — since `verifier-orchestrator` must be able to
  predict this exact path to check for an already-authored test before
  deciding whether to dispatch to this component at all (`R-VERIFY-002`).
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-007.md:
# R-AUTHOR-007

**R-AUTHOR-007** — A model-call error MUST be reported as a distinct
  failure mode from "the authored test ran but failed" — mirrors R-GEN-008's
  classification distinction, consumed by `verifier-orchestrator` to tell
  "could not author a test" apart from "the test says the criterion isn't
  met."
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-008.md:
# R-AUTHOR-008

**R-AUTHOR-008** — `VAR-ANTHROPIC-API-KEY` MUST never appear in output,
  logs, or provenance — only the model identifier actually used is
  recorded. Since `D18`, this component no longer holds that credential
  at all (`llm-endpoint`/`R-ENDPOINT-005` does), so this is now a
  structural guarantee, not just a checked one — stated here regardless,
  as the component-local half of that guarantee's coverage.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-009.md:
# R-AUTHOR-009

**R-AUTHOR-009** — The prompt MUST instruct the model to wrap its test
  file's content exactly as:

  ```
  -----BEGIN FILE <nonce>-----
  <the complete, exact test file content, verbatim>
  -----END FILE <nonce>-----
  ```

  with `<nonce>` a fresh, per-call random value in the instruction
  and the extraction regex — same mechanism `generator` already uses
  (`R-GEN-015`, `D38`), for one file. MUST also state the model has
  no tool/file access and must answer from the bundle alone.

  `author_test` MUST extract strictly from between the markers,
  discarding anything outside (fence, narration, preamble/postamble).
  No matching BEGIN/END pair MUST be a distinct authoring failure —
  nothing written to cache or disk, same posture `R-AUTHOR-007`
  states for a `model_call_error`.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-010.md:
# R-AUTHOR-010

**R-AUTHOR-010** — The prompt MUST always state this corpus's
  dependency-resolution convention: how the component under test
  resolves its OWN dependencies. It MUST also say, in those words, that
  the component under test itself needs no custom loader: a plain
  `import <module_name>` (`D97`).

  MUST state: no dependency is statically importable; resolution is
  dynamic, at runtime, from
  `<repo_root>/gen/<dependency-slug>/<module_name>.py` (flat) or
  `.../<module_name>/__init__.py` (package), else the tool's own copy
  (`D199`), so omitting one never makes it missing — never interceptable by
  name-based `sys.modules` injection or `mock.patch`. To fake a
  dependency, write a fake module file under a fresh temporary
  `repo_root` — **always flat-module shape** (`D97`): every real
  loader checks flat first. `module_name` is, in those words, "the slug with hyphens
  replaced by underscores", never `"__init__"`.

  MUST include a literal snippet with the line
  `sys.modules[module_name] = module` **before**
  `spec.loader.exec_module(module)`, which a dataclass needs (`D96`).
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-011.md:
# R-AUTHOR-011

**R-AUTHOR-011** — The prompt MUST include each entry of
  `dependency_interfaces` (`D100`, `R-ASSEMBLE-009`), one per
  dependency, and MUST instruct the model that any fake it writes for a
  dependency's behavior MUST match that dependency's real, documented
  call signature and return shape exactly, never invented or simplified.
  A dependency's contract is public, unlike the target's own
  implementation (`R-AUTHOR-002`).

  Prose alone proved insufficient for return shape (`D113`): the prompt
  MUST also include one worked example — given a documented return type
  with named fields, the fake MUST expose every field, never a bare
  list/string/number even if the test reads only one.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-012.md:
# R-AUTHOR-012

**R-AUTHOR-012** — The prompt MUST always include the frontmatter
  `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` requires on every such document: `id`, `title`,
  `status`, `owners` always, `status` exactly one of
  `draft`/`ratified`/`deprecated` (`D105`). This applies to every
  frontmatter-bearing document a fixture constructs (`component.md`,
  `specs/vars/VAR-*.md`, `specs/decisions/D<N>.md`).

  It MUST also state: every `requirements/` file needs a matching
  `acceptance/` file with a `Covers:` tag, for every fixture component
  (`D105`, `R-LINT-008`); `status: ratified` also sets a placeholder
  `last_ratified_commit` (`D107`, `R-LINT-002`); a unit file
  (`constraints.md`, or anything under `requirements/`, `interface/`,
  `acceptance/`) carries no frontmatter at all (`R-LINT-016`, `D115`);
  and a test MUST NEVER `import yaml` or any other not-already-installed
  third-party package — write and parse frontmatter as plain text
  (`D125`).
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-013.md:
# R-AUTHOR-013

**R-AUTHOR-013** — The prompt MUST instruct that a synthetic fixture
  (`R-AUTHOR-012`) SHOULD default to `sealed: true` (short, fake
  `source_path` not under `gen/`) unless the criterion specifically
  concerns `realizes`/capability-linkage: sealed exempts it from
  `realizes` and the capability machinery, sidestepping a whole
  `spec-linter` rule class (`R-LINT-006`). Only when a criterion
  genuinely needs `realizes`-driven behavior MUST the fixture supply a
  resolvable `P-<id>` (`D103`).
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-014.md:
# R-AUTHOR-014

**R-AUTHOR-014** — The prompt MUST state that any list-valued
  frontmatter field (`owners`, `depends_on`, `realizes`, `uses_var`) in
  a synthetic fixture (`R-AUTHOR-012`) MUST use YAML flow style,
  showing the literal example `[a, b]`, never block style. This corpus's frontmatter reader does
  not recognize block style as a list, and every real spec file already
  uses flow style (`D104`).
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-015.md:
# R-AUTHOR-015

**R-AUTHOR-015** — The prompt MUST instruct that whenever a test
  constructs a synthetic fixture (`R-AUTHOR-012`) and the criterion
  depends on a precondition the target checks against `spec-linter`,
  the test MUST call `lint()` against the fixture first and assert zero
  hard-fail findings before exercising the real behavior (`D110`);
  self-check alone is necessary but not sufficient (`R-AUTHOR-020`).
  The prompt MUST include the exact call as a literal worked snippet,
  not prose: `lint(None, repo_root)` — `paths` first, positionally
  `None`, never one positional argument (`D116`/`D117`). Otherwise an
  `R-AUTHOR-012`–`014` failure surfaces as a confusing deep failure
  (`D104`).
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-016.md:
# R-AUTHOR-016

**R-AUTHOR-016** — `author_test` MUST treat every `CriterionBundle`
  field access as optional: a bundle (dict or object) missing a field
  — `dependency_interfaces` above all — MUST read as if that field
  were absent (empty/`None`), never raise `AttributeError`/`KeyError`.
  `CriterionBundle` is duck-typed (`D94`), and this corpus has more
  than one bundle-shaped producer, some narrower than
  `spec-bundle-assembler`'s canonical shape (`R-ASSEMBLE-009`) —
  `author_test` owns that compatibility, not either producer.

  Found once a second producer predated `R-AUTHOR-011` and never
  carried `dependency_interfaces` (`D106`, closed for real by `D119`):
  crashed with a bare `AttributeError`.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-019.md:
# R-AUTHOR-019

**R-AUTHOR-019** — The call to `llm_endpoint.complete()` MUST pass
  only `prompt`, `model`, and `backend` — mirroring `generator`'s own
  call exactly — and MUST NOT forward `seed` or any other bookkeeping
  parameter. `complete()` forwards every param verbatim to the real
  backend (`R-ENDPOINT-001`), which turns each into a CLI flag; `seed`
  is not a real flag, so forwarding it fails every real (non-mocked)
  call outright. `seed` is `author_test`'s own cache-key input only.

  Found once a real retry ran for the first time (`D108`): all 14
  criteria failed identically with a generic backend error.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-020.md:
# R-AUTHOR-020

**R-AUTHOR-020** — `author_test` MUST statically validate a response
  before accepting it, never relying on model self-check alone.

  **Syntax check:** `ast.parse()` the extracted content first. A
  `SyntaxError` is a distinct failure (`model_call_error` category
  `malformed_code`); nothing is cached or written (`R-AUTHOR-009`).

  **Fake-arity check, best-effort:** parse every `name(args) ->
  ReturnType` signature from each `dependency_interfaces` entry; a comma
  inside brackets never splits a parameter (`dict[str, str]` is one). Walk
  the test's top-level `FunctionDef`s, simple `name = other_name`
  aliases resolved to their target's arity (`D126`), and string
  literals that parse as Python (`D113`); for a name matching a
  dependency function, compare parameter counts (`*args`/`**kwargs`
  satisfy any). A name more than one dependency defines matches if it fits any of their
  arities (`D166`). A mismatch is a distinct failure
  (`fake_signature_mismatch`, naming the function and both arities).
  Skip what can't be parsed unambiguously (`D110`).
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-021.md:
# R-AUTHOR-021

**R-AUTHOR-021** — The prompt MUST instruct that every field read from
  a value the target itself returns (not only a faked dependency's
  data) MUST use dual dict-or-attribute access, never assumed to be
  one shape — this corpus's duck-typing convention (`D94`) means any
  component may return either shape in a given round.

  Found at `D112`: one `provenance-tracker` batch applied dual access
  inconsistently, correctly for one criterion, bare for three others.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-022.md:
# R-AUTHOR-022

**R-AUTHOR-022** — The prompt MUST instruct that a test MUST NEVER
  assert a fake was used by reaching into `sys.modules` under a
  guessed key — real loaders key dynamically (often `repo_root`- or
  hash-qualified, `R-AUTHOR-010`), so any guess is unreliable. To
  confirm a fake ran, its own code MUST record its invocation to a
  **file** (`R-AUTHOR-024`), never an in-process list — the test
  can't reliably re-locate the module object that wrote to it either.

  Found at `D123`: a guessed `sys.modules["real_name"]` assertion
  failed once the loader (correctly) keyed under something else.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-023.md:
# R-AUTHOR-023

**R-AUTHOR-023** — The prompt MUST instruct that a test asserting a
  wall-clock "own write time" field falls within a `[before, after]`
  window MUST truncate `before`/`after` to the same precision the
  field's own documented format carries (e.g. whole seconds for a
  `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` example with no fractional digits) — never
  compare a truncated-on-write timestamp against microsecond-precision
  bounds directly.

  Found at `D129`: `before`/`after` captured at full microsecond
  precision against a whole-second-documented format fails a
  correctly-implemented candidate on almost every real run.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-024.md:
# R-AUTHOR-024

**R-AUTHOR-024** — Confirming a dynamically-loaded fake was invoked
  MUST use a file-based invocation log — the fake appends its
  invocation record to a file under a path the test controls — never
  an in-process, module-level list read via any `sys.modules` lookup.
  A correct candidate may key `sys.modules` dynamically (`R-GEN-018`),
  so the key is never predictable from the test's side; only a file
  survives regardless of which module object the candidate used.

  Found (`D144`): an earlier fix (`D143`) instructed reading
  `sys.modules[module_name]` under the bare dependency name — the
  guessed-key failure `R-AUTHOR-022` already forbade.
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-025.md:
# R-AUTHOR-025

**R-AUTHOR-025** — The prompt MUST name the component under test's own
  module concretely: its slug (`component_id` without `comp-`) with
  every hyphen replaced by an underscore, so `comp-foo-bar` is
  `foo_bar`, written as the exact statement `import foo_bar` — never
  left for the test author to infer from a function name or from the
  `component_id` itself (`comp_foo_bar` is wrong). The generator may
  lay the module out as `<module>.py` or a `<module>/` package; the
  import is the same either way (`D189`).
documents.requirements/R-AUTHOR-026.md:
# R-AUTHOR-026

**R-AUTHOR-026** — A bundle MAY carry `module_names`, a list of module
  names. When it is non-empty, the prompt MUST name each of them, in
  order, as a module under test, written as the exact statement
  `import <name>`, in place of `R-AUTHOR-025`'s derived name, which the
  prompt then never offers as an import. A capability scenario's
  `component_id` (`capabilities/<P-id>`) names no module, so its caller
  passes the realizing components' modules here (`D198`). When it is
  absent or empty, `R-AUTHOR-025` applies.
