documents.component.md:
---
id: comp-verifier-orchestrator
title: Verifier Orchestrator
status: draft
owners: [pipeline-team]
depends_on: [comp-criterion-compiler, comp-generator, comp-test-author, comp-spec-bundle-assembler]
realizes: [P-ZERO-EDIT, P-AMBIGUITY-GATE]
model_pin: claude-opus-5-5
sealed: false
---

# Verifier Orchestrator

## Purpose

Runs every applicable verification gate against one component's generated
output and produces a single, structured pass/fail verdict: `compiled`
criteria (via `criterion-compiler`), `generated-test` criteria, `llm-judge`
criteria, the contract/property tests derived from `interface/`, and the
interface drift check.

## Scope

**In scope:** dispatching each acceptance criterion to the right checking
mechanism by its declared `kind`; running the interface drift check;
aggregating mutation scores; producing one `VerificationReport`.

**Out of scope:** the license/secret scans (separate components);
*performing* an `llm-judge` evaluation or *authoring*
`generated-test` code (this component dispatches to an injectable judge and
an injectable `test_author` and records their results — it does not itself
judge or author anything, see the note below); **re-deciding a criterion's
declared `kind`** — `compiled`/`generated-test`/`llm-judge` is fixed at
spec-authoring time in `acceptance/`, lint-checked (R-LINT-010), and never
reconsidered here. Giving this component (or `test-author`) the power to
override that declaration at verification time was considered and
explicitly rejected: it would make `kind:` advisory rather than normative,
and would turn this component's own dispatch logic into a judgment call,
breaking the determinism cache-key validity and R-VERIFY-008's
idempotency claim both depend on.

## Definitions

No deltas from `specs/glossary.md`.

## Behavior

See `requirements/`.

## Interfaces

See `interface/`.

## Data

See `interface/data/`.

## Acceptance criteria

See `acceptance/`.

All thirteen criteria are `kind: compiled` — this component coordinates
checking mechanisms (some of which involve judgment or external calls), but
the coordination itself is deterministic dispatch-and-record logic, testable
by mocking `criterion-compiler` and the judge callable. A fourth component
in this corpus whose entire acceptance set is `compiled`.

## Non-functional constraints

See `constraints.md`.

## Open questions

## Change log

See the decisions, `D27` onward; `D274` adds fixture guidance to `interface/`.
documents.constraints.md:
# Verifier Orchestrator — Non-Functional Constraints

- **Determinism of orchestration, not of what it orchestrates.** This
  component's own dispatch and aggregation MUST be deterministic
  (R-VERIFY-008); an injected `llm-judge` or `test_author` callable's
  output is not covered.
- **`kind:` is read-only input.** This component and `test_author` MUST
  NOT alter or reinterpret a criterion's declared `kind`; it is fixed at
  spec-authoring time and lint-checked.
- **No bypassing `skipped` or the `generated-test`/`llm-judge` `fail`
  asymmetry.** A `skipped` `llm-judge` result MUST never become `pass`,
  and an unauthored `generated-test` result MUST never become `skipped`
  (R-VERIFY-005/010); the distinction is load-bearing for the
  multi-model coverage metric (`notes/metrics.md`).
- **Performance.** Checks SHOULD take time proportional to the
  component's own size caps (`D17`); no new budget is set.
documents.interface/cli.md:
# CLI

```
hotdocs verify-component <component-id> [--repo-root=<dir>] [--format=json|text]
```

Not `hotdocs verify`, `provenance-tracker`'s readiness check (`D190`).

`main(argv)` receives `argv` beginning with `<component-id>`. Each flag
takes its value as `--flag=value` or as the next argument;
`--repo-root` defaults to the current directory, `--format` to `text`.
`json` prints the `VerificationReport`; `text` prints `<component_id>:
<overall>` then one indented `<criterion id>: <result>` line each.

| Exit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Overall verdict `pass`. |
| `1` | Overall verdict `fail`. |
| `2` | Usage error: no `<component-id>`, invalid `--format`, unknown argument, a flag last with no value, or no `specs/components/<slug>/component.md`. |
documents.interface/data/VerificationReport.md:
# `VerificationReport`

```json
{
  "component_id": "comp-foo",
  "criteria": [
    { "id": "AC-FOO-001", "covers": "R-FOO-001", "kind": "compiled", "result": "pass" },
    { "id": "AC-FOO-002", "covers": "R-FOO-002", "kind": "llm-judge", "result": "skipped", "rationale": null },
    { "id": "AC-FOO-003", "covers": "R-FOO-003", "kind": "generated-test", "result": "pass",
      "test_authoring": { "model": "gpt-5", "seed": 0, "prompt_version": "v1", "cache_hit": false } }
  ],
  "requirement_results": { "R-FOO-001": "pass", "R-FOO-002": "fail", "R-FOO-003": "pass" },
  "interface_drift": false,
  "mutation_score": 0.92,
  "overall": "pass"
}
```

`mutation_score` is `null` for a sealed component (`R-VERIFY-017`).

`result` is one of `pass` / `fail` / `skipped`, `spec-linter`'s
`severity` vocabulary. `test_authoring` is present only on
`generated-test` criteria that actually dispatched to `test_author` this
run (absent on a cache hit with no fresh authoring call, and absent on
every other `kind`): it carries `test-author`'s provenance to
`provenance-writer` inside this report, as `rationale` does for
`llm-judge`.

`covers` (R-VERIFY-011) is the same `Covers:` value every criterion already
carries in its own file — exposed here so `requirement_results` is
auditable, not just asserted. `requirement_results` (R-VERIFY-011) is the
graph projection of `criteria` onto `R-id`s via `covers`: `pass` only if
every covering criterion is `pass`, `fail` otherwise (a `skipped`
`llm-judge` criterion counts as `fail` for this purpose — "not yet
demonstrated" and "demonstrated wrong" are the same signal here).
Deliberately **boolean-only** — no Gherkin text, no `rationale`, no
expected/actual values — this is the field `generator`'s retry mechanism
(R-GEN-010) consumes, and it must never carry anything that discloses what
a specific test checked.

**This `skipped`-counts-as-`fail` rule is independent of `overall`'s**
(R-VERIFY-005: a `skipped` `llm-judge` finding alone never fails
`overall`): `overall` decides whether to block the merge,
`requirement_results` what a retry should attend to. In the example,
`AC-FOO-002` is `skipped`, giving `R-FOO-002: fail`, while `overall` is
`pass`.

**`failure_detail`** (R-VERIFY-012) — present only on a `compiled` or
`generated-test` criterion whose `result` is `fail`:

```json
{ "id": "AC-FOO-004", "covers": "R-FOO-004", "kind": "compiled", "result": "fail",
  "failure_detail": { "message": "result.foo equals 5 failed", "expected": 5, "actual": 3 } }
```

Mirrors `llm-judge`'s `rationale` one `kind` family over — every `kind`
that can fail now carries its own structured account of why. Exposed
for provenance/review-packet/human consumption only: it never reaches
`requirement_results` (already boolean-only, above) or
`retry_feedback`'s `R-id`-only channel (`R-GEN-012`).
documents.interface/library.md:
# Library

```
verify(component_id: str, repo_root: Path, judge=None, test_author=None) -> VerificationReport
GATE_VERSION: str  # "verifier-orchestrator@2.0.0" (R-VERIFY-015)
```

`verify` returns a **dataclass** instance whose fields are attributes
(`report.overall`, `report.criteria`), with a `to_dict()` giving the
JSON form. Each `criteria` entry is a plain **dict** (`c["id"]`,
`c["result"]`), as is `requirement_results`: never a bare-dict report,
never criterion objects (`D190`).

`judge`/`test_author` are the glossary's "Injected `judge`/`test_author`
callable shape" (`D65`): one `bundle` argument, unlike `spec-linter`'s
three-argument `judge` (`R-LINT-015`). Omit `judge` to run with every `llm-judge` criterion reporting
`skipped`. `test_author` is the equivalent for `generated-test` criteria
lacking a cached test (R-VERIFY-009) — **but omitting it degrades
differently**: a `generated-test` criterion with nothing cached and no
`test_author` configured reports `fail`, not `skipped` (R-VERIFY-010).

It loads `spec-bundle-assembler` from `<repo_root>/gen/spec-bundle-assembler/`
and the sealed `criterion-compiler` from
`<repo_root>/pipeline/criterion-compiler/`, either else from the tool
root (`D199`); a test plants a fake dependency at that path. A fixture
component under test is never `sealed`, unless its criterion concerns
sealed verification (`R-VERIFY-017`): a sealed one runs only its
characterization tests, never its compiled or generated ones. An
unsealed fixture component lints clean only with `realizes: [P-<ID>]`
naming a capability file the fixture also writes under `specs/product/`
(`R-LINT-006`). Name fixture functions other than `foo`:
`spec-bundle-assembler`'s interface text declares `foo(x)`, which
`test-author`'s fake-arity check (`R-AUTHOR-020`) would match. Every
fixture criterion has at least one Given, one When and one Then step
(`R-LINT-010`). `verify` checks no precondition against `spec-linter`,
so a test does not lint its fixture (`R-AUTHOR-015`).

Implements: `specs/architecture/step-phrase-grammar.md`, `SPEC_GUIDELINES.md`
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-001.md:
# R-VERIFY-001

**R-VERIFY-001** — For every `compiled`-kind criterion in a component's
  `acceptance/` directory, this component MUST invoke `criterion-compiler`
  to produce test scaffolding, execute it against `gen/<component>/`, and
  record a pass/fail per criterion.

  Executing that scaffolding MUST scope the import search path
  (`PYTHONPATH` for `pytest`) to `gen/<component>/` itself, never a
  broader ancestor such as `gen/` — `criterion-compiler`'s emitted
  `import <module_name>` (`R-COMPILE-013`) only resolves to the real
  module at that specific scope; any broader scope resolves it as an
  empty implicit namespace package instead, since `gen/<component>/`
  has no `__init__.py`. The same scoping applies to any sandboxed copy
  of `gen/<component>/` used for mutation testing (R-VERIFY-006).
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-002.md:
# R-VERIFY-002

**R-VERIFY-002** — For every `generated-test`-kind criterion, this
  component MUST obtain the test code — from cache if already authored for
  this criterion's content, or by dispatching to an injectable
  `test_author` callable otherwise (R-VERIFY-009) — execute it against
  `gen/<component>/`, and record a pass/fail per criterion.

  "From cache" here means: this component itself MUST check, before
  ever calling `test_author`, whether the glossary's "Criterion test
  filename" (`D63`) already exists directly under
  `verification/<component>/generated-test/` for this criterion — never
  a separate, self-invented cache location or naming scheme (a content
  hash, a nested subdirectory) — and use it as-is if so. This is a
  file-presence check this component performs itself, distinct from
  (and prior to) whatever internal cache `test_author` may consult on
  its own side when it IS dispatched (`R-AUTHOR-004`/`005`).
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-003.md:
# R-VERIFY-003

**R-VERIFY-003** — For every `llm-judge`-kind criterion, this component
  MUST invoke an injectable judge callable **exactly once**, passing
  exactly the same `CriterionBundle` `test_author` receives for that
  criterion (`R-VERIFY-009`) — never a separate, narrower payload — and
  record its pass/fail + rationale, or record `skipped` when no judge is
  configured. (`capability-scenario-verifier`'s bundle is necessarily
  narrower; see the glossary's "Injected `judge`/`test_author` callable
  shape," `D65`.) Call shape and result handling follow the
  graceful-degradation posture of `spec-linter`'s R-LINT-015. This
  component's own behavior is dispatch and recording, not judgment,
  which is why every requirement here is deterministic. Exactly once is
  deliberate: a dual-call design that compares two judges was
  considered and deferred (`notes/initial-ideas.md` §14).
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-004.md:
# R-VERIFY-004

**R-VERIFY-004** — This component MUST perform the interface drift check:
  every callable `interface/library.md`/`interface/cli.md` documents MUST
  exist in `gen/<component>/` with a matching parameter list; any missing
  callable or parameter mismatch MUST be recorded as a hard failure.

  **One-directional, not set equality** (`D84`): a module defining
  additional public names `interface/` never documented (a helper class,
  a return-type dataclass) MUST NOT itself count as drift. The check's
  job is "does the documented interface still work," never "does nothing
  else exist."
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-005.md:
# R-VERIFY-005

**R-VERIFY-005** — The overall verdict MUST be `fail` if any `compiled` or
  `generated-test` criterion fails, or the interface drift check fails, or
  any `llm-judge` criterion is evaluated and fails. A `skipped` `llm-judge`
  finding MUST NOT by itself cause an overall `fail` — `skipped` means "not
  evaluated," not "violated," consistent with `spec-linter`'s existing
  severity semantics.
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-006.md:
# R-VERIFY-006

**R-VERIFY-006** — For `generated-test`-kind criteria, this component MUST
  compute and report the mutation score, and the overall verdict MUST be
  `fail` if it falls below 0.8, or 0.9 when a `generated-test` criterion
  is freeform-derived, written with no Given/When/Then block
  (`SPEC_GUIDELINES.md` §5, `D80`).

  **A single score for the whole component, a union across all of its
  own `generated-test` criteria's test files — never an average of
  per-criterion scores** (`D124`): generate each mutant once, against the
  whole candidate module; it counts as killed if *any* of those test
  files fails against it. `VerificationReport.mutation_score` is exactly
  one number per component (`interface/data/VerificationReport.md`).

  **Exactly four mutation operators, one mutant per site** (`D159`),
  with these exact swaps (`D172`) — the bar was calibrated against them,
  so a regeneration MUST NOT change them: a comparison with exactly one
  operator has it swapped `==`↔`!=`, `<`↔`>=`, `>`↔`<=`, `is`↔`is not`,
  `in`↔`not in` (a chained comparison is not a site); an `and`/`or`
  flipped to the other; a binary `+`↔`-`, `*`↔`/`, `//`↔`%`; a boolean
  constant negated. Never numeric constants or anything else.
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-007.md:
# R-VERIFY-007

**R-VERIFY-007** — This component MUST produce one structured
  `VerificationReport` — per-criterion results, mutation scores, interface
  drift result, and the overall verdict — consumed by `provenance-writer`
  and `review-packet-builder`.
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-008.md:
# R-VERIFY-008

**R-VERIFY-008** — Given the same `gen/<component>/` content, the same
  `acceptance/` content, and a judge callable that itself returns
  consistent results, this component's own orchestration logic MUST be
  idempotent: re-running it MUST reproduce the same `VerificationReport`.
  This claims this component's *own* determinism, not that `llm-judge`
  evaluations are reproducible, hence the condition on the judge.
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-009.md:
# R-VERIFY-009

**R-VERIFY-009** — For a `generated-test`-kind criterion with no cached
  test yet, this component MUST dispatch to an injectable `test_author`
  callable, passing exactly the `CriterionBundle`
  `spec-bundle-assembler.assemble_criterion(component_id, criterion_id,
  repo_root)` returns for that criterion, and use the returned test
  code. It MUST NOT build its own `CriterionBundle`: a second producer
  with a narrower field set silently starved `test-author` of
  `dependency_interfaces` (`D119`). Its role is dispatch and recording,
  as in R-VERIFY-003; the authoring happens inside the injected
  callable, which is why this requirement is `kind: compiled` despite
  coordinating non-deterministic work.
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-010.md:
# R-VERIFY-010

**R-VERIFY-010** — Unlike a `skipped` `llm-judge` finding, a
  `generated-test` criterion with no cached test and no `test_author`
  configured MUST be recorded as `fail`, not `skipped`. `llm-judge` is
  for qualities no test could capture, so "not evaluated" is a
  legitimate, visible gap; a `generated-test` criterion exists because
  a real, mutation-tested check is possible, so an unauthored one is a
  verification gap the mutation-score gate (R-VERIFY-006) presumes
  absent.
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-011.md:
# R-VERIFY-011

**R-VERIFY-011** — The `VerificationReport` MUST include a
  `requirement_results` field: one `pass`/`fail` entry per `R-id` the
  component declares, computed by projecting each criterion's own
  `result` onto the `R-id`(s) it `Covers:` — the traceability edges
  `R-LINT-008`/`009` enforce and `corpus-graph-builder` materializes,
  reused rather than recomputed. A requirement is `pass` only if
  **every** criterion covering it is `pass`; **any** covering criterion
  that is `fail` or `skipped` makes it `fail`, since "not fully
  demonstrated" and "demonstrated wrong" both mean unverified.

  `requirement_results` MUST contain **only** `R-id` keys and
  `pass`/`fail` values — never a criterion's Gherkin text, `rationale`,
  expected/actual values, or anything else that could let a consumer
  reconstruct what a specific test checked. That keeps
  `spec-bundle-assembler`'s R-ASSEMBLE-001 exclusion of `acceptance/`
  from being undone through this field, whoever reads it.
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-012.md:
# R-VERIFY-012

**R-VERIFY-012** — A `compiled` or `generated-test` criterion whose
  `result` is `fail` MUST additionally carry a `failure_detail` field:
  `{message, expected, actual}`. `message` is a short, human-readable
  description of what failed (an assertion summary, a traceback's final
  line). `expected`/`actual` carry the compared values whenever the
  underlying check is a direct equality/containment match — always
  populated for a `compiled` criterion, since the step-phrase grammar's
  assertion templates (`specs/architecture/step-phrase-grammar.md`) name
  what was compared. **Each value MUST be its original Python type**
  (`D85`): an int, float, bool, or `None` MUST NOT be left as the raw
  string pytest's failure text renders it as; a parser that can locate
  the compared values MUST recover their real type (e.g. via
  `ast.literal_eval`), since `5 == 5` and `"5" == "5"` differ.
  `expected`/`actual` MAY be `null` for a `generated-test` criterion
  whose assertion this component cannot structurally interpret, in which
  case `message` alone is still required. A `pass` or `skipped`
  criterion's `failure_detail` MUST be absent.

  `failure_detail` MUST NOT reach `requirement_results` (`R-VERIFY-011`)
  or `retry_feedback`'s `R-id`-only channel (`R-GEN-012`); it is exposed
  on `criteria[]` for provenance, review-packet, and human use only.
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-013.md:
# R-VERIFY-013

**R-VERIFY-013** — Every dynamically loaded module (the component
  under test, `criterion-compiler`, `spec-bundle-assembler`, and any
  other dependency) MUST be cached, if at all, keyed by
  `(repo_root, module_name)` — never by `module_name` alone. A bare
  module-name key collides across two different `repo_root`s using the
  same component slug in one process (this component's own tests use
  slug `"foo"` against a fresh `tmp_path` each time), so a later call
  could silently reuse an earlier call's stale module (`D120`; the same
  bug class `R-TRACK-011` closed for `provenance-tracker`).
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-014.md:
# R-VERIFY-014

**R-VERIFY-014** — Every test run MUST have a wall-clock timeout,
  killing the whole process tree: 300 seconds for a run on unmutated
  code, and for a mutant's run 2 seconds or 10× the unmutated suite's
  own run time, whichever is larger. A mutant whose run times out
  counts as killed; a timed-out run on unmutated code fails that
  criterion (`D158`, after a mutant made a loop infinite).

  A mutant's tests MUST run with both the working directory and
  `PYTHONPATH` set to the mutated copy, never `repo_root`, so a test's
  relative `sys.path` entry (e.g. `gen/foo`) cannot import the original
  module (`D159`), and with pytest's `--noconftest`, so a hand suite's
  `verification/<slug>/conftest.py` above the generated tests cannot
  import it either (`D280`).
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-015.md:
# R-VERIFY-015

**R-VERIFY-015** — The module MUST define `GATE_VERSION`, currently
  `"verifier-orchestrator@2.0.0"`, readable without calling `verify`.
  Any change to the mutation operators, the mutation threshold, the
  timeout rule, or how a criterion's `kind` is dispatched MUST bump it
  in this requirement, since a provenance hit reuses this gate's
  verdict only while its version is unchanged (`D163`).
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-016.md:
# R-VERIFY-016

**R-VERIFY-016** — A criterion's id MUST be taken exactly from its
  file's `# AC-...` heading — including an optional lowercase letter
  suffix such as `AC-FOO-003b` — and passed unchanged everywhere,
  including to `assemble_criterion`. Never case-transformed or
  re-derived from the file name (`D163`).
documents.requirements/R-VERIFY-017.md:
# R-VERIFY-017

**R-VERIFY-017** — For a component whose `component.md` frontmatter has
  `sealed: true` and a single-line `source_path: <path>` (`D170`),
  `verify` MUST verify the code at `<repo_root>/<source_path>`, not
  `gen/<slug>/`: that directory is where the module is loaded from for
  interface drift (`R-VERIFY-004`) and what tests may import, and a
  missing `source_path` directory makes `overall` `fail`, never an
  exception. Its criteria are
  verified only by the characterization tests: the `test_*.py` files
  directly in `verification/<slug>/` (hand-maintained, never authored by
  `test_author`).

  A `compiled` or `generated-test` criterion `AC-X-NNN` is `pass` iff at
  least one test function named `test_` plus the id lowercased with
  hyphens as underscores (`test_ac_x_nnn`), exactly or followed by `_`
  and more text, exists in those files and every such test passes. It is
  `fail` otherwise; with no matching test its `failure_detail.message`
  is `no characterization test`. `test_author` and the cached-test lookup
  are never used. `llm-judge` criteria follow `R-VERIFY-003`.

  Mutation testing is not run: `mutation_score` is `null` and never
  gates `overall`, which is `pass` iff no criterion failed and there is
  no interface drift. Files named `.sealed-provenance.json` and
  `__pycache__` directories under `source_path` are ignored.

# R-VERIFY-018

**R-VERIFY-018** — `main(argv)` MUST implement `interface/cli.md`
  exactly: both flag forms, the defaults, JSON and text output, exit
  `0`/`1` for a passing/failing verdict, and `2` for every listed usage
  error. Its usage message names `hotdocs verify-component`, never
  `hotdocs verify` (`D162`, `D190`).
